# Part I Design Manager

# Chapter 1 Introduction

Design Manager (DM) is the control panel of the Aether EDA Tools. Its main purpose is to control and manage design libraries, models and cells, views of design and so on, in short your entire design hierarchy. Design Manager manages your design processes by Schematic Editor and Layout Editor, as well dozens of toolboxes, such as EDIF-IN, EDIF-OUT, GDS-IN, GDS-OUT, etc. The goal of Design Manager is to make your design process simpler and more productive.

## 1.1 Design Manager Setup

In shell prompt, type source < aether_inst_path >/setup.bash & or source < aether_inst_path >/setup.csh & and hit enter. This will initialize the environment of Aether .

## 1.2 Starting Design Manager

- 1. In shell prompt, type aether & and hit enter. This will start a Design Manager which provides the access to the entire Aether tools’ suite. The window is shown Figure 1.1 .


- Chapter 1. Introduction


![image 2](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2.png)

Figure 1.1 Design Manager Window

- 2. Design Manager’s user interface consists of four sub-windows: Library, Category, Cell and View browsers, and a window for operational messages. Among the four browser windows, the Category window can be turned oﬀ.
- 3. Design Manager’s Library browser is a tree widget. Users could specify combined libraries in lib.defs by ASSIGN a COMBINE property to the libDef.
- 4. Design Manager’s View browser is a tab used to display various status information of views. The view browser is shown Figure 1.2 .

![image 3](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3.png)

Figure 1.2 View Browser

- 5. Design Manager’s Show ﬁles is a tab widget and consists of two tabs:Library and Cell tabs. The ﬁles in library display in Library tab, and the ﬁles in cell display in Cell tab.
- 6. In the operational message window, the Design Manager assigns diﬀerent colors to a text in order to indicate the types of messages:


4 Aether Reference Manual, 2025.09

1.3. Mouse Operations

- • Black: note
- • Red: error
- • Blue: warning


## 1.3 Mouse Operations

- 1. If you select one of the Library/Category/Cell/View items and click the right mouse button, a sub-menu of actions will pop up. Respectively, a sub-menus of actions are listed in Figure 1.3 .

![image 4](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4.png)

Figure 1.3 Mouse Actions

- 2. Double click on a cell item, if the cell has one view only, Design Manager will start the corresponding design tool according to the existing view.
- 3. Double click on a view item and the Design Manager will start the corresponding design tool according to the selected view.
- 4. Click on a view item, and the type is Layout or Schematic or Symbol, then shows thumbnail of the view.

## 2.1 New Library

Menu: File -> New Library ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5.png)

This command is used to create a new library. The form is shown in Figure 2.1 .

![image 6](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6.png)

Figure 2.1 New Library Form

Name: sets the name for the new library. In Directory: sets the path for the new library on the disk. Technology: sets the technology information for the new library.

- • Attach To Library: attaches the library to the existing technology library.


7

- • Reference To Libraries: the new library can refer to multiple existing technology libraries. If you choose this option, the technology ﬁles of selected libraries will be merged together in the new library.
- • Load ASCII File: creates a technology based on the ASCII ﬁle.
- • Do Not Need: the new library does not need a technology ﬁle.


GDS Layer Map: speciﬁes the GDS layer mapping ﬁle. This ﬁle is used during GDS import and export.

Display Resource: speciﬁes the Display Resource ﬁle. When a display resource ﬁle is speciﬁed, it will be merged with the display.drf in Aether run directory.

||Note: GDS Layer Map and Display Resource will be grayed out unless Reference To Libraries or Load From File is selected.|
|---|
|
|---|

Figure 2.2 Parameter Settings in New Library

- 2. In the Name ﬁeld, type the name of the library you want to create, such as, LibraryCase. Note: The new library name cannot be the same as another library.
- 3. Specify the destination directory in which you want to create the new library. You can also type a directory path in the In Directory ﬁeld.
- 4. Select an existent technology library from Attach To Library.


- 5. Press OK button, the LibraryCase library is created.

## 2.2 New Cell/View

Menu: File -> New Cell/View ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 9](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9.png)

This command is used to create a new cell with a view or a new view for the existing cell. The form is shown in Figure 2.4 .

![image 10](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10.png)

Figure 2.4 New Cell/View Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the library name where a cell or a view is created. If you have selected a library in DM before invoking the command, the name of the selected library will be ﬁlled out automatically, otherwise Aether will ﬁll it out with the name of the ﬁrst library in DM list.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the name of a cell to create. If you have selected a cell in DM before invoking the command, the name of the selected cell will be ﬁlled out automatically, otherwise Aether will leave it empty.

View Name: speciﬁes the view name which is created in a cell. Default value is the same as a View Type .

View Type: speciﬁes the type of a view. Aether supports the following view types, Default view type is Schematic.

- • Layout: layout view which can be edited in Aether .
- • Schematic: schematic view which can be edited in Aether .
- • Symbol: symbol view which can be edited in Aether .
- • Verilog: Verilog view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • SystemVerilog: SystemVerilog view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • VerilogA: Verilog-A view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • VerilogAMS: Verilog-AMS view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • Conﬁg: conﬁguration view for mixed-mode simulation setup.
- • PhysConﬁg: physical conﬁguration view for physical hierarchy.
- • Dspf: parasitics in Dspf format.
- • Cdl: CdlText view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • Hspice: HspiceText view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • Spectre: SpectreText view which can be edited in a text editor.
- • Spice: SpiceText view which can be edited in a text editor.


- • Floorplan: ﬂoorplan view which can be edited in Aether.
- • Platform: platform view which can be edited in Aether.


Add To Category: adds the cell to a speciﬁed category. If category does not exist, Aether will create it automatically.

Application: The application is used to determine open editor.

• Open With: speciﬁes the editor version to open view.

## 2.3 Refresh

Menu: File -> Refresh ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 24](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile24.png)

This command refreshes data in a memory. It is used primarily in situations when several people work with the same data simultaneously. This function can refresh data of a library list, design, CDF, technology and device “deﬁne”.

||Note: Only data in a memory is refreshed. If data is not opened in a memory, this command does not produce any eﬀect.|
|---|
|
|---|


The following options are available:

Update Library List: refresh a library list. If it is enabled, it acts the same way as File -> Refresh All Libraries.

Design: refresh designs modiﬁed by others. If designs in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Layout: refresh layout modiﬁed by others. If layouts in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Schematic: refresh schematic modiﬁed by others. If schematic in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Symbol: refresh symbol modiﬁed by others. If symbols in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Conﬁg: refresh conﬁg modiﬁed by others. If conﬁg in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Physconﬁg: refresh physconﬁg modiﬁed by others. If physconﬁg in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

CDF: refresh CDF modiﬁed by others. If a CDF data in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is visible.

Tech: refresh technology modiﬁed by others. If technology data in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is visible.

Device Deﬁne: refresh “device deﬁne” modiﬁed by others. If a “device deﬁne” data in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Constraint: refresh constraint modiﬁed by others. If constraints in memory are not modiﬁed by others, this option is not visible.

Example 2.8 This example demonstrates the refresh of a schematic design.

- 1. Launch two Aether , open ChargePump/cp_amp/schematic in diﬀerent Aether


. Because of the ﬁle lock, only one window can edit the design, the other window has read permission only. Add a wire in the design and save it in the editable window. Activate the command File -> Refresh in the other Aether , the Refresh form appears and indicates the designs which have been changed, as shown in Figure 2.18

![image 25](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile25.png)

Figure 2.18 Refresh Design

- 2. Mark the design in a form, click OK button, the modiﬁcation will be read from the disk and shown in a readonly window.


## 2.4 Refresh Libraries

Menu: File -> Refresh Libraries ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 26](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile26.png)

This command refreshes data in design manager and update all cells boundary in selected library.

||Note: Only refresh data on design mananger when data is diﬀerent with disk. If data is not opened in a memory, this command does not produce any eﬀect.|
|---|
|
|---|


The following options are available: Library: selected refresh libraries. Filter: set ﬁlter for selecting refresh libraries. Update Cell Boundary: update all cells in selected libraries.

Oﬀ: It only refreshes the cells or views under selected libraries, such as the number change of cells or views. The default mode is Oﬀ.

On: It refreshes not only mentioned above, but the boundary of bottom cells.

## 2.6 Import

### 2.6.1 GDS

Menu: File ->Import ->GDS ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 37](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile37.png)

This command is used to import GDSII ﬁle to OpenAccess database. The GDSII ﬁle is de facto standards in layout design. You may set the following options.

![image 38](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile38.png)

Figure 2.28 Import GDS Form

GDS File Name: speciﬁes the GDS ﬁle to translate. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a GDS ﬁle by button.

![image 39](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile39.png)

Library Name: speciﬁes the destination library for the GDS ﬁle contents. If the library doesn’t exist, Aether will create it automatically.

Top Cell Name: speciﬁes the top-level cell to translate. If you want to import part of a design, specifying a topCell is one way to accomplish this. By default, Aether translates all cells in the GDS ﬁle.

Target Library Path: speciﬁes the path name (including the library name) for the library. Use this argument only if the library does not exist. If not

speciﬁed, the library is in ./<library> where <library> is the value of Library Name. Technology Mode: The following options are for technology used during import.

- • Load From Aether Tech File: loads an Aether technology ﬁle which is in ASCII text format. If you set nothing, Aether will use default technology ﬁle if user allows.
- • Attach To Tech Library: speciﬁes the technology library to use during the translation. If the library does not exist, Aether creates it. The default value for this argument is the destination library speciﬁed with the Library Name.
- • Reference To Tech Libraries: creates an incremental technology database that derives from one or more of the speciﬁed parent technology databases.
- • Load From Other Tech File: loads an other technology ﬁle which is in ASCII text format.
- • Do Not Need Technology: no technology is needed during import. It is default value. And if no technology in library, Aether will generate the technology according to GDS ﬁle’s content automatically.


Display Resource File: displays resource ﬁle that match with technology ﬁle. This option is enabled only when user chooses Load From Aether Tech File or Load From Other Tech File. It is in ASCII text format too.

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle that records the options for importing GDS. Users can choose ﬁle by button, save options to ﬁle by button, and load options from ﬁle by Load button.

![image 40](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile40.png)

![image 41](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile41.png)

![image 42](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile42.png)

Figure 2.29 General Tab

Layer Map File: speciﬁes a layer mapping ﬁle to be used during translation. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full or relative path. You can choose a Layer Map File by button.

![image 43](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile43.png)

The format for the map ﬁle is: <oaLayerName> <oaLayerPurpose> <gdsLayer> <gdsPurpose> If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, Aether creates stream objects on the layer and purpose numbers found in the technology library using the gdsLayer and gdsPurpose names speciﬁed in the map ﬁle. Stream objects on layer and type combinations not found in the map ﬁle are not translated. If gdsIn cannot ﬁnd the layer or purpose in the technology library, a warning message is issued, but Aether attempts to create it.

By default, if you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, stream layers and types translate to the names L<gdsLayer> and P<gdsPurpose> respectively. If the layer name or purpose name is not in the technology library, Aether attempts to add it.

Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

##### Note:

- • You cannot specify the same gdsLayer/gdsPurpose type combination for multiple entries. If you do, an error is issued and the entry is ignored. When you are merging layers, if gdsLayer and gdsPurpose combinations match the same layer and purpose combinations in the database, a warning is issued.
- • If layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is not empty, Aether will use speciﬁed layer mapping ﬁle directly. if layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is empty, Aether will not use any layer mapping ﬁle. if layer mapping ﬁle is unchecked, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(gds.map) under the library speciﬁed by Attach To Tech Library. If Attach To Tech Library is not speciﬁed, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(gds.map) under the library speciﬁed by Library Name.


- Table 2.1 Layer Mapping File of Import GDS

|# oaLayerName<br><br>|oaLayerPurpose<br><br>|gdsLayer|gdsPurpose|
|---|---|---|---|
|PImp|drawing<br><br>|13<br><br>|13|
|Metal1|drawing1|1<br><br>|1|
|Via1|drawing2<br><br>|2<br><br>|2|
|Metal2<br><br>|drawing3<br><br>|3<br><br>|3|
|Via2|drawing4<br><br>|4|4|
|Metal3|drawing5<br><br>|5<br><br>|5|
|Via3|drawing6<br><br>|6|6|
|Metal4|drawing7<br><br>|7|7|
|Via4<br><br>|drawing8|8|8|
|Metal5|drawing9|9|9|
|Via5<br><br>|drawing10<br><br>|10|10|


Cell Map File: speciﬁes the cell mapping ﬁle to use during import. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Cell Map File by button. If you use the asterisk (*) character in the cellmap ﬁle in place of the library name, the translator searches all the reference libraries for the mapped cellname.

![image 44](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile44.png)

The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<destination library name> <destination cell name> <destination view name> <stream structure name>

If you specify a cell mapping ﬁle, Aether creates stream structures and instances of that structure found in the map ﬁle as the destination library, cell, and view name speciﬁed. No case conversion is processed on these names. Aether translates stream structures and instances not found in the mapping ﬁle using the structure names in the GDS ﬁle.

Lines in the cellMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

- Table 2.2 Cell Mapping File of Import GDS


|# library name<br><br>|cell name|view name|stream name|
|---|---|---|---|
|desLib|nand2<br><br>|layout|nand2_1|
|sdesLib<br><br>|nand2|layout|nand2_2|
|desLib<br><br>|cellNu|layout<br><br>|cellNu|
|*|cellNu|layout<br><br>|cellNew|


Each stream name in the cell mapping ﬁle must be unique.

Reference Libraries: speciﬁes one or more libraries in which to search for master cells. You specify multiple libraries with a quoted, space-separated list.

Max Number Of Cell: speciﬁes the number of cells. If the number of cells exceeds the value of Max Number Of Cell, those cells within speciﬁed range will be imported in the original library, and the rest of cells will be put into the new libraries. The maximum value is 100000, and the minimum value is 20000, the default is 100000.

Translate Existing Cells: speciﬁes the mode for translated data.

- • Append: speciﬁes whether the translated data will be appended to an existing or a new design. For example:

- – If a design corresponding to a given GDS structure is found, the data in the stream ﬁle will be appended to that design. There is no check for duplicate data.
- – If a design corresponding to a given GDS structure is not found, a


new design is created with the translated data.

- • Overwrite: replaces an existing design with the translated data.
- • Ignore: skips an existing design. Any cell in the stream ﬁle that corresponds to a pre-existing oaDesign is silently skipped.


Cell Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for cell name.

- • Preserve: preserves cell name.
- • Upper: converts cell names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts cell names to lower case.


Label Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for label name.

- • Preserves: preserve label name.
- • Upper: converts label names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts label names to lower case.


Pin Attribute Number: speciﬁes the pin attribute number. If the number is 0, nothing converts. The valid value is 1~127. Default value is 0.

Translate Entire Hierarchy: speciﬁes translating entire hierarchy. Translation Depth: speciﬁes the hierarchical depth to translate to. The default depth is 32.

![image 45](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile45.png)

Figure 2.30 Advanced Tab

Skip Empty Cells: speciﬁes whether to skip empty cells. Translate Existing Cells: speciﬁes the mode for translated data.

- • Append: speciﬁes whether the translated data will be appended to an existing or a new design. For example:

- – If a design corresponding to a given GDS structure is found, the data in the stream ﬁle will be appended to that design. There is no checking for duplicate data.
- – If a design corresponding to a given GDS structure is not found, a new design is created with the translated data.


- • Overwrite: replaces an existing design with the translated data.
- • Ignore: skips an existing design. Any cell in the stream ﬁle that corresponds to a pre-existing oaDesign is silently skipped.
- • Rename: rename the cell from newly imported GDS if it has the same name as an existing cell.


Cell Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes preﬁx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the preﬁx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Cell Name Suﬃx: speciﬁes suﬃx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the suﬃx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Ignore Cell Name Preﬁx&Suﬃx For Top Cell: speciﬁes whether to ignore preﬁx and suﬃx for top name. If Yes is selected, ignore the preﬁx and suﬃx for top cell. The default value is No.

Detect Via: detects the standard via and creates them in the database. Note that we need all standard via defs are deﬁned in technology. Layer map ﬁles are welcomed.

##### Via Exclusion Map File: vias exclude data ﬁle.

![image 46](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile46.png)

- Figure 2.31 Geometry Tab

Ignore Zero Path Width: speciﬁes how to deal with paths with zero width. Report Self Intersecting Shape: speciﬁes whether to give warning message when meeting self-intersecting shapes.

Convert [ ] To < > : speciﬁes whether converting [ ] to < > . Default value is No, nothing converts. Only choosing Yes, converting will be worked

Size Ratio: speciﬁes size ratio to scale shapes and instances. Default value is 1.0.

![image 47](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile47.png)

- Figure 2.32 Misc Tab


Do Not Output Message: Speciﬁes whether to output message.The default value is unchecked.

![image 48](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile48.png)

- Figure 2.33 File Tab


Via Map File: speciﬁes a via mapping ﬁle that deﬁnes which structures to recognize as customViaDef masters. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Cell Map File by button.

![image 49](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile49.png)

Split Layer Name: speciﬁes whether to print layer information in split column in the log ﬁle. The default value is unchecked. The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<Structure Name> <oaCustomViaDef Name> <Layer1 Name/Number> <Layer2 Name/Number>

Lines in the ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

Example Via Mapping File:

- Table 2.3 Via Mapping File of Import GDS


|# custom via|master<br><br>|layer1 name/number|layer2 name/number|
|---|---|---|---|
|via1|m1m2via<br><br>|m1 10<br><br>|m2 20|
|via2|m2m3via<br><br>|m2 20<br><br>|m3 30|


Property Map File: speciﬁes the property mapping ﬁle to use during import. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Cell Map File by button.

![image 50](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile50.png)

The format for the map ﬁle is: <stream id> <object type> <destination property name>

If you specify a property mapping ﬁle, Aether creates stream properties with id and object type combinations found in the map ﬁle using the property name speciﬁed. Aether creates stream properties on id and object type combinations not found in the mapping ﬁle with the name STREAM PROPERTY #<strmid>.

Valid objects types are: Dot, Line, Path, Polygon, Rect, Text, ArrayInst, and ScalarInst.

If you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, Aether interprets stream properties values as a list of properties separated by the property separator character with the form:

##### <property name> = <property value>

For example, height=10, width=20 yields two properties, the ﬁrst named height with a value of 10, and the second named width with a value of 20.

Lines in the property map ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

- Table 2.4 Property Mapping File of Import GDS


|# stream Id|object<br><br>|name|
|---|---|---|
|1|Rect<br><br>|instP11|
|2|Polygon<br><br>|poly1|
|3<br><br>|Path|sigName|
|4<br><br>|Text<br><br>|pad32|
|5|Pin<br><br>|io_term|


Object Map File: speciﬁes the object map ﬁle name. Ignore Object Properties: speciﬁes whether to input object properties in the object map ﬁle. The default value is unchecked. Log File: speciﬁes the log ﬁle name. If this option is omitted, the log ﬁle name defaults to gdsIn.log. Split Layer Name: speciﬁes whether to print layer information in split column in the log ﬁle. The default value is unchecked.

### 2.6.2 LEF

Menu: File -> Import -> LEF ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 52](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile52.png)

This command is used to import LEF ﬁle to OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

![image 53](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile53.png)

Figure 2.35 Import LEF Form

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle that records the options of Import LEF. Users can choose ﬁle by Browser button, save options to ﬁle by Save button, and load options from ﬁle by Load button.

LEF File Name: speciﬁes the LEF ﬁle to translate. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a LEF ﬁle by Browser button.

Library Name: speciﬁes the destination library for the LEF ﬁle contents. If the library doesn’t exist, Aether will create it automatically.

Target Library Path: speciﬁes the path name (including the library name) for the library. Use this argument only if the library does not exist. If not speciﬁed, the library is in ./<library> where <library> is the value of Library Name.

Attach To Tech Library: speciﬁes the technology library to use during the translation. If the library does not exist, Aether creates it. The default value for this argument is the destination library speciﬁed with the Library Name.

Reference To Tech Libraries: creates an incremental technology database that derives from one or more of the speciﬁed parent technology databases.

Do Not Need Technology: no technology is needed during import. it is default value. And if no technology in library, Aether will generate the technology according to LEF ﬁle’s content automatically.

Layer Map File Names: speciﬁes a quoted, space-separated list of one or more layer mapping ﬁles to be used during translation. You must specify the complete path for each layer map ﬁle. The format for the map ﬁle is:

<layerName> <layerNumber>

If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, maps LEF objects found on the speciﬁed layerName to the speciﬁed layerNumber. If a layer number does not exist in the technology library, the translator attempts to create it.

If you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, LEF layer names map to layer numbers in a sequential manner, starting at 0.

Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character (#) are ignored.

![image 54](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile54.png)

Figure 2.36 Layer Map File Format

Overwrite Design: replaces MACROS in an existing design with the translated data. If this option is omitted, the default behavior is to update the existing library. This option does not aﬀect the DBU value in an existing technology database.

View Name: speciﬁes the output view name. The default view name is abstract.

Create Pin Label: creates pin labels in designs. Labels are added on the term for each pin ﬁgure of the terminal at the location of the pin ﬁgure.

Comment Char: identiﬁes the comment character.

Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer used for pin label text. If pin labels are used, and this option is not speciﬁed, the pin label text layer defaults to text. If the speciﬁed layer does not exist in the technology database, it is added.

Label Height: speciﬁes an integer value for the pin label text height in database units (DBU). If pin labels are used, and this option is omitted, the pin label text height defaults to the DBU value in the technology database for maskLayout views.

Pin Purpose: speciﬁes the purpose for pin to translate, default is drawing for pin’s purpose.

Import Colored Shapes As Locked: speciﬁes to translate the shapes with mask in LEF ﬁle to the shapes with locked color in OpenAccess database.

### 2.6.3 DEF

Menu: File -> Import -> DEF ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 55](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile55.png)

This command is used to import DEF ﬁle to OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

![image 56](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile56.png)

Figure 2.37 Import DEF Form

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle that record the options of Import DEF. Users can choose ﬁle by Browser button, save options to ﬁle by Save button, and load options from ﬁle by Load button.

DEF File Name: speciﬁes the DEF ﬁle to translate. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a DEF ﬁle by Browser button.

Library Name: speciﬁes the destination library for the DEF ﬁle contents. If the library doesn’t exist, Aether will create it automatically.

Target Library Path: speciﬁes the path name (including the library name) for the library. Use this argument only if the library does not exist. If not speciﬁed, the library is in ./<library> where <library> is the value of Library Name.

Attach To Tech Library: speciﬁes the technology library to use during the translation. If the library does not exist, Aether creates it. The default value for this argument is the destination library speciﬁed with the Library Name.

Reference To Tech Libraries: creates an incremental technology database that derives from one or more of the speciﬁed parent technology databases.

Do Not Need Technology: no technology is needed during import. it is default value. And if no technology in library, Aether will generate the technology according to DEF ﬁle’s content automatically.

Layer Map File Names: speciﬁes the layer mapping ﬁle to use during translation. You must specify the complete path to the ﬁle. The format for each line of the map ﬁle is:

<layerName> <layerNumber>

If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, import def maps DEF objects found on the speciﬁed layerName to the speciﬁed layerNumber. The layerMap ﬁle is referenced during translation before looking up the layer names in the technology library. This permits mapping a layer name to a diﬀerent layer name in the technology library. If a layer number does not exist in the technology library, an error is generated.

Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character (#) are ignored.

![image 57](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile57.png)

Figure 2.38 Layer Map File Format

Reference Libraries: speciﬁes one or more libraries in which to search for master cells. You specify multiple libraries with a quoted, space-separated list.

Reference View(s): speciﬁes one or more view names to search for master cells. You specify multiple views with a quoted, space-separated list. By default, the refViews list contains abstract. If you use this option, only the views you speciﬁed are searched.

Overwrite Design: replaces an existing design with the translated data. If this option is omitted, the default behavior is to update the existing library.

View Name: speciﬁes the name of the output view, which defaults to layout if this option is omitted.

Use Custom Vias: speciﬁes that the translator creates and uses custom via instead of existing standard via for all vias in the DEF ﬁle.

Create Routing Data: ignores any routing data during translation including the vias section.

Create Module Hierarchy: speciﬁes that the translator creates a module hierarchy based on hierarchical names of instances and nets in the DEF ﬁle. Instead, the translator escapes hierarchy delimiters in the names of instances and nets in the OpenAccess database. The default is to create a module hierarchy based on hierarchical names of instances and nets.

Set Via All Non Default: speciﬁes all the ﬂags to indicate that the parameter values are to be considered as non default values.

Comment Char: identiﬁes the comment character.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the name of the output cell, which defaults to the name speciﬁed in the DEF ﬁle using the DESIGN construct if this option is omitted.

Pin Purpose: speciﬁes the purpose for pin to translate, default is drawing for pin’s purpose.

Import Colored Shapes As Locked: speciﬁes to translate the shapes with mask in DEF ﬁle to the shapes with locked color in OpenAccess database.

Example 2.13

The example shows how to import an cdl ﬁle in Aether and generate schematic, follow these steps:

### 2.6.5 EDIF 200

Menu: File -> Import -> EDIF 200 ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 72](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile72.png)

This command is used to import EDIF 200 ﬁle to OpenAccess database. The EDIF 200 ﬁle is de facto standards in schematic design. You may set the following options.

![image 73](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile73.png)

Figure 2.45 Import EDIF 200 Form

EDIF File Name: speciﬁes the EDIF ﬁle to translate. You can specify the ﬁle name with an absolute or relative path for importing. You can choose an EDIF ﬁle by Browser button.

Target Library Path: speciﬁes the path name for the library which is used for edif ﬁle generation. If it is not speciﬁed, the default value is ’.’.

Skip Libraries: do not translate libraries which are deﬁned here during importing edif. These libraries’ contents will be skipped.

Sheet Libraries: speciﬁes the sheet libraries when importing edif. Overwrite Existing Library: replaces an existing library with the translated data.

Overwrite Existing Cell: replaces an existing cell with the translated data. Overwrite Existing View: replaces an existing view with the translated data.

##### Case Sensitivity:

- • Preserve: preserves library/cell/view/pin/wire name.
- • Upper: converts library/cell/view/pin/wire name to upper case.
- • Lower: converts library/cell/view/pin/wire name to lower case.


##### Distance Unit:

- • 160 unit =inch(25.4mm): speciﬁes 160 unit as grid spacing in the schematic
- • From Technology: speciﬁes grid spacing according to the technology deﬁnition.


##### Net Name:

- • Default: adds and displays wire name to nets by default.
- • Keep Net Name With EDIF: adds and displays wire name to nets according to edif ﬁle’s setting.
- • Add Net Label To All Segments: adds and displays wire name to all net segments.


Font Resize: resizes font when translating edif ﬁle to schematic. Inspect: checks the validity of the edif ﬁle.

### 2.6.6 Import Verilog

Menu: File -> Import -> Verilog ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 76](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile76.png)

This command is used to translate verilog(a) ﬁle to OpenAccess database. After importing, it will generate verilog(a) view in Design Manager. You may set the following options.

![image 77](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile77.png)

Figure 2.48 Import Verilog Form

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle which record the options of Import Verilog. Users can choose ﬁle by Browser button, save options to ﬁle by Save button, and load options from ﬁle by Load button.

Verilog(A) File Name: specify the Verilog(A) ﬁle to translate. You can choose a Verilog(A) ﬁle by + button or delete a VerilogA ﬁle by -.

- • : selects verilog(a) ﬁle which is to be imported.

![image 78](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile78.png)

- • : deletes verilog(a) ﬁle which has been added.


![image 79](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile79.png)

Library Name: specify library name. Target Library Path: specify the path name for the library which is used for dspf or spice ﬁle generation. If it is not speciﬁed, the default value is ’.’.

• : selects library path.

![image 80](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile80.png)

Top Cell Name: specify the top cell in verilog(a) ﬁle. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.

Reference Libraries: specify the reference libraries, when importing verilog, if some cell have same name with cells in reference libraries deﬁned here, it will not generate these cells’ verilog view, but will using verilog views in reference libraries.

• : select reference libraries.

![image 81](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile81.png)

Reference View(s): specify the reference view list. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.

##### Options:

- • Overwrite Design: decides whether to replace existing design. This option is enabled only when View Type is Verilog, VerilogA, Verilog&Netlist
- • Separate Design: decides whether to separate design after importing. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • Create Black Box: decides whether to create black box after importing. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • Tolerate Errors: decides whether to tolerate errors when importing verilog. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • Validate Instance Terms: decides whether to validate instance terms. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • Global Module: specify global module name. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • High Net: specify high net name. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • Low Net: specify low net name. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.
- • View Type: specify views which are generated after importing.

- – Verilog: generates verilog view. Select this type, the default name of View Name is verilog.
- – VerilogA: generates veriloga view. Select this type, the default name of View Name is veriloga.
- – Netlist: generates netlist view. Select this type, the default name of View Name is netlist.
- – Layout: generates layout view. Select this type, the default name of View Name is abstract.
- – Verilog&Netlist: generates verilog and netlist view. Select this type, the default name of View Name is netlist and Verilog View Name is enabled. Default view type is Verilog.


- • View Name: specify view name which is generated after importing.
- • Verilog View Name: specify view name of verilog view. This option is enabled only when View Type is Verilog&Netlist.


- • VerilogA Include Path: specify veriloga include path. This option is enabled only when View Type is Netlist or Layout.

### 2.6.7 Netlist

Menu: File -> Import -> Netlist ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 85](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile85.png)

This command is used to translate cdl or verilog(a) ﬁle to OpenAccess database. After importing, it will generate schematic view in Design Manager. You may set the following options.

![image 86](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile86.png)

Figure 2.51 Import Netlist Form

Netlist Type: speciﬁes the type of netlist, only CDL and Verilog are available now. The default type is CDL.

CDL File Name: speciﬁes the CDL ﬁle name. Only available when Netlist Type is CDL.

Verilog File Name: speciﬁes the verilog ﬁle name. Only available when Netlist Type is Verilog.

Verilog Library File Name: speciﬁes the extra verilog ﬁles name. Only available when Netlist Type is Verilog.

Target Library Name: speciﬁes the generated design library name. Target Library Path: speciﬁes the generated path. If not speciﬁed, the current directory is considered by default. Top Cell Name: speciﬁes the top cell name. Reference Library List: speciﬁes the reference library names.

Device Map File Name: speciﬁes a map ﬁle to be used during translation. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full or relative path. You can choose a Map File by Browser button and edit the Map File by Edit button.

##### Options:

- • Overwrite Existing Library: decides whether to replace existing Library. The default value is unchecked.
- • Overwrite Existing Cell: decides whether to replace existing Cell. The default value is unchecked.
- • Overwrite Existing View: decides whether to replace existing View. The default value is checked.
- • Auto Check: decides whether to do check after the generation is complete. The default value is unchecked.
- • Simple Route: decides whether to use simple route mode. In this mode there will be no routing, instead short lines will be created, and the placement layout will be simpler too. The default value is unchecked.
- • Optimize Schematic Generation: decides whether to use Optimize Schematic Options after netlist main placement.
- • Simple Placement X Spacing: speciﬁes the spacing between instances of X coordinate, only available in Simple Route mode.
- • Simple Placement Y Spacing: speciﬁes the spacing between instances of Y coordinate, only available in Simple Route mode.
- • Create Top Cell Symbol: speciﬁes whether to create top cell symbol, valid only if Top Cell Name is speciﬁed. The default state is No.
- • Enable Sub-Circuit Recognition: speciﬁes whether need sub-circuit identiﬁcation. The default state is No.
- • Schematic Style: speciﬁes the generation style, default state is auto. The transistor mode is recommended when import CDL netlist, while gate mode for CDL and Verilog.


##### Optimize Schematic Options:

- • Power Nets: speciﬁes the power net names to ﬁnd power instances for placement, the placement will place power inst up to its connect inst.
- • Ground Nets: speciﬁes the ground net names to ﬁnd ground instances for placement, the placement will place ground inst down to its connect inst.
- • Schematic Analysis Templates: speciﬁes the templates to analyze, then extract the data deﬁned in the template and generate schematics and symbols to replace schematic instances.


- • Place Schematic As In Layout: decides whether to use coordinates in the ﬁle within CDL File Name deﬁned. The default value is unchecked.


##### Connection Options:

- • Power Net Connection: speciﬁes the power net for connecting those terminals with same name to the power net.
- • Ground Net Connection: speciﬁes the ground net for connecting those terminals with same name to the ground net.

### 2.6.8 DXF

Menu: File -> Import -> DXF ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 93](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile93.png)

This command is used to import DXF ﬁle to OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

![image 94](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile94.png)

Figure 2.56 Import DXF Form

DXF File Name: sets the DXF ﬁle name with an absolute or relative path for importing. Choose a DXF ﬁle by Browser button.

Library Name: sets the library name for imported DXF. If the library doesn’t exist, it will be created.

Top Cell Name: sets the top cell name for imported DXF. If cell name is empty, the base name of DXF ﬁle is used as default name. For example, if the top cell name is empty and the ﬁle is “importDxf.dxf ” , the default top cell name is “importDxf ” .

Technology: sets the technology information for selected library.

- • Attach To Tech Library: attaches the library to some existing technology library.
- • Load From Tech File: loads the technology ﬁle directly for the selected library.
- • Do Not Need Technology: the library does not need technology. This is default option.


Unit: speciﬁes the relation of unit in DXF and in OA.

- • Apply DXF Drawing Unit: uses the unit in DXF. The translated data in OA will have the same signiﬁcance with the data in DXF. For example, the unit in DXF is mm, the unit in OA is um, the data is 1mm in DXF. After translating, the value in OA is 1000, the data is 1mm. Default is checked.

Table 2.5 Example for Apply DXF Drawing Unit

|DXF Data|OA Unit<br><br>|OA Value<br><br>|OA Data|
|---|---|---|---|
|1mm<br><br>|mm|1|1mm|
|1mm<br><br>|um|1000<br><br>|1mm|
|1mm|nm<br><br>|1000000|1mm|
|1mm|m<br><br>|0.001|1mm|


- • 1 DXF Unit = XXX User Unit: only sets the data in value, no signiﬁcance. For example, the unit in DXF is mm, the unit in OA is um. When 1 DXF Unit = 1 User Unit, the data is 1mm in DXF, then after translating, the value in OA is 1, the data is 1um. The Table 2.6 is illustrated when unit in OA is um.


- Table 2.6 Example for 1 DXF Unit = XXX User Unit


|DXF Data<br><br>|Scale|OA Value<br><br>|OA Data|
|---|---|---|---|
|1mm|1<br><br>|1<br><br>|1um|
|1mm<br><br>|10|10<br><br>|0.01mm or 10um|
|1mm|1000|1000<br><br>|1000um or 1mm|
|1mm<br><br>|0.001<br><br>|0.001|1nm or 0.001um|


Connect 0 Width Path: connects the same layer head-tail 0 width paths. Default is checked.

Convert Closed 0 Width Path to Rectangle/Polygon: converts closed 0 width path to polygon or rectangle. Default is checked.

Convert Arc to 0 Width Path: converts arcs to 0 width path. Default is checked.

Arc Segments: speciﬁes segments of polygon. Default is 32. Note: The shape type may be changed in translation from DXF to OpenAccess database, shape type contrast is as follows:

- Table 2.7 Shape Type Contrast in DXF and OA


|DXF Shape Type<br><br>|OA Shape Type|
|---|---|
|LWPOLYLINE(closed)|Polygon|
|LWPOLYLINE(unclosed)<br><br>|Path|
|LINE<br><br>|Path|
|SPLINE|Path|
|TEXT|Text|
|MTEXT|Text|
|CIRCLE|Circle|
|ELLIPSE<br><br>|Ellipse or Polygon|
|ARC<br><br>|Arc or Path|
|DIMENSION<br><br>|The General Shapes|
|SOLID|Polygon or Path|
|HATCH<br><br>|Polygon or Path|
|BLOCK|Cell|
|INSERT|Instance or Array Instance|

![image 95](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile95.png)

Figure 2.57 Parameter Settings in the Import DXF

### 2.6.10 OASIS

Menu: File ->Import ->OASIS ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 107](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile107.png)

This command is used to import OASIS(Open Artwork System Interchange) ﬁle to OpenAccess database. The OASIS ﬁle is deﬁned as an interchange and encapsulation format for hierarchical integrated circuit mask layout information. You may set the following options.

![image 108](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile108.png)

Figure 2.64 Import OASIS Form

OASIS File Name: speciﬁes the OASIS ﬁle to translate. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a OASIS ﬁle by button.

![image 109](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile109.png)

Library Name: speciﬁes the destination library for the OASIS ﬁle contents. If the library doesn’t exist, Aether will create it automatically.

Top Cell Name: speciﬁes the top-level cell to translate. If you want to import part of a design, specifying a topCell is one way to accomplish this. By default, Aether translates all cells in the OASIS ﬁle.

Target Library Path: speciﬁes the path name (including the library name) for the library. Use this argument only if the library does not exist. If not speciﬁed, the library is in ./<library> where <library> is the value of Library Name.

Technology Mode: The following options are for technology used during import.

- • Load From Aether Tech File: loads an Aether technology ﬁle which is in ASCII text format. If you set nothing, Aether will use default technology ﬁle if user allows.
- • Attach To Tech Library: speciﬁes the technology library to use during the translation. If the library does not exist, Aether creates it. The default value for this argument is the destination library speciﬁed with the Library Name.
- • Reference To Tech Libraries: creates an incremental technology database that derives from one or more of the speciﬁed parent technology databases.
- • Load From Other Tech File: loads an other technology ﬁle which is in ASCII text format.
- • Do Not Need Technology: no technology is needed during import. It is default value. And if no technology in library, Aether will generate the technology according to OASIS ﬁle’s content automatically.


Display Resource File: displays resource ﬁle which matches with technology ﬁle. This option is enabled only when user chooses Load From Aether Tech File or Load From Other Tech File. It is in ASCII text format too.

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle that records the options of Import OASIS. Users can choose ﬁle by button, save options to ﬁle by button, and load options from ﬁle by button.

![image 110](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile110.png)

![image 111](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile111.png)

![image 112](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile112.png)

![image 113](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile113.png)

Figure 2.65 General Tab

Layer Map File: speciﬁes a layer mapping ﬁle to be used during translation. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full or relative path. You can choose a Layer Map File by button.

![image 114](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile114.png)

The format for the map ﬁle is: <oaLayerName> <oaLayerPurpose> <oasisLayer> <oasisPurpose>

If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, Aether creates oasis objects on the layer and purpose numbers found in the technology library using the oasisLayer and

oasisPurpose names speciﬁed in the map ﬁle. Oasis objects on layer and type combinations not found in the map ﬁle are not translated.

If aoIn cannot ﬁnd the layer or purpose in the technology library, a warning message is issued, but Aether attempts to create it.

By default, if you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, oasis layers and types translate to the names L<oasisLayer> and P<oasisPurpose> respectively. If the layer name or purpose name is not in the technology library, Aether attempts to add it.

Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

##### Note:

- • You cannot specify the same oasisLayer/oasisPurpose type combination for multiple entries. If you do, an error is issued and the entry is ignored. When you are merging layers, if oasisLayer and oasisPurpose combinations match the same layer and purpose combinations in the database, a warning is issued.
- • If layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is not empty, Aether will use speciﬁed layer mapping ﬁle directly. If layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is empty, Aether will not use any layer mapping ﬁle. If layer mapping ﬁle is unchecked, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(oasis.map) under the library speciﬁed by Attach To Tech Library. If Attach To Tech Library is not speciﬁed, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(oasis.map) under the library speciﬁed by Library Name.


- Table 2.8 Layer Mapping File of Import OASIS


|# oaLayerName<br><br>|oaLayerPurpose|oasisLayer|oasisPurpose|
|---|---|---|---|
|PImp<br><br>|drawing|13|13|
|Metal1<br><br>|drawing1|1<br><br>|1|
|Via1|drawing2<br><br>|2|2|
|Metal2<br><br>|drawing3|3<br><br>|3|
|Via2<br><br>|drawing4|4<br><br>|4|
|Metal3|drawing5|5<br><br>|5|
|Via3|drawing6|6<br><br>|6|
|Metal4|drawing7<br><br>|7<br><br>|7|
|Via4<br><br>|drawing8|8<br><br>|8|
|Metal5|drawing9<br><br>|9<br><br>|9|
|Via5|drawing10|10|10|


Input Unmappend Lpp: speciﬁes whether to input layers in the layer map ﬁle. The default value is unchecked.

Cell Map File: speciﬁes the cell mapping ﬁle to use during import. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Cell Map File by button. If you use the asterisk (*) character in the cellmap ﬁle in place of the library name, the translator searches all the reference libraries for the mapped cellname.

![image 115](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile115.png)

The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<destination library name> <destination cell name> <destination view name> <oasis structure name>

If you specify a cell mapping ﬁle, Aether creates oasis structures and instances of that structure found in the map ﬁle as the destination library, cell, and view name speciﬁed. No case conversion is processed on these names. Aether translates oasis structures and instances not found in the mapping ﬁle using the structure names in the OASIS ﬁle.

Lines in the cellMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

- Table 2.9 Cell Mapping File of Import OASIS


|# library name|cell name<br><br>|view name|oasis name|
|---|---|---|---|
|desLib|nand2<br><br>|layout|nand2_1|
|sdesLib<br><br>|nand2<br><br>|layout|nand2_2|
|desLib<br><br>|cellNu<br><br>|layout|cellNu|
|*<br><br>|cellNu<br><br>|layout|cellNew|


Each oasis name in the cell mapping ﬁle must be unique.

Reference Libraries: speciﬁes one or more libraries in which to search for master cells. You specify multiple libraries with a quoted, space-separated list.

Cell Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for cell name.

- • Preserve: preserves cell name.
- • Upper: converts cell names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts cell names to lower case.


Label Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for label name.

- • Preserve: preserves label name.
- • Upper: converts label names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts label names to lower case.


Pin Attribute Number: speciﬁes the pin attribute number. If the number is 0, nothing converts. The valid value is 1~127. Default value is 0.

Translate Entire Hierarchy: speciﬁes translating entire hierarchy.

Translation Depth: speciﬁes the hierarchical depth to translate to. The default depth is 32.

![image 116](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile116.png)

Figure 2.66 Advanced Tab

Skip Empty Cells: speciﬁes whether to skip empty cells. Translate Existing Cells: speciﬁes the mode for translated data.

- • Append: speciﬁes whether the translated data will be appended to an existing or a new design. For example:

- – If a design corresponding to a given OASIS structure is found, the data in the oasis ﬁle will be appended to that design. There is no check for duplicate data.
- – If a design corresponding to a given OASIS structure is not found, a


new design is created with the translated data.

- • Overwrite: replaces an existing design with the translated data.
- • Ignore: skips an existing design. Any cell in the oasis ﬁle that corresponds to a pre-existing oaDesign is silently skipped.
- • Rename: renames the cell from newly import OASIS if it has the same name as an existing cell.


Cell Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes preﬁx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the preﬁx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Cell Name Suﬃx: speciﬁes suﬃx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the suﬃx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Ignore Cell Name Preﬁx&Suﬃx For Top Cell: speciﬁes whether to ignore preﬁx and suﬃx for top name. If Yes is selected, ignore the preﬁx and suﬃx for top cell. The default value is No.

Detect Via: detects the standard via and creates them in the database. Note that we need all standard via defs are deﬁned in technology. Layer map ﬁles are welcomed.

##### Via Exclusion Map File: vias exclude data ﬁle.

![image 117](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile117.png)

- Figure 2.67 Geometry Tab

Ignore Zero Path Width: speciﬁes how to deal with paths with zero width. Report Self Intersecting Shape: speciﬁes whether to give warning message when meeting self-intersecting shapes.

Convert [ ] To < > : speciﬁes whether converting [ ] to < > . Default value is No, nothing converts. Only choosing Yes, converting will be worked

Size Ratio: speciﬁes size ratio to scale shapes and instances. Default value is 1.0.

Text Height: speciﬁes text height. Default value is 1.0.

![image 118](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile118.png)

- Figure 2.68 Misc Tab


Do Not Output Message: Speciﬁes whether to output message.The default value is unchecked.

![image 119](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile119.png)

- Figure 2.69 File Tab


Via Map File: speciﬁes a via mapping ﬁle that deﬁnes which structures to recognize as customViaDef masters. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Via Map File by button.

![image 120](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile120.png)

The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<Structure Name> <oaCustomViaDef Name> <Layer1 Name/Number> <Layer2 Name/Number>

Lines in the ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

Example Via Mapping File:

- Table 2.10 Via Mapping File of Import OASIS


|# custom via<br><br>|master<br><br>|layer1 name/number|layer2 name/number|
|---|---|---|---|
|via1<br><br>|m1m2via|m1 10|m2 20|
|via2|m2m3via|m2 20<br><br>|m3 30|


Property Map File: speciﬁes the property mapping ﬁle to use during import. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Cell Map File by button.

![image 121](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile121.png)

The format for the map ﬁle is: <oasis id> <object type> <destination property name>

If you specify a property mapping ﬁle, Aether creates oasis properties with id and object type combinations found in the map ﬁle using the property name speciﬁed. Aether creates oasis properties on id and object type combinations not found in the mapping ﬁle with the name OASIS PROPERTY #<strmid>.

Valid objects types are: Dot, Line, Path, Polygon, Rect, Text, ArrayInst, and ScalarInst.

If you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, Aether interprets oasis properties values as a list of properties separated by the property separator character with the form:

##### <property name> = <property value>

For example, height=10, width=20 yields two properties, the ﬁrst named height with a value of 10, and the second named width with a value of 20.

Lines in the property map ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

- Table 2.11 Property Mapping File of Import OASIS


|# oasis Id|object|name|
|---|---|---|
|1|Rect<br><br>|instP11|
|2|Polygon|poly1|
|3|Path<br><br>|sigName|
|4<br><br>|Text|pad32|
|5|Pin<br><br>|io_term|


Object Map File: speciﬁes the object map ﬁle name. Ignore Object Properties: speciﬁes whether to input object properties in the object map ﬁle. The default value is unchecked. Log File: speciﬁes the log ﬁle name. If this option is omitted, the log ﬁle name defaults to oasisIn.log. Split Layer Name: speciﬁes whether to print layer information in split column in the log ﬁle. The default value is unchecked.

Example 2.20 The example shows how to import a OASIS ﬁle, follow these steps:

- 1. Activate the command File ->Import ->OASIS, the Import OASIS form appears.


![image 122](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile122.png)

Figure 2.70 Parameter settings in the Import OASIS

- 2. In the OASIS File Name ﬁeld, type the name of the ﬁle which you want to translate, such as, ~/work/aether/data/oasis/oasisin/test.oas.
- 3. In the Library Name ﬁeld, type the name of library which you want to be translated, such as, test.
- 4. Keep other options as default.
- 5. Press OK button, the ~/work/aether/data/oasis/oasisin/test.oas is translated to OpenAccess database.

## 2.7 Export

### 2.7.1 GDS

Menu: File ->Export ->GDS ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 123](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile123.png)

This command is used to export GDSII ﬁle from OpenAccess database. The GDSII ﬁle is de facto standard in layout design. You may set the following options.

![image 124](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile124.png)

Figure 2.71 Export GDS Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the library to translate. The library must exist in the library deﬁnitions ﬁle in the current working directory. If the Cell

Name and View Name options are not speciﬁed, all the cells in the library are translated. If a cell has more than one view of maskLayout viewType, the views are translated as cellName, cellName_0, cellName_1, and so forth where cellName is the name of cell being translated.

Cell Name: speciﬁes a set of cells to translate. The cell names must be separated by white space. If you want to export parts of a design, using this option to specify the required cells is one way to accomplish this. Aether translates the speciﬁed cells together with their sub-cells, recursively, down to the depth speciﬁed by the optional Translation Depth or Translate Entire Hierarchy. Aether ensures that no cell is translated multiple times. If the View Name option is not speciﬁed, the default view name layout is used. If this option is not used, Aether export all cells in the library that is speciﬁed with Library Name.

View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the cells to translate. If you don’t set Cell Name, this option will be not eﬀective for export.

GDS File Name: speciﬁes the output GDS ﬁle. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for export. You can choose a GDS ﬁle by

button.

![image 125](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile125.png)

Technology Library Name: speciﬁes the technology library to use during the translation. If you specify a library name, the library must exist. The default value is the library speciﬁed with the Library Name.

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle that record the options of Export GDS. Users can choose ﬁle by button, save options to ﬁle by button, and load options from ﬁle by button.

![image 126](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile126.png)

![image 127](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile127.png)

![image 128](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile128.png)

![image 129](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile129.png)

Figure 2.72 General Tab

Layer Map File: speciﬁes a layer mapping ﬁle to be used during translation. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full or relative path. You can choose a Layer Map File by button.

![image 130](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile130.png)

Output Unmapped Lpp: speciﬁes whether to output the unmapped layer. The format for the map ﬁle is: <oaLayerName> <oaLayerPurpose> <gdsLayer> <gdsPurpose> If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, objects on layer and purpose combinations found in the map ﬁle are created on the GDS layer and data type speciﬁed in the ﬁle. Objects on layer and purpose combinations not included in the map ﬁle are not created. If you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, objects are created on their corresponding layer number and purpose 0. Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored. Note:

- • The layer mapping ﬁle can specify multiple entries for the same database layer/purpose pair if the GDS layer/data type pair values are diﬀerent (see the two Metal5 entries in the example layer mapping ﬁle). The complete line in the layer mapping ﬁle must be unique. If there are duplicate entries, a warning is issued and the duplicate entry is ignored.
- • If layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is not empty, Aether will use the speciﬁed layer mapping ﬁle directly. if layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is empty, Aether will not use any layer mapping ﬁle. if layer mapping ﬁle is unchecked, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(gds.map) under the library speciﬁed by Technology Library Name. If Technology Library Name is not speciﬁed, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(gds.map) under the library speciﬁed by Library Name.

Cell Map File: speciﬁes the cell mapping ﬁle to use during export. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose a Cell Map File by button.

![image 131](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile131.png)

The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<library name> <cell name> <view name> <stream structure name>

Aether writes cells (and instances of that cell) from the map ﬁle as the Stream structure name speciﬁed. No case conversion is processed on these names. Cells and instances not found in the mapping ﬁle translate with the same cell names as used in the OpenAccess database.

|desLib<br><br>|cellNu|layout<br><br>|cellNu|
|*<br><br>|cellNu<br><br>|layout|cellNew|


Each stream name in the cell mapping ﬁle must be unique. Cell Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for cell name.

- • Preserve: preserve cell name.
- • Upper: converts cell names to upper case.


- • Lower: converts cell names to lower case.


Label Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for label name.

- • Preserve: preserve label name.
- • Upper: converts label names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts label names to lower case.


Pin Attribute Number: speciﬁes the pin attribute number. If the number

is 0, nothing converts. The valid value is 1-127. Default value is 0. Translate Entire Hierarchy: speciﬁes translate entire hierarchy. Translation Depth: speciﬁes the hierarchical depth to translate to. The

default depth is 32. Allow Multi-Thread: speciﬁes whether to allow multiple threads. The default value is unchecked. Do Not Output Message: speciﬁes whether to output message. The default value is not unchecked. Export GDS From VM: speciﬁes whether export GDS from virtual memory. The default value is unchecked. Compress GDS File: speciﬁes whether to compress GDS ﬁle. The default value is unchecked. Compress Ratio: speciﬁes the compress level. The valid value is 1-9. Default value is 6. Export GDS With MT: speciﬁes export with MT mode. This will generate diﬀerent GDS ﬁles from top cell and die cells separately.

![image 132](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile132.png)

Figure 2.73 Advanced Tab

Smash VCells: speciﬁes whether to smash VCells. Smash Vias: speciﬁes whether to smash vias. The default value is No. Smash Any Angle Instance: speciﬁes whether to smash any angle instances. The default value is No.

Cell Name Up To 32: speciﬁes that Aether conforms to the 32-character limit on structure names. Cellview names mapped using the this argument are output to the cell mapping ﬁle gdsOut.cell.automap. By default, Aether does not conform to the 32-character limit on structure names.

Output Property Value Only: speciﬁes whether Aether creates only property values. By default, Aether creates properties formatted as <property name> = <property value>.

Skip Empty Cells: speciﬁes whether to skip empty cells.

Export Cells Referenced In Other Library: speciﬁes whether Aether does not create cells referenced from a library other than the one speciﬁed by the library argument or not. By default, Aether exports cells referenced from other libraries.

• Add Library Name As Preﬁx: adds the preﬁx using <other_libName>_ for these cells that reference from other libraries. If you select All, all reference cells will be added the preﬁx. If you select Conﬂicted, just add the preﬁx for these conﬂicted cells. When Export Cells Referenced

In Other Library is No, the option will not take eﬀect. The sketch is shown below.

![image 133](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile133.png)

Figure 2.74 The Behavior of Add Library Name As Preﬁx Option

##### • Keep Cell Name In Library: speciﬁes a library to keep cell name. When Export Cells Referenced In Other Library is Yes and Add Library Name As Preﬁx is Conﬂicted, the option will take eﬀect.

Cell Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes preﬁx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the preﬁx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Use Top Cell Name: uses top cell name as preﬁx. If it is checked, Cell Name Preﬁx is not enabled and top cell name is used as the preﬁx for all cells. The default value is unchecked.

Cell Name Suﬃx: speciﬁes suﬃx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the suﬃx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Ignore Cell Name Preﬁx&Suﬃx For Top Name: speciﬁes whether to ignore preﬁx and suﬃx for top name. If Yes is selected, ignore the preﬁx and suﬃx for top cell. The default value is No.

Text Namespace: speciﬁes name space mapping for textDisplays. Some textDisplays, such as oaAttrDisplay, either require or support name space mapping. For consistency, any of the OpenAccess name space (except OS name spaces like oaUnixNS and oaWinNS) can be speciﬁed. The valid arguments for this option are “native” , “cdba” , “lef” , “def” , “verilog” , “vhdl” , “spef” , “spice” , and “spf” . “cdba” is used as the default.

Scale UU/DBU: redeﬁnes the uu/dbu in design when exporting.

Allow Check Hcl Matched: speciﬁes whether to allow check hcl matching. The default value is unchecked.

Convert Unlocked Shape: converts unlocked shapes. The three options are Gray, Locked and Ignore, the default value is Gray.

![image 134](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile134.png)

- Figure 2.75 Geometry Tab


Output Paths As Polygons: converts orthogonal and diagonal oaPath objects, and orthogonal oaPathSeg objects, to polygons and writes the polygons as boundary records. This option does not aﬀect the output of routes. If this option is not used, Aether writes oaPathSegs as path records.

##### Output Rectangles As Boxes: converts rectangles as boxes.

Convert Text Display: speciﬁes whether Aether translate textDisplays or not. Only oaAttrDisplay, oaPropDisplay and oaTextOverride textDisplay objects are translated. The oaInstAttrDisplay and oaInstPropDisplay objects are not translated. textDisplays are translated as labels and written as GDS TEXT records. This translation is asymmetric, which means that in a round trip translation, TEXT records translate back to OpenAccess as oaText objects, not as oaTextDisplay objects.

Save GuardRing To Cell: speciﬁes whether Aether outputs guardring as cell or not.

Output Zero Width Path: speciﬁes whether Aether outputs path which width is zero or not.

Filter Label: speciﬁes Aether whether to output label or not. Convert <> To []: speciﬁes whether to convert <> to []. Default value is No, nothing converts. Only choosing Yes, converting will be worked. Ignore Line Type Object: speciﬁes whether to ignore line type object. The default value is No.

Donut Number Sides: speciﬁes the number of sides for the boundary that is generated when writing donut objects. The default value for this argument is 128.

Ellipse Number Sides: speciﬁes the number of sides for the boundary that is generated when writing ellipse objects. The default value for this argument is 128.

Max Vertices In Polygon/Path: speciﬁes maximum vertices in polygon/path when exporting. By default, it is 2000.

Via Cut Converting Threshold: speciﬁes the via cut number. The valid value is 16~900000000. Default value is empty.

Convert Pin To: converts the pin to the speciﬁed object type. Default value is geometry.

Do Not Output Message: speciﬁes whether to output message. The default value is unchecked.

Output Evaluation Failure PCell: speciﬁes whether to output the evaluation failure pcell instance. The default value is unchecked.

Output Unbound Instance: speciﬁes whether to output the unbound instance. The default value is unchecked.

Output Unbound Via: speciﬁes whether to output the unbound via. The default value is unchecked.

Allow Check HCL Matched: speciﬁes whether to allow check HCL matching. The default value is unchecked.

Convert Unlocked Shape: converts unlocked shapes. The three options are Gray, Locked and Ignore, the default value is Gray.

Via Map File: produces a via mapping ﬁle that lists all of the structures written to the GDS ﬁle that are masters for CustomViaDefs. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose a Cell Map File by button.

### 2.7.2 OASIS

Menu: File ->Export ->OASIS ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 142](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile142.png)

This command is used to export OASIS ﬁle from OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

![image 143](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile143.png)

- Figure 2.80 Export OASIS Form


Library Name: speciﬁes the library to translate. The library must exist in the library deﬁnitions ﬁle in the current working directory. If the Cell Name and View Name options are not speciﬁed, all the cells in the library are translated. If a cell has more than one view of maskLayout viewType, the views are translated as cellName, cellName_0, cellName_1, and so forth where cellName is the name of cell being translated.

Cell Name: speciﬁes a set of cells to translate. The cell names must be separated by white space. If you want to export parts of a design, using this option to specify the required cells is one way to accomplish this. Aether translates the speciﬁed cells together with their sub-cells, recursively, down to the depth speciﬁed by the optional Translation Depth or Translate Entire Hierarchy. Aether ensures that no cell is translated multiple times. If the View Name option is not speciﬁed, the default view name layout is used. If this option is not used, Aether exports all cells in the library that is speciﬁed with Library Name.

View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the cells to translate. If you don’t set Cell Name, this option will be not eﬀective for export.

OASIS File Name: speciﬁes the output OASIS ﬁle. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for export. You can choose an OASIS ﬁle by button.

![image 144](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile144.png)

Technology Library Name: speciﬁes the technology library to use during the translation. If you specify a library name, the library must exist. The default value is the library speciﬁed with the Library Name.

Template File: template ﬁle is a ﬁle that records the options of Export OASIS. You can choose ﬁle by button, save options to ﬁle by button, and load options from ﬁle by Load button.

![image 145](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile145.png)

![image 146](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile146.png)

![image 147](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile147.png)

- Figure 2.81 General Tab


Layer Map File: speciﬁes a layer mapping ﬁle to be used during translation. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full or relative path. You can choose a Layer Map File by button.

![image 148](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile148.png)

Output Unmapped Lpp: speciﬁes whether to output the unmapped layer. The format for the map ﬁle is: <oaLayerName> <oaLayerPurpose> <gdsLayer> <gdsPurpose> If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, objects on layer and purpose combinations found in the map ﬁle are created on the GDS layer and data type speciﬁed in the ﬁle. Objects on layer and purpose combinations not included in the map ﬁle are not created. If you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, objects are created on their corresponding layer number and purpose 0. Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored. Note:

- • The layer mapping ﬁle can specify multiple entries for the same database layer/purpose pair if the GDS layer/data type pair values are diﬀerent (see the two Metal5 entries in the example layer mapping ﬁle). The complete line in the layer mapping ﬁle must be unique. If there are duplicate entries, a warning is issued and the duplicate entry is ignored.


- • If layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is not empty, Aether will use the speciﬁed layer mapping ﬁle directly. if layer mapping ﬁle is checked and layer mapping file is empty, Aether will not use any layer mapping ﬁle. if layer mapping ﬁle is unchecked, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(gds.map) under the library speciﬁed by Technology Library Name. If Technology Library Name is not speciﬁed, Aether will use layer mapping ﬁle(gds.map) under the library speciﬁed by Library Name.
