Cell Map File: speciﬁes the cell mapping ﬁle to use during export. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose a Cell Map File by button.

![image 149](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile149.png)

The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<library name> <cell name> <view name> <stream structure name>

Aether writes cells (and instances of that cell) from the map ﬁle as the Stream structure name speciﬁed. No case conversion is processed on these names. Cells and instances not be found in the mapping ﬁle are translated with the same cell names as used in the OpenAccess database.

Lines in the cellMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

- Table 2.17 Cell Mapping File of Export OASIS


|# library name|cell name<br><br>|view name<br><br>|stream name|
|---|---|---|---|
|desLib|nand2<br><br>|layout<br><br>|nand2_1|
|sdesLib<br><br>|nand2|layout|nand2_2|
|desLib|cellNu<br><br>|layout<br><br>|cellNu|
|*|cellNu<br><br>|layout<br><br>|cellNew|


Each stream name in the cell mapping ﬁle must be unique. Cell Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for cell name.

- • Preserve: preserve cell name.
- • Upper: converts cell names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts cell names to lower case.


Label Name Case Sensitivity: checks the sensitivity for label name.

- • Preserve: preserve label name.
- • Upper: converts label names to upper case.
- • Lower: converts label names to lower case.


Pin Attribute Number: speciﬁes the pin attribute number. If the number

is 0, nothing converts. The valid value is 1~127. Default value is 0. Translate Entire Hierarchy: speciﬁes translate entire hierarchy. Translation Depth: speciﬁes the hierarchical depth to translate to. The

default depth is 32. Allow Multi-Thread: speciﬁes whether to allow multiple threads. The default value is unchecked. Export OASIS From VM: speciﬁes whether to export OASIS from virtual memory. The default value is unchecked. Compress OASIS File: speciﬁes whether to compress OASIS ﬁle. The default value is unchecked. Compress Ratio: speciﬁes the compress level. The valid value is 1-9. Default value is 6. Export OASIS With MT: speciﬁes export with MT mode. This will be generate diﬀerent OASIS ﬁles from top cell and die cells separately.

![image 150](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile150.png)

Figure 2.82 Advanced Tab

Smash VCells: speciﬁes whether to smash VCells. Smash Vias: speciﬁes whether to smash vias. The default value is No. Smash Any Angle Instance: speciﬁes whether to smash any angle instances. The default value is No. Skip Empty Cells: speciﬁes whether to skip empty cells.

Export Cells Referenced In Other Library: speciﬁes whether Aether does not create cells referenced from a library other than the one speciﬁed by the library argument or not. By default, Aether exports cells referenced from other libraries.

• Add Library Name As Preﬁx: adds the preﬁx using <other_libName>_ for these cells that reference from other libraries. If you select All, all reference cells will be added the preﬁx. If you select Conﬂicted, just add the preﬁx for these conﬂicted cells. When Export Cells Referenced In Other Library is No, the option will not take eﬀect. The sketch is shown below.

![image 151](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile151.png)

Figure 2.83 The Behavior of Add Library Name As Preﬁx Option

##### • Keep Cell Name In Library: speciﬁes a library to keep cell name. When Export Cells Referenced In Other Library is Yes and Add Library Name As Preﬁx is Conﬂicted, the option will take eﬀect.

Sub Master Inﬁx: it is used as an intermediate string for customizing pcell (parameterized cell) and standard via cell names. The default value is “_empy_aether_” .

Cell Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes preﬁx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the preﬁx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Use Top Cell Name: uses top cell name as preﬁx. If it is checked, Cell Name Preﬁx is not enabled and top cell name is used as the preﬁx for all cells. The default value is unchecked.

Cell Name Suﬃx: speciﬁes suﬃx for cell name. If it is speciﬁed, the value is used as the suﬃx for all cells. The default value is empty.

Ignore Cell Name Preﬁx&Suﬃx For Top Name: speciﬁes whether to ignore preﬁx and suﬃx for top name. If Yes is selected, ignore the preﬁx and suﬃx for top cell. The default value is No.

Text Namespace: speciﬁes name space mapping for textDisplays. Some textDisplays, such as oaAttrDisplay, either require or support name space mapping. For consistency, any of the OpenAccess name space (except OS name spaces like oaUnixNS and oaWinNS) can be speciﬁed. The valid arguments for this option are “native” , “cdba” , “lef” , “def” , “verilog” , “vhdl” ,

“spef” , “spice” , and “spf” . “cdba” is used as the default. Scale UU/DBU: redeﬁnes the uu/dbu in design when exporting.

![image 152](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile152.png)

- Figure 2.84 Geometry Tab


Output Paths As Polygons: converts orthogonal and diagonal oaPath objects, and orthogonal oaPathSeg objects, to polygons and writes the polygons as boundary records. This option does not aﬀect the output of routes. If this option is not used, Aether writes oaPathSegs as path records.

Convert Text Display: speciﬁes whether Aether translate textDisplays or not. Only oaAttrDisplay, oaPropDisplay and oaTextOverride textDisplay objects are translated. The oaInstAttrDisplay and oaInstPropDisplay objects are not translated. textDisplays are translated as labels and written as GDS TEXT records. This translation is asymmetric, which means that in a round trip translation, TEXT records translate back to OpenAccess as oaText objects, not as oaTextDisplay objects.

Save GuardRing To Cell: speciﬁes whether Aether output guardring as cell or not.

Output Zero Width Path: speciﬁes whether Aether output path which width is zero or not.

Filter Label: speciﬁes whether Aether output label or not. Convert <> To [ ]: speciﬁes whether converting <> to [ ]. Default value is No, nothing converts. Only choosing Yes, converting will be worked. Ignore Line Type Object: speciﬁes whether to ignore line type object. The default value is No. Convert Circle To Polygon: speciﬁes whether to convert circle to polygon. The default value is No.

Donut Number Sides: speciﬁes the number of sides for the boundary that is generated when writing donut objects. The default value for this argument is 128.

Ellipse Number Sides: speciﬁes the number of sides for the boundary that is generated when writing ellipse objects. The default value for this argument is 128.

Max Vertices In Polygon/Path: speciﬁes maximum vertices in polygon/path when exporting. By default, it is 2000.

Via Cut Converting Threshold: speciﬁes the via cut number. The valid value is 16~900000000. Default value is empty.

Convert Pin To: converts the pin to the speciﬁed object type. Default value is geometry.

![image 153](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile153.png)

- Figure 2.85 Misc Tab


Do Not Output Message: speciﬁes whether to output message. The default value is unchecked.

Output Evaluation Failure PCell: speciﬁes whether to output the evaluation failure pcell instance. The default value is unchecked.

Output Unbound Instance: speciﬁes whether to output the unbound instance. The default value is unchecked.

Output Unbound Via: speciﬁes whether to output the unbound via. The default value is unchecked.

Allow Check HCL Matched: speciﬁes whether to allow check HCL matching. The default value is unchecked.

Convert Unlocked Shape: converts unlocked shapes. The three options are Gray, Locked and Ignore, the default value is Gray.

![image 154](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile154.png)

- Figure 2.86 File Tab


Via Map File: produces a via mapping ﬁle that lists all of the structures written to the OASIS ﬁle that are masters for CustomViaDefs. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose a Via Map File by button.

![image 155](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile155.png)

The format for the mapping ﬁle is:

<Structure Name> <oaCustomViaDef Name> <Layer1 Name/Number> <Layer2 Name/Number>

Lines in the ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

Example Via Mapping File:

|via2<br><br>|m2m3via<br><br>|m2 20<br><br>|m3 30|


Property Map File: speciﬁes the property mapping ﬁle to use during export. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose a Property Map File by button.

![image 156](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile156.png)

The format for the map ﬁle is: <stream id> <object type> <property name>

If you specify a property mapping ﬁle, Aether creates properties with property name and object type combinations found in the map ﬁle using the Stream Id speciﬁed. Properties not be found in the map ﬁle are not created. Valid object types are: Blockage, Donut, Dot, Ellipse, Line, Path, Polygon, Rect, Text, ArrayInst, and ScalarInst.

By default, if you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, properties are not written to the Stream ﬁle.

Lines in the property map ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

- Table 2.19 Property Mapping File of Export OASIS


|# stream Id|object<br><br>|name|
|---|---|---|
|1|Rect|instP11|
|2|Polygon<br><br>|poly1|

|4<br><br>|Text|pad32|
|5<br><br>|Pin<br><br>|io_term|
|6|ScalarInst<br><br>|contact|


Object Map File: speciﬁes the object map ﬁle name. Do Not Output Object Properties: speciﬁes whether to output object properties in the object map ﬁle. Log File: speciﬁes the log ﬁle name. If this option is omitted, the log ﬁle name defaults to oasisOut.log. Split Layer Name: speciﬁes whether to print layer information in split column in the log ﬁle. The default value is unchecked. Backup Oasis And Log Files: speciﬁes whether to back up Oasis ﬁle and log ﬁle. The default value is unchecked.

Example 2.22 The example shows how to export an OASIS ﬁle, follow these steps:

- 1. Activate the command File ->Export ->OASIS, the Export OASIS form appears.


![image 157](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile157.png)

Figure 2.87 Parameter Settings in the Export OASIS

- 2. In the OASIS File Name ﬁeld, type the name of the ﬁle which you want to write, such as, $HOME/work/aether/data/oasis/oasisout/test.oasis.
- 3. In the Library Name ﬁeld, type the name of library which you want to be translated, such as, test.
- 4. Keep other options as default.
- 5. Press OK button, the OpenAccess database is translated to $HOME/work/aether/data/oasis/oasisout/test.oasis.

Flat: selects Flat mode, LEF ﬁle is exported by the input view.

### 2.7.6 Netlist

Menu: File -> Export -> Netlist ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 172](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile172.png)

This command is used to export netlist ﬁle from OpenAccess database. The netlist formats supported in Aether include hspice, cdl, pspice, verilog, veriloga. You may set the following options.

![image 173](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile173.png)

Figure 2.97 Export Netlist Form - General

Netlist View: sets the top design.

- • Library Name: sets the library name which is to be exported.
- • Cell Name: sets the top cell name which is to be exported.


- • View Name: sets the view name which is to be exported.


Simulation Type: sets the netlist format type of exporting. Output File: sets the output netlist ﬁle name.

Netlist View List: speciﬁes the views order for searching when creating netlist. This view list requires a particular sequence. When exporting netlist, Aether will search view names speciﬁed here by order, Once ﬁnding one under the cell, Aether will use this view to export netlist. The default value of this option is diﬀerent according to Simulation Type. See the following table.

Stop View List: speciﬁes the views to identify the stopping view when creating netlist. This view list dose not require a particular sequence. When exporting netlist, Aether will search view names speciﬁed in Netlist View List ﬁrst, after ﬁnding one, it will judge whether this view is a stop view according to Stop View List, if yes, netlist will treat it as stop cell, the context under this view will be not exported any more. The default value of this option is diﬀerent according to Simulation Type. See the following table.

Table 2.20 Simulation Type

|Simulation Type|Netlist View List|Stop View List|
|---|---|---|
|SPICE3|spiceText spice schematic<br><br>|spiceText spice|
|CDL|cdlText auCdl schematic<br><br>|cdlText auCdl|
|HSPICE<br><br>|hspiceText hspiceD schematic<br><br>|hspiceText hspiceD|
|Spectre<br><br>|spectreText spectre schematic|spectreText spectre|
|PSPICE<br><br>|schematic| |
|Verilog<br><br>|verilog systemVerilog behavior functional schematic symbol|verilog systemVerilog symbol|
|Veriloga|veriloga schematic symbol<br><br>|veriloga symbol|


Skip Libraries: sets the libraries to be skipped. The cell under the library will be ignored during exporting.

Skip Cells Below: sets the cells to be skipped. The cells listed here will be exported as an empty subckt.

Parasitic RC: enables to export the estimating parasitic device. Top Only: enables to only export the top design. Display Result: enables to display the output ﬁle after exporting.

Accept Open View: continues to export netlist without aborting when meeting open view. Open view is the subckt which has no schematic view, or

device has no template and simulation information. The open views will be skipped during exporting.

Export Netlist From VM: speciﬁes whether export netlist from virtual memory. The default value is unchecked.

![image 174](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile174.png)

Figure 2.98 Export Netlist Form - Format

Name Case: sets name case of net name.

- • Preserve: keeps name case of net name in schematic
- • Upper: exports upper case net name.
- • Lower: exports lower case net name. Max. Line Length: sets the length of a line in netlist. Max. Errors Number: sets the max number of errors.


![image 175](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile175.png)

- Figure 2.99 Export Netlist Form - HDL


Note: Some options(about HDL) are disabled. Group Net to Bus: sets exporting bus net in bus format or single-bit format. Power Name: lists the power name used in verilog. Ground Name: lists the ground name used in verilog. Index Name Format As: sets single bit net name format. Propagate Hierarchical Data Type: propagate hierarchical data type used in verilog. Netlist Without Text View: controls whether to output the content of verilog text ﬁles.

Global Sim Time: speciﬁes the value of Global Sim Time and its default value is 1. Specify the value of Unit and its default value is ns. The Unit value can be set [ps ns us ms s].

Global Sim Precision: speciﬁes the value of Global Sim Precision and its default value is 1. Specify the value of Unit and its default value is ns. The Unit value can be set [ps ns us ms s].

Header: sets head section which will be included in verilog.

![image 176](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile176.png)

- Figure 2.100 Export Netlist Form - CDL


Global Net Support: lists the global nets at the beginning of netlist. Ground As 0: exports gnd signal as 0. Print Empty SUBCKT: When exporting cdl netlist, for cdl stop cells, this option can control whether it exports .subckt deﬁnition for these stop cells. CDL stop cell includes:

- • There are schematic and symbol view under the cell and this cell has CDL deﬁnition in Device Deﬁne and Device Type=X.
- • There are schematic, symbol and auCdl view under the cell and this cell


has auCdl simulation information in CDF Editor and namePreﬁx=X. CDL Pin Separator: inserts “/” between input and output port. Display Pin Info: displays pin information for subckt. Case Sensitive and Rename: renames signal and instance names in case of naming collision. Trim Exclamation: trims exclamation for global signals.

LVS Pin Style: also exports port name when exporting net name as LVS netlist format.

Print CDF Parameters For SUBCKT: speciﬁes whether to export subckt parameter deﬁnition in SUBCKT line.

Power Name: lists the power name used in CDL. Ground Name: lists the ground name used in CDL. Resistor Threshold Value: threshold value for resistor. If you deﬁne this option, it will export "*RESI =$value" statement at the head of cdl netlist. Cell Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes the preﬁx for cell name used in CDL. Cell Name Suﬃx: speciﬁes the suﬃx for cell name used in CDL. Bus Delimiter: bus bit net name bracket style.

- • None: none
- • <>: angle bracket
- • [ ]: square bracket
- • { }: brace


Hierarchy/Flat: speciﬁes exporting hierarchy netlist or ﬂatten.

- • Hierarchy Netlist: hierarchical format.
- • Flat Netlist: ﬂatten format.


Check: converts device parameter in device deﬁnition. These options only work for res/cap/diode in analog library. If schematic contains res,cap or diode of analog lib.

- • Resistors: converts resistors parameters.

- – Value: exports resistors value. If Resistance Value=Oﬀ, it would not export the value of resistors in cdl netlist. (Only works for res in analog lib.
- – Size: exports resistors size. If Resistance Size=Oﬀ, it would not export W and L values of resistors in cdl netlist.


- • Capacitors: converts capacitors parameters.

- – Value: exports capacitors value
- – Area: exports capacitors area
- – Size: exports capacitors size


- • Diodes: converts diodes parameters.


- – Area: exports diodes area


- – Perimeter: exports diodes perimeter


Include File: sets ﬁle which will be included in CDL. Header: sets head section which will be included in CDL.

![image 177](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile177.png)

Figure 2.101 Export Netlist Form - SPICE

Package: speciﬁes available spice simulation types. Global Net Support: lists the global nets at the beginning of netlist. Ground As 0: exports gnd signal as 0. Global G_SUB: supports G_SUB pin for pspice. Without .END Card: enables “.END” statement for subckt. Trim Exclamation: trims exclamation for global signals. Circuit NO. Separator: names separator in ﬂattened netlist. Power Name: lists the power name used in spice-style netlist. Ground Name: lists the ground name used in spice-style netlist. Quote For .Include: sets quoting mark for “.Include” statements. Bus Delimiter: speciﬁes bus bit net name bracket style. Hierarchy/Flat: speciﬁes exporting hierarchy netlist or ﬂatten.

- • Hierarchy Netlist: hierarchical format.
- • Flat Netlist: ﬂatten format.


Quotes For Expression: speciﬁes export None,” or "" for expression. The option is unavailable when Package is Spectre.

- • None: checks this option on, it will export the expression directly without adding any markings when exporting netlist.
- • ”: checks this option on, it will add ” for expression when exporting netlist.
- • "": checks this option on, it will add "" for expression when exporting netlist, the default mode for this option is checked on.


Map [] To _: maps [] to _ for hspice. The default value is not checked. Header: sets head section which will be included in spice-style netlist.

Note: All options in the netlist form will be saved to ﬁle by Aether automatically, and the netlist form will load the saved option back after startup.

### 2.7.7 DXF

Menu: File -> Export -> DXF ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 189](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile189.png)

This command is used to export dxf ﬁle from OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

![image 190](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile190.png)

Figure 2.112 Export DXF Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the library to translate. The library must exist in the library deﬁnitions ﬁle in the current working directory.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell to translate. View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the cell to translate. If the View Name option is not speciﬁed, the default view name layout is used. Layer: speciﬁes which layers to export. If there is no layer speciﬁed, all layers will be exported. Hierarchy: if this option is selected, export hierarchical information. Sub Cell: if this option is selected, the shape of selected cells will be exported. Cell Rules:

- • Sub cell Name: select sub cell(s) from the subcell name list, the shape of selected sub cells will be exported. It supports wildcard character of


##### *. Note:

sub cell name list only contains cells in library of Library Name.

- • Sub Cell Layer: speciﬁes which subcell layers to export. If there is no layer speciﬁed, all layers will be exported.
- • Delete: deletes this line rule.
- • Add Rule: adds a new cell rule for DXF cell rules.
- • Delete All: deletes all rules.


Unit: speciﬁes unit used in DXF ﬁle. The valid values are um, mm, cm and inch. The default unit is um. If the speciﬁed unit is diﬀerent from the unit in design, there is no numerical transform.

Unit Conversion: if the speciﬁed unit is diﬀerent from the unit in design, there is a transformation of unit when this option is checked.

Dimension Style: speciﬁes dimension style. The valid values are Standard, ISO-25 and Annotation. The default is ISO-25.

Donut Number Sides: speciﬁes the number of sides for the boundary that is generated when writing donut objects. The default value for this argument is 32.

The format for the map ﬁle is:

<LayerName> <LayerPurpose> <AutoCadColorIndex> <LayerIsFill>

If you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, objects are created on their corresponding layer name and purpose drawing.

##### Note:

• If map ﬁle is checked and map ﬁle is not empty, AetherFPD will use the speciﬁed map ﬁle directly. If map ﬁle is checked and map ﬁle is empty, AetherFPD will report error message.

Table 2.21 Sample Map File

|LayerName<br><br>|LayerPurpose|AutoCadColorIndex|LayerIsFill|
|---|---|---|---|
|Metal1|drawing<br><br>|235|0|


DXF File Name: speciﬁes the output DXF ﬁle. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for export. You can choose a DXF ﬁle by Browser button.

This command is used to export FPV ﬁle from OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

Figure 2.120 Export FPV Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the library to translate. The library must exist in the library deﬁnitions ﬁle in the current working directory.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell to translate. View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the cell to translate.

FPVLef File Name: speciﬁes the output FPVLef ﬁle. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose an FPVLef ﬁle by button. The FPV ﬁle format develops from the LEF ﬁle format, the supported keywords are as follows.

![image 200](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile200.png)

Table 2.22 KeyWords

|KeyWord|Description|
|---|---|


|UNITS|Deﬁne the units of measure in FPV, and only DATABASE MICRONS is used in FPV ﬁle now.|
|---|---|
|MACRO<br><br>|Deﬁne the pattern group information.|
|TYPE<br><br>|Deﬁne the pattern group type(eg: DiﬀPair).|
|SIZE<br><br>|Deﬁne the size of pattern group.|
|PIN<br><br>|Deﬁne the pin information in pattern group.|
|DIRECTION|Deﬁne the direction of pin.|
|USE<br><br>|Deﬁne the use of pin.|
|PORT|Deﬁne the port information in pin.|
|LAYER<br><br>|Deﬁne the metal layer of port in pin.|
|RECT|Deﬁne the size and location of port in pin.|
|END<br><br>|Deﬁne the end tag about port, pin, pattern group and LIBRARY.|


##### For Example:

|VERSION 5.7 ; BUSBITCHARS " [ ] " ; DIVIDERCHAR "/" ; UNITS<br><br>DATABASE MICRONS 1000 ; END UNITS MACRO Group1<br><br>TYPE d i f f ; SIZE 4 by 4 ; PIN IN<br><br>USE SIGNAL ; DIRECTION INPUT ; PORT<br><br>LAYER M4 ; RECT 3.5 3.5 4.0 4.0 ;<br><br>END PORT<br><br>LAYER M1 ; RECT 0.3 0.9 0.8 1.2 ;<br><br>END<br><br>END IN END Group1 END LIBRARY<br><br>|
|---|


### 2.7.9 FPVDef

Menu: File -> Export -> FPVDef ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 201](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile201.png)

This command is used to export FPVDef ﬁle from OpenAccess database. You may set the following options.

![image 202](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile202.png)

Figure 2.121 Export FPVDef Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the library to translate. The library must exist in the library deﬁnitions ﬁle in the current working directory.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell to translate. View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the cell to translate.

FPVDef File Name: speciﬁes the output FPVDef ﬁle. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative for exporting. You can choose an FPVDef ﬁle by button. The FPVDEF ﬁle format develops from the FPV standard DEF ﬁle format. The contents include: UNITS(Unit Distance), VIAS(Via Definition), COMPONENTS(soft block), PATTERNGROUPS(pattern group), PINS(Pin Deﬁne), NETS(Net info). The supported key word list as follows.

![image 203](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile203.png)

Table 2.23 Key Words

|Key Word<br><br>|Description|
|---|---|


|UNITS<br><br>|Deﬁne the units of measure in FPV, and only DATABASE MICRONS is used in FPV ﬁle now.|
|---|---|
|VIAS<br><br>|Deﬁne the vias information.|
|VIARULE<br><br>|Deﬁne the rule of via.|
|CUTSIZE|Deﬁne the cut size of via.|
|LAYERS<br><br>|Deﬁne the layers involved in via.|
|CUTSPACING|Specify the cut spacing in via.|
|ENCLOSURE|Specify the cut spacing in via.|
|ROWCOL<br><br>|Specify the cut spacing in via.|
|PINS|Deﬁne the pins information.|
|NET|Deﬁne the pin name and connection information.|
|DIRECTION|Deﬁne the direction of pin.|
|USE<br><br>|Deﬁne the purpose of pin.|
|PORTS|Deﬁne the port information in pins.|
|END<br><br>|Deﬁne the end tag about port, pin, pattern group.|


##### For Example:

UNITS DISTANCE MICRONS 1000 VIAS 1

M1_GT_0 VIARULE M2_M1 CUTSIZE 70 70 LAYERS M1 V1 M2 CUTSPACING 90 90 ENCLOSURE 5 5 5 5 ROWCOL 1 3

END M2_M1_0

END COMPONENTS

PATTERNGROUPS 2

- G1 Current_Mirror 59370 79951 N

- G2 Differential_Pair 132020 110391 N


PINS 1

A NET A DIRECTION INPUT USE CLOCK PORTS 2

LAYER M1 RECT 0 0 20 20 LAYER M2 POLYGON (60 70) (65 70) (65 65) (70 65)

(70 60) (60 60)

END A END PINS

NETS 1 A

(PIN A) VIA M2_M1_0 −9818 7542 N ROUTED M1 20 (−9818 7542) (−6830 7542) (7542 1469)

(7535 1469) (7542 1422) (7534 1422) (7532 1450)

## 2.8 Recent Working Folder

Open Recently is used to record the design you have recently opened. The Open Recently is shown in Figure 2.122 .

![image 204](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile204.png)

Figure 2.122 Open Recently

.

##### Add To Recently:

- 1. Add a currently open design at the position 1 of Open Recently list.
- 2. Add all viewtypes supported by Aether , including netlist. However, it supports up to 10 records, and the excess will be discarded.
- 3. The list of Open Recently is displayed in the File menu and expanded in a tiled manner.
- 4. For the design opened by binding, record in the default opening order.
- 5. Design won’t be added to Open Recently list, if the design is opened failed or not supported by Aether . Record Edit Mode:


- 1. Open Recently will record the R/W status when opening for the ﬁrst time and exiting design.
- 2. If you use Make Editable to change a readonly design to editable, and open the design again from the Open Recently list without closing the current design, the modiﬁed status will not take eﬀect. It can only take eﬀect after closing design. From Open Recently:


- 1. The design will be opened in the recently edit mode and it will be updated


2.9. Exit

to the position 1 of Open Recently list. The window which is opened from Open Recently list will be raised to the top.

- 2. Design will be removed from Open Recently list, when design is opened failed.

131

Update Instances: speciﬁes whether to choose to update the inter-view relations of the design hierarchy. Notice that the target library may have a hierarchical structure from the source library.

There is an example to illustrate this command for more details. There are three libraries: A, B and C. The library A includes two cells cell_a1 and cell_a2, and cell_a1 references cell_a2. The library B includes one cell cell_b1, and cell_b1 references A/cell_a1. The library C includes one cell cell_c1, and cell_c1 references A/cell_a2.

Figure 3.2 Diagram of Instances

- • New Copied: updates only the cellview references you copied from the source library.

The below example illustrates the action options. We will copy the entire A library onto a designated location of /tmp and rename it as B.

- – Unchecked: B/cell_a1 will reference the original A/cell_a2.
- – Checked: B/cell_a1 will reference a duplicated B/cell_a2, B/-


cell_b1 will reference A/cell_a1 yet.

- • All: updates all hierarchical relations and name with To Library.


– Checked: B/cell_a1 will reference a duplicated B/cell_a2, and overwrite and break the existed instance relation between A/cell_a1 and B/cell_b1. cell_b1 will reference a duplicated B/cell_a1.

||Note: if you select Update Instances, the instance relation changing only take place between source library and target library. For example, C/cell_c1 always references A/cell_a2 whatever you select Update Instances or not.|

Add To Category: speciﬁes the category which the new cellview belong to. You can choose the existed category or specify a new one.

Show Copy List: displays the customizable views to copy in table. The source cellview will be copyed to the target cellview when the checkbox is checked in each row.

## 3.5 Change Library References

Menu: Edit -> Change Library References ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 248](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile248.png)

This command is used to batch change the references of libraries.

![image 249](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile249.png)

Figure 3.27 Change Library References Form

In Library: speciﬁes the target library for the operation. From Library: speciﬁes the old reference library/libraries to be changed. To Library: speciﬁes the new reference library to be changed. From View: speciﬁes the view of From Library.

All: changes all references related to the From Library. All layout: changes all layout-type references related to the From Library. All schematic: changes all schematic-type references related to the From Library. All symbol: changes all symbol-type references related to the From Library. Self Input: changes references related to the From Library with speciﬁed names.

To View: ﬁxed to "As Is", meaning the new reference has the same view name and view type as the old reference.

Filter: ﬁlters the data in the library list. Show Selected Libraries Only: shows only the selected libraries in In Library, From Library, and To Library list boxes. Change List: displays all the selected libraries in the In Library, From Library, and To Library list boxes. Add: adds all the selected libraries in the In Library, From Library, and To Library list boxes to the Change List section. Replace: replaces the entry in the Change List section. Move Up: moves the entry up the order in the Change List section. Move Down: moves the entry down the order in the Change List section. Delete: deletes the entry from the Change List section. OK: submits the selected references and closes the form. Apply: submits the selected references and keeps the form open. Cancel: closes the form without saving any changes. Help: opens the online help system to display information about using this form.

## 3.8 Property

Menu: Edit -> Property ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

### 3.8.1 Library Property Editor

![image 264](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile264.png)

Figure 3.35 Library Property Editor

Library: properties about library.

- • Name: shows library name.
- • Owner: shows owner of library.


- • Group: shows group of library owner.
- • Last Modify: shows last modiﬁed time.
- • Cell Number: shows number of cell in library.
- • Library Size: shows disk size of library by Load button.
- • Technology: shows technology library of speciﬁed library.
- • Read Path: shows library path to read.
- • Write Path: shows library path to write.


Permission: accesses permission about library.

- • Owner: shows access permission of owner, r is for read, w is for write, x is for execute.
- • Group: shows access permission of group, r is for read, w is for write, x is for execute.
- • Other: shows access permission of other, r is for read, w is for write, x is for execute. Note: you can reference it from directory access in Linux.


Property: shows and edits user property

- • Name(Range): shows user property name.
- • Value: shows user property value.
- • Add: adds user property.


![image 265](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile265.png)

Figure 3.36 Add Property

- – Name: speciﬁes user property name.
- – Type: speciﬁes user property type. There are ﬁve property type: String, Int, Float, Boolean, Time.
- – Value: speciﬁes user property value. How to specify value depends on property type. For example, when type is Time, valid value is Mar 19 18:34:48 2012.


- – Minimum: speciﬁes minimum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float, Time.
- – Maximum: speciﬁes maximum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float, Time.
- – Choices: speciﬁes choice values of user property. It is valid for String.


- • Modify: modiﬁes selected user property.

Menu: Tools -> Delete Empty/Unbound Cell ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 291](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile291.png)

This command does delete empty and unbound cells operation in one library. Aether uses ’*’ to match string.

![image 292](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile292.png)

Figure 4.2 Delete Empty/Unbound Cell Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the library name. Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name. View Name: speciﬁes the view name, it is changeless. Delete Type: speciﬁes the delete type.

Library: speciﬁes the library which data is in. Cell/Library File: speciﬁes the cell or ﬁle which data is in. View/Cell File: speciﬁes the view of ﬁle which data is in. Mode: speciﬁes the mode of data, which is read or edit. Save: speciﬁes whether to save data or not if data is modiﬁed. Purge All: selects all data to purge. Purge None: selects no data to purge. Save All: saves modiﬁed data which are selected, and purges selected data.

# Chapter 6Options

## 6.1 Settings

Menu: Options -> Settings ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 319](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile319.png)

This command is used to set options for Aether . Four parts are included in this form: General, Symbol, Verilog and Check.

181

![image 320](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile320.png)

###### Figure 6.1 General in Settings Form

General: general settings for Aether , these may inﬂuence on schematic, symbol, or layout editor.

![image 321](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile321.png)

Figure 6.2 General in Settings Form

##### • Mouse Wheel Behavior: speciﬁes behavior of mouse wheel. Defaultis Zoom In/Out At The Center View.

- – Zoom In/Out At The Center View: when this option is selected, zoom in/out as original by center of view port.
- – Zoom In/Out At The Mouse Cursor: when this option is selected, zoom in/out as original by mouse cursor.


- – Scroll Draw Area: when this option is selected, scroll draw area(view port) up/down. If you press Shift, it will scroll view port left/right.


- • Mouse Wheel Scale: speciﬁes the scale for zooming with mouse wheel. The value range is [1,10], default is 1.
- • Right Mouse Zoom By: speciﬁes zoom behavior of right mouse. Default is Line.

- – Line: Aether will draw a line when you zoom by right mouse.
- – Area: Aether will draw an area when you zoom by right mouse.


- • Open Design Mode: speciﬁes to open mode when you open design again. Default is New Window.

– Single Window: speciﬁes to open window in single window mode

when you open design again.

– Single Window With Tab: speciﬁes to open window in tab mode

when you open design again.

– New Window: speciﬁes to open window in new window mode when

you open design again.

- • Keep The Form Of Some Commands On Top: keeps form on top, it is valid for Print, Fill Dummy, Create Symbol View, Trace Net, Trace Short, Find Marker and Cross Probe .
- • The Command Option Form Escape When Hit Enter Key: speciﬁes to hide form of command when you press Enter.
- • Close Waves When Escape MDE Cross Probe: speciﬁes to close iWave after exiting from Cross Probe in MDE.
- • Popup Message Box If Design Is Opened With ReadOnly Mode: speciﬁes to pop up message box to prompt user when opening read-only design in edit mode.
- • Restart Action: speciﬁes to restart action when you invoke command again. For example, when you invoke Move, and have selected object and set reference point, at this time, you invoke command by shortcut, if this option is on, Aether will restart Move and let you set reference point again. Default is on.
- • Inﬁx: when inﬁx mode turned on and a command started with bind key, the current cursor point is used as the starting point automatically. Somebody will feel it is very favor because he can quickly create the ﬁrst point in editor. But somebody will feel it terrible because a strange point is added to his action.


- • Color Mode: it will inﬂuence the color of library/cell/view in DM when design is opened. Default is oﬀ.


If option is on, the color of library/cell/view will be adopted as following rules:

Table 6.1 Color Mode

|Color|Range<br><br>|Priority<br><br>|Note|
|---|---|---|---|
|darkRed|design opened in editable|1| |
|Cyan|design opened in read only<br><br>|2| |
|Gray<br><br>|library has no read right|3<br><br>|only for library|
|Blue|library has no write right<br><br>|4|only for library|
|Black|no design opened<br><br>|5| |


![image 322](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile322.png)

Figure 6.3 DM Color Mode

For example, in the above ﬁgure, 018um_PDK is a system library, which you only have read right, so it’s color is blue. When you open MA.ma_tb.layout which has an instance references from 018um_PDK.

![image 323](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile323.png)

Figure 6.4 DM Color Mode under Open

Now 018um_PDK is in the above ﬁgure, because one cell in it is opened in read only mode. However MA, ma_tb, layout is in red because this design is opened in write mode. Through this way, you can watch relations between libraries and cells. If you open a top cell and show all hierarchy, and if you ﬁnd a cell in this library is black, you can conﬁrm this cell is not be used by top cell. So you can delete this cell from this library.

Note: Color could be in wrong way in some occasions. If you see it, please invoke Windows -> Close & Purge in DM to purge all designs ﬁrst.

- • Sort Name By Numerical Order: speciﬁes sort name by numerical order or ASCII order. Default is on.
- • Use Aether Script Namespace: speciﬁes cdf script command use namespace aecdf. Default is oﬀ.
- • Check Copy Consistency: when this option is turned on, the copy operations will to be checked for consistency. If both of them is inconsistent(ﬁle size or modiﬁcation time), the copy operations will to be terminated and pop-up warning message. Default is oﬀ.
- • Switch MX And MY Shortcut In Commands: when this option is turned on, if you execute the command in edit or create, the way of using shortcut key between Mirror X and Mirror Y will be exchanged. Default is oﬀ.
- • Display Origin As X/Y In Property: when this option is turned on, origin will display as coordinates in property, otherwise it is displayed as point. Default is oﬀ.
- • Netlist Remove Device: when this option is turned on, lxRemoveDevice will not added into netlist. Default is oﬀ.
- • Snap Mode: speciﬁes snap mode for Create and Edit commands.


- – Create: speciﬁes the snap mode for Create commands, for example, Create -> Polygon.

∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. ∗ XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. ∗ YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.

- – Edit: speciﬁes the snap mode for Edit commands, for example, Move.


∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. ∗ XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. ∗ YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.

- • Font: speciﬁes the font Aether used. You can use to select your font.

![image 324](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile324.png)

- • Text Editor: speciﬁes the text editor Aether used. Aether use Vim as default editor. You can set your own editor. It is used when you open an ASCII viewer, for example, Verilog view.
- • Text Editor For Read-Only: speciﬁes the text editor Aether used. Aether uses vim as default editor. You can set your own editor. It is used when you open an ASCII viewer, for example, Verilog view. If the speciﬁed view you have write access permission, Aether will use it to open view.
- • Window Title Format: implements customization of the design window. You can set your own editor. The default content in the input box is: [%l/%c/%v %m %d %x].


- – %l: speciﬁes the lib name.
- – %c: speciﬁes the cell name.
- – %v: speciﬁes the view name.
- – %m: speciﬁes the access mode, for example: Editing, Reading.
- – %d: speciﬁes the display depth.
- – %x: if you open schematic or layout through conﬁg, it will bring a conﬁg message.
- – %a: this is used to control the position of tool names displayed in the title.


![image 325](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile325.png)

###### Figure 6.5 Title without %a

![image 326](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile326.png)

###### Figure 6.6 Title with %a

![image 327](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile327.png)

- Figure 6.7 Title with %x


- • HTML Viewer: speciﬁes the HTML viewer you are used to open manual. Aether provides manual in HTML format and use this viewer to open HTML ﬁle.


- – Default: default viewer, Aether set Firefox as default viewer.
- – Speciﬁed: speciﬁes your own viewer.


Symbol: symbol settings for Aether , these will inﬂuence on Import Verilog and Generate Symbol View functions.

![image 328](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile328.png)

Figure 6.8 Symbol In Settings Form

- • Pin Spacing: speciﬁes the spacing setting for pins, which is the positive multiple of Minor Spacing. The value range is [1,30000], default is 2.


- • Pin Wire Length: speciﬁes the length for pin wires, which is the positive multiple of Minor Spacing. The value range is [1,30000], default is 4.
- • Pin Shape: speciﬁes the shape for pins, including Block, Square and Round, default is Square.

![image 329](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile329.png)

Figure 6.9 Pin Shape

- • Origin: speciﬁes original point of pin name. including TopLeft, CenterLeft and BottomLeft, default is TopLeft.
- • Label: selects label types. Now Aether provides the following three options. Default is {pinName}.

- – {pinName}
- – {instanceName}
- – {cellName}


- • Font Height: speciﬁes the height of label. Default value is 0.0625.
- • Font Style: speciﬁes font. Default value is stick. Aether supports the following fonts:


- – euroStyle
- – gothic
- – math
- – roman
- – script
- – stick
- – ﬁxed
- – swedish


- – milSpec


![image 330](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile330.png)

Figure 6.10 Font

Verilog: compile verilog settings for Aether , these will inﬂuence on Import Verilog, Compile Verilog(A) View, Generate Netlist View, Export Netlist and Generate Symbol View functions.

Version: settings for version control. Only shows, when version-control is set in aether.rc.

# Part II Schematic Editor

# Chapter 8Introduction

Aether -SE is a full-function schematic and symbol editor. This tool supports many advanced functions such as real-time ERC run, inherited connection, etc. In addition, Aether -SE supports import and export standard formats like EDIF, CDL, HSPICE, and Spectre.

## 8.1 Schematic Editor Window

The following is Aether Schematic Editor Window.

![image 379](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile379.png)

###### Figure 8.1 Schematic Editor Window

8.2. Starting Schematic Editor Window

- 1. Command Menu

Aether supports tear-oﬀ menu mode. If you want to use one or more commands of a menu frequently, you can click LMB on the dashed line, the menu will change to a menu window. Click LMB on the menu window, you can select command directly.

![image 380](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile380.png)

Figure 8.2 Command Menu in Schematic Editor

- 2. Icon Menu


The Icon Menu locates at the top of the working area. It includes frequently used commands. Click LMB on the Icon Menu, you can execute the command directly.

Besides, you can change the location of icon menu and modify the frequently used commands by yourself in Toolbar.

## 8.2 Starting Schematic Editor Window

Click schematic view from Aether Design Manager to start the Aether -SE.

## 8.3 Using Command

1. Mouse Button Commands

• Click Left Mouse Button (LMB)

- – Select an object.
- – With press Shift key to multi-select objects.
- – Create an object.


Aether Reference Manual, 2025.09 209

• Click Right Mouse Button (RMB)

- – While adding an instance, click RMB to activate Rotate command.
- – While adding a wire, click RMB to change Draw Mode.
- – If any command is not active, click RMB to wake up the last com-


mand.

2. Cancel Commands

- • Press Esc key to cancel current active command.
- • Turn on Modal Commands option, new command cancels previous command automatically.

Library: chooses your library. Cell: chooses your cell. View: chooses the view. Filter: speciﬁes a ﬁlter for library/cell/view, default is *. Application: the application is used to determine the open editor.

- • Open With: speciﬁes the editor version to open view.
- • Open For: opens the design with edit or read mode. The default value is Edit.

- – Edit: opens the design with edit mode.
- – Read: opens the design with read mode.


- • Open In: speciﬁes the window to open the design in. The default value is New Window.


- – New Tab: opens the design in new tab.
- – Current Tab: opens the design in current tab.
- – New Window: opens the design in new window.


About Recovery: if autosave cell view exists, when opening this cell view, Aether will let you choose which kind of cell view to open.

![image 391](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile391.png)

Figure 9.2 Open Autosave

If you click Yes, then Aether will open the autosave data, if you click No, Aether will open the original data. Regardless of the cell view type opened, autosave data will remain on disk until Save or Save A Copy to itself is executed.

In EIP and Descend command, Aether will not reopen the already opened design. If autosave data has already been opened, Aether will open the autosave data for

EIP or Descend. If original data has already been opened, Aether will open the original data for EIP or Descend.

If user has already opened the autosave data, then execute Discard Edits, Aether will close the autosave data and open the original data for users, but the autosave data will not be removed from disk.

Alternatively you can open your design from the Design Manager.

9.11. Design Property

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

Property: shows system or user properties.

- • System: shows system properties. Default is oﬀ. Most of system properties cannot be modiﬁed.
- • User: shows user properties. Default is on. User properties can be modiﬁed when the design is writable.


System: lists the system properties.

- • Library Name: the library name of current design.
- • Cell Name: the cell name of current design.
- • View Name: the view name of current design.
- • BBox: the boundary of current design.
- • View Type: the view type of current design.
- • Mode: the read/write permissions of current design.


- • Creation Time: the creation time of current design.
- • Last Save Time: the last save time of current design.
- • InstName Preﬁx: the preﬁx of the instance’s name, you can set as you need.


User: lists the user properties

- • Property: the user property name.
- • Value: the user property value.
- • Add: adds a user property. If you click this button, the form pops up as shown in Figure 9.17 .


![image 416](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile416.png)

Figure 9.17 Add Property

- – Name: speciﬁes a user property name. There are four reserved property names.

∗ lvsIgnore: ignores a design cell in a hierarchy during the lvs netlisting. The SUBCKT contents of the cell will be empty in the resulting netlist.

∗ nlAction: speciﬁes the behavior for a netlister (spice/cdl) with respect to the cell. The only type recognized is ignoring (case sensitive).

∗ schType: speciﬁes a type for schematic, for example, patchcord, noConn, supply, border, parasitic. You can deﬁne your own type and use it. The purpose of this property is pure informative - it is visible in Edit -> Properties.

∗ netSet: speciﬁes a net set, now Aether doesn’t use it. You can also add your own properties.

- – Type: speciﬁes a user property type. There are ﬁve property types: String, Int, Float, Boolean, Time.
- – Value: speciﬁes a user property value. How to specify a value depends on the property type. For example, when type is Time, valid value is Mar 19 18:34:48 2012.


9.12. Pin Order

- – Minimum: speciﬁes a minimum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float and Time.
- – Maximum: speciﬁes a maximum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float and Time.
- – Choices: lists choices for the value of a user property. It is valid for String.


- • Modify: modiﬁes a selected user property.

![image 417](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile417.png)

Menu: File -> Print ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

Scope: speciﬁes a print scope.

- • Cellview: prints the current design.


- • Area: speciﬁes an area in the current design for printing.
- • Library: prints all designs in the current library. You can set View Name List , but cannot set Skip External Libraries , Skip Libraries , Skip Cells Below and Print To Multi-pages .
- • Hierarchy: prints all designs in the hierarchy of a current design. When it is enabled, you can set Skip External Libraries , Skip Libraries , and Skip Cells Below , but cannot set View Name List and Print To Multipages .


Skip External Libraries: skips designs in external libraries. It only can be set when you select Hierarchy .

View Name List: speciﬁes which view to print when you select Library . Skip Library: speciﬁes which library not to print when you select Hierarchy

. Skip Cells Below: speciﬁes which cell not to print when you select Hierarchy

.

Paper Size: speciﬁes a paper size. Aether supports A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, USLegal, USLedger, USLP, USVT, B0, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, USLetter. Default is A4.

Font: speciﬁes a font. Aether supports Times Roman, Times Bold, Times Italic, Times BoldItalic, Helvetica, Helvetica Oblique, Helvetica Bold, Helvetica Bold Oblique, Courier, Courier Oblique, Courier Bold, Courier Bold Oblique. Default is Times Roman.

||Note: Font is used in Print Title only.|
|---|
|
|---|


Orientation: speciﬁes the orientation of a paper.

- • Auto: automatic selection of Portrait or Landscape orientation according to the size of a design.
- • Portrait: prints in a portrait orientation.
- • Landscape: prints in a landscape orientation.


Color: speciﬁes a color mode for print.

- • Mono: prints in black and white colors.
- • Poly: prints in color. • Gray: prints in gray.


Print To: speciﬁes the output format to print.

- • Ps File: prints to ps ﬁle.
- • Pdf File: prints to a pdf ﬁle. If there is no ps2pdf binary in your OS, Aether will fail to print in this mode.
- • Printer: submits to a printer directly.


File Name: speciﬁes a ﬁle name to print. It is on when Print To Ps File or Print To Pdf File is selected.

Print Command: speciﬁes a print command when submitting to a printer. Default is lp.

Display Resource: speciﬁes a display resource ﬁle that deﬁnes how to print a line, color and ﬁll.

Print Title: prints a title. Default is on. No Tiny Pin: ignores a tiny pin. Default is oﬀ. Print To Multi-pages: splits design to print in multi-pages.

- • Rows: speciﬁes rows of a split.
- • Columns: speciﬁes columns of a split.

## 9.18 Open Recently

Open Recently is used to record the design you have recently opened. The Open Recently is shown in Figure 9.34 .

9.18. Open Recently

![image 445](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile445.png)

Figure 9.34 Open Recently

.

##### Add To Recently:

- 1. Add a currently open design at the position 1 of Open Recently list.
- 2. Add all viewtypes supported by Aether , including netlist. However, it supports up to 10 records, and the excess will be discarded.
- 3. The list of Open Recently is displayed in the File menu and expanded in a tiled manner.
- 4. For the design opened by binding, record in the default opening order.
- 5. Design won’t be added to Open Recently list, if the design fails to open or is unsupported by Aether .


##### Record Edit Mode:

- 1. Open Recently will record the read or write edit mode when opening for the ﬁrst time and exiting design.
- 2. If you use Make Editable to change a readonly design to editable, and open the design again from the Open Recently list without closing the current design, the modiﬁed status will not take eﬀect. It can only take eﬀect after closing design.


##### From Open Recently:

- 1. The design will be opened in the recently edit mode and it will be updated to the position 1 of Open Recently list. The window which is opened from Open Recently list will be raised to the top.
- 2. Design will be removed from Open Recently list, when the design fails to open.

## 10.13 Background

Menu: View -> Background ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to display design contents as a background. The form is shown in Figure 10.15 .

Figure 10.15 Background

Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the design to be set as a background. You can select the design by Browse button. Any of the Schematic, Symbol or Layout view can be selected. The default is empty.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the design. View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the design. X: speciﬁes origin X coordinate. The default value is 0. Y: speciﬁes origin Y coordinate. The default value is 0.

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 488](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile488.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.


- • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.

![image 489](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile489.png)

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for MX.

![image 490](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile490.png)

- • MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


Display: display the design as the background. The default value is on. Dilute: display the design as diluted which makes the display diﬀerent from the editing design. The default value is oﬀ. Unset: unset the background and reset all options to default.

Menu: View -> View List ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

If there are more than two symbols for a cell, it will list all available symbol view names. You can quickly switch view by using this View List.

# Chapter 11Create

## 11.1 Instance

Menu: Create -> Instance ToolBar: BindKey: I Tcl Command: None

![image 492](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile492.png)

This command is used to create instance. An instance is a reference to a design, representing the inclusion of that design as a part of the contents of a diﬀerent design. The referenced design is the master of the instance. Designer can design a hierarchy circuit by Create Instance.

![image 493](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile493.png)

Figure 11.1 Create Instance

##### Library Name: speciﬁes library. Cell Name: speciﬁes cell. View Name: speciﬁes view.

253

Instance Name: speciﬁes instance name. The instance name must be unique among all instances.

- • Preﬁx of instance Name is referenced from:

- – system property named InstName Preﬁx in Design Property.
- – Device Type in Device Deﬁne.
- – Default preﬁx is I_ followed by an arbitrary integer.


- • Instance names could be separated by space, for example, I0 I1 I2.
- • I<0> and I<0:10> are valid.


Magnify: speciﬁes instance magnify.

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 494](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile494.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.

![image 495](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile495.png)

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for MX.

![image 496](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile496.png)

- • MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


At Origin: speciﬁes the origin of instance. Where the origin of the instance’s master is located relative to the coordinate system of the parent design in which the instance is placed. By this option, instance’s origin coincides with origin of master of instance. It is mutual exclusive with Justiﬁcation.

Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes how to locate the original point of object. Aether calculates the original point based on the Justiﬁcation and the object’s bounding box.

- • LeftBottom
- • CenterBottom
- • RightBottom


- • LeftCenter
- • CenterCenter
- • RightCenter
- • LeftTop
- • CenterTop
- • RightTop


Now we use labels to explain it. Please notice the little cross near the labels.

![image 497](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile497.png)

Figure 11.2 Justiﬁcation Example

Array: speciﬁes array of instances.

- • Rows: speciﬁes row number of array instance. Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- • Cols: speciﬁes column number of array instance. Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- • Snap: speciﬁes snap mode of array instance in Manual.


- – AnyAngle: places array instance at any angle.
- – Diagonal: places array instance at X/Y direction and 45-degree direction.
- – Orthogonal: places array instance at X/Y direction only.


Parameters: speciﬁes parameters of instance. If master is a parametrized cell, you should specify its parameters when creating instance of it. Parameters are diﬀerent when you create diﬀerent instance.

• Reset All: resets all parameters to default value.

Menu: Create -> Cascade Circuit ToolBar:

![image 508](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile508.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to create cascade circuit. One cascade instance is a reference to a cascade circuit, representing the array instance circuit. The referenced design is the master of each element cell of the cascade circuit.There is not array instance in cascade circuit. It’s a abstract array instance for accelerating the tool.

The circuit created by this command should be regular. For example, the input of next circuit is the output of previous. The topological graph is:

![image 510](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile510.png)

Library Name: speciﬁes the master library name of element in cascade circuit.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the master cell name of element in cascade circuit. View Name: speciﬁes the master view name of element in cascade circuit. Pin Connection: speciﬁes pins conneciton between element instances in cascade circuit.

- • Rows: speciﬁes row number of cascade circuit instance.Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- • Cols: speciﬁes column number of cascade circuit instance.Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- • Load X-panel: speciﬁes a .csv ﬁle by the Browse button from the directory. You can deﬁne cascade circuit arrays like the following table.


![image 511](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile511.png)

- • Direction: speciﬁes connection directions of pins.Default value depends on pins position in master symbol view. If the pins is horizontal in symbol view, the default direction is H and the other is V. The value of this option is H, V or G.

- – H: means this pin will be connected in horizontal direction.
- – V: means this pin will be connected in vertical direction.
- – G: means the pins in all symbols are connected to the same net at


the top schematic.

## 11.3 Loop Circuit

Menu: Create -> Loop Circuit ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 518](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile518.png)

This command is used to help you to create complex logical connections by special block-loop circuit, which is like as a black box, but the logic net will be extended when export netlist,

![image 519](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile519.png)

Figure 11.22 Create Loop Circuit Form

Library Name: speciﬁes the master library name of element in loop circuit. Cell Name: speciﬁes the master cell name of element in loop circuit. View Name: speciﬁes the master view name of element in loop circuit. Net Setting: speciﬁes Pin/Net connection by following table.

- • Pin Name: speciﬁes names of pins. Those pins are from the master design and cannot be edited.
- • Net Name: speciﬁes net name of each pin. It must have valid net name value. The conditional strings to the input text by following lable are supported.


Table 11.1 Input Text String Formats

|The Allowed Input Characters<br><br>|Explanation|
|---|---|
|Letter<br><br>|Allow to input any letters.|
|Number|Allow to input any number.|
|+, -, *, /, ()<br><br>|Only allow put them in the < > ; The division operation (/) will take the whole by rounded.|
|!<br><br>|Only allow to append to the end of the string.|
|< ><br><br>|Only one can exist in per input box, and support arithmetic expressions in < > .|


Loop Setting: speciﬁes the looping variable in loop circuit. If there are two or more items, the sequence of operation is from top to bottom.

- • Name: speciﬁes the name of looping variable.
- • From: speciﬁes the start value, the value must be a non-negative integer.
- • To: speciﬁes the end value, the value must be a non-negative integer.
- • : adds a new line into Loop Setting table.

![image 521](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile521.png)

![image 522](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile522.png)

- • : moves the selected line up.

![image 523](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile523.png)

- • : moves the selected line down.

## 11.4 Wire

Menu: Create -> Wire ToolBar: BindKey: W

![image 532](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile532.png)

Tcl Command: None This command is used to create wire in current design.

![image 533](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile533.png)

Figure 11.29 Create Wire

Draw Mode: speciﬁes how to create wire. Default value is Route.

- • AnyAngle: draw a straight line between two points at following angle:

– Lock Angle: speciﬁes more modes in AnyAngle. ∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.

- • XFirst: draw wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis.
- • YFirst: draw wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- • L45: draw wire along X-axis or Y-axis ﬁrst, then along 45-degrees direction.
- • 45L: draw wire along 45-degrees direction, then along X-axis or Y-axis.
- • Route: route wire between 2 points. Aether will create wire by embedded route algorithm.


Fly Line: speciﬁes to generate ﬂy line. Fly line is a special line. Aether will draw a dotted line between two points at any angle as wire.

Wire Snapping: if turn it on, the nearest node will be marked by diamond cartoon.

If you hold Shift or Ctrl, Aether will show wire cartoon which connect to node. If you press F5 Aether will create wire connect to node which has diamond cartoon automatically. You can hold Shift/Ctrl and click LMB too.

Color: speciﬁes wire color, default color is cadeBlue. Aether supplies 33 kinds of color. This option is disable when Fly Line is checked.

Line Style: speciﬁes line style of wire, default style is solid. Aether supplies 7 kinds of style.This option is disable when Fly Line is checked.

Narrow: speciﬁes to create narrow wire. It is default value.

11.5. Wide Wire

Wide: speciﬁes to create wide wire.

• Width: speciﬁes wire width. Default value is 0.0625.

Note: If you turn on the Wide, its behavior is the same as Create Wide Wire. But the Style is disabled in wide wire mode.

Example 11.6 The example shows how to create wire with diﬀerent color and style.

1. Activate Create -> Wire, change Color and Style to create wire. As following:

![image 534](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile534.png)

Figure 11.30 Wires in Schematic

Draw Mode: speciﬁes how to create wire. Default value is Route.

- • XFirst: draw wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis.
- • YFirst: draw wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- • L45: draw wire along X-axis or Y-axis ﬁrst, then along 45-degrees direction.
- • 45L: draw wire along 45-degrees direction, then along X-axis or Y-axis.

Fly Line: speciﬁes to generate ﬂy line. Fly line is a special line. Aether will draw a dotted line between two points at any angle as wire.

## 11.6 Wire Name

Menu: Create -> Wire Name ToolBar: BindKey: L Tcl Command: None

![image 537](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile537.png)

This command is used to assign a name to a wire.

![image 538](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile538.png)

Figure 11.32 Create Wire Name

Wire Names: speciﬁes wire names. It can be single or bus names. The conditional strings to the input text by following table are supported.

Table 11.2 Input Text String Formats

|Input Text String|Output in the Schematic|
|---|---|
|D< 1:3 ><br><br>|D< 1 > D< 2 > D< 3 >|
|D< 1,3,5 >|D< 1 > D< 3 > D< 5 >|
|D< 1:5:2 ><br><br>|D< 1 > D< 3 > D< 5 >|
|< *2 > A,B<br><br>|A A B|
|< *2 > (A,B),C<br><br>|A B A B C|
|< *2 > (A,< *2 > (C,D),B<br><br>|A C D C D A C D C D B|
|A< 0:2*2 ><br><br>|A< 0 > A< 0 > A< 1 > A< 1 > A< 2 > A< 2 >|
|A< (0:2)*2 >|A< 0 > A< 1 > A< 2 > A< 0 > A< 1 > A< 2 >|


Font Height: speciﬁes height of wire names. Default value is 0.0625. Font: speciﬁes font. Default value is stick. Aether supports the following fonts:

- • euroStyle


- • gothic
- • math
- • roman
- • script
- • stick
- • ﬁxed
- • swedish
- • milSpec


![image 539](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile539.png)

Figure 11.33 Font

Oﬀset: speciﬁes oﬀset between mouse cursor and wire name. Its’ range is from -8 to 32, default is 6.

Placement: speciﬁes how to place wire name.

- • Single: places wire names one by one through LMB.
- • Multiple: places wire names one time through one line. Bus Expansion: switch on the parser for bus names.


Overbar: add over line on the wire name. Aether implements over line by underscore(_). For example, when you specify wire name as a_bc_d, the eﬀect is as follows:

![image 540](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile540.png)

![image 541](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile541.png)

(a) Turn Oﬀ (b) Turn On

Figure 11.34 Overbar for Create Wire Name

Display Bundles Vertically: displays bundles vertically or not. For example, when you specify wire name as a,bc,d, the eﬀect is as follows:

![image 542](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile542.png)

![image 543](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile543.png)

(a) Turn Oﬀ (b) Turn On

Figure 11.35 Display Bundles Vertically for Create Wire Name

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 544](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile544.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.

![image 545](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile545.png)

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for MX.


![image 546](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile546.png)

- • MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes how to locate the original point of object. Aether calculates the original point based on the Justiﬁcation and the object’s bounding box.

- • LeftBottom
- • CenterBottom
- • RightBottom
- • LeftCenter
- • CenterCenter
- • RightCenter
- • LeftTop
- • CenterTop
- • RightTop

Figure 11.74 Create Note Shape

Shape: speciﬁes a note shape deﬁnition by selecting one of the following types:

- • Line
- • Rectangle


- • Polygon
- • Circle
- • Ellipse
- • Arc


Default is Line. Line Style: speciﬁes a style of outline by selecting one of the following types:

- • Solid
- • Dashed


![image 609](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile609.png)

Figure 11.75 Line Style

Default is Solid. Draw Mode: speciﬁes how to draw line and polygon. It is valid only Line or Polygon is selected.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis.
- • YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- • L45: draws wire along X-axis or Y-axis ﬁrst, then along 45-degrees direction.
- • 45L: draws wire along 45-degrees direction, then along X-axis or Y-axis.


![image 610](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile610.png)

Figure 11.76 Draw Mode/Method

Note Text: speciﬁes contents of note shape. You can deﬁne it or keep default. Height: speciﬁes the height of note text. Default value is 0.0625. Font: speciﬁes font. Default value is stick. Aether supports the following fonts:

- • euroStyle
- • gothic
- • math
- • roman
- • script
- • stick
- • ﬁxed
- • swedish
- • milSpec

## 11.15 Symbol View

Menu: Create -> Symbol View ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 617](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile617.png)

This command is used to create symbol view from speciﬁed schematic view. The pins’ information in symbol view will be the same as those in schematic view.

![image 618](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile618.png)

Figure 11.83 Create Symbol View Form

From To: speciﬁes name of schematic and symbol view.

- • Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of schematic design.
- • Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of schematic design.
- • From View Name: speciﬁes the view name of schematic design.
- • To View Name: speciﬁes the view name of symbol design.
- • Modify / Replace: speciﬁes to modify or replace the existing view, it is available only when the target view exists.


– Modify: modiﬁes the existing symbol view. – Replace: replaces the existing symbol view.

Pin Options: speciﬁes how to place pins in symbol view.

- • Left Pins: speciﬁes pin names placed on the left side. Default are input pins.
- • Right Pins: speciﬁes pin names placed on the right side. Default are output pins.
- • Top Pins: speciﬁes pin names placed on the top side.
- • Bottom Pins: speciﬁes pin names placed on the bottom side.
- • : moves the selected pin from Pin List to Left/Right/Top/Bottom Pins. Once pin has been moved by this way, it will be deleted from its original position automatically.

![image 619](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile619.png)

- • Pin List: lists all pins of schematic, if one pin does not exist in Left/Right/Top/Bottom Pins, this pin will display in red color in Pin List. It allows to multiple select in this list.
- • Filter Duplicate Pins: speciﬁes whether to ﬁlter duplicate pins. This option is checked by default mode.
- • Exclude Inherited Connection Pins: speciﬁes how to do with inherited connection pins.


- – None: not exclude any inherited pins.
- – All: exclude all inherited pins.
- – Pins: speciﬁes the excluded inherited pins.


Symbol Options: speciﬁes the pin spacing and shape.

![image 620](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile620.png)

Figure 11.84 Symbol Options

- • Reverse Pin Order: reverses pin order in symbol view compared with schematic view.
- • Pin Spacing: speciﬁes the space between the adjacent pin names. Default is 2*Minor_Spacing.
- • Pin Wire Length: speciﬁes the length of wire which connect to pin. Default is 4*Minor_Spacing.
- • Pin Shape: speciﬁes what pin looks like. Default is Square.

- – Block
- – Square – Round


![image 621](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile621.png)

Figure 11.85 Pin Shape

- • Origin: speciﬁes original point of pin name. Default is TopLeft.


- – TopLeft
- – CenterLeft
- – BottomLeft


Label Options: speciﬁes advanced options for label.

![image 622](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile622.png)

Figure 11.86 Label Options

• Label: selects label types. Now Aether provides the three options:

- – {pinName}
- – {instanceName}
- – {cellName}


- • Font Height: speciﬁes the height of label. Default value is 0.0625.
- • Font Style: speciﬁes font. Default value is stick. Aether supports the following fonts:


- – euroStyle
- – gothic
- – math
- – roman
- – script
- – stick
- – ﬁxed
- – swedish
- – milSpec


![image 623](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile623.png)

Figure 11.87 Font

## 11.17 Create Voltage Vmax/Vmin

Menu: Create -> Create Voltage Vmax/Vmin ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 650](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile650.png)

This command is used to create max/min voltage of net in the schematic.

![image 651](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile651.png)

Figure 11.113 Create Voltage Vmax/Vmin

Update: if you click it, the dataset information in the form will be refreshed via the constraint ﬁle.

Mode: speciﬁes the mode of creating max/min voltage of net by constraint ﬁle, default is Replace.

- • Replace: every max/min voltage of the net that coexists in the schematic and constraint ﬁle will be recreated by using the max/min voltage in the constraint ﬁle.
- • Update: update the max/min voltage of net in the schematic by using the max/min voltage in the constraint ﬁle.
- • Override Manual Voltage Inputs: speciﬁes whether to override manual voltage inputs, default is false. If it is checked, the manually written max/min voltage will be overridden. In addition, if the manually written maxvoltage and minvoltage are both 0, the voltage value will not be considered as a manually written value.


Exclude Voltage: speciﬁes whether to exclude the voltage, default is false.

- • if the condition is <, exclude the voltage smaller than the conditional value.


- • if the condition is >, exclude the voltage larger than the conditional value.


Example 11.23 The example shows how to create max/min voltage in the schematic.

1. Activate the command Create -> Create Voltage Vmax/Vmin, set parameters like this.

![image 652](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile652.png)

Figure 11.114 Parameter for Create Voltage Vmax/Vmin

2. Click OK, the max/min voltage of net in the schematic will be created.

## 12.3 Copy

Menu: Edit -> Copy ToolBar: BindKey: C Tcl Command: None

This command generates duplicate(s) of the selected object(s). When you activate Copy and press F3, the form appears.

![image 659](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile659.png)

Figure 12.4 Copy Form

Snap Mode: speciﬁes the angles along which you can move objects. • Orthogonal: moves objects along X-axis or Y-axis direction.

- • Diagonal: moves objects along 45-degrees direction.
- • AnyAngle: moves objects along any angle.


![image 660](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile660.png)

Figure 12.5 Snap Mode

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 661](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile661.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.


![image 662](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile662.png)

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for MX.

![image 663](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile663.png)

- • MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


Rows and Columns: deﬁnes the size of an array which you can copy objects to. Default value is 1. For example, the following ﬁgure shows copying an instance to an array of 3x3.

## 12.15 Find/Replace

Menu: Edit -> Find/Replace ToolBar: BindKey: F2 Tcl Command: None

![image 750](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile750.png)

This command is used to search objects in designs and then replace them.

![image 751](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile751.png)

Figure 12.52 Find/Replace Form

Search For: sets the searching type. In: sets the searching scope. If the Search By is set to Cell, the searching scopes are as follows:

- • Current Cellview: searches in the editing cellview.
- • Current To Bottom: searches from the current level to the bottom level in the cellview.
- • Top to Current: searches from top level to the current level in the cellview.


- • Top to Bottom: searches from top level to the bottom level in the cellview.
- • Current Library: searches in the cellviews in current library.


If the Search By is set to Selected, the search scopes are just Current Cellview and Current To Bottom. Add Criteria: adds a line of ﬁelds in the form to allow users to search more speciﬁcally.

![image 752](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile752.png)

Figure 12.53 Criteria of Find/Replace Form

Cyclic Field: sets option of searching for speciﬁc attributes, instances, libraries, view names, or properties for this type of object as Figure 12.54. The cyclic ﬁeld selections can be changed to reﬂect the attributes of the type of object which you select in the Search For ﬁeld. For more information, please see objects criteria table below.
