Condition Cyclic Field: sets option of searching for character strings or numerals that are exactly matched (==) or are not matched (!=); to get matches that contain a string, a leading and/or trailing asterisk must be used. The symbols <, <=, >, >= are used where applicable. EXIST and !EXIST

locate or exclude discrete blocks of information anywhere in the string.

Value Field: sets the value of the attribute or property to be used in the search. In the text ﬁeld, you can specify the search string using the wild card characters.

Delete: deletes this line of criteria from the form.

![image 753](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile753.png)

Figure 12.54 Criteria of Find/Replace Form

Replace With: replaces the objects’ matching results with a new object, attribute value, or property value. The cyclic ﬁeld contains the frequently used properties. In the text ﬁeld, you can specify the value of the property with which you want to replace the original value.

• Add Criteria: adds a line of ﬁelds in the form to allow users to replace more speciﬁcally.

Search: sets more operations for searching conditions.

- • Match Method: sets the way of matching when there are multiple matching criteria.

– All Conditions: all criteria must be met when searching objects.

This is the default value of Match Method.

– Any Condition: at least one of the criteria must be met when

searching objects.

- • Search By: sets the search scope condition.


- – Cell: search in the hole bbox of cell.
- – Selected: search within the selected objects.


- • Zoom To: zooms to the centers the cellview around the current object in the search group when you click Find, Previous, or Next.
- • Case Sensitive: searches object with considering case sensitivity.
- • Wildcard Match: searches and ﬁnds object with wild card. Check it,


*, ?, . and [] are supported by Find, * and {} are supported by Replace and Replace All, else, regular expressions are supported. It is checked in AetherAdv by default. This option is valid in Advance Aether.

- Table 12.2 Wildcard Illustrations

|Wildcard<br><br>|Parse Expression|
|---|---|


|*<br><br>|Matches any sequence of zero or more characters when used by Find. Indicates the content of nth wild card character if current * is the nth * in replacing string when used by Replace or Replace All.|
|---|---|
|?|Matches any single character. Only used by Find.|
|.<br><br>|Matches any single character. Only used by Find.|
|[A-Z]|The 26 English letters and the range of letter is from A to Z. Only used by Find.|
|[0-9]|The 10 digits and the range of digit is from 0 to 9. Only used by Find.|
|[abc]<br><br>|The character is one of a, b or c. Only used by Find.|
|{n}|Indicates the content of nth wild card character. Only used by Replace or Replace All.|


- Table 12.3 Regular Expression


|Regular Expression<br><br>|Parse Expression|
|---|---|


|[A-Z]<br><br>|The 26 English letters and the range of letter is from A to Z.|
|---|---|
|A{1,3}<br><br>|The number of characters A within [1,3].|
|[0-9]{1,2}<br><br>|The range of number is from 0 to 99.|
|\d|The range of number is from 0 to 9.|
|A?<br><br>|The range of character is A{0,1}, or character A.|
|\d?<br><br>|The range of number is from 0 to 9.|
|A|B|C<br><br>|Character A or B or C.|


|[^A]<br><br>|All single character or number except the character A.|
|---|---|
|A+<br><br>|The letter A combination of the string, such as: A, AA, AAA...|
|A{n}|Multiple character A.|
|A{n,}|The number range of continuous character A is equal or greater than n.|
|A{n,m}<br><br>|The number range of continuous character A is equal or greater than n and is equal or less than m.|


- • Current Figure: shows which object in the search group is highlighted as you click Previous or Next.
- • Figure Count: after clicking Find, show the number of objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Auto Highlight Next After Replacing: after clicking Replace, auto highlight next object.
- • Save Changes: after clicking Replace All, auto save the objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Preview Replace(No Edits): after clicking Replace or Replace All, preview the current object(s) replacement information on the design manager form.


Search Results: sets more operations for ﬁnding results.

- • Add Select: selects the current object in the search group.
- • Select All: selects all objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Replace: edits or replaces the current object with the settings shown in the Replace ﬁeld.
- • Replace All: replaces all objects found by Find/Replace with the settings shown in the Replace ﬁeld.


Find: searches for objects matching the settings in the Find/Replace form. Previous: highlights the previous object in the search group. Next: highlights the next object in the search group. Cancel: closes the Find/Replace form.

## 12.16 Property

Menu: Edit -> Property ToolBar: BindKey: Q Tcl Command: None

![image 767](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile767.png)

This command is used to edit the attributes of objects in the design.

![image 768](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile768.png)

Figure 12.63 Property Form

Apply To: ﬁlters objects by cell or by type. Common: edits properties common to a group of selected objects. Attribute: represents the characteristics of the object.

![image 769](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile769.png)

Figure 12.64 Schematic Property Form - Instance

- • Instance Attributes: sees the ﬁgure Figure 12.64.


- – Reset Instance Labels Display: resets the display and position of all instance labels to their deﬁnition in the symbol view.
- – Library Name: edits the library name of the master cell for this instance.
- – Cell Name: edits the cell name of the master cell for this instance.
- – View Name: edits the view name of the master cell for this instance.
- – Instance Name: edits the instance name of this instance.
- – Display: displays the corresponding content in schematic. ∗ Oﬀ: disables the display. ∗ Value: displays the value only. ∗ Name: displays the name only. ∗ Both: displays as “name = value” style.
- – Rotate: sets whether the instance is rotated or mirrored.
- – Origin: displays the X and Y coordinates of the origin of the instance. this is displayed as point in default, if Display Origin As X/Y In Property is turned on in DM-> Option-> Settings, this will display as coordinates.


- – Pins: displays the pins and connections of instance. ∗ Pin Direction: displays the direction of pins. ∗ Pin Name: displays the name of pins. ∗ Net Name: displays the net name connected to pins.


![image 770](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile770.png)

Figure 12.65 Schematic Property Form - Wire

- • Wire Attributes: sees the ﬁgure Figure 12.65.


- – Name: sets the name of net which includes the wire.

- – Property Name: speciﬁes the name of the property that can be used to override the default global signal. In other words, the name of the property whose value redeﬁnes the name of the net. The tool evaluating the expression searches for the property that has this name to get the value to inherit for the net.
- – Default Name: speciﬁes the default property name of the global signal or net name. The system uses the default net name - for example vdd!, gnd!, or vss! - when an inherited connection has not been established. The name must be speciﬁed as a global scalar value.
- – Evaluated Name: contains the result of evaluating the net expression for the current descending path of the window.
- – Height: edits the height of the net expression.

- – Font: edits the text style of the net expression.

Property: sets the properties of the object and allow you to add their own properties to an object. see Figure 12.79.

User Property: displays property name. Master Value: displays the master symbol property value. Local Value: edits the local instance property value. Display: speciﬁes whether the system displays the property name and property value in the schematic.

- • Oﬀ: displays neither the name nor the value.
- • Value: displays only the value.
- • Name: displays only the name of the property.
- • Both: displays both the name and the value, separated by an equal sign.


![image 785](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile785.png)

Figure 12.80 Property Form - Add Property

Add: allows you to add a new property. See Figure 12.80.

- • Name: edits property name.

- – leDummy: indicates that the LE design is dummy.
- – lvsIgnore: ignores a design cell in a hierarchy during the lvs netlisting. The SUBCKT contents of the cell will be empty in the resulting netlist.
- – nlAction: speciﬁes the behavior for a netlister (spice/cdl) in respect to the cell. The only type recognized is ignore (case sensitive).
- – schType: speciﬁes a type for schematic, for example, patchcord, noConn, supply, border, parasitic. You can deﬁne your own type and use it. The purpose of this property is pure informative - it is visible in Edit -> Properties.
- – netSet: speciﬁes a net set, now Aether doesn’t use it.
- – nlignore: speciﬁes a type for ignore, for example, Setting up a spectre means that ignore takes eﬀect when the spectre is released.


- • Type: selects property type.
- • Value: speciﬁes property value.
- • Minimum: sets the minimum value of range, enabled for int, ﬂoat, time type.
- • Maximum: sets the maximum value of range, enabled for int, ﬂoat, time type.
- • Choices: sets the option for string type.


![image 786](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile786.png)

Figure 12.81 Property Form - Delete Property

Delete: allows user to delete the selected property. See Figure 12.81.

- • Name List: lists all the property names.
- • Delete All: if check this option, all items will be selected.


Modify: opens the Modify Property form, which lets you change the deﬁnition for any property created with Add.

First: highlights the ﬁrst object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties.

Previous: highlights the previous object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties.

Next: highlights the next object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties.

Last: highlights the last object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties.

Apply: saves the edit and keeps the form opening. OK: saves the edit and closes the form. Cancel: aborts the edit and closes the form.

## 14.10 Navigator

Menu: Hierarchy -> Navigator ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 855](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile855.png)

This command mainly displays the objects of the current design through Navigator form, and provides some quick commands by the right bottom menu of Navigator Tree Nodes.

Navigator Form: Navigator form displays relationships between the hierarchical objects. This is a useful system for manipulating large datasets, distinguishing diﬀerent objects by diﬀerent icons. This form will provide you some functions about search and classiﬁcation, so that you can use more eﬃciently.

![image 856](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile856.png)

- Figure 14.36 Navigator Form


Mode: speciﬁes the type to control the nodes displayed on the Navigator tree, the default model is All.

![image 857](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile857.png)

- Figure 14.37 Modes of schematic


Modes(in schematic): in schematic view, there are six diﬀerent modes, they are All, Instances, Nets, Pins, Nets And Pins, Cells mode.

All: lists all types of objects on Navigator tree. A certain depth of hierarchical relationship will be displayed when expand the Hierarchy Instance type node.

Instances: lists the all instances and ﬂattens instances of current design. At this mode, hierarchy instance and vector Instance are both expandable, the instance included in hierarchy instance and bit member on vector instance will be diplayed, when expand them.

Nets: lists all nets of current design and nets in hierarchy instance will be displayed under the instance node. Every bit member of bundle net and bus net also will be listed.

Pins: lists all pins of current design, and pins in hierarchy instance will be displayed under the instance node. Every bit member of bus pin also will be listed. The name of pin node on the Navigator tree are combined with their net name and pin name.

Nets And Pins: lists all the nets and pins of current design. This mode is composed of Nets and Pins, therefore, it will not be repeated here.

Cells: lists all the Cell of current design, and the corresponding instances will be listed under the Cell node.

Search: uses this wiget to control the displayed of objects in the Navigator tree, and it will temporarily remember previous search records until restart. At the same time, you can choose the query method, including ﬁnd method, matching method and case matching. Setting them through the menu by clicking the bottom on the right.

Path: displays current node path, you can copy the path by right bottom.

Name(Tree): displays the contents corresponding to the current selected mode. Click the rightmost arrow to sort, and the sort rule is setting by Design Manager -> setting -> Sort Name By Numberical Order.

Navigator Right Button Menu: to help you operate the corresponding object directly throught the Navigator Tree Node, The Navigator tree provides some right bottom menu, the speciﬁc menu is decide by the node type you click on. There might be some diﬀerences between diﬀerent versions.

![image 858](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile858.png)

Figure 14.38 Navigator Right Button Menu

Open Instance(Read): this command is available for root node and instance node of both layout and schematic view. It is used to open the corresponding instance of selected node. The open mode is based on Design Manager -> Setting -> Open Design Mode.

Open CellView: this command is available for root node, instance node and cell node, it is used to open corresponding view of selected Cell.

![image 859](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile859.png)

Figure 14.39 Open CellView Form

View Type: lists the existing views in CellView. Open Mode: speciﬁes the open mode. Default is Edit mode. Open In: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in which window. The default value is New Window.

- • New Tab: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in new tab.
- • Current Tab: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in current tab.


- • New Window: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in new window.


Copy Path: puts the contents of the path column of the current node into the clipboard. This command which is available for all node.

Select All: selects all nodes on Navigator tree, which is available for all nodes.

Deselect All: deselects all nodes on Navigator tree, which is available for all nodes.

Expand All: expands all level of current node, which is available for all expandable nodes.

Collapse All: collapses all level of current node, which is available for all expandable nodes.

![image 860](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile860.png)

Figure 14.40 Navigator Instance Menu

Descend Edit: executes Descend Edit command to the corresponding object of current selected node.

Ignore Instances: executes Ignore Instances command to the corresponding object of current selected nodes.

Trace Net(Schematic): executes schematic Trace Net related commands, this command is available to the schematic pin and net node. it has a submenu contains:

![image 861](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile861.png)

Figure 14.41 Navigator Schematic Trace Net Menu

Add Trace Net: executes Trace Net to the corresponding pins or nets of selected nodes.

Remove Trace: executes Remove Trace to the corresponding pins or nets of selected nodes.

Remove All Traces: executes Remove All Traces to clear all traces.

Signal Type: available to all nets, starts with Navigator Options form.

Min/Max Voltage: sets the net’s voltage.

![image 862](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile862.png)

Figure 14.42 Min/Max Voltage Form

Net Name: need to set the net name of voltage. Min Voltage: sets the min voltage for this net. Max Voltage: sets the max voltage for this net.

Options...: available to all nodes, start with Navigator Options form. This form main function is to set the maximum number of diﬀerent type nodes to display. If the object number is more than the number speciﬁed here, a further node will replace all nodes of this type and point out the accurate number. Only positive integers are valid here, and the unit is one thousand.

![image 863](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile863.png)

Figure 14.43 Navigator Options Form

Max Number Of FigGroups(K): controls the maximum number of ﬁggroup nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Instances(K): controls the maximum number of instance nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Nets(K): controls the maximum number of net nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Pins(K): controls the maximum number of pin nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Ungenerated Instances(K): controls the maximum number of ungenerated instance nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Ungenerated Pins(K): controls the maximum number of ungenerated pin nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Menu: Verify -> Check Hierarchy ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

##### Mode:

- • All: perform a check for all designs used in the current hierarhy. Not checked by default.
- • Only Modiﬁed: perform a check for only modiﬁed designs used in the current hierarchy. This is a default setting.


Referenced Libraries: Choose whether to check other libraries which are referenced by the current design library.

- • Check: If this option is selected, you can specify other library names manually or by clicking Select Library to choose libraries you want to check.
- • Do Not Check: This is a default setting.


Save Schematic: choose whether to save a design if there exist check errors.

- • Yes: This is a default setting.

- – Save With Errors: save a design directly even if there exist check errors
- – Save Ask Me With Errors: the tool will ask for your conﬁrmation before saving.


- • No: do not save a design if there exist check errors.


View Name List: set which views are to be checked in the design hierarchy.

## 16.5 Check Rule

Menu: Verify -> Check Rule ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 909](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile909.png)

This command is used to set check rule for function of Check And Save, Check and Check Hierarchy.

Figure 16.7 Check Rule Setup Form

.

Packaged Checks: sets check rule to predeﬁned value according to rule classes, default mode is Normal.

![image 911](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile911.png)

Figure 16.8 Packaged Checks Classes

- • None: when modifying any rules, Packaged Checks will change to this option.
- • Normal: when modifying any rules, click Apply or OK, the set rules will be saved as Normal class.
- • Logical Only: sets all Logical rules as Warning, Physical and Name rules as Ignored.
- • Physical Only: sets all Physical rules as Warning, Logical rules as Ignored.
- • VHDL: sets Name -> VHDL Syntax as Error, other rules keep values intact.
- • Verilog: sets Name -> Verilog HDL Syntax as Error, other rules keep values intact.


##### Logical: sets Logical check rules.

Figure 16.9 Logical Rule Form

##### Physical: sets Physical check rules.

![image 913](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile913.png)

Figure 16.10 Physical Rule Form

|Rule Name|Introduction<br><br>|Default Value|
|---|---|---|
|Floating Nets|Check Wires which do not connect to other wires or instance pins, but do not check wires which are connected by name to other wires or instance pins<br><br>|Warning|
|Floating Input Pins<br><br>|Check device input pins, schematic symbol input pins and schematic output pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins|Warning|
|Floating Output Pins<br><br>|Check device output pins, schematic symbol output pins and schematic input pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins<br><br>|Warning|
|Floating I/O Pins|Check device inputoutput pins, schematic symbol inputoutput pins and schematic inputoutput pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins<br><br>|Warning|
|Floating Switch Pins|Check device switch pins and schematic symbol switch pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins|Warning|
|Shorted Output Pins<br><br>|Check device output pins and schematic symbol output pins which are connected to other device output pins or schematic symbol output pins|Warning|
|Plain Globals<br><br>|Check for the non-default globals within in the cell view<br><br>|Ignored|
|Pin Direction Collision<br><br>|Check for any bit terminal’s direction that is inconsistent with the direction of the multi-bit terminal<br><br>|Ignored|
|Conﬂict Global Signals<br><br>|Check pins whose names conﬂict with global signals|Warning|
|Conﬂict Internal/External Nets<br><br>|Check nets which are connected between instance pins, whose names conﬂict with schematic pins|Ignored|


###### Table 16.1 Logical Rule Table

|Rule Name|Introduction<br><br>|Default Value|
|---|---|---|
|Unconnected Wires|Check wire end segment which does not connect to any other pins or wires<br><br>|Ignored|
|Physical Floating Wires<br><br>|Check wire who is a branch of one connected wire, whose end segment which does not connect to any other pins or wires<br><br>|Ignored|
|Solder On CrossOver|Check solder on wire crossovers|Warning|
|Overlapping Instances|Check instances which are overlapped|Warning|
|Percent Overlap Allowed|Instance whose distance between others is less than this value deﬁned here will be considered as overlapping with other instances, this option is enabled when Overlapping Instances is Warning or Error|10|
|Pin Name Maximum Label Oﬀset<br><br>|Check distance between pin name and pin according to the value set in Maximum Oﬀset From Pins|Ignored|
|Maximum Oﬀset From Pin<br><br>|The maximum distance between pin and pin name, this option is enabled when Pin Name Maximum Label Oﬀset is Warning or Error|0.1|
|Maximum Label Oﬀset<br><br>|Check distance between wire name and wire according to the value set in Maximum Oﬀset From Wire<br><br>|Ignored|
|Maximum Oﬀset From Wire<br><br>|The maximum distance between wire and wire name, this option is enabled when Maximum Label Oﬀset is Warning or Error|0.1|


Table 16.2 Physical Rule Table

Name: sets Name check rules.

![image 914](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile914.png)

Figure 16.11 Name Rule Form

##### Cross View: sets Cross View check rules.

![image 915](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile915.png)

Figure 16.12 Cross View Rule Form

|Rule Name<br><br>|Introduction<br><br>|Default Value|
|---|---|---|
|Connection By Name|Check wires or pins whose names are the same as other wires name or pins, but these wires or pins do not connect with each other<br><br>|Ignored|
|Instance/Net Name Collision<br><br>|Check instance name is in conﬂict with net name|Warning|
|Pin/Net Name Collision<br><br>|Check pin name is in conﬂict with net name<br><br>|Error|
|Verilog HDL Syntax<br><br>|Check Verilog HDL syntax for instance and net names|Ignored|
|VHDL Syntax<br><br>|Check VHDL syntax for instance and net names|Ignored|
|Instance Name Syntax<br><br>|Check instance name syntax in schematic according to the contents speciﬁed in Instance Name Expression|Ignored|
|Instance Name Expression|Speciﬁes expressions for checking instance name syntax, this option is enabled when Instance Name Syntax is Warning or Error| |
|Pin Name Syntax<br><br>|Check pin name syntax in schematic according to the contents speciﬁed in Pin Name Expression<br><br>|Ignored|
|Pin Name Expression|Speciﬁes expression for checking pin name syntax, this option is enabled when Pin Name Syntax is Warning or Error| |
|Net Name Syntax<br><br>|Check net name syntax in schematic according to the contents speciﬁed in Net Name Expression<br><br>|Ignored|
|Net Name Expression<br><br>|Speciﬁes expression for checking net name syntax, this option is enabled when Net Name Syntax is Warning or Error| |


###### Table 16.3 Name Rule Table

|Rule Name|Introduction<br><br>|Default Value|
|---|---|---|
|Inconsistent Pin|Check pins in schematic are inconsistent with pins in symbol view<br><br>|Error|
|Inconsistent Inherited Pin<br><br>|Check inherited pins in schematic are inconsistent with pins in symbol view<br><br>|Ignored|
|Inconsistent Pin Order|Check pin order in schematic is inconsistent with pin order in symbol view|Warning|
|Inconsistent Pin Direction|Check pins direction is inconsistent with pins direction in symbol view|Error|
|Match With Verilog Pins<br><br>|Check pins in schematic is inconsistent with pins in verilog view<br><br>|Warning|
|Match Inherited Terminals<br><br>|When the option is enabled, it checks if the inherited terminals are consistent<br><br>|Ignored|
|Match Terminal Net Expressions|When the option is activated, it ensures the consistency of the terminal network expression|Ignored|

Show Ignored: show markers for objects you have marked by Ignore button. Option is selected by default.

Ignore: assign a property ignored to a marker. Restore: remove ignored property from a marker. Restore All: remove ignored property from all markers. Zoom to Markers: allows you to magnify the marker in schematic and show it in the center of window. Default value is 2. Marker Blink: make the marker blink. Marker Width: set a maker outline. Default value is 5. Severity: list ﬁlter by a marker type.

- • None: shortcut to unselect all the types.

- • Warning: display warning markers.
- • Critical Error: display critical error markers.
- • Acknowledged Warning: display acknowledged warning markers.
- • Signed Oﬀ Critical Error: display signed-oﬀ critical error markers.
- • Info: display information markers.
- • Error: display error markers.
- • Annotation: display annotation markers.
- • Signed Oﬀ Error: display signed-oﬀ error markers.

: deletes the ﬁlter by selecting items on the Parasitic Filters panel. : edits one or more ﬁlters parameter values. If this button is checked, Mod-

- • Name: sets name for the ﬁlter, name must be unique.
- • Owner: displays the name of the currently edited constraint view, and this parameter is not allowed to be changed.
- • Enabled: sets the ﬁlter enabled or disabled.


- – true: enables ﬁlter.
- – false: disables ﬁlter.


- • Notes: sets notes for ﬁlter.
- • Type: sets type for ﬁlter.

- – C: sets ﬁlter applied to capacitance.
- – R: sets ﬁlter applied to resistance.
- – L: sets ﬁlter applied to inductance.


- • Subtype: sets ﬁlter applied to coupled, decoupled, or both. Resistance or inductance ﬁlter has no subtype parameter.

- – both: sets ﬁlter applied to both coupled and decoupled capacitance, only one capcacitance ﬁlter which subtype is both can exist for particular design object.
- – coupled: sets ﬁlter applied to coupled, and creates a second ﬁlter on the same design object which subtype is decoupled is allowed.
- – decoupled: sets ﬁlter applied to decoupled, and creates a second ﬁlter on the same design object which subtype is coupled is allowed.


- • Include: sets which parasitics should be included.

- – all: all parasitics should be included.
- – none: none of the parasitics should be included.
- – threshold: all parasitics over the threshold value should be in-


cluded.

- • Threashold: sets the numeric threshold value if threshold is selected for Include.
- • Scale: sets the numeric scale value.

Menu: Window -> Component ToolBar: BindKey: F4 Tcl Command: None

This command is used to show/hide Component window. Component provides a short-cut for symbol.

Note: If you close Component, the LSW in layout editor and None in symbol editor are closed too. If you open it, the other two panels are opened too.

When a library is added to the library list, All symbols that come with Aether or created by a designer will show in the Component panel.

Create the device quickly using the Component panel, auto set lib/cell/view name for create instance form.

# Chapter 23Options

## 23.1 Settings

Menu: Options -> Settings ToolBar: BindKey: O Tcl Command: None

![image 1037](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1037.png)

This command is used to set options for schematic editor and symbol editor. It has Display, Editor and Net.

Display: sets display settings, which decides how to display schematic/symbol view.

505

![image 1038](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1038.png)

###### Figure 23.1 Display in Settings Form

- • Grid: speciﬁes how to draw the grid in schematic/symbol editor.

- – Minimum Resolution: manufacturing grid.
- – Minor Spacing: speciﬁes space between minor grid.
- – Major Step: speciﬁes step between major grid, the space between major grid is multiple of minor spacing and major step.
- – Type: speciﬁes grid type, default is Dot. ∗ None: doesn’t show grid. ∗ Dot: shows grid in dot. ∗ Line: shows grid in line.
- – Snap Cursor to Minor Ratio: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves. Aether deﬁnes snap spacing as multiple of minor spacing if the checkbox is checked, or the snap spacing is equal to 0.00625.
- – Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of grid dot(50 ~255). Default is 80.


- • Window: speciﬁes how to draw schematic/symbol objects in window.


– Axis Type: speciﬁes how to display axis in schematic/symbol view.

Default is None.

∗ Large: displays axis in large mode. ∗ Small: displays axis in small mode. ∗ None: does not display axis.

– Show: speciﬁes whether show schematic/symbol objects. ∗ Default Parameter: shows default parameter of device. ∗ Cross Cursor: shows cross cursor.

![image 1039](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1039.png)

Figure 23.2 Show Cross Cursor

- • Dimming: speciﬁes dimming settings for display.


- – Enable Dimming: speciﬁes that you can change the brightness of objects.
- – Dimming Mode: speciﬁes the mode of dimming. Default is Automatic.

∗ Automatic: dims the objects automatically either when you select an object. The selected objects are not dimmed.

![image 1040](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1040.png)

Figure 23.3 Automatic

∗ Always: all objects are dimmed except selected objects, even if no object is selected.

![image 1041](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1041.png)

Figure 23.4 Always

- – Dimming Intensity: speciﬁes the brightness of dimmed objects. The default value is 50. If set to 0, no objects are dimmed. If set to 100, dimmed objects are not visible.


![image 1042](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1042.png)

![image 1043](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1043.png)

(a) Intensity = 40 (b) Intensity = 80

Figure 23.5 Dimming Intensity

- • Zoom: speciﬁes how to zoom in schematic.

- – Dynamic Zoom: enables dynamic zoom in schematic.
- – Zoom Mode: speciﬁes which zoom mode to use.

∗ Pan To Selected: pans the selected objects to the center of the window.

∗ Zoom To Selected: zooms the corresponding objects in schematic when selected objects are changed in layout.

∗ Zoom To Fit: keeps the schematic always ﬁt in the window.

- – Zoom To: speciﬁes the zoom scale when zoom mode is Zoom To Selected.


- • Others: speciﬁes other settings for display.


- – Display Device: speciﬁes which display device to use. Aether will list display devices declared in display.drf.
- – Ellipse/Donut Segments: speciﬁes segments of ellipse and donut. Default is 32.
- – Shape Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of shapes displayed in SE. Valid is from 0 to 200 in percentage, default is 100.


![image 1044](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1044.png)

![image 1045](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1045.png)

(a) Original Brightness (100) (b) Half Brightness (50)

Figure 23.6 Shape Brightness

• Net Highlighting: speciﬁes whether the schematic editor dynamically highlights the items of the same net.

- – Highlighting Connections By Name: speciﬁes whether show the connections between items of the same net.
- – The Limit Of Net Highlighting Connections: speciﬁes the limit of the net highlighting connections. If the checkbox is checked, and the number of the connections is greater than the limit, do not show the connections, otherwise, show all connections. Default limit is 50.


Editor: speciﬁes the setting for schematic/symbol editor.

![image 1046](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1046.png)

Figure 23.7 Editor in Settings Form

- • Shadow Surrounding Objects In Edit In Place Command: when EIP is applied, the surrounding objects will displayed in special color to distinguish from objects in EIP design.
- • Keep Action: if it is not checked, each action will exit immediately after execution.
- • Repeat Last Action: if you click ";", Aether will re-invoke the last action launched from menu again. For example, if the last action you used is Copy, you are in default action now, and you click ";", Copy is launched again.
- • Direct Move: you can move or stretch object in default action when it switches on. If you are afraid to move object carelessly, you can switch it oﬀ.
- • Keep Selected: if you want to keep selected objects no matter in preselect or post-select mode, please switch it on.
- • Allow Opening Design In Multiple Window: Aether only opens one design in one window in default. If you want view design in multiple windows, you can switch it on.


- • Auto Popup Command Option Form: Aether will not pop up form on most occasions, and you should press F3 to pop it up. But if you want form to pop up automatically, you can switch it on.
- • Auto Add Pin Name: when this option is On, the pin name will be created automatically with the speciﬁed pin. That is, when you place the pin on the wire, the default pin name will be the same as the net name; when you place the pin in blank area, the pin name is a sequence number, for example:inout1, inout2, inout3.... Only the ipin, opin and iopin are supported.
- • Turn Oﬀ Check Rule In Realtime Check: when this option is on, the real-time checking will skip these settings in Check Rule Setup-> Logical.
- • Double Click to: speciﬁes behavior of double click on instance.

– Descend Edit: Aether will descend in a symbol by edit mode when

you double click on instance.

– Descend Read: Aether will descend in a symbol by read mode

when you double click on instance.

– None: does nothing.

- • Auto Backup Interval: speciﬁes time interval for auto backup. Aether provides auto backup feature in order to protect your data. When computer power is oﬀ suddenly, it will keep your last modiﬁed data. Default is 10 minutes.
- • Disable Auto Dimming: when ADV Trace Net and PVE reverse label are executed after checking, dimming eﬀect is automatically turned on. Default is checking.
- • Undo Limit: speciﬁes the upper limit of undo times. Valid is from 0 to 127, default is 50.


Net: speciﬁes how to name net automatically.

![image 1047](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1047.png)

Figure 23.8 Net in Settings Form

23.2. Key Mapping

• Name Rules Of Net: speciﬁes the rule to name net.

- – Bus Range Order: speciﬁes how to sort bus net name, default is Ascending.

∗ Ascending: sort bus net name by ascending. ∗ Descending: sort bus net name by descending.

- – Net Name Method: speciﬁes how to name net, default is Prefix. ∗ Preﬁx: names net by preﬁx. Net name will be prefix + digital.

∗ Derived: names net by derived. Net name will be device_name

+ net_name_separator + port_name.

- – Net Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes preﬁx of net name when you switch Preﬁx on.
- – Net Name Separator: speciﬁes separator between device_name and port_name.


Save/Load Mode: speciﬁes the mode for save and load.

• File: speciﬁes ﬁle path. Press Save, options will be saved to the ﬁle speciﬁed in lineedit at rightside. Press Load, will load options from the speciﬁed ﬁle.

: ﬁnds the next matched message.

Sometimes, you need to take snapshot, but default background is in black, which will result in a bad eﬀect in snapshot. Using this command, you can set Background to white. It will be much better than in black. And you can save your modiﬁcation in order to use next time.

Color: speciﬁes color to use. These colors are deﬁned in display.drf. Line Width: shows line width to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Line Style: shows line Style to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Fill: shows ﬁll Color to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Outline: shows outline Color to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Fill Style: shows ﬁll style to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Load: loads user color setting from rc ﬁle. Save As: saves the current color setting as a rc ﬁle. Apply: applies the setting to current section, current project or current user.

##### • Apply the setting to current section: the setting is only valid during

the current AetherMW event period

- • Apply the setting to current project: the setting is only valid for the current project
- • Apply the setting to current user: the setting is only valid for the current user


Reset: restores the default color scheme of Schematic Editor.

- • Reset to black: restores the default color scheme of black background.
- • Reset to white: restores the default color scheme of white background.


# Part III Symbol Editor

# Chapter 24Introduction

Aether -SYM is a full-function symbol editor. This tool supports many functions to create and edit symbol shape. In addition, Aether -SYM supports to create kinds of evaluated text such as @instancename, @cellname, @cdsparam() etc.

- Chapter 24. Introduction

mand.

About Recovery: if autosave cell view exists, when opening this cell view, Aether will let you choose which kind of cell view to open.

![image 1097](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1097.png)

Figure 25.2 Open Autosave

If you click Yes, then Aether will open the autosave data, if you click No, Aether will open the original data. Regardless of the cell view type opened, autosave data will remain on disk until Save or Save A Copy to itself is executed.

In EIP and Descend command, Aether will not reopen the already opened design. If autosave data has already been opened, Aether will open the autosave data for

EIP or Descend. If original data has already been opened, Aether will open the original data for EIP or Descend.

If user has already opened the autosave data, then execute Discard Edits, Aether will close the autosave data and open the original data for users, but the autosave data will not be removed from disk.

Alternatively you can open your design from the Design Manager.

Property: shows system or user properties.

modiﬁed when the design is writable. System: lists the system properties.

- • Mode: the read/write permissions of current design.

25.11. Design Property

- • Property: the user property name.
- • Value: the user property value.
- • Add: adds a user property. If you click this button, the form pops up as shown in Figure 25.14 .


![image 1119](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1119.png)

Figure 25.14 Add Property

- – Name: speciﬁes a user property name. There are four reserved property names.

∗ lvsIgnore: ignores a design cell in a hierarchy during the lvs netlisting. The SUBCKT contents of the cell will be empty in the resulting netlist.

∗ nlAction: speciﬁes the behavior for a netlister (spice/cdl) with respect to the cell. The only type recognized is ignoring (case sensitive).

∗ schType: speciﬁes a type for schematic, for example, patchcord, noConn, supply, border, parasitic. You can deﬁne your own type and use it. The purpose of this property is pure informative - it is visible in Edit -> Properties.

∗ netSet: speciﬁes a net set, now Aether doesn’t use it. You can also add your own properties.

- – Type: speciﬁes a user property type. There are ﬁve property types: String, Int, Float, Boolean, Time.
- – Value: speciﬁes a user property value. How to specify a value depends on the property type. For example, when type is Time, valid value is Mar 19 18:34:48 2012.
- – Minimum: speciﬁes a minimum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float and Time.
- – Maximum: speciﬁes a maximum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float and Time.


- – Choices: lists choices for the value of a user property. It is valid for String.


- • Modify: modiﬁes a selected user property.

![image 1120](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1120.png)

Figure 25.15 Modify Property

- • Delete: deletes selected user property.

## 25.15 Open Recently

Open Recently is used to record the design you have recently opened. The Open Recently is shown in Figure 25.25 .

25.15. Open Recently

![image 1137](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1137.png)

Figure 25.25 Open Recently

.

##### Add To Recently:

- 1. Add a currently open design at the position 1 of Open Recently list.
- 2. Add all viewtypes supported by Aether , including netlist. However, it supports up to 10 records, and the excess will be discarded.
- 3. The list of Open Recently is displayed in the File menu and expanded in a tiled manner.
- 4. For the design opened by binding, record in the default opening order.
- 5. Design won’t be added to Open Recently list, if the design fails to open or is unsupported by Aether .


##### Record Edit Mode:

- 1. Open Recently will record the read or write edit mode when opening for the ﬁrst time and exiting design.
- 2. If you use Make Editable to change a readonly design to editable, and open the design again from the Open Recently list without closing the current design, the modiﬁed status will not take eﬀect. It can only take eﬀect after closing design.


##### From Open Recently:

- 1. The design will be opened in the recently edit mode and it will be updated to the position 1 of Open Recently list. The window which is opened from


- Open Recently list will be raised to the top.
- 2. Design will be removed from Open Recently list, when the design fails to open.

Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the design to be set as a background. You can select the design by Browse button. Any of the Schematic, Symbol or Layout view can be selected. The default is empty.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the design. View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the design. X: speciﬁes origin X coordinate. The default value is 0. Y: speciﬁes origin Y coordinate. The default value is 0.

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 1179](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1179.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.


• MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for

![image 1180](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1180.png)

##### MY.

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for


![image 1181](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1181.png)

##### MX.

• MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation

of 90 degrees. Display: display the design as the background. The default value is on. Dilute: display the design as diluted which makes the display diﬀerent from the editing design. The default value is oﬀ. Unset: unset the background and reset all options to default.

## 26.14 View List

Menu: View -> View List ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1182](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1182.png)

It is not a command but to list the schematic or symbol view under the cell which the current view belongs to. If you click it, Aether will open the corresponding design. It will not list the current view already opened. For example, if the current design is ChargePump/cp_amp/schematic, it will list symbol only. If there are more than two symbols for a cell, it will list all available symbol view names. You can quickly switch view by using this View List.

## 27.8 Pin

Menu: Create -> Pin ToolBar: BindKey: P Tcl Command: None

![image 1227](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1227.png)

This command is used to create pin. Pin represents the physical connections of terminals to nets. A terminal can have multiple pins where multiple physical connections can correspond to one logical connection.

![image 1228](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1228.png)

Figure 27.29 Create Pin

Pin Names: speciﬁes pin names. It can be single or bus names. The conditional strings to the input text by following tabel are supported.

Table 27.1 Input Text String Formats

|Input Text Strings|Output in the Schematic|
|---|---|
|D< 1:3 ><br><br>|D< 1 > D< 2 > D< 3 >|
|D< 1,3,5 >|D< 1 > D< 3 > D< 5 >|
|D< 1:5:2 >|D< 1 > D< 3 > D< 5 >|
|< *2 > A,B<br><br>|A A B|
|< *2 > (A,B),C|A B A B C|
|< *2 > (A,< *2 > (C,D),B|A C D C D A C D C D B|
|A< 0:2*2 >|A< 0 > A< 0 > A< 1 > A< 1 > A< 2 > A< 2 >|
|A< (0:2)*2 >|A< 0 > A< 1 > A< 2 > A< 0 > A< 1 > A< 2 >|


Direction: speciﬁes pin type. it has

- • Input
- • Output
- • InputOutput
- • Switch


You can switch between them by pressing Space. Signal Type: speciﬁes signal type for the pin. There are 10 types of signal type, including

- • Signal
- • Ground
- • Power
- • Clock
- • Analog


- • TieOﬀ
- • TieHi
- • TieLo
- • Scan
- • Reset


Default is Signal. Shape: speciﬁes what pin looks like. Default is Square.

- • Block
- • Square
- • Square(with wire)
- • Round
- • ActHi
- • CommActLO
- • IeeeActLO


![image 1229](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1229.png)

Figure 27.30 Shape in Create Pin

Label Oﬀset: speciﬁes distance between pin shape and pin name. Valid range is from 0 to 32. Default is 1.

Figure 27.31 Label Oﬀset

Display Pin Name: speciﬁes display pin name. Default is on.

Placement: speciﬁes how to place pin.

- • Single: places pin one by one through LMB.
- • Multiple: places pin at one time.


Bus Expansion: switch on the parser for bus names.

## 28.15 Find/Replace

Menu: Edit -> Find/Replace ToolBar: BindKey: F2 Tcl Command: None

![image 1361](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1361.png)

Figure 28.44 Find/Replace Form

Search For: sets the searching type. In: sets the searching scope. If the Search By is set to Cell, the searching scopes are as follows:

- • Current Cellview: searches in the editing cellview.
- • Current Library: searches in the cellviews in current library. If the Search By is set to Selected, the search scopes is just Current Cellview. Add Criteria: adds a line of ﬁelds in the form to allow users to search more speciﬁcally.


![image 1362](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1362.png)

Figure 28.45 Criteria of Find/Replace Form

Attribute Cyclic Field: sets option of searching for speciﬁc attributes, instances, libraries, view names, or properties for this type of object as shown in Figure 28.46. The cyclic ﬁeld selections can be changed to reﬂect the attributes of the type of object which you select in the Search For ﬁeld. For more information, please see objects criteria table below.

The following table lists Find/Replace objects criteria for symbol view. Table 28.1 Object Criteria Table of Symbol

|Objects<br><br>|Property<br><br>|Condition/Logic|Values|
|---|---|---|---|

| |PinType|==, !=<br><br>|input, output, inputoutput, switch, jumper, unused, tristate|
| |Property<br><br>|==, !=|text of name and value|
|PinName<br><br>|TermName|==, !=<br><br>|text|
| |Font<br><br>|==, !=|stick, gothic, math, roman, script, euroStyle, swedish, ﬁxed, and milspec|


| |Justify|==, !=<br><br>|centerCenter, lowerLeft, centerLeft, upperLeft, lowerCenter, upperCenter, lowerRight, centerRight, and upperRight|
|---|---|---|---|
| |Height<br><br>|<, <=, >, >=, ==, !=|number|
| |Orient<br><br>|==, !=|R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX, MXR90|
| |Visible<br><br>|==, !=|visible, invisible|
|SymbolShape|FillStyle<br><br>|==, !=<br><br>|outline, ﬁlled|
|NoteShape|LineStyle|==, !=|solid, dashed|
|NoteText<br><br>|Label<br><br>|==, !=|text|
| |Font|==, !=<br><br>|stick, gothic, math, roman, script, euroStyle, swedish, ﬁxed, and milspec|

| |Visible<br><br>|==, !=<br><br>|visible, invisible|
|---|---|---|---|


Condition Cyclic Field: sets option of searching for character strings or numerals that are exactly matched (==) or are not matched (!=); to get matches that contain a string, a leading and/or trailing asterisk must be used. The symbols <, <=, >, >= are used where applicable. EXIST and !EXIST locate or exclude discrete blocks of information anywhere in the string.

Value Field: sets the value of the attribute or property to be used in the search. In the text ﬁeld, you can specify the search string using the wild card characters.

Delete: deletes this line of criteria from the form.

![image 1363](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1363.png)

Figure 28.46 Criteria of Find/Replace Form

Replace With: replaces the objects’ matching results with a new object, attribute value, or property value. The cyclic ﬁeld contains the frequently used properties. In the text ﬁeld, you can specify the value of the property with which you want to replace the original value.

• Add Criteria: adds a line of ﬁelds in the form to allow users to replace more speciﬁcally.

Search: sets more operations for searching conditions.

- • Match Method: sets the way of matching when there are multiple matching criteria.


– All Conditions: all criteria must be met when searching objects.

This is the default value of Match Method.

– Any Condition: at least one of the criteria must be met when

searching objects.

- • Search By: sets the search scope condition.

- – Cell: search in the hole bbox of cell.
- – Selected: search within the selected objects.


- • Zoom To: zooms to the centers the cellview around the current object in the search group when you click Find, Previous, or Next.
- • Case Sensitive: searches object with considering case sensitivity.
- • Wildcard Match: searches and ﬁnds object with wild card. Check it,


*, ?, . and [] are supported by Find, * and {} are supported by Replace and Replace All, else, regular expressions are supported. It is checked in AetherAdv by default. This option is valid in Advance Aether.

- Table 28.2 Wildcard Illustrations

|Wildcard|Parse Expression|
|---|---|


|*|Matches any sequence of zero or more characters when used by Find. Indicates the content of nth wild card character if current * is the nth * in replacing string when used by Replace or Replace All.|
|---|---|
|?|Matches any single character. Only used by Find.|
|.|Matches any single character. Only used by Find.|
|[A-Z]|The 26 English letters and the range of letter is from A to Z. Only used by Find.|
|[0-9]<br><br>|The 10 digits and the range of digit is from 0 to 9. Only used by Find.|
|[abc]<br><br>|The character is one of a, b or c. Only used by Find.|
|{n}|Indicates the content of nth wild card character. Only used by Replace or Replace All.|


- Table 28.3 Regular Expression


|Regular Expression|Parse Expression|
|---|---|


|[A-Z]<br><br>|The 26 English letters and the range of letter is from A to Z.|
|---|---|
|A{1,3}<br><br>|The number of characters A within [1,3].|
|[0-9]{1,2}|The range of number is from 0 to 99.|
|\d<br><br>|The range of number is from 0 to 9.|
|A?<br><br>|The range of character is A{0,1}, or character A.|
|\d?<br><br>|The range of number is from 0 to 9.|
|A|B|C<br><br>|Character A or B or C.|
|[^A]<br><br>|All single character or number except the character A.|
|A+<br><br>|The letter A combination of the string, such as: A, AA, AAA...|
|A{n}|Multiple character A.|
|A{n,}<br><br>|The number range of continuous character A is equal or greater than n.|
|A{n,m}|The number range of continuous character A is equal or greater than n and is equal or less than m.|


- • Current Figure: shows which object in the search group is highlighted as you click Previous or Next.
- • Figure Count: after clicking Find, show the number of objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Auto Highlight Next After Replacing: after clicking Replace, auto highlight next object.
- • Preview Replace(No Edits): after clicking Replace or Replace All, preview the current object(s) replacement information on the design manager form.


Search Results: sets more operations for ﬁnding results.

- • Add Select: selects the current object in the search group.
- • Select All: selects all objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Replace: edits or replaces the current object with the settings shown in the Replace ﬁeld.
- • Replace All: replaces all objects found by Find/Replace with the settings shown in the Replace ﬁeld.


Find: searches for objects matching the settings in the Find/Replace form.

Previous: highlights the previous object in the search group. Next: highlights the next object in the search group. Cancel: closes the Find/Replace form.

Example 28.8 The example shows how to execute wildcard in Find/Replace.

|---|---|---|
|Replace PN_in_1, PN_in_2 with PIN_1_in, PIN_2_in<br><br>|PN_*_*<br><br>|PIN_{2}_{1}|
|Replace PIN_Y_1_a with PIN_Y_1<br><br>|PIN_*_*_*<br><br>|PIN_*_*|

|Replace tip_in_1, tap_in_2 with topi_in_1, topa_in_2<br><br>|t.p_*,t[ai]p_* or t[aj]p_*<br><br>|top*_* or top{1}_{2}|

.

Packaged Checks: sets check rule to predeﬁned value according to rule classes, default mode is Normal.

![image 1411](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1411.png)

Figure 31.4 Packaged Checks Classes

- • None: when modifying any rules, Packaged Checks will change to this option.
- • Normal: when modifying any rules, click Apply or OK, the set rules will be saved as Normal class.
- • Logical Only: sets all Logical rules as Warning, Physical and Name rules as Ignored.
- • Physical Only: sets all Physical rules as Warning, Logical rules as Ignored.
- • VHDL: sets Name -> VHDL Syntax as Error, other rules keep values intact.
- • Verilog: sets Name -> Verilog HDL Syntax as Error, other rules keep values intact.


##### Logical: sets Logical check rules.

Figure 31.5 Logical Rule Form

##### Physical: sets Physical check rules.

![image 1413](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1413.png)

Figure 31.6 Physical Rule Form

|Rule Name|Introduction<br><br>|Default Value|
|---|---|---|
|Floating Nets|Check Wires which do not connect to other wires or instance pins, but do not check wires which are connected by name to other wires or instance pins<br><br>|Warning|
|Floating Input Pins<br><br>|Check device input pins, schematic symbol input pins and schematic output pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins|Warning|
|Floating Output Pins<br><br>|Check device output pins, schematic symbol output pins and schematic input pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins<br><br>|Warning|
|Floating I/O Pins|Check device inputoutput pins, schematic symbol inputoutput pins and schematic inputoutput pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins<br><br>|Warning|
|Floating Switch Pins|Check device switch pins and schematic symbol switch pins which do not connect to any other wires or pins|Warning|
|Shorted Output Pins<br><br>|Check device output pins and schematic symbol output pins which are connected to other device output pins or schematic symbol output pins|Warning|
|Plain Globals<br><br>|Check for the non-default globals within in the cell view<br><br>|Ignored|
|Pin Direction Collision<br><br>|Check for any bit terminal’s direction that is inconsistent with the direction of the multi-bit terminal<br><br>|Ignored|
|Conﬂict Global Signals<br><br>|Check pins whose names conﬂict with global signals|Warning|
|Conﬂict Internal/External Nets<br><br>|Check nets which are connected between instance pins, whose names conﬂict with schematic pins|Ignored|

Search Scope: specify the scope of a search.

Aether have integrated layout editor, schematic editor and symbol editor in main window, layout editor has panel named LSW, schematic editor has panel named Component, but symbol editor has not the corresponding panel. For example, if

33.11. Worldwide View

you open layout editor and symbol editor at same time, if you switch layout editor to symbol editor, the window of symbol editor will change. And it will make you feel bad. So Aether provided the default panel named None in symbol editor window. And the panel size is the same as size of LSW.

# Chapter 34 Options

## 34.1 Settings

Menu: Options -> Settings ToolBar: BindKey: O Tcl Command: None

![image 1448](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1448.png)

This command is used to set options for schematic editor and symbol editor. It has Display, Editor and Net.

Display: sets display settings, which decides how to display schematic/symbol view.

691

![image 1449](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1449.png)

Figure 34.1 Display in Settings Form

- • Grid: speciﬁes how to draw the grid in schematic/symbol editor.

- – Minimum Resolution: manufacturing grid.
- – Minor Spacing: speciﬁes space between minor grid.
- – Major Step: speciﬁes step between major grid, the space between major grid is multiple of minor spacing and major step.
- – Type: speciﬁes grid type, default is Dot. ∗ None: doesn’t show grid. ∗ Dot: shows grid in dot. ∗ Line: shows grid in line.
- – Snap Cursor to Minor Ratio: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves. Aether deﬁnes snap spacing as multiple of minor spacing if the checkbox is checked, or the snap spacing is equal to 0.00625.
- – Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of grid dot(50 ~255). Default is 80.


- • Window: speciﬁes how to draw schematic/symbol objects in window.


- – Axis Type: speciﬁes how to display axis in schematic/symbol view. Default is None.

∗ Large: displays axis in large mode. ∗ Small: displays axis in small mode. ∗ None: does not display axis.

- – Show: speciﬁes whether show schematic/symbol objects. ∗ Default Parameter: shows default parameter of device. ∗ Cross Cursor: shows cross cursor.


![image 1450](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1450.png)

Figure 34.2 Show Cross Cursor

- • Dimming: speciﬁes dimming settings for display.


- – Enable Dimming: speciﬁes that you can change the brightness of objects.
- – Dimming Mode: speciﬁes the mode of dimming. Default is Automatic.


∗ Automatic: dims the objects automatically either when you select an object. The selected objects are not dimmed.

![image 1451](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1451.png)

Figure 34.3 Automatic

∗ Always: all objects are dimmed except selected objects, even if no object is selected.

![image 1452](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1452.png)

Figure 34.4 Always

- – Dimming Intensity: speciﬁes the brightness of dimmed objects. The default value is 50. If set to 0, no objects are dimmed. If set to 100, dimmed objects are not visible.


![image 1453](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1453.png)

![image 1454](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1454.png)

(a) Intensity = 40 (b) Intensity = 80

Figure 34.5 Dimming Intensity

- • Zoom: speciﬁes how to zoom in schematic.

- – Dynamic Zoom: enables dynamic zoom in schematic.
- – Zoom Mode: speciﬁes which zoom mode to use.


∗ Pan To Selected: pans the selected objects to the center of the window.

∗ Zoom To Selected: zooms the corresponding objects in schematic when selected objects are changed in layout.

∗ Zoom To Fit: keeps the schematic always ﬁt in the window.

– Zoom To: speciﬁes the zoom scale when zoom mode is Zoom To Selected.

- • Others: speciﬁes other settings for display.


– Display Device: speciﬁes which display device to use. Aether will

list display devices declared in display.drf.

– Ellipse/Donut Segments: speciﬁes segments of ellipse and donut.

Default is 32.

– Shape Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of shapes displayed in SE.

Valid is from 0 to 200 in percentage, default is 100.

![image 1455](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1455.png)

![image 1456](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1456.png)

(a) Original Brightness (100) (b) Half Brightness (50)

Figure 34.6 Shape Brightness

Editor: speciﬁes the setting for schematic/symbol editor.

![image 1457](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1457.png)

Figure 34.7 Editor in Settings Form

- • Shadow Surrounding Objects In Edit In Place Command: when EIP is applied, the surrounding objects will displayed in special color to distinguish from objects in EIP design.
- • Keep Action: if it is not checked, each action will exit immediately after execution.


- • Repeat Last Action: if you click ";", Aether will re-invoke the last action launched from menu again. For example, if the last action you used is Copy, you are in default action now, and you click ";", Copy is launched again.
- • Direct Move: you can move or stretch object in default action when it switches on. If you are afraid to move object carelessly, you can switch it oﬀ.
- • Keep Selected: if you want to keep selected objects no matter in preselect or post-select mode, please switch it on.
- • Allow Opening Design In Multiple Window: Aether only opens one design in one window in default. If you want view design in multiple windows, you can switch it on.
- • Auto Popup Command Option Form: Aether will not pop up form on most occasions, and you should press F3 to pop it up. But if you want form to pop up automatically, you can switch it on.
- • Auto Add Pin Name: when this option is On, the pin name will be created automatically with the speciﬁed pin. That is, when you place the pin on the wire, the default pin name will be the same as the net name; when you place the pin in blank area, the pin name is a sequence number, for example:inout1, inout2, inout3.... Only the ipin, opin and iopin are supported.
- • Turn Oﬀ Check Rule In Realtime Check: when this option is on, the real-time checking will skip these settings in Check Rule Setup-> Logical.
- • Double Click to: speciﬁes behavior of double click on instance.

- – Descend Edit: Aether will descend in a symbol by edit mode when you double click on instance.
- – Descend Read: Aether will descend in a symbol by read mode when you double click on instance.
- – None: does nothing.


- • Auto Backup Interval: speciﬁes time interval for auto backup. Aether provides auto backup feature in order to protect your data. When computer power is oﬀ suddenly, it will keep your last modiﬁed data. Default is 10 minutes.
- • Disable Auto Dimming: when ADV Trace Net and PVE reverse label are executed after checking, dimming eﬀect is automatically turned on. Default is checking.


- • Undo Limit: speciﬁes the upper limit of undo times. Valid is from 0 to 127, default is 50.


Net: speciﬁes how to name net automatically.

![image 1458](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1458.png)

Figure 34.8 Net in Settings Form

• Name Rules Of Net: speciﬁes the rule to name net.

- – Bus Range Order: speciﬁes how to sort bus net name, default is Ascending.

∗ Ascending: sort bus net name by ascending. ∗ Descending: sort bus net name by descending.

- – Net Name Method: speciﬁes how to name net, default is Prefix. ∗ Preﬁx: names net by preﬁx. Net name will be prefix + digital.

∗ Derived: names net by derived. Net name will be device_name

+ net_name_separator + port_name.

- – Net Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes preﬁx of net name when you switch Preﬁx on.
- – Net Name Separator: speciﬁes separator between device_name and port_name.


Save/Load Mode: speciﬁes the mode for save and load.

- • Reset to white: restores the default color scheme of white background.


# Part IV Floorplan Editor

# Chapter 35 Introduction

Aether-FPV facilitates circuit analysis or porting, enabling automatic layout and routing. Subsequently, the layout and routing results can be conveniently adjusted using the display and editing functionalities, allowing for easy reﬁnement. Finally, the results are exported to the layout, providing guidance for the physical layout and routing of the chip.

## 35.3 Using Command

- 1. Mouse Button Commands


This tool supports standard 3-buttons mouse. In general, button assignments are the following.

![image 1500](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1500.png)

- 2. Pan

![image 1501](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1501.png)

Figure 35.5 Pan

- 3. Exactly Select Overlapped Object


Sometimes, objects are overlapped each other, which will take trouble to exactly select one of the objects. Aether-FPV lets you press a key to select an object. The system set the key V as default, you can also modify it by Key Mapping command.

To exactly select an overlapped object, you should

- • Slide the cursor in overlap area, it will automatically highlight the nearest object from the cursor.
- • Press V key to switch the highlighted object you want to select.
- • Click the left mouse button to select the highlighted object. The following ﬁgure illustrates the process of selection the overlapped object. The order of highlighting object obeys the layer number from low to high.


35.4. Similarities and Diﬀerences with Layout

![image 1502](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1502.png)

Figure 35.6 Select Overlapped Object by V

## 35.4 Similarities and Diﬀerences with Layout

The Aether-FPV is developed based on Aether. In Aether-FPV, there are some obvious changes as follows:

- • Some menus have been removed, such as Create, Verify, SDL and so on.
- • Some actions have been added, such as Global Display, Detail Display, Group Placement and so on. Some actions have been removed, such as Create Path, Create Rectangle, Create Polygon and so on.
- • In color form, some options have been removed, such as Instance, Marker, Trace and so on, some options have been added, such as Align, Neighbor, Symmetric Horizontal and so on.
- • In setting form, some options have been added, such as Constant Highlighting, Simple FlyLine Highlighting, Select Link Editing and so on, some options have been deleted, such as Snap Pattern, Show Rulers Within Window, Select Partial Via and so on.
- • In objﬁlter, some options have been removed, such as Shapes, Instance, Vias and so on, some options have been added, such as Align, SimpleFlyLine, Rectilinear Fly Line and so on.

About Recovery: if autosave cell view exists, when opening this cell view, Aether will let you choose which kind of cell view to open.

![image 1513](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1513.png)

Figure 36.2 Open Autosave

If you click Yes, then Aether will open the autosave data, if you click No, Aether will open the original data. Regardless of the cell view type opened, autosave data will remain on disk until Save or Save A Copy to itself is executed.

In EIP and Descend command, Aether will not reopen the already opened design. If autosave data has already been opened, Aether will open the autosave data for

EIP or Descend. If original data has already been opened, Aether will open the original data for EIP or Descend.

If user has already opened the autosave data, then execute Discard Edits, Aether will close the autosave data and open the original data for users, but the autosave data will not be removed from disk.

Alternatively you can open your design from the Design Manager.

36.10. Open Recently

exporting the netlist or extracting parameters.

- – Type: speciﬁes a user property type. There are ﬁve property types: String, Int, Float, Boolean, Time.
- – Value: speciﬁes a user property value. How to specify a value depends on the property type. For example, when type is Time, valid value is Mar 19 18:34:48 2012.
- – Minimum: speciﬁes a minimum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float and Time.
- – Maximum: speciﬁes a maximum value of user property. It is valid for Int, Float and Time.
- – Choices: lists choices for the value of a user property. It is valid for String.

.

##### Add To Recently:

- 1. Add a currently open design at the position 1 of Open Recently list.
- 2. Add all viewtypes supported by Aether , including netlist. However, it supports up to 10 records, and the excess will be discarded.
- 3. The list of Open Recently is displayed in the File menu and expanded in a tiled manner.
- 4. For the design opened by binding, record in the default opening order.
- 5. Design won’t be added to Open Recently list, if the design fails to open or is unsupported by Aether .


##### Record Edit Mode:

- 1. Open Recently will record the read or write edit mode when opening for the ﬁrst time and exiting design.
- 2. If you use Make Editable to change a readonly design to editable, and open the design again from the Open Recently list without closing the current design, the modiﬁed status will not take eﬀect. It can only take eﬀect after closing design.


##### From Open Recently:

1. The design will be opened in the recently edit mode and it will be updated to the position 1 of Open Recently list. The window which is opened from

36.11. Close

Open Recently list will be raised to the top.

2. Design will be removed from Open Recently list, when the design fails to open.

## 38.1 Label

Menu: Create -> Label ToolBar: BindKey: L Tcl Command: None

This command is used to create label. It is created by Manual or Auto mode.

![image 1580](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1580.png)

Figure 38.1 Create Label

##### Mode: switches Manual or Auto mode.

• Manual: creates label by manual mode. This option is selected by default.

747

• Auto: creates label by auto mode. Label is created for object. Manual: selects Manual mode. Label can be created by Label text.

![image 1581](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1581.png)

Figure 38.2 Create Label

Label: speciﬁes the label to create. The following table lists samples of the input text.

: clears contents of Label quickly. Expand Bus Label: switches on the parser for bus label.

![image 1582](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1582.png)

Overbar: adds overline on the label. Aether implements overline by underscore(_). For example, when you specify label as a_bc_d, the eﬀect is as follows:

![image 1583](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1583.png)

(a) Turn Oﬀ (b) Turn On

Figure 38.3 Overbar for Create Label

Pick Nets: picks nets from schematic view or ﬁle. Aether will treat nets as labels.

![image 1585](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1585.png)

Figure 38.4 Pick Nets

- • From Schematic: picks nets from schematic view. It is default.


- – Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of schematic view.
- – Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of schematic view.
- – View Name: speciﬁes the view name of schematic view.
- – : short-cut to pop up browser to select schematic view.

![image 1586](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1586.png)

- – : reloads nets from schematic view.

![image 1587](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1587.png)

- – Exclude Default Nets: removes the default nets from nets in schematic view.


- – Pin Only: lists the pins in Nets & Pins.
- – Select: selects the name from the edit box below.
- – Split Bus Net: lists the bus net in bit form. Such as bus net A< 0:2> will be split into A< 0> ,A< 1> and A< 2> .
- – Nets & Pins: lists the nets and pins in schematic view.
- – : adds selected nets and pins to Label.


![image 1588](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1588.png)

- • From File: picks nets from speciﬁed ﬁle. Aether will add the nets’ name to Label automatically. There should be only one word per line in the ﬁle.


|Net1<br><br>Net2<br><br>Net3<br><br><br>|
|---|


Height: speciﬁes height of label. Default value is 1. Font: speciﬁes font. Default value is stick. Aether supports the following fonts:

- • euroStyle
- • gothic
- • math
- • roman
- • script
- • stick • ﬁxed
- • swedish • milSpec


![image 1589](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1589.png)

Figure 38.5 Font

Drafting: Aether will display label in human readable direction even if you rotate note text by 180/270 degrees.

![image 1590](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1590.png)

Figure 38.6 Drafting

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 1591](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1591.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.


• MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for

![image 1592](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1592.png)

##### MY.

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for


![image 1593](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1593.png)

##### MX.

• MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.

Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes how to locate the original point of object. Aether calculates the original point based on the Justiﬁcation and the object’s bounding box.

- • LeftBottom
- • CenterBottom
- • RightBottom
- • LeftCenter
- • CenterCenter
- • RightCenter
- • LeftTop
- • CenterTop
- • RightTop Now we use labels to explain it. Please notice the little cross near the labels.


![image 1594](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1594.png)

Figure 38.7 Justiﬁcation Example

Method speciﬁes the method to create label.

- • Step: creates labels one by one. It is default.
- • Serial: creates the serial labels as a sequence or a matrix, when there is more than one label deﬁned in Label.


- – Snap: speciﬁes snap mode when creating labels. ∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. ∗ XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. ∗ YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- – Array: speciﬁes expanding method.

∗ Checked: creates the bus labels as a matrix whose ﬁrst dimension length is deﬁned in Rows. The ﬁrst of all labels and the oﬀsets of both dimensions will be determined with sequential LBM-Click for three times. However, it will be created as a sequence while the labels are not suﬃcient.

∗ Unchecked: creates the labels as a sequence. The ﬁrst label and the oﬀset will be speciﬁed by LBM-Click successively.

- – Rows: speciﬁes ﬁrst dimension length while the Array is checked.


- • Batch: creates more labels at one time. You should specify the space between the labels.

– X Spacing: speciﬁes the space align x-direction. – Y Spacing: speciﬁes the space align y-direction.

- • Line: creates more labels when you draw a line overlap shapes.


- – Snap: speciﬁes snap mode when creating labels. ∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. ∗ XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. ∗ YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- – Auto Rotate: Aether will rotate the label according to direction of line.
- – Selected Objects Only: only creates labels on shapes which ∗ overlaps with line. ∗ is selected.
- – Skip Width > =: skips the shapes which width is greater than or equal to speciﬁed width.


- • Whole: speciﬁes to create one label even if there are spaces between them. For example, A B C D, Aether will create only one label ‘A B C D’ when Whole is selected. And Expand Bus Label is invalid too.
- • Label Layer: speciﬁes which layer to create label.


- – Auto: speciﬁes layer according rule Label Layer in Technology Manager.
- – Active Layer: speciﬁes active layer as label layer.
- – Select Layer: speciﬁes the layer of label.


Attach To Shape: attaches the label to speciﬁed shape. After attached, label should be copied/moved/deleted when attached shape is copied/moved/deleted. It is valid when Method is Step, Line, Whole. Default is oﬀ.

Keep Last Label: keeps the last label in Label when there is no label left. Default is oﬀ

##### Convert To Polygon Text: converts label to polygon.

- • Non45: does not allow 45 degree segment.
- • Snap Grid: snap points of polygon to grid.
- • Space: speciﬁes distance between labels.
- • Polygon Width: speciﬁes the width of edges of polygon. It should be an even. And you can set cd-font-path in section Options of aether.rc by custom deﬁned font.


Auto: selects Auto mode. Label can be created by automation.

![image 1595](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1595.png)

Figure 38.8 Create Auto Label

- • From Pin/Net: sets pin and shape that can be created label from net name. If state is unchecked, pin and shape cannot be created label. The default state is checked.
- • From Instance: sets instance that can be created label from instance name or cell name. If state is unchecked, instance cannot be created label. The default state is checked.
- • Instance Name: sets instance that can be created label from instance name. The default state is checked.
- • Cell Name: sets instance that can be created label from cell name. The default state is unchecked.
