## 38.2 P and R Objects

### 38.2.1 Boundary

Menu: Create -> P&R Objects -> Boundary ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1612](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1612.png)

This command is used to create boundary in current design view.

Boundary Type: speciﬁes create boundary type.

- • P&R: in digital circuit design, P&R boundary is applications that limit the scope of the place and route of the block boundaries. Only one P&R boundary is allowed per cellview.

![image 1613](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1613.png)

Figure 38.25 P&R Boundary

- • Snap: snap boundary is an application that supports the design of any line macro or standard cell. Snap boundary must be rectangular, and snap boundary is needed to snap cells with straight (non-rectangular) P&R boundary. As P&R boundary, only one snap boundary is allowed per cellview.

![image 1614](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1614.png)

Figure 38.26 Snap Boundary

- • Area: area boundary is used for physical block, it is used to indicate an area of the block, and it is used for various purposes deﬁned by the design method. Each area boundary has a unique name.


![image 1615](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1615.png)

Figure 38.27 Area Boundary

Create Method: speciﬁes create method which method is used to create the boundary objects.

- • Select From Layout: selects the objects you need from current design. Once you have selected the objects, use the OK or Hide button to create the boundary.
- • Rectangle: creates a rectangle area for the boundary. Press OK or Hide button and draw a rectangle on the design.
- • Polygon: speciﬁes a polygon area for the boundary. In the P&R boundary type and Area boundary type, valid snap modes are any angle, diagonal, orthogonal, xﬁrst, yﬁrst.


Example 38.5 The example shows how to create an area boundary.

- 1. Select the objects from layout, as follows:


![image 1616](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1616.png)

Figure 38.28 Create Area Boundary Result

- 2. Choose Create -> P&R Objects -> Boundary. From the Boundary Type choose Area. In the Boundary Name ﬁeld, type the name of the library you want to create, such as test. From the Create Method choose Select From Layout, as follows:

![image 1617](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1617.png)

Figure 38.29 Form Settings

- 3. Press OK. The area of the selected objects shows a yellow boundary, as follows:


![image 1618](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1618.png)

Figure 38.30 Create Area Boundary Result

### 38.2.2 Blockage

Menu: Create -> P&R Objects -> Blockage ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1619](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1619.png)

This command is used to create blockage in current design view.

![image 1620](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1620.png)

Figure 38.31 Create Blockage Form

Blockage Type: selects the type of blockage to create.

- • Placement: in this area, you cannot place instances.
- • Routing: in this area, you cannot create vias or routes for a wire.
- • Pin: in the blockage area and layer, you cannot created pins.
- • Screen: only when nets reach the maximum density speciﬁed on the blockage can nets be created in the blockage area.
- • Slot: in the blocked area on its layer, you cannot create slotting.
- • Fill: in the blocked area on its layer, you cannot create ﬁll.
- • Wiring: in the blockage area on the given layer, you cannot create wires, except for stacked vias.
- • Feedthru: in the blockage area, you cannot create feedthrus.


Material: selects is the material of blockage. However, there are some special types of blockages that cannot select the material. When Blockage Type is Placement, the Material ﬁeld will be grayed out.

![image 1621](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1621.png)

Figure 38.32 Material’s Choose Area

Layer: selects the layer based on the selected material. The layers displayed are those with one of the above materials, which are deﬁned in the technology ﬁle. The default material is all . When Blockage Type is Placement, the Layer ﬁeld will be grayed out.

Max Density: When Blockage Type is Placement or Screen, you can set maximum percentage of the total design area that the metal may occupy.

Attach To Owner: according to the type of blockage, an instance or a cluster is designated as the owner of the blockage.

Snap Mode: selects mode to use when you enter points.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. • YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.


Example 38.6 The example shows how to create an area blockage.

1. Choose Create -> P&R Objects -> Blockage. The settings as shown in the following ﬁgure:

## 39.3 Copy

Menu: Edit -> Copy ToolBar: BindKey: C Tcl Command: None

![image 1629](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1629.png)

This command makes duplicate(s) of you selected object(s). When you activate Copy and press F3, the form appears.

![image 1630](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1630.png)

Figure 39.4 Copy Form

To Layer: changes into another layer when copy shape(s). It’s invalid to Instance.

Resize: expands(+) or shrinks(-) each side of shape(s) by the Resize option. Default value is 0.

Synchronize Group: creates synchronized ﬁggroup for source object and new copied object if new copied object is the same as source object. The edits of source object will reproduce to new copied object, and vice versa. Default is unchecked.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes the angles along which you can move objects.

- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • XOnly: draws wire along X-axis only.
- • YOnly: draws wire along Y-axis only.


![image 1631](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1631.png)

Figure 39.5 Draw Mode/Method

Maintain Color While Copying: speciﬁes the source object lock state and color information to be copied verbatim to the newly generated object when Copy or MakeCell. Default is checked.

Chain Mode: chooses a chain mode for copy.

- • All: copies all devices in a chain.
- • Selected: copies only selected devices.
- • Expand To Left: copies the selected device and all devices to the left of the selected device in the chain.
- • Expand To Right: copies the selected device and all devices to the right of the selected device in the chain.


Maintain Map Relationship While Copying: copies the map relationship on the objects to the new objects. Default is unchecked. When this option is checked, Copy Connectivity is checked at the same time.

Copy Connectivity: copies the net on the object to the new object. Default is unchecked.

![image 1632](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1632.png)

Figure 39.6 Copy 2 Rectangles with Nets

Increment Bus Net Name: increments the bus bit on the object to the new object. The option is activated only when the Copy Connectivity option is checked.

![image 1633](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1633.png)

Figure 39.7 Increase Index of Bus Bit from 1 to 2

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 1634](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1634.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.
- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for


![image 1635](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1635.png)

![image 1636](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1636.png)

##### MX.

• MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.

Rows and Columns: let you copy objects to array objects. Default value is 1. For example, the following ﬁgure shows copying an instance to 3x3 objects.

![image 1637](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1637.png)

Figure 39.8 Copying a Shape to 3 Rows and 3 Columns

Y-Pitch and X-pitch: Indicate the horizontal and vertical distance between the center of shapes. These options are activated only when the Auto Arrange option is turned on. The default value depends on the User Units. The button after the text box restores the default value.

Delta X and Y: sets the pitch when copying objects. Default values are 0.

![image 1638](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1638.png)

Figure 39.9 Copy - Delta

Note: Delta with Array of Rows or Columns are supported only when either of row and columns is 1. or when both row and col are 1.

Show Instance Contents: display instance contents when executing copy.

Auto Change Instance Label Name: if the instance name label is created by Create Label By Instance and this option is checked, the instance will be ordered when executing copy.

Spacing: speciﬁes the distance of aligned ﬁgures to the reference. Snap Target: speciﬁes the highlight mode of the target object or the reference object.

- • Edge: highlights the object’s edges.
- • Point: highlights the object’s points, edge’s middle point and object’s center point.


Snap Mode: chooses a snap mode for align, AnyAngle, XFirst, YFirst are options for snap mode.

- • AnyAngle: aligns by both X and Y directions.
- • XFirst: aligns by X direction ﬁrst, if X direction oﬀset is 0 and reference is line, align also by Y direction.
- • YFirst: aligns by Y direction ﬁrst, if Y direction oﬀset is 0 and reference is line, align also by X direction.


Hide: hides the form. Cancel: cancels the align command.

## 39.13 Advanced Align

### 39.13.1 Distributed Align

Menu: Edit -> Advanced Align -> Distributed Align ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1704](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1704.png)

This command is used to distribute and align shapes in current design. After invoking Distributed Align command and pressing F3, the Distributed Align form appears.

![image 1705](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1705.png)

Figure 39.53 Distributed Align Form

Reference: speciﬁes the reference of alignment by setting the following options.

- • Mode: speciﬁes the reference mode by selecting one of the following options.

- – Point: uses point as a reference to align.
- – Object: uses object as a reference to align and speciﬁes which type of objects to be used, the default is Instance.

∗ Instance: speciﬁes the reference object as instance. ∗ Any Shape: speciﬁes the reference object as any shape. ∗ Group: speciﬁes the reference object as group. ∗ Row: speciﬁes the reference object as row.

- – Layer: uses speciﬁc layer as a reference to align.


- • Direction: speciﬁes the alignment direction of reference. The default is Horizontal.

- – Horizontal: aligns selected shapes horizontally.
- – Vertical: aligns selected shapes vertically.


- • Type: speciﬁes which edge or point of objects to be used for reference. It has diﬀerent types based on Reference Mode and Direction. It will be enabled if Reference Mode is Object or Layer, the default is Center. If the Direction is Horizontal, it includes:


- – Top Edge: sets to top edge alignment.
- – Center: sets to center alignment.
- – Bottom Edge: sets to bottom edge alignment.


##### If the Direction is Vertical, it includes:

- – Left Edge: sets the left edge alignment.
- – Center: sets the center alignment.
- – Right Edge: sets the right edge alignment.


##### And only if Reference Mode is Object Instance, it includes Origin.

– Origin: sets the origin alignment. Clear Reference: uses to clear reference line. Align: speciﬁes how to align shapes by setting the following options:

- • Mode: speciﬁes the align mode by selecting one of the following options:


– Object: aligns shapes and speciﬁes which type of selected objects

to be used, the default is Instance. ∗ Instance: speciﬁes the reference object as instance. ∗ Any Shape: speciﬁes the reference object as any shape. ∗ Group: speciﬁes the reference object as group. ∗ Row: speciﬁes the reference object as row.

– Layer: aligns shapes by using speciﬁc layer.

- • Type: speciﬁes which edge or point of objects is used to align. It has diﬀerent types based on diﬀerent option settings. If Reference Mode is Point, the default is Bottom Left.


- – Top Left: sets the alignment to top to left.
- – Top Center: sets the alignment to top to center.
- – Top Right: sets the alignment to top to right.
- – Center Left: sets the alignment to center to left.
- – Center Center: sets the alignment to center to center.
- – Center Right: sets the alignment to center to right.
- – Bottom Left: sets the alignment to bottom to left.
- – Bottom Center: sets the alignment to bottom to center.
- – Bottom Right: sets the alignment to bottom to right.


##### If Reference Mode is Object or Layer, Align Type depends on Direction and the default is Center. If the Direction is Horizontal, it includes:

- – Top Edge: sets to top edge alignment.
- – Center: sets to center alignment.
- – Bottom Edge: sets to bottom edge alignment. If the Direction is Vertical, it includes:
- – Left Edge: sets the left edge alignment.
- – Center: sets the center alignment.
- – Right Edge: sets the right edge alignment.


##### Only if Align Mode is Object Instance, it includes Origin.

– Origin: sets the origin alignment. Distributed Type: distance calculating methods when distributing shapes.

- • Space: calculates distances by shapes boundaries of bounding boxes.
- • Pitch: calculates distances by shapes center of bounding boxes. If the reference line is horizontal, the distributed part will be below:

![image 1706](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1706.png)

Figure 39.54 Distributed Align Horizontal Type

- • : sets the distance in horizontal.

![image 1707](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1707.png)

- • Orthogonal: sets the distance in vertical direction.

– : the objects on the left of the reference object move down and

![image 1708](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1708.png)

the objects on the right of the reference move up.

– : the objects on the left of the reference object move up and the

### 39.16.2 Attach/Detach

Menu: Edit -> Advanced -> Attach/Detach ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1754](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1754.png)

This command is used to attach object(s) to another object(s), making the selected object(s) become a child(ren) of the target object(s). For example, you select object A to attach to object B, then B will become parent of A. This command can also detach objects, removing their parent-child relationship.

Example 39.23

The example shows how to attach objects to the other one and remove attach relationship between attached object(s).

- 1. Activate the command Edit -> Advanced -> Attach/Detach.
- 2. Select rectangle in current design, display attach cartoon, at the same time, rectangle will be highlighted in yellow, then click instance. Now the instance becomes parent of the rectangle.


Figure 39.85 Attach Operation

- 3. Move the instance, the rectangle moves following the instance.

![image 1756](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1756.png)

Figure 39.86 Move Attached Instance

- 4. Select rectangle again, display attach cartoon, at the same time, rectangle and instance will be highlighted in yellow, then click blank in current design.


Figure 39.87 Detach Operation

- 5. The attach relationship between rectangle and instance is removed. Move the instance, the rectangle does not move.


![image 1758](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1758.png)

Figure 39.88 Move Detached Instance

##### • Rectilinear Fly Line Attributes: sees the Figure 39.92.

- – Width: edits the width of the pathSegs in rectilinear ﬂy line.
- – Length: displays the length of rectilinear ﬂy line. Can not be modiﬁed.
- – Net Name: sets the net name connected to rectilinear ﬂy line.
- – Net Criticality: sets a weighting factor that determines the priority for this net.
- – Edit Members Properties: if clicking this button, it will descend the rectilinear ﬂy line and show the pathSeg property in it.


## 39.18 Component Editor

Menu: Edit -> Component Editor ToolBar: BindKey: Ctrl+Q Tcl Command: None

![image 1764](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1764.png)

This command is mainly used to edit the properties of components. There are diﬀerent components editing interfaces, including Bump/Pad, Pin, Channel, Inductor, Block, Domain and ESD.

Bump/Pad: editor page for editing the Bump/Pad Component.

![image 1765](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1765.png)

Figure 39.93 Bump/Pad Component Editor Form

- • Component Type: speciﬁes the type of Component.

- – Bump: speciﬁes the Component type is Bump.
- – Pad: speciﬁes the Component type is Pad.


- • Signal Type: speciﬁes the signal type of created Bump/Pad Component.

- – None: speciﬁes the signal type is None.
- – Power: speciﬁes the signal type is Power.
- – Ground: speciﬁes the signal type is Ground.
- – Signal: speciﬁes the signal type is Signal.


- • Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation mode.


- – R0: represents no change in orientation.
- – R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- – R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- – MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.


- – MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.
- – MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


- • Pin Names: sets the pin name of Bump/Pad Component. Only bundle name is acceptable.
- • Library Name: sets the library name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Cell Name: sets the cell name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • View Name: sets the view name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Width: sets the width of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Length: sets the length of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Layer: sets the layer of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Label Layer: sets the layer of the pin label corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.


Pin: editor page for editing the Pin Component.

![image 1766](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1766.png)

Figure 39.94 Pin Component Editor Form

- • Pin Names: sets the name of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Space: sets the spacing between the corresponding instantiated pins of the Pin Component when the Pin Names is bus name.
- • Pin Width: sets the width of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Pin Length: sets the length of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Pin Layer: sets the layer of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Label Layer: sets the label layer of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Order: sets the placement order of the pins corresponding to the Pin Component.

- – In Order: sets pin placement in order according to Pin Names.
- – Reverse Order: sets pin placement in reverse order according to Pin Names.


- • Separate: speciﬁes the interval mode when Pin Names is bus name.


- – None: speciﬁes no interval.
- – Odd-Even: speciﬁes Odd-Even interval.
- – Even-Odd: speciﬁes Even-Odd interval.


- – Two-Bits: speciﬁes Two-Bits interval.
- – Three-Bits: speciﬁes Three-Bits interval.


- • Cross: sets whether the placement of the pins corresponding to the Pin Component should be interleaved.


- – None: speciﬁes no cross.
- – Cross: speciﬁes cross. Channel: editor page for editing the Channel Component.


![image 1767](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1767.png)

Figure 39.95 Channel Component Editor Form

- • Channel Name: sets which modules are connected to the Channel Component.
- • Net Names: sets which nets are included in the Channel Component.
- • Pin: sets whether the routing width and spacing in the Channel Component are consistent with the pins.

- – Width: sets routing width in the Channel Component.

∗ Same to Pin: speciﬁes generating routing based on the width of the pins.

∗ Specify: speciﬁes the width of the generated routing.

- – Space: sets routing space in the Channel Component.


∗ Same to Pin: speciﬁes generating routing based on the space of the pins.

∗ Specify: speciﬁes the space of the generated routing.

- • Layer: sets the layer for routing.


– Specify: sets the speciﬁc layers for routing.

∗ Horizontal Layers: speciﬁes the layers for horizontal routing. ∗ Vertical Layers: speciﬁes the layers for vertical routing.

– Range: sets the range of the routing layers. ∗ Top Layer: speciﬁes the top layer of routing range. ∗ Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the bottom layer of routing range.

Inductor: editor page for editing the Inductor Component.

837

• Polygon: a polygon will be drawn as the selection area.

![image 1781](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1781.png)

Snap Mode: chooses a snap mode for drawing a polygon area.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. • YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.

##### Note:

• If you press the left button of mouse without releasing, you can move mouse. Then at the second point you can release the left button.

## 42.5 Advanced Trace Net

### 42.5.1 Trace

Menu: Query-> Advanced Trace Net -> Trace ToolBar:

![image 1876](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1876.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to trace nets in layout design, which supports logic and physical operations in trace rules.

![image 1877](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1877.png)

Figure 42.33 Advanced Trace Net Form

Trace Mode: speciﬁes the mode for trace.

- • Physical Trace Net: traces and highlights the nets physically connected in the design.
- • Logic Trace Net: traces and highlights the nets which are connected in schematic.
- • From Net: traces and highlights the shapes which are physically connected on the same net.
- • Across Pycell: allows trace to pass through pycell.


Preview: sets preview options.

- • Show Preview: dynamically traces and highlights around the shapes which the pointer hovers over. It also displays layer name and net name.
- • Color: selects the color of trace net cartoon. cycle means the ﬁrst trace uses the color at the top of the list, the subsequent traces use the next


colors in the sequence. In addition, chooses the color in the list to specify the color of all traces.

Trace Region: speciﬁes the region for traces.

• Hierarchy Range: speciﬁes the start level and stop level for trace.

- – Top To Bottom: traces will pass from level 0 to level 50.
- – Current To Bottom: traces will pass from current level to level 50.
- – Top To Current: traces will pass from level 0 to the current level.
- – Top To Stop Level: traces will pass from level 0 to the stop level which is speciﬁed in View -> Display Depth - > Set Display Depth.
- – Current To Stop Level: traces will pass from the current level to the stop level which is speciﬁed in View -> Display Depth - > Set Display Depth.
- – User Deﬁned: traces enable Start and Stop ﬁelds to specify the start level and the stop level. Traces will pass from the start level to the stop level.

∗ Start: speciﬁes the hierarchy level which the trace starts. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Hierarchy Range is set to User Deﬁne.

∗ Stop: speciﬁes the hierarchy level which the trace stops. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Hierarchy Range is set to User Deﬁne.

- – Area: speciﬁes the area that nets can be traced.


∗ Entire View: traces nets in entire view. This option is selected

by default. ∗ View Area: traces nets in current view area. ∗ By Area: traces nets in a rectangular or polygonal area which

is speciﬁed by user. Click Rectangle or Polygon button to specify the required shape for trace.

Connection Setup: chooses and sets the constraint group which is deﬁned in technology ﬁle to be used for trace.

- • Stack Layers: speciﬁes the Start Layer and End Layer for trace. It can narrow down the trace scope.


- – Start Layer: speciﬁes the start layer for trace. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Stack Layers is checked.


- – End Layer: speciﬁes the end layer for trace. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Stack Layers is checked.


- • Setup: speciﬁes the custom/custom_mt trace rule for trace. This ﬁeld can be manipulated when the Connection Setup is set to Custom/Custom _MT.


![image 1878](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1878.png)

![image 1879](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1879.png)

(a) Custom Setup Form (b) CustomMT Setup Form

Figure 42.34 Custom Options Form

In Custom Setup Form, the display format of each rule is Layer. In Custom MT Setup Form, the display format of each rule is Instance: Layer

- – Via Layers: uses this part to customize the via layers rules.


∗ Use Custom Via Layers: speciﬁes whether to use the via layers deﬁned in the table below. When this option is selected, the lists deﬁned in the table below are enabled. Conversely, all the via layers from the technology ﬁle are enabled.

∗ Via Layers Table: this table will display all via layers that you have added or all the via layers from the technology ﬁle. Use the

individual check boxes to decide which one works when tracing. ∗ : adds a new item to the Via Layers Table. ∗ : deletes the items selected in the Via Layers Table. ∗ Reset To Default: deletes any via layers that you may have

![image 1880](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1880.png)

![image 1881](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1881.png)

added, and adds the via layers deﬁned in the technology ﬁle.

- – Connected Layers: uses this part to customize the connected layers rules.

∗ Use Connected Layers: speciﬁes whether to use the connected layers deﬁned in the table below. If the option is deselected, connected layers will not work when tracing.

∗ Connected Layers Table: this table will display all connected layers that you have added. Use the individual check boxes to decide which one works when tracing.

∗ : adds a new item to the Connected Layers Table.

![image 1882](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1882.png)

∗ : deletes the items selected in the Connected Layers Table. ∗ Reset To Default: deletes any connected layers that you may

![image 1883](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1883.png)

have added, and adds the connected layers deﬁned in the technology ﬁle.

- – Stop Layers: uses this part to customize those layers which will stop tracing a net. The Advanced Trace Net command stops tracing those connected shapes, which overlap the stopLayer shape.

∗ Use Stop Layers: speciﬁes whether to use the stop layers deﬁned in the table below. If the option is deselected, stop layers will not work when tracing.

∗ Stop Layers Table: this table will display all stop layers that you have added. Use the individual check boxes to decide which one works when tracing.

∗ : adds a new item to the Stop Layers Table. ∗ : deletes the items selected in the Stop Layers Table. ∗ Reset To Default: deletes any stop layers that you may have added, and adds the stop layers deﬁned in the technology ﬁle.

![image 1884](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1884.png)

![image 1885](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1885.png)

- – Exclude Purposes: uses this part to customize those layer purposes to be excluded for tracing.


∗ Use Exclude Purposes: speciﬁes whether to use the exclude layer purposes deﬁned in the browser ﬁeld for tracing.

- – Load/Save Options: this part provides settings for saving and loading.

∗ Via Layers: speciﬁes save (or load) via layer settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Connected Layers: speciﬁes save (or load) Connected layer settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Stop Layers: speciﬁes save (or load) Stop layer settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Exclude Purposes: speciﬁes save (or load) Exclude Purposes settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Save As: speciﬁes the name and path of the ﬁle to save in, according to the option of Load/Save Options.

∗ Load From: uses this button to choose which setting ﬁle to be load, according to the option of Load/Save Options.

- – Load MT Connection: in Custom MT Setup form, use this button to load multi-tech trace rule.
- – Apply: uses this button to make the options on this form eﬀective when tracing, and save the setting on to the ﬁle in default path.
- – OK: uses this button to make the options on this form eﬀective when tracing, and save the setting on to the ﬁle in default path. And closes the form.
- – Cancel: closes the form.
- – Save: uses this button to save the options on this form to the ﬁle in default path, according to the option of Load/Save Options.


Hide: hides the form and keeps the command. Cancel: closes the form and exits the command.

# Chapter 43 FloorPlan

## 43.1 Auto Placement From Selected

Menu: FloorPlan -> Auto Placement From Selected ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1922](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1922.png)

This command is used to generate selected objects from schematic view, and then automatically place selected objects in ﬂoorplan.

![image 1923](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1923.png)

Figure 43.1 Auto Placement From Selected

View Type: speciﬁes the view to select instances. The default is FloorPlan view type.

##### • FloorPlan: selects the FloorPlan instances. • Schematic: selects the Schematic instances.

Placement Area: shows the area mode for auto placement. The default selection is Shape.

901

- • Shape: speciﬁes the Shape mode to select a shape for auto placement.
- • Custom Area: speciﬁes the Custom Area mode to draw an area for auto placement.

- – Rectangle: draws the rectangle area for auto placement.
- – Shape: draws the polygon area for auto placement.


- • Shape: speciﬁes the Point mode to point a location for auto placement.


Create In Group: speciﬁes whether to add the placed instances to the group. The default is checked.

Create Virtual Pins And Boundary: speciﬁes whether to generate Virtual Pins And Boundary. The default is checked.

Placement Options: opens Auto Placement Options form for auto placement.

![image 1924](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1924.png)

Figure 43.2 Auto Placement Options

- • Placement Style: speciﬁes Analog or Digital mode for auto placement. The default is Analog mode.


– Analog: controls the placement of analog schematic. – Digital: controls the placement of digital schematic.

- • Location: speciﬁes the location of Instances, Pattern Groups, Pins. The default is checked.

– Min X Space: speciﬁes the Minimum X Space of objects. The

default value is 1.

– Min Y Space: speciﬁes the Minimum Y Space of objects. The

default value is 1.

- • Cell Boundary: speciﬁes the boundary for the logic cells. The default is checked. If unchecked, uses the bbox as the boundary for the logic cells. If checked and no layer in Layer is selected, uses the PR Boundary as the boundary for the logic cells. If checked and a valid layer is selected, uses the boundary of the selected layer as the boundary for the logic cells.

– Layer: chooses the layer for Cell Boundary.

- • Placement Options: speciﬁes placement options for engine of placement.

– Honor Current Pins Placement: speciﬁes that automatically

placed the objects according to the position of the pins.

- • Digital Placement: speciﬁes the Digital mode placement options.


- – Supply: speciﬁes whether Power, Ground are shared. The default is share.

∗ Shared: speciﬁes that power and ground are shared. ∗ Unshared: speciﬁes that power and ground are unshared.

- – Power Term: speciﬁes the term of power. The default is unchecked.

∗ Term name: speciﬁes name of term. The default value is

VDD* vdd* VCC* vcc*.

∗ Space Of Diﬀerent Power: speciﬁes the space of diﬀerent power term.

- – Ground Term: speciﬁes the term of Ground. The default is unchecked.


∗ Term name: speciﬁes name of term. The default value is VSS*

##### vss* GND GROUND Ground gnd ground.

∗ Space Of Diﬀerent Ground: speciﬁes the space of diﬀerent ground term.

- – Tap Cell: speciﬁes whether to ﬁll tap cells, The default is unchecked.

∗ Lib/Cell/View: speciﬁes Lib/Cell/View of tap cell. ∗ Mode: speciﬁes mode of tap cell.

· Normal: speciﬁes that tap cells of diﬀerent rows are placed in the same position.

· Cross: speciﬁes that tap cells of diﬀerent rows are placed in the interlaced position.

∗ Tap Cell Space: speciﬁes the space of ﬁlled tap cell.

- – Filler Cell: speciﬁes whether to ﬁll ﬁller cells. The default is unchecked.

∗ Lib/Cell/View: speciﬁes Lib/Cell/View of ﬁller cell.

- – Cap Cell: speciﬁes whether to ﬁll cap cells. The default is unchecked.


∗ Lib/Cell/View: speciﬁes Lib/Cell/View of cap cell.

## 43.2 Auto Placement From File

Menu: FloorPlan -> Auto Placement From File ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 1932](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1932.png)

This command is used to generate all objects from Aether File, and then automatically place all objects. It has Generate, PR Boundary tabs.

Generate: speciﬁes the objects generation mode and their ﬂoorplans.

![image 1933](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1933.png)

Figure 43.10 Generate Tab

FPV File Name: speciﬁes the FPV ﬁle to use. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a FPV ﬁle by button. The FPV ﬁle format develops from the LEF ﬁle format, the supported keywords are as follows.

![image 1934](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1934.png)

Table 43.1 KeyWords

|KeyWord<br><br>|Description|
|---|---|


|UNITS<br><br>|Deﬁne the units of measure in FPV, and only DATABASE MICRONS is used in FPV ﬁle now.|
|---|---|
|MACRO<br><br>|Deﬁne the pattern group information.|
|TYPE<br><br>|Deﬁne the pattern group type(eg: DiﬀPair).|
|SIZE|Deﬁne the size of pattern group.|
|PIN<br><br>|Deﬁne the pin information in pattern group.|
|DIRECTION<br><br>|Deﬁne the direction of pin.|
|USE|Deﬁne the use of pin.|
|PORT<br><br>|Deﬁne the port information in pin.|
|LAYER<br><br>|Deﬁne the metal layer of port in pin.|
|RECT<br><br>|Deﬁne the size and location of port in pin.|
|END<br><br>|Deﬁne the end tag about port, pin, pattern group and LIBRARY.|


##### For Example:

910 Aether Reference Manual, 2025.09

VERSION 5.7 ; BUSBITCHARS " [ ] " ; DIVIDERCHAR "/" ; UNITS

DATABASE MICRONS 1000 ; END UNITS MACRO Group1

TYPE d i f f ; SIZE 4 by 4 ; PIN IN

USE SIGNAL ; DIRECTION INPUT ; PORT

LAYER M4 ; RECT 3.5 3.5 4.0 4.0 ;

END PORT

LAYER M1 ; RECT 0.3 0.9 0.8 1.2 ;

END

END IN END Group1 END LIBRARY

DEF File Name: speciﬁes the DEF ﬁle to use. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a DEF ﬁle by button.

![image 1935](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1935.png)

Reference Libraries: speciﬁes one or more libraries in which to search for master cells. You can choose multiple libraries by button.

![image 1936](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1936.png)

Constraint File Name: speciﬁes the Constraint ﬁle to use. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full path or relative path for importing. You can choose a Constraint ﬁle by button. List of options available for users:

![image 1937](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1937.png)

Symmetry: deﬁnes a symmetry constraint between pairs of blocks.

- • Writing format 1:

- – Parameters: ∗ -member: two members of the pair.

∗ -direction: the direction of symmetry axis. Literal:

horizontal, vertical.

- – Example:


|symmetry sym1 −member "G1,G2" −direction horizontal sym2 −member "G3,G4" −direction v e r t i c a l<br><br>|
|---|


- • Writing format 2:


- – Parameters:

∗ -symmetric: the direction of symmetry axis. Literal:

horizontal, vertical.

- – Example:


|G1<br><br>top "G2" −symmetric horizontal G3<br><br>right "G4" −symmetric v e r t i c a l<br><br>|
|---|


The diagram below illustrates the concept of Symmetry Constraint.

![image 1938](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1938.png)

![image 1939](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1939.png)

(a) Horizontal Symmetry (b) Vertical Symmetry

Figure 43.11 Symmetry

Axis deﬁnes a symmetric group.

• Writing format:

- – Parameters:

∗ -member: deﬁnes the member lists in symmetric groups, where single object implies self-symmetry.

∗ -direction: deﬁnes the direction of symmetric axis. Literal:

horizontal, vertical.

- – Example:


|symmetry<br><br>sym1 −member "G1,G2" −direction v e r t i c a l axis<br><br>a1 −member "sym1 ,G3" −direction v e r t i c a l<br><br>|
|---|


The diagram below illustrates the concept of Axis Constraint.

![image 1940](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1940.png)

Figure 43.12 Axis

Align deﬁnes an alignment constraint.

- • Writing format 1:

- – Parameters: ∗ -obj: deﬁnes constraint objects.

∗ -edge: deﬁnes edges of constrained objects. The following options are available.

· topEdge: speciﬁes the top edge of the object as the reference.

· leftEdge: speciﬁes the left edge of the object as the reference.

· bottomEdge: speciﬁes the bottom edge of the object as the reference.

· rightEdge: speciﬁes the right edge of the object as the reference.

· center: speciﬁes the center point of the object as the reference.

· hCenter: speciﬁes the horizontal centerline of the object as the reference.

· vCenter: speciﬁes the vertical centerline of the object as the reference.

- – Example:


|align<br><br>ali1 −obj "G1" −edge topEdge −obj "G2" −edge topEdge ali2 −obj "G3" −edge hCenter −obj "G4" −edge topEdge<br><br>|
|---|


- • Writing format 2:


- – Parameters:


∗ -align: deﬁnes alignment type. The following options are available.

· topAlign: aligns with the top edge as the reference. · leftAlign: aligns with the left edge as the reference. · bottomAlign: aligns with the bottom edge as the

reference. · rightAlign: aligns with the right edge as the reference.

· h_centerAlign: aligns with horizontal centerline as the reference.

· v_centerAlign: aligns with vertical centerline as the reference.

- – Example:


|G1<br><br>right "G2" −align topAlign<br><br>|
|---|


The diagram below illustrates the concept of Align Constraint.

![image 1941](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1941.png)

![image 1942](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1942.png)

(a) Top To Top (b) Top To HCenter

Figure 43.13 Align

Neighbor deﬁnes a neighbor constraint.

- • Writing format 1:


– Parameters:

∗ neighbor deﬁnes neighbor type. · top: places the object above the reference. · bottom: places the object below the reference. · left: places the object to the left of the reference. · right: places the object to the right of the reference. · upperLeft: places the object to the top left of the

reference. · upperRight: places the object to the top right of the reference. · lowerLeft: places the object to the bottom left of the reference. · lowerRight: places the object to the bottom right of the reference.

– Example:

|G1<br><br>top "G2" G3<br><br>right "G4"<br><br>|
|---|


The diagram below illustrates the concept of neighbor constraints.

![image 1943](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1943.png)

![image 1944](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1944.png)

(a) Top (b) Right

Figure 43.14 Neighbor

- • Generate: speciﬁes the objects generation mode, the default is checked.

- – Pattern Groups: speciﬁes the generation of the instance, pattern group.
- – I/O Pins: speciﬁes the generation of I/O Pins.

∗ Except Global Pins: speciﬁes not to generate the Global Pins while generating I/O Pins.

- – PR Boundary: speciﬁes the generation of the PR Boundary.


- • Preserve: speciﬁes that the objects are preserved. The existing objects remain in their current positions and new objects are incrementally generated, the default is unchecked.

- – Boundary: speciﬁes that the boundary is preserved, the default is unchecked.
- – Pins: speciﬁes that the pins are preserved, the default is unchecked.
- – Pattern Groups: speciﬁes that the Pattern Groups are preserved, the default is unchecked.
- – Component: speciﬁes that the Component is preserved, the default is unchecked.


- • Location: speciﬁes the location of Instance, Pattern Groups, Pins, the default is checked.


– Min X Space: speciﬁes the Minimum X Space of objects. The

default value is 1.

– Min Y Space: speciﬁes the Minimum Y Space of objects. The

default value is 1.

– Auto Placement: speciﬁes to use automatic engine for

placement. The default is checked.

- • Placement Options: speciﬁes placement options for engine of placement.


– Honor Current Pins Placement: speciﬁes that the objects are automatically placed according to the position of the pins.

PR Boundary: according to the options, controls the PR Boundary generation.

![image 1945](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1945.png)

Figure 43.15 Boundary Tab

- • Shape: selects to generate rectangle boundary or polygon boundary.


- – Rectangle Origin(x y): speciﬁes the lower left point of the rectangle PR Boundary which is generated by Area Estimation settings.
- – Polygon Points List((x1 y1)(x2 y2)...): speciﬁes points of the polygon PR Boundary.


- – Custom Area: speciﬁes the drawing area of generation cartoon for PR Boundary.


∗ Rectangle: drag-left to draw a rectangular box to make a new object shape.

∗ Polygon: drag-left to draw a polygon box to make a new object shape.

- • Area Estimation: speciﬁes parameters for generating the PR Boundary.


- – LA ComboBox: there are following four options for user to specify: Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width, but you only can choose one of the remaining three because LB ComboBox will have one.

∗ LA Line Edit: speciﬁes the LA ComboBox parameter.

- – LB ComboBox: there are following four options for user to specify: Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width, but you only can choose one of the remaining three because LA ComboBox will have one.


∗ LB Line Edit: speciﬁes the LB ComboBox parameter.

∗ Except Global Pins: speciﬁes not to generate the Global Pins while generating I/O Pins.

- – PR Boundary: speciﬁes the generation of the PR Boundary.


- • Preserve: speciﬁes that the objects are preserved. The existing objects remain in their current positions and new objects are incrementally generated, the default is unchecked.


- – Boundary: speciﬁes that the boundary is preserved, the default is unchecked.
- – Pins: speciﬁes that the pins are preserved, the default is unchecked.
- – Pattern Groups: speciﬁes that the Pattern Groups are preserved, the default is unchecked.
- – Component: speciﬁes that the Component is preserved, the default


is unchecked.

- • Location: speciﬁes the location of Instances, Pattern Groups, Pins, the default is checked.

– Min X Space: speciﬁes the Minimum X Space of objects. The

default value is 1.

– Min Y Space: speciﬁes the Minimum Y Space of objects. The

default value is 1.

– Auto Placement: speciﬁes to use automatic engine for placement.

The default is checked.

- • Soft Block: shows soft block cell which allows to be generated in Conﬁgure Physical Hierarchy ->Soft Block Mode as table list.

- – Lib/Cell/View: shows the binding physical Lib/Cell/View of soft block.
- – Parameter Changed: shows whether Soft Block parameters have changed in Conﬁgure Physical Hierarchy ->Soft Block Mode.
- – Layout Exists: shows whether the binding physical Lib/Cell/View of soft block exists.
- – Regenerated: controls whether the instance is generated or regenerated.


- • Placement Options: speciﬁes placement options for engine of placement.


##### – Honor Current Pins Placement: speciﬁes that automatically

placed the objects according to the position of the pins.

I/O Pins: according to the options, controls the I/O Pins generation.

![image 1952](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1952.png)

Figure 43.21 I/O Pins Tab

- • All Pins: shows the options that can change all items in the label list.

– Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin label list which can be applied

to all items.

– Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin label list which can be applied

to all items.

– Height: speciﬁes the height of the pin label list which can be applied

to all items.

- • Pin Label: shows the options of pin label.


- – Create Label As: speciﬁes whether to create pin label. ∗ Label: creates a label as a pin label. ∗ Pin Name: creates pin label as pin name.
- – Height: speciﬁes the height of pin label. The default value is 0.02.
- – Auto: if this option is selected, the label will be created with 0.8 times of the pin’s height.
- – Font: speciﬁes the font of pin label.


- – Drafting: speciﬁes when this option is turned on, pin labels will be displayed from left to right (horizontal) or bottom to top (vertical), regardless of its actual orientation.
- – Rotate: speciﬁes the orientation of pin label.
- – Justiﬁcation: is used to set the pin label’s justiﬁcation.
- – Layer: speciﬁes on which layer the pin label will be used. ∗ Pin Layer: speciﬁes layer of pin label same as layer of pin. ∗ Layer: speciﬁes which layer will be used by choosing layer.


PR Boundary: according to the options, controls the PR Boundary generation.

![image 1953](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1953.png)

Figure 43.22 Boundary Tab

- • Shape: selects to generate rectangle boundary or polygon boundary.


- – Rectangle Origin(x y): speciﬁes the lower left point of the rectangle PR Boundary which is generated by Area Estimation settings.
- – Polygon Points List((x1 y1)(x2 y2)...): speciﬁes points of the polygon PR Boundary.


- – Custom Area: speciﬁes the drawing area of generation cartoon for PR Boundary.


∗ Rectangle: drag-left to draw a rectangular box to make a new object shape.

∗ Polygon: drag-left to draw a polygon box to make a new object shape.

- • Area Estimation: speciﬁes parameters for generating the PR Boundary.


– LA ComboBox: there are following four options for user to specify: Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width, but you only can choose one of the remaining three because LB ComboBox will have one.

∗ LA Line Edit: speciﬁes the LA ComboBox parameter.

– LB ComboBox: there are following four options for user to specify: Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width, but you only can choose one of the remaining three because LA ComboBox will have one.

∗ LB Line Edit: speciﬁes the LB ComboBox parameter.

Style: according to the options, controls the placement of logic schematic.

![image 1954](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1954.png)

Figure 43.23 Style Tab

##### • Placement Mode: speciﬁes Analog or Digital mode.The default isAnalog mode.

– Analog: controls the placement of analog schematic. – Digital: controls the placement of digital schematic.

###### • Supply: speciﬁes whether Power, Ground are shared. The default isshare.

- – Shared: speciﬁes that power and ground are shared.
- – Unshared: speciﬁes that power and ground are unshared.


###### • Cell Boundary: speciﬁes the boundary for the logic cells. The defaultis PR Boundary.

- – By BBox: if the Cell Boundary is unchecked, use the bbox as the boundary for the logic cells.
- – By PR Boundary: if the Cell Boundary is checked and no layer is selected, use the PR Boundary as the boundary for the logic cells.
- – By layer: if the Cell Boundary is checked and a valid layer is selected, use the boundary of the selected layer as the boundary for


the logic cells.

- • Power Term: speciﬁes the term of power, the default is unchecked.

- – Term name: speciﬁes name of term, the default value is VDD* vdd* VCC* vcc*.
- – Space Of Diﬀerent Power: speciﬁes the space of diﬀerent power


term.

- • Ground Term: speciﬁes the term of Ground, the default is unchecked.

- – Term name: speciﬁes name of term, the default value is VSS* vss* GND GROUND Ground gnd ground.
- – Space Of Diﬀerent Ground: speciﬁes the space of diﬀerent ground


term.

- • Tap Cell: speciﬁes whether to ﬁll tap cells, the default is unchecked.

- – Lib/Cell/View: speciﬁes Lib/Cell/View of tap cell.
- – Mode: speciﬁes mode of tap cell.

∗ Normal: speciﬁes that tap cells of diﬀerent rows are placed in the same position.

∗ Cross: speciﬁes that tap cells of diﬀerent rows are placed in the interlaced position.

- – Tap Cell Space: speciﬁes the space of ﬁlled tap cell.


- • Filler Cell: speciﬁes whether to ﬁll ﬁller cells, the default is unchecked.

– Lib/Cell/View: speciﬁes Lib/Cell/View of ﬁller cell.

- • Cap Cell: speciﬁes whether to ﬁll cap cells, the default is unchecked.


– Lib/Cell/View: speciﬁes Lib/Cell/View of cap cell.

Pin Info Filter: ﬁlters the pins by keyword.

![image 1986](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1986.png)

- • Pin Name Filter: sets the string of object to ﬁlter.


![image 1987](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile1987.png)

- Figure 43.52 Pin Name Filter


- – Find With: sets the ﬁlter method between the found objects and searching string.


∗ All Of The Words: ﬁlters the objects matched all of the string. ∗ Any Of The Words: ﬁlters the objects matched any of the

string. ∗ The Exact Phrase: ﬁlters the objects matched string with exact phrase.

∗ None Of The Words: ﬁlters the objects excluded the string.

- – Match Word: ﬁlters objects by all words of object name. ∗ SubString: ﬁlters the objects that include the string. ∗ PreFix: ﬁlters the objects that begin with the string. ∗ Exactly: ﬁlters the objects with the whole string exactly. ∗ Suﬃx: ﬁlters the objects that end with the string.
- – Using Case: sets the case sensitive between the found objects and searching string.


∗ Insensitive Match: ﬁlters the objects ignoring the case with searching string.

∗ Sensitive Match: ﬁlters the objects considering the case with searching string.

- • Side Filter: sets side of object to ﬁlter.
- • Status Filter: sets status of object to ﬁlter.
- • Layer Filter: sets string of object layer to ﬁlter. The option deﬁnition is the same as Pin Name Filter.
- • Width Filter: sets width of object to ﬁlter.
- • Height Filter: sets height of object to ﬁlter.
- • Type Filter: sets type of object to ﬁlter.
- • State Filter: sets connection status of object to ﬁlter for Level-1 Pins.

sequence. ∗ OK: clicks it to adjust pin order. ∗ Cancel: clicks it to cancel adjusted.

routing.

## 43.7 Pin Alignment

Menu: FloorPlan -> Pin Alignment ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2021](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2021.png)

This command is used to align pins in top cell or soft block instance. First, you should choose the reference pins from top cell, normal instance or soft block instance, then choose the alignment pins in top cell or soft block instance, the cell containing the alignment pins must have the P&R boundary otherwise this command would do nothing. After these two steps, the alignment pins will be aligned to reference pins which have the same net name.

## 43.9 Extract Floorplan

Menu: FloorPlan - >Extract Floorplan ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2056](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2056.png)

This command is used to extract ﬂoorplan net status(open, short or illegal) and set connectivity for ﬂoorplan objects.

![image 2057](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2057.png)

Figure 43.111 Current CellView Form

Current CellView: extracts all ﬁgures(including pin ﬁgures) of the top-level and pin ﬁgures of top-level instantiated masters of the current editing design.

![image 2058](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2058.png)

Figure 43.112 Hierarchy CellViews Form

Hierarchy CellViews: extracts either an entire hierarchical design or selected lower-level cellviews from the current editing design.

##### • Settings:

- – Selected Instances: speciﬁes whether to check the instance is selected in current editing design.
- – Edited Only: checks whether the design has been modiﬁed after the last extracting operation.
- – Search Depth: speciﬁes the depth to ﬁnd from the current editing design.
- – Library Cell View: lists all available instances found according to settings.


∗ Library: shows library name of instance. ∗ Cell: shows cell name of instance. ∗ View: shows view name of instance.

∗ Number: number of lib/cell/view selected. ∗ Refresh: refreshes lib/cell/view list in the form. ∗ Select All: selects all lib/cell/view in the form. ∗ Deselect All: deselects all lib/cell/view in the form.

- – Selected By: selection ﬁlter settings, supports wildcards. ∗ Library: ﬁlters the name of libraries. ∗ Cell: ﬁlters name of cells. ∗ View: ﬁlters name of views.
- – Save Extracted CellViews: speciﬁes whether to save the design after extracting.


![image 2059](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2059.png)

Figure 43.113 Extract By Area Form

By Area: speciﬁes the area of the design in which objects will be extracted. You can enter the coordinates in the following formats:

- • X1 Y1 X2 Y2
- • X1,Y1,X2,Y2
- • (X1, Y1) (X2, Y2)
- • (X1 Y1) (X2 Y2)
- • (X1 Y1),(X2 Y2)


Select Area: uses the rectangle area drawn in the design.

![image 2060](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2060.png)

Figure 43.114 Extract By Nets Form

By Nets: a text ﬁeld to specify net names of the design in which objects will be extracted. You can enter multiple net names using space as the only separator.

Selected Nets: uses the nets of the objects(which have been selected in design) to override any names in the lineedit.

Unveriﬁed Areas: extracts all unveriﬁed connectivity areas generated when modifying the design.

![image 2061](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2061.png)

Figure 43.115 Extract Unveriﬁed Areas Form

## 43.10 Paper Convert

Menu: FloorPlan -> Paper Convert ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2078](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2078.png)

This command is mainly used to convert the component into a real device. applies only to the following components: Bump, Pad, Pin, Block, Inductor and ESD. Before starting the conversion, ensure that the active FloorPlan or Layout is associated with the corresponding Schematic via an SDL relationship.

![image 2079](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2079.png)

Figure 43.132 Paper Convert Form

Bump: sets the default value for the Bump Component conversion.

- • Library Name: sets the library name of the device associated with the Bump Component.
- • Cell Name: sets the cell name of the device associated with the Bump Component.
- • View Name: sets the view name of the device associated with the Bump Component.
- • Pin Width: sets the width of the pin corresponding to the Bump Component.
- • Pin Length: sets the length of the pin corresponding to the Bump Component.
- • Pin Layer: sets the layer where the pin corresponding to the Bump Component is located.
- • Pin Label Layer: sets the layer where the label of the pin corresponding


to the Bump Component is located.

Pad: sets the default value for the Pad Component conversion.

- • Library Name: sets the library name of the device associated with the Pad Component.
- • Cell Name: sets the cell name of the device associated with the Pad Component.
- • View Name: sets the view name of the device associated with the Pad Component.
- • Pin Width: sets the width of the pin corresponding to the Pad Component.
- • Pin Length: sets the length of the pin corresponding to the Pad Component.
- • Pin Layer: sets the layer where the pin corresponding to the Pad Component is located.
- • Pin Label Layer: sets the layer where the label of the pin corresponding to the Pad Component is located.


Block/Inductor/ESD: sets the default value for the Block, Inductor and ESD Component conversion.

- • Reference Libraries: speciﬁes the relevant list of libraries. When the component does not specify a Lib/Cell/View, it will search for the speciﬁed cell in the library in the list.
- • Block Name Mapping File: speciﬁes the mapping ﬁle between the component and cell name. The cell name in the mapping ﬁle will serve as the basis for the search mentioned above.


Pin: sets the default value for the Pin Component conversion.

- • Top/Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the Pin Component that is attached to the bottom or top side of the component.
- • Top/Bottom Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the label for the Pin Component that is attached to the bottom or top side of the component.
- • Left/Right Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the Pin Component that is attached to the left or right side of the component.
- • Left/Right Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the label for the Pin Component that is attached to the left or right side of the component.

## 43.11 Update From Schematic

Menu: Floorplan->Update From Schematic ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2093](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2093.png)

This command is used to update ﬂoorplan based on Aether schematic. It may update the diﬀerences of instances, pins, connectivity, etc., which includes Update, I/O Pins, PR Boundary tabs.

Update: speciﬁes the update options on existing ﬂoorplan components and whether to generate new ﬂoorplan components.

![image 2094](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2094.png)

Figure 43.144 Update Tab

- • Update: speciﬁes the update options and decide to change or remove the existing ﬂoorplan components.


- – Update Selected Floorplan Components Only: updates the selected instances and pins in ﬂoorplan only. Checking this option will


- automatically disable the generation of new components in Object group. if Update Instance Master Mode Replacing or Creating is enabled and set to Creating, you can set the Minimum Space value. Uncheck this option, the generation of new components options will be restored to the previous settings.
- – Update Nets And Instance Name Mismatches Only: speciﬁes only update connectivity, instance name, terminal name, pin name. If this option checked, it will automatically disable all other options on this form, except Update Selected Floorplan Components Only. Uncheck this option, all other options except Update Selected Floorplan Components Only will be restored to the previous settings.
- – Update Instance Master Mode: speciﬁes whether to update an incorrect master instance to the correct master. The default update mode is Replacing.

∗ Replacing: this mode will replace the incorrect instance, at the same place, with the correct instance with correct master.

∗ Creating: this mode will generate a marker on the incorrect master instance, and rename this instance with suﬃx _old. Then create the correct master instance below the incorrect one. When renaming the incorrect instance, if the new name has been used, the new correct master will not be generated.

- – Update Floorplan Parameters: speciﬁes whether to update the parameters on ﬂoorplan instances based on their counterparts components on corresponding schematic.
- – Update Net Signal Type: speciﬁes whether to update the signal type of net.
- – Delete Unmatched Pins: deletes ﬂoorplan pins that are not matched in the schematic. Redundant nets and terminals from the ﬂoorplan view are not deleted at the same time. When this option is disabled, the unmatched pins in the ﬂoorplan view will not be deleted, while a marker will be put on it.
- – Delete Unmatched Instances: deletes ﬂoorplan instances that are not matched in the schematic. When this option is disabled, the unmatched instances in the ﬂoorplan view will not be deleted, while a marker will be put on it.
- – Minimum Space: speciﬁes the minimum space between instances to all others objects.


- • Objects: speciﬁes whether to generate ungenerate ﬂoorplan components.


- – Instances: speciﬁes the generation of the Instance. Checking this option will automatically enable the I/O Pins Tab, on the contrary, it will disable the I/O Pins Tab.
- – I/O Pins: speciﬁes the generation of I/O Pins. Checking this option will automatically enable the PR Boundary Tab, on the contrary, it will disable the PR Boundary Tab.

∗ Except Global Pins: speciﬁes not generating the Global Pins while generating I/O Pins.

- – PR Boundary: speciﬁes the generation of the PR Boundary.


I/O Pins: according to the options, they control the I/O Pins generation.

![image 2095](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2095.png)

Figure 43.145 I/O Pins Tab

- • All Pins: this part is used to modify all the Pins Table List items.


- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer which will be used to generate pins. Its optional list is determined according to the following conditions:


- 1. if the constraint group is set by Options->SDL Options >Connectivity, the list will contain those valid layers deﬁned in


- the constraint group, whose function is Poly, Li, Metal.
- 2. if there are no valid layers deﬁned in constraint group or without constraint group, then the list will contain all layers deﬁned in technical ﬁle whose function is Poly, Li, Metal.
- 3. if the above two situations are not satisﬁed, then the list will contain all layers deﬁned in LSW.


- – Width: speciﬁes the width for generating pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Height: speciﬁes the Height for generating pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Num.: speciﬁes the number of pins to generate. The default value is 1, any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Create: speciﬁes whether to generate pins.
- – Apply: makes the settings of Layer, Width, Height, Num., Create applies to all items in Pins Table List.


- • Selected Pins: this part is used to modify the selected items in Pins Table List.


- – Search Net Name: a search lineedit is used to search Net Name in Pins Table List.
- – Net Name: displays the selected pin’s net name of schematic.
- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer of each selected pins. It is an optional list which is the same as the All Pins ->Layer.
- – Width: speciﬁes the width of each selected pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Height: speciﬁes the height of each selected pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Num.: speciﬁes the number of each selected pins. The default value is 1, any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.


- – Create: speciﬁes whether to create for each selected pins.
- – Modify: makes the settings of Layer, Width, Height, Num., Create applies to the selected items in Pins Table List.


- • Pins Table List: shows the ungenerate pins of schematic.

- – Net Name: shows pin’s net name of schematic.
- – Layer: shows the pin layer this action will create for each pin.
- – Width: shows the pin width this action will create for each pin.
- – Height: shows the pin height this action will create for each pin.
- – Num.: shows this action will generate how many nums for each pin.

tion result, it contains 4 selections Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width. Use the two comboxes to set diﬀerent combinations.

height. The default is 1. ∗ Height: speciﬁes the design boundary height. The default is 10. ∗ Width: speciﬁes the design boundary width. The default is 10.

## 43.13 Conﬁgure Physical Hierarchy

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2103](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2103.png)

This command controls how the physical hierarchy is generated from your logical design, including which logical components are to be ignored in the physical implementation and which physical views are used to implement the logical components.

Figure 43.152 PhysConﬁg Editor

Save: saves changes to the ﬁle, it can only be used when window is changed. Make Read Only: makes window not editable. When it pressed, it will change to Make Editable.

Discard Edit: discards edit, it can only be used when window is changed.

Import Floorplan File...: loads the Soft Block Parameters from the ﬁle exported by Export Floorplan File..., and deﬁnes the parameters into instances according to the binding physical Lib/Cell/View.

Export Floorplan File...: exports Soft Block Tab data to Floorplan ﬁle. Close: clicks it to close the window.

Help: clicks it to show the manual.

Occurrence Entry: controls occurrence mode. When the icon is pressed, you are working in occurrence mode. In this mode, all changes in instance table or attribute table only inﬂuence the instances that you edited. Otherwise, these changes will replicate to all other identical instances. As shown in following ﬁgure, without occurrence mode, changes of M1:A in instance table or attribute table also applied to M2:A, but not to M3:A, because M1 and M2 have same cellviews, M3 has diﬀerent cellviews. With occurrence mode, changes of M1:A only applied to M1:A.

##### Net Constraint: this is used to set net constraint for every net. It has Net Constraint, Design CG, Route Type, Shielding, Layer Stacking and Equal Length. You may set the following options.

![image 2135](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2135.png)

Figure 44.7 Net Constraint Form 1

![image 2136](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2136.png)

Figure 44.8 Choose the Table Header to be Displayed

- • Table Header: selects table header that you need.
- • Net Name: displays the net name.
- • Priority: speciﬁes the priority of the network, mainly deﬁning the sequence of nets. The smaller the priority, the higher the priority. When priorities are the same, the net above has a higher priority than the one below. You can modify the priority of each net. The minimum value is 0.
- • Design CG: this section deﬁnes the individual design constraint group (wire constraint group) for each net. It mainly deﬁnes the layer, layer direction, width, space, via, and cut number of the net. For nets that belong to the same group (Symmetry, Diff Pair, Bus, Bundle), when only one is deﬁned, the other nets in the same group will also simultaneously have a design constraint group added. If you delete the design constraint group of a net, the design constraint groups of the other nets in the same group will also be deleted. If you delete a design constraint group within the net constraint, the sub-items managed by the corresponding design constraint group will also be deleted.


![image 2137](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2137.png)

Figure 44.9 Add Design CG In Net Constraint

- – Create Design CG: creates a new design constraint group, and a Net Design CG form will pop up for you to conﬁgure the creation of the design constraint group.


![image 2138](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2138.png)

Figure 44.10 Net Design CG In Net Constraint

∗ Wire Constraint Group: it is a collection of wire constraint groups in techﬁle and design constraint groups that you have created.

∗ Design CG: displays all available design constraint group options. Switching to a diﬀerent design constraint group will change the other information accordingly.

∗ Cuts Number: speciﬁes the number of vias for the current design constraint group.

∗ Via: speciﬁes the selected via type. · Min Rules And ViaDef: uses the smallest rule in the tech-

ﬁle. · ViaDef Defaults: follows the rule deﬁned in viadef. · Minimum Rules: uses the more stringent rule from either

minimum rule or viadef defaults.

∗ Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the bottom layer of the current design constraint group.

∗ Top Layer: speciﬁes the top layer of the current design constraint group.

∗ Table: the number of rows in the table below is controlled by

bottom layer and top layer. · Layer: the layers used in the current constraint group. · Dir: routes direction of the layer. · Swap H/V: clicks RMB on the Dir, then clicks the item to

exchange Horizontal and Vertical.

![image 2139](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2139.png)

Figure 44.11 Swap Vertical/Horizontal

· Min W: speciﬁes the minimum width of the layer. · Min S: speciﬁes the minimum space between layers. · W/S: sets the values for width and space, separated by “,” .

- – Add To Design CG: displays all created design constraint group, you can choose one to add to current net.

![image 2140](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2140.png)

Figure 44.12 Remove Design CG In Net Constraint

- – Delete Design CG: deletes the selected design constraint group from the current net. Other unselected items that are also part of this design constraint group will be deleted as well.
- – Remove From Design CG: removes design constraint group from the current net. If other nets remain in the design constraint group, remove only the selected net. If all nets of the design constraint group are to be removed, you will need to conﬁrm before proceeding.

Similarly, OUTA<2> is alse redundant except for the left of the second column, which is above the second column. These redundancies are to ensure equal length.

As shown in Equal Length Example 2, the endpoints of the middle four columns are the selected net pins, and the OUTA<2> vertical nets extends part way up in order to maintain equal length. The diﬀerence from example 1 is that the yellow nets don’t need to be rqual length.

# Chapter 45MPT

## 45.1 Options

Menu: MPT->Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2179](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2179.png)

This command is used to set the following options that are related to colors.

1061

![image 2180](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2180.png)

Figure 45.1 Multiple Patterning Options Form

Color Engine: speciﬁes whether to recolor the graph. Default is Oﬀ.

• Oﬀ: checks this option, it will not recolor the graph. And the toolbar is

.

![image 2181](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2181.png)

• On: checks this option, it will recolor the graph according to the settings of Coloring Method and Shape Assignment. And the toolbar is

![image 2182](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2182.png)

.

Coloring Method: speciﬁes how to color, this option only works if Color Engine is checked On. Default is Interactive.

- • Interactive: checks this option, it will automatically colorize the connected graphics on the same layer. And the toolbar is .

![image 2183](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2183.png)

- • Managed: checks this option, it will both automatically colorize the connected graphics on the same layer, but also on the same layer which violates the constraint rule. And the toolbar is .


![image 2184](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2184.png)

Shape Assignment: speciﬁes how to color a graph, this option only works for isolated graphs which unlocked when Color Engine is checked On. Default is Random.

- • Random: checks this option, it will colorize the graph randomly according to the layer’s mask color. Mainly for gray graphics or in the region of color violation graphics.


45.1. Options

- • ASIS: checks this option, it will keep the original color when editing graphics.
- • LayerDefault: checks this option, it will keep the original color when creating graphics.
- • Gray: checks this option, it will not colorize the graphics.


Display color: speciﬁes whether to display mask color. Default is Show.

• Show: checks this option, it will display mask color. And the toolbar is

.

![image 2185](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2185.png)

• Hide: checks this option, it will not display mask color. And the toolbar is .

![image 2186](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2186.png)

Maintain Color While Copying: speciﬁes the source object lock state and color information to be copied verbatim to the newly generated object when Copy or MakeCell. Default is checked.

Propagate Locks While Locking: speciﬁes that lock information is automatically passed to the connected layer graph. Default is checked.

• Override Locked Color: checks this option, it passes the lock information automatically to the connected layer lock graph. Default is not checked, it only takes eﬀect when Propagate Locks While Locking is checked.

Propagate Locks: speciﬁes the design which is created or edited to automatically pass the lock information to the same layer lock graph that is connected, when Color Engine is opened. Default is not checked.

Coloring Stop Level: speciﬁes the hierarchy level of the colored graph. Valid is from 0 to 50. Default is 0.

Auto Recolor When Turning On Color Engine: speciﬁes how to recolor when color engine turns from oﬀ to on.

- • Never: checks this option, it will not recolor.
- • Always Ask: checks this option, a dialog will pop up when shapes in current cellview need to be recolored. You can choose whether to recolor or not.
- • Always: checks this option, it always needs to recolor.


Only Report Once For Duplicated Color Conﬂict Cells: speciﬁes whether only report once for duplicated color conﬂict cells or not.

Color Locking Check Rule: speciﬁes which rule needs to be checked.

- • HCL Over HCL In Hierarchy: checks this option, this rule will be checked.


- • HCL Over DbLock Shape In Hierarchy: checks this option, this rule will be checked.
- • Uncolored: checks this option, this rule will be checked.
- • Unlocked: checks this option, this rule will be checked.

## 45.4 Color Locking Check

Menu: MPT->Color Locking Check ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2219](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2219.png)

45.4. Color Locking Check

This command is used to check the color conﬂict of the Multiple Patterning Technology. The speciﬁc rules are classiﬁed as follows:

Table 45.1 Color Locking Check Rule

|Diﬀ Color - HCL Over HCL In Hierarchy<br><br>|The shape in an instance is colored with the diﬀerent color by multiple Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|---|---|
|Same Color - HCL Over HCL In Hierarchy<br><br>|The shape in an instance is colored with the same color by multiple Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|Diﬀ Color - HCL Over DbLock Shape In Hierarchy|The shape in an instance has been colored and locked, but at the same time is colored with the diﬀerent color by Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|Same Color - HCL Over DbLock Shape In Hierarchy|The shape in an instance has been colored and locked, but at the same time is colored with the same color by Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|Uncolored<br><br>|The shape is uncolored.|
|Unlocked<br><br>|The shape is unlocked.|


Which rule will be checked and whether to report once for duplicated color conﬂict cells or not are conﬁgured in Multiple Patterning Options. The check result is displayed in the Window -> Annotation Assistant. The check result will generate a marker on the corresponding shape, as follows:

![image 2220](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2220.png)

Figure 45.21 Color Locking Check Marker

||Note: Color Locking Check only checks 1000 markers by default. When the 1000th mark is checked, the check is stopped, and the following information is prompted on the DM: Not all conﬂicts are detected. There are 1000 markers of color locking check; Aether supply to set PANDA_COLORCHECK_LIMIT environment variable, this environment variable can be set to deﬁne the upper limit of the Color Locking Check check. The input value of this environment variable is an integer from 1 to 4000, If the value is invalid, the default value of 1000 is used. If the value is greater than 4000, the upper limit is set to 4000.|
|---|
|
|---|
