## 47.10 Component List

Menu: Window -> Component List ToolBar:

![image 2259](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2259.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is mainly used to create components. There are diﬀerent types of components: Bump/Pad, Pin, Channel, Inductor,Block, Domain and ESD.

Bump/Pad: speciﬁes the option settings of Bump/Pad Component. It has three diﬀerent shapes: circle, square, octagon.

![image 2260](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2260.png)

Figure 47.5 Component List: Bump

![image 2261](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2261.png)

Figure 47.6 Create Bump Component Form

- • Component Type: speciﬁes the type of Component. Default is Bump.

- – Bump: speciﬁes the Component type is Bump.
- – Pad: speciﬁes the Component type is Pad.


- • Signal Type: speciﬁes the signal type of created Bump/Pad Component. Default is None.


- – None: speciﬁes the signal type is None.
- – Power: speciﬁes the signal type is Power.
- – Ground: speciﬁes the signal type is Ground.
- – Signal: speciﬁes the signal type is Signal.


- • Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation mode. Default value is R0 and this option will be enabled when Mode is Center Radius and Speciﬁed Size is checked. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degrees counterclockwisete.

- – R0: represents no change in orientation.
- – R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- – R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- – MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.
- – MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.
- – MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


- • Mode: speciﬁes the mode to create Bump/Pad Component.

- – Center Radius: speciﬁes the Bump/Pad Component will be created by center radius.
- – Boundary: speciﬁes the Bump/Pad Component will be created by boundary.
- – Bump/Pad Ring: speciﬁes the Bump/Pad Component will be created as ring.


- • Bump Diameter: speciﬁes the diameter of Bump/Pad Component if the option is checked. The default value is 60 and this option will be not enabled when Mode is Boundary.
- • Speciﬁed Size: speciﬁes the width and height of Bump/Pad Component if the option is checked. This option is mutually exclusive with Bump Diameter and will be not enabled when Mode is Boundary.
- • Width: speciﬁes the width of Bump/Pad Component.
- • Height: speciﬁes the height of Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Names: speciﬁes the pin name of Bump/Pad Component.


- • Create In Group: speciﬁes whether created Bump/Pad Components in group. The option will be enabled if the number of Bump/Pad Components is more than 1.
- • Array: speciﬁes the array of Bump/Pad Components.

- – Cols: speciﬁes the column number of Bump/Pad Component array. Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- – X-Pitch: speciﬁes the length of distance between Bump/Pad Component centers in X direction.
- – Rows: speciﬁes the row number of Bump/Pad Component array. Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- – Y-Pitch: speciﬁes the length of distance between Bump/Pad Component centers in Y direction.
- – Delta: speciﬁes whether needs to be oﬀset. ∗ X: speciﬁes the oﬀset between diﬀerent rows. ∗ Y: speciﬁes the oﬀset between diﬀerent cols.


- • Ring: speciﬁes the option settings of the ring of Bump/Pad Components. The following options will be shown and enabled if Mode is Bump/Pad Ring.

- – Rows: speciﬁes the row number of the ring of Bump/Pad Component. Default value is 1, maximum is 2.
- – Generate Method: speciﬁes the generate method.

∗ Inside: speciﬁes the ring will be generated inside the select rectangle shape.

∗ Outside: speciﬁes the ring will be generated outside the select rectangle shape.

- – Location: speciﬁes which location of the ring of Bump/Pad Components will be generated. Default is all.
- – Space to Shape: speciﬁes the space between shape and row1.
- – Array Pitch: speciﬁes the pitch of the same rows of the ring.
- – X-Oﬀset: speciﬁes the oﬀset relative to the array growth direction.
- – Y-Oﬀset: speciﬁes the oﬀset of the diﬀerent rows of the ring.


- • Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.


- • View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Length: speciﬁes the length of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin label corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.


Pin: speciﬁes the option settings of Pin Component.

![image 2262](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2262.png)

Figure 47.7 Component List: Pin

![image 2263](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2263.png)

Figure 47.8 Create Pin Component Form

- • Pin Names: speciﬁes the name of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Space: speciﬁes the spacing between the corresponding instantiated pins of the Pin Component when the Pin Names is bus name.
- • Pin Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.


- • Pin Length: speciﬁes the length of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Pin Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Label Layer: speciﬁes the label layer of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Order: speciﬁes the placement order of the pins corresponding to the Pin Component. Default is In Order.

– In Order: speciﬁes pin placement in order according to Pin Names. – Reverse Order: speciﬁes pin placement in reverse order according

to Pin Names.

- • Separate: speciﬁes the interval mode when Pin Names is bus name. Default is None.

- – None: speciﬁes no interval.
- – Odd-Even: speciﬁes Odd-Even interval. – Even-Odd: speciﬁes Even-Odd interval. – Two-Bits: speciﬁes Two-Bits interval.
- – Three-Bits: speciﬁes Three-Bits interval.


- • Cross: speciﬁes whether the placement of the pins corresponding to the Pin Component should be interleaved. Default is None.


- – None: speciﬁes no cross.
- – Cross: speciﬁes cross.


Channel: speciﬁes option settings of Channel Component and it has three diﬀerent shapes.

![image 2264](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2264.png)

Figure 47.9 Component List: Channel

![image 2265](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2265.png)

(a) Create Rectangle/Polygon Channel Component Form

![image 2266](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2266.png)

(b) Create Path Channel Component Form

Figure 47.10 Create Channel Component Form

- • Channel Name: speciﬁes which modules are connected to the Channel Component.
- • Net Names: speciﬁes which nets are included in the Channel Component. If you have already selected pins, the names of selected pins are automatically ﬁlled into this option.
- • Channel Width: speciﬁes the width of Channel Component. The option is displayed only when creating path shape Channel Component. Default value is 2 * manufacturing grid.
- • Pin: speciﬁes whether the routing width and spacing in the Channel Component are consistent with the pins.

– Width: speciﬁes routing width in the Channel Component. Default

is Same to Pin. ∗ Same to Pin: speciﬁes generating routing based on the width of the pins. ∗ Specify: speciﬁes the width of the generated routing.

– Space: speciﬁes routing space in the Channel Component. Default

is Same to Pin. ∗ Same to Pin: speciﬁes generating routing based on the space of the pins. ∗ Specify: speciﬁes the space of the generated routing.

- • Layer: speciﬁes layer for routing. Default is Specify.


- – Specify: if this option is checked, Horizontal Layers and Vertical Layers will be shown. Please choose the same number of horizontal


- and vertical layers. ∗ Horizontal Layers: speciﬁes the layers for horizontal routing. ∗ Vertical Layers: speciﬁes the layers for vertical routing.
- – Range: if this option is checked, Top Layer and Bottom Layer will be shown.


∗ Top Layer: speciﬁes the top layer of routing range. ∗ Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the bottom layer of routing range.

Inductor: speciﬁes option settings of Inductor Component and it has two diﬀerent shapes.

![image 2267](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2267.png)

Figure 47.11 Component List: Inductor

![image 2268](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2268.png)

Figure 47.12 Create Inductor Component Form

- • Inductor Name: speciﬁes the corresponding name for the instantiation of Inductor Component.
- • Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the device associated with the Inductor Component.


- • Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the device associated with the Inductor Component.
- • View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the device associated with the Inductor Component.
- • Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation mode. Default value is R0. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degrees counter-clockwisete.

- – R0: represents no change in orientation.
- – R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- – R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- – MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.
- – MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.
- – MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


- • Speciﬁed Size: speciﬁes the width and height of Inductor Component if the option is checked.
- • Width: speciﬁes the width of Inductor Component.
- • Height: speciﬁes the height of Inductor Component.


Block: speciﬁes option settings of Block Component and it has two diﬀerent shapes.

![image 2269](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2269.png)

Figure 47.13 Component List: Block

![image 2270](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2270.png)

Figure 47.14 Create Block Component Form

- • Block Name: speciﬁes the corresponding name for the instantiation of Block Component.
- • Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the device associated with the Block Component.
- • Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the device associated with the Block Component.
- • View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the device associated with the Block Component.
- • Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation mode. Default value is R0. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degrees counter-clockwisete.


- – R0: represents no change in orientation.
- – R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- – R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- – MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.

- – MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.

- • Speciﬁed Size: speciﬁes the width and height of Block Component if the option is checked.

Domain: speciﬁes option settings of Domain Component and it has two different shapes.

## 47.11 LSW

Menu: Window -> LSW ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2292](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2292.png)

This command is used to show/hide LSW window. Note: If you close LSW, the Component in schematic editor and None in symbol editor are closed too. If you open it, the other two panels are opened too.

### 47.11.1 LSW Introduction

LSW means layer select window. You can modify the layer in LSW without changing technology.

![image 2293](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2293.png)

Figure 47.35 Layer Select Window

When layout is opened in MT mode, you can modify the die layer in LSW independently without changing technology.

![image 2294](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2294.png)

Figure 47.36 Layer Select Window in MT mode

Menu: there is a menu item for LSW, Edit. Technology Library Name: lists the technology library name.

Layer Status List: switches layer status. You can set status as you want ﬁrst, then you save status to A, B, C or D. If necessary, you can switch layer status from A to B quickly.

![image 2295](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2295.png)

Figure 47.37 Layer Checkbox

Layer Checkbox: ﬁlters the display of layers by their attributes, Valid, Used, Routing and MPT (only shown with MPT Support selected.)

![image 2296](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2296.png)

Figure 47.38 Active LPP

Active LPP: shows the active layer-purpose pair. Popup menu records the LPPs used recently.

Set Fill/Visible/Selectable: sets layer status: ﬁll/visible/selectable.

![image 2297](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2297.png)

Figure 47.39 All Visible

- • AV: sets all layers visible. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. AV as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; AV-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; AV-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • NV: sets all layers invisible, except for active LPP. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. NV as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; NV-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; NV-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • AS: sets all layers selectable. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. AS as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; AS-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; AS-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • NS: sets all layers unselectable. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. NS as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; NS-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; NS-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.


AF and NF only display, when Show Fill Buttons item in Edit -> Options is selected.

- • AF: sets all layers ﬁlled. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. AF as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; AF-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; AF-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • NF: sets all layers unﬁlled. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. NF as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; NF-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; NF-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.


Die Table: show in MT mode. Display or control all layers of dies.

![image 2298](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2298.png)

Figure 47.40 Die Table

- • Inst Name: display Inst Name of die, top cell will be displayed with Top.
- • V: sets all layers of die visible or invisible.
- • S: sets all layers of die selectable or unselectable.


Find/Filter: ﬁnds or ﬁlters layers by input string. Click Find/Filter button to switch between ﬁnd mode and ﬁlter mode. The popup menu at the right shows the setups for ﬁnd and ﬁlter mode. To see more details, LSW-> Find/Filter

Layer Set: lists the layer set. Layer set is a set of layers. Default layer sets include All, System. You can specify your own layer set by LSW -> Edit -> Layer Set.

Layer Table Header: lists the layer-purpose pairs’ information as column name. Now Aether supports 9 columns Icon, Layer Name, Purpose Name, Color, GDS Number, Visible, Selectable, Validity, and Member with 5 displayed by default.

![image 2299](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2299.png)

Figure 47.41 Layer-Purpose Pair

- • Icon: layer-purpose pair icon
- • Layer Name: layer name of layer-purpose pair
- • Purpose Name: purpose name of layer-purpose pair
- • Color: color icon of layer-purpose pair
- • GDS Number: GDS number of layer-purpose pair
- • Visible: visible state of layer-purpose pair
- • Selectable: selectable state of layer-purpose pair
- • Validity: valid state of layer-purpose pair
- • Member: member state of layer-purpose pair
- • Inst Name: display Inst Name of die in MT mode


![image 2300](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2300.png)

- Figure 47.42 Inst Name

- 47.11.2 Find/Filter This command has 2 modes, Find and Filter, Default: Find.


![image 2301](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2301.png)

- Figure 47.43 Find/Filter Bar


Find/Filter Button: The mode can be switched by clicking this button. Input ComboBox: inputs strings for Find/Filter. Press Enter to record strings in ComboBox popup list. Setup Popup Menu: selects items to set up the conﬁg for Find or Filter mode.

![image 2302](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2302.png)

Figure 47.44 Setup Popup Menu

- • Find With: the items listed in the Find With section are used to specify the search operator for Find/Filter: And(All Of The Words), Or(Any Of The Words), Exactly(The Exact Phrase), and Not(None Of The Words).
- • Match Word: the items listed in the Match Word section are used to specify the matching mode for a word: Substring, Preﬁx, Exactly, Suﬃx.
- • Using Case: the Using Case section is used to specify the case insensitivity of Find/Filter operation.


In Find mode, searching operation is used to ﬁnd an active Layer-Purpose Pair(LPP), according to the input words. The ﬁrst LPP that matches the search criteria becomes the active LPP. Find Operation just acts on LPPs in the current Layer Table. If Used checkbox is selected, the un-used LPPs will not be found by this operation.

In Filter mode, only the LPPs that match the search criteria are displayed in the Layer Table. Active LPP doesn’t change.

### 47.11.3 Layer Table Header

You sort layer-purpose pairs and change their status by clicking the Layer Table Header.

![image 2303](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2303.png)

Figure 47.45 Layer Table Header

When layout is opened in MT mode, column Inst Name will be inserted in ﬁrst column.

![image 2304](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2304.png)

- Figure 47.46 Layer Table Header in MT mode


By default, LPPs are sorted by their priority, the sort-indicator displays in column Icon. Click column Icon again, the sort order will be reversed. Clicking on Inst Name, Icon, Layer Name, Purpose Name, Color, GDS Number headers can trigger the sort action. Clicking on same header section again in succession, the sort order will be reversed. If you want to sort Visible, Selectable, Validity and Member, please Press Ctrl and click on the header. Without pressing Ctrl, clicking Visible, Selectable, Validity or Member will toggle all layers’ visible state, selectable state or valid state.

![image 2305](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2305.png)

- Figure 47.47 Layer Table Header Right Click Menu


Right-click on Layer Table Header to show/hide the table’s column.

### 47.11.4 Layer Table

You select active layer-purpose pair(LPP), and change LPP’s status by interacting with the Layer Table.

![image 2306](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2306.png)

Figure 47.48 Layer Table

The Layer Table display status indicates the layer-purpose pair’s information, such as visibility, selectability, validity, and ﬁll state.

- • Icon Display: if the layer-purpose pair is invisible, the icon will be hidden.
- • Icon Fill: if the layer-purpose pair is unﬁlled, the icon will be unﬁlled.
- • Background Color: if the layer-purpose pair is unselectable, the background color will be gray.


- • Font Color: if the layer-purpose pair is invalid, the font color will be red.


Diﬀerent interactive operations lead to diﬀerent reactions.

- • Left Mouse Button: clicking and dragging on left mouse button to change an active LPP.
- • Middle Mouse Button: clicking and dragging on middle mouse button to change the visibility of LPP. Ctrl+ middle mouse click to start Display Resource Editor.
- • Right Mouse Button: clicking and dragging on right mouse button to change the selectability of LPP.
- • Mouse Hover over: hovering over a LPP to display the tip information of the LPP.


![image 2307](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2307.png)

Figure 47.49 Layer Table tip

Menu: Edit -> Layer Sets ToolBar: BindKey: None

![image 2310](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2310.png)

Delete: deletes layer sets. You can use Shift or Ctrl to multiple select.

### 47.11.6 Options

Menu: Edit -> Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2316](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2316.png)

This command is used to set options for LSW

![image 2317](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2317.png)

Figure 47.53 Options for Layer Select Window

Recent Used Max Count: the maximum of layers in Active LPP popup list. Valid range is from 0 to 60. 10 is default value.

Find History Max Count: the maximum of search items Aether can remember. Valid range is from 0 to 60. 10 is default value.

Show Layer Tips: shows layer tips when mouse on the layer-purpose pair. Show Fill Buttons: controls whether AF and NF buttons are displayed/hidden. By default, they are hidden.

Scope of Used Layers With Display Depth: controls the Layer Table to display only the layers between the current display depth and the maximum display depth when Used is checked.

Load A: sets shortcut for the A button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load B: sets shortcut for the B button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load C: sets shortcut for the C button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load D: sets shortcut for the D button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load E: sets shortcut for the E button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load F: sets shortcut for the F button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load G: sets shortcut for the G button of Layer Status List in LSW. Load H: sets shortcut for the H button of Layer Status List in LSW.

Menu: Edit -> Validity ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

Menu: Edit -> Save To Tech ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2320](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2320.png)

### 47.11.8 MPT Support

Menu: Edit -> MPT Support ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2321](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2321.png)

This command is used to set multi-pattern mode for LSW.

![image 2322](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2322.png)

Figure 47.54 Multi-Pattern Mode for Layer Select Window

Layer-Purpose Pair: lists the multi-pattern layer-purpose pairs. You can select some multi-pattern layer-purpose pairs to create shapes.

![image 2323](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2323.png)

Figure 47.55 Multi-Pattern Layer-Purpose Pair

- • Group Name: group name of multi-pattern layer-purpose pair.
- • Icon: multi-pattern layer-purpose pair icon. You can deﬁne mask colors in display.drf. Default colors are red for mask1, green for mask2, yellow for mask3, blue for mask4. Thick line for locked and thin line for unlocked.
- • Layer Name: layer name of multi-pattern layer-purpose pair.
- • Purpose Name: purpose name of multi-pattern layer-purpose pair.
- • Mask Color Icon: mask color icon of multi-pattern layer-purpose pair. The colors are red for mask1, green for mask2, yellow for mask3, blue for mask4.


When MPT Support is selected, MPT checkbox is displayed,

![image 2324](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2324.png)

Figure 47.56 Layer Checkbox

MPT LPPs will be raised up to the top of the Layer Table, Group Name of MPT LPP and Color Column will be displayed.

![image 2325](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2325.png)

Figure 47.57 Multi-Pattern Layer-Purpose Pair Status

The Group Name row indicates a group of LPPs with same layer name and same purpose name. The visible checkbox and selectable checkbox represent the state of all the color LPPs in this group.

Checked: means all LPPs in this group are visible or selectable. Unchecked: means that all LPPs are invisible or unselectable. Partial Checked: means that parts of the LPPs are visible or selectable, others are not.

Double Clicking on Group name row, hides or shows the color LPPs in this group.

### 47.11.9 Layer Setting

When you double click LMB in LSW, Layer Setting pops up. Layer Setting lets you specify layer. The modiﬁcations take eﬀect even if you don’t save these.

![image 2326](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2326.png)

Figure 47.58 Layer Setting

All Valid: sets all layers as valid. None Valid: sets all layers as invalid. Add: adds a layer with layer number and purpose number. Modify: modiﬁes layer name or purpose. Delete: deletes current selected layer. Save Tech: saves changes to the tech. Default: loads last saved tech. OK: applies changes and closes. Cancel: discards changes and closes

You can add new layers in Purpose in Technology Manager and modify in Layer Setting form, and add Purpose settings form, extracting Purpose setting from Layer Setting;

![image 2327](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2327.png)

Figure 47.59 Technology Manager Window

##### Add: adds Purpose with Name, Number and Abbrev. Modify: modiﬁes Name and Abbrev. Delete: deletes Purpose.

It supports exiting Technology Manager without saving technology. You can choose Yes to exit Manager without saving.

![image 2328](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2328.png)

Figure 47.60 Warning Message Popup without Saving

### 47.11.10 Layer Set Manager

The Layer Set Manager in the LSW lists all the layer sets that are available in the current design window.

![image 2329](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2329.png)

###### Figure 47.61 Layer Set Manager

Layer Set Manager Table: lists the layer set information. Now Aether supports three columns: Name, Visibility, and Selectability.

- • Name: layer set name.
- • Visibility: sets visibility state of layer-purpose pairs in layer set.
- • Selectability: sets selectability state of layer-purpose pairs in layer set.
- • +: sets layer-purpose pairs listed in the Layer Table and in corresponding layer set at the same time to visible or selectable.
- • -: sets layer-purpose pairs listed in the Layer Table and in corresponding layer set at the same time to invisible or deselectable.


All layer sets selected in the Layer Set Manager are considered active and a layer-purpose pair is listed in the Layer Table if it is a member of at least one of the selected layer sets.

Example 47.6

The example shows how to select one or more layer sets and turn on or oﬀ the visibility and selectability.

- 1. To select a single layer set, click that layer set.

![image 2330](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2330.png)

Figure 47.62 Single Layer Set

- 2. To select multiple adjacent layer sets, click the ﬁrst layer set in the sequence, and then hold down the shift key and click the last layer set in the sequence.


![image 2331](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2331.png)

Figure 47.63 Multiple Adjacent Layer Sets

- 3. To select multiple non-adjacent layer sets, select a layer set, and then hold down the Ctrl key and click the other layer sets that you want to select.

![image 2332](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2332.png)

Figure 47.64 Multiple Non-adjacent Layer Sets

- 4. Set a layer set as active and turn on the visibility and selectability of all its member layer-purpose pairs by clicking the layer set with the middle mouse button. The visibility and selectability for all other layer-purpose pairs are turned oﬀ.

This command displays the m(Member) column in the Layer Table. To add layerpurpose pairs or remove them from the current layer set, you need to select or deselect the corresponding check box in the m column.

## 47.12 Worldwide View

Menu: Window -> Worldwide View ToolBar: BindKey: 1 Tcl Command: None

## 47.13 Annotation Assistant

Menu: Window -> Annotation Assistant ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2335](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2335.png)

This command is used to display marker information reported by Floorplan -> Extract Floorplan and MPT -> Color Locking Check operations. It has Connectivity, CFS, CLCR tabs. The form is shown in Figure 47.66 .

![image 2336](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2336.png)

Figure 47.66 Annotation Assistant

Zoom To Markers: allows you to magnify the marker from results and show it in the center of window. Default value is 2.

Tree: check result tree. Connectivity: displays the result of command SDL -> Extract Layout.

- • Illegal Connections: displays illegal connections.
- • Incomplete Nets: displays if there aren’t physical connections between objects belonging to the same net in the current cell view.
- • Shorts: displays if there are physical connections between objects belonging to diﬀerent nets in the current cell view.
- • Visible: if you check it, all the child markers are shown in current window.


CFS: displays the result of command SDL -> Check From Schematic.

- • Connectivity: displays the result of connectivity.
- • Dummy Instances: displays the result of dummy instances.
- • Masters: displays the result if masters are diﬀerent between layout and schematic.
- • Names: displays the result if names are diﬀerent between layout and schematic.


- • Parameters: displays the result if parameter value is diﬀerent between layout and schematic.
- • Unbound: displays the result of instances, pin and net, which is in layout but not in schematic.
- • Ungenerated: displays the result of instances, pin and net, which is in schematic but not in layout.
- • Visible: if you check it, all the child markers are shown in current window.
- • Color: you can choose diﬀerent color to highlight the corresponding instance,pin or net in schematic or layout.


CLCR: displays the result of command MPT -> Color Locking Check.

- • Color locking check rules: displays diﬀerent check results according to diﬀerent check rules.
- • Visible: if you check it, all the child markers are shown in current window, on the contrary, markers are not showed in current window.


Delete: deletes the marker which you choose in the tree. Delete parent in tree, all the child markers will be deleted. Support multiple selection.

Delete All: deletes all markers. Description: shows the speciﬁc information of the marker which you choose

.

# Chapter 48 Options

## 48.1 Settings

Menu: Options -> Settings ToolBar: BindKey: E Tcl Command: None

![image 2340](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2340.png)

This command is used to set options for Aether-FPV. It includes Display, Editor, Measure and Gravity. There are some added and deleted content in setting page based on the Aether-LE, See Also: Layout Editor -> Options -> Settings 68.1 for other common parts.

Display: sets display settings for Aether-FPV, which decides how to display layout view.

1131

![image 2341](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2341.png)

Figure 48.1 Display in Settings Form

- • Grid: speciﬁes how to draw the grid in layout editor.


- – Minimum Resolution: manufacturing grid.
- – Minor Spacing: speciﬁes space between minor grid.
- – Major Step: speciﬁes step between major grid, the space between major grid is multiple of minor spacing and major step.
- – X Snap Spacing: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves in the x direction.
- – Y Snap Spacing: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves in the y direction.
- – Type: speciﬁes grid type, default is Dot. ∗ None: doesn’t show grid. ∗ Dot: shows grid in dot. ∗ Line: shows grid in line.
- – Snap Cursor To Minor Ratio: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves. Aether deﬁnes snap spacing as multiple of minor spacing if the


- checkbox is checked, or the snap spacing is equal to manufacturing grid.
- – Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of grid dot(50 ~255). Default is 80.


- • Pattern Group: controls the added display content inside.

- – Group Name: speciﬁes whether to show group name or not.
- – Group Type: speciﬁes whether to show group type or not.
- – Constraint Highlighting: speciﬁes whether to enable constraint highlighting or not when the mouse is placed over the group.

![image 2342](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2342.png)

(a) Oﬀ (b) On

![image 2343](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2343.png)

Figure 48.2 Constraint Highlighting

- – Simple FlyLine Highlighting: speciﬁes whether to enable simple ﬂyLine highlighting or not when the mouse is placed over the group.


![image 2344](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2344.png)

(a) Oﬀ (b) On

![image 2345](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2345.png)

Figure 48.3 Simple FlyLine Highlighting

- • Instance: speciﬁes how to draw instance in layout editor.


– Show: speciﬁes how to show instance’s attributes.

∗ Inst Name: speciﬁes whether to show instance name or not.

∗ Cell Name: speciﬁes whether to show cell name of instance or

not. ∗ Origin: speciﬁes whether to show origin of instance or not. ∗ F-Style: speciﬁes whether to show instance in F-Style or not.

F-Style illustrates the rotation of instance.

![image 2346](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2346.png)

Figure 48.4 F-Style

∗ Device Name: speciﬁes whether to show device name of instance or not. It is used when showing instance’s content.

![image 2347](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2347.png)

Figure 48.5 Device Name(M0, M1, M2 and M3 are device names)

∗ Pin Name: speciﬁes whether to show pin name and attached label, the default is unchecked. The display depth of these pin names and labels is from level 0 to level N (N is current display depth).

![image 2348](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2348.png)

![image 2349](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2349.png)

(a) Checked (b) Unchecked

Figure 48.6 Pin Name Option

- • Keep Action: if it is not checked, every action will ﬁnish after executing.
- • Repeat Last Action: if you click ";", Aether will re-invoke the last action launched from menu again. For example, if the last action you used is Copy, you are in default action now, and you click ";", Copy is launched again.
- • Direct Move: you can move or stretch object in default action when it switches on. If you are afraid to move object carelessly, you can switch it oﬀ.
- • Keep Selected: if you want keep selected objects no matter in pre-select or post-select mode, please switch it on.
- • Allow Opening Design In Multiple Window: Aether only opens one design in one window in default. If you want view design in multiple windows, you can switch it on.
- • Allow Stretching Bump/Inductor Component: speciﬁes whether to allow stretching Bump, Pad or Inductor Component.
- • Display Reference Point: displays reference point in some commands, for example, Move.
- • Auto Popup Command Option Form: Aether will not pop up form at most occasions, and you should press F3 to pop form up. But if you want form pop up automatically, you can switch it on.


- • Show Rulers When Stretching Rectangles: displays rulers when user stretches rectangle.
- • Select Inside Objects In Group: speciﬁes that you can edit objects inside group without ungrouping it.
- • Auto Backup Interval: speciﬁes time interval for auto backup. Aether provides auto backup feature in order to protect your data. When computer power oﬀ suddenly, it will keep your last modiﬁed data. Default is 10 minutes.
- • Disable Auto Dimming: when ADV Trace Net and PVE reverse label are executed after checking, dimming eﬀect is automatically turned on. Default is checking.
- • Undo Limit: speciﬁes the upper limit of undo times. Valid is from 0 to 127, default is 50.
- • Snap Pattern Snapping: if this option is selected, enables snap pattern snapping.

Sometimes, you need to take snapshot, but default background is in black, which will result in a bad eﬀect in snapshot. Using this command, you can set Background to white. It will be much better than in black. And you can save your modiﬁcation in order to use next time.

Color: speciﬁes color to use. These colors are deﬁned in display.drf. Line Width: shows line width to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Line Style: shows line Style to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Fill: shows ﬁll Color to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Outline: shows outline Color to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Fill Style: shows ﬁll style to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Load: loads user color setting from rc ﬁle. Save As: saves the current color setting as a rc ﬁle. Apply: applies the setting to current section, current project or current user.

- • Apply the setting to current section: the setting is only valid during the current AetherMW event period
- • Apply the setting to current project: the setting is only valid for the current project


• Apply the setting to current user: the setting is only valid for the current user

Default: restores the default color scheme of Layout Editor.

## 48.6 Route Options

Menu: Options -> Route Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2433](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2433.png)

This command is used to set options for Aether-Route. It has Pin, Trunk and Common. You can set the following options.

##### Pin: provides a setting interface for Clock, Power and Ground, Label Pin, Prefer Pin, Device Connected, Trunk Width, Bus Width, etc.

![image 2434](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2434.png)

###### Figure 48.59 Pin in Route Options Form

- • Clock Included When Nets Are Selected Automatically: speciﬁes to include the clock when nets are selected automatically, default is selected.
- • Power And Ground Included When Nets Are Selected Automatically: speciﬁes to include power and ground when nets are selected automatically, default is not selected.
- • Identify Label Pin: speciﬁes to identify the label pin, default is not selected.
- • Extract Pin: speciﬁes how pins and nets are to be connected, default is Pin Shape Or Net Shape Only.

– Pin Shape Or Net Shape Only: speciﬁes to connect only pin or

net shape.

– Net Through Same Layer: speciﬁes to connect shapes on the

same layer as the pin.

– Whole Net On Routing Layers: speciﬁes to connect the entire

net on the routing layer associated with the pin.

- • Connect All Pins When Multiple Pins Of Supply: speciﬁes to connect all pins of the same net when there multiple pins for the same supply in a pattern group or instance. The default is not selected and the pins will be connected according to the priority of the highest metal, the widest pin, and the nearest pin. If there are multiple nets with the same signal, signal net automatically selects the connection pin based on the shortest path.
- • Prefer Pin: speciﬁes the priority for pin identiﬁcation, default is Pin Layer.

- – Pin Layer: speciﬁes to prioritize the identiﬁcation of the highest metal layer pin within a pattern group. If there are multiple pins in the higher layer, then speciﬁes to prioritize those with a larger width.
- – Pin Width: speciﬁes to prioritize the identiﬁcation of the widest metal pin within a pattern group. If there are multiple pins of the same width, then speciﬁes to prioritize those in higher layer levels.


- • Update Connectivity When Routing: speciﬁes to update physical connectivity. Default is not selected.
- • Extract Connectivity To Level: speciﬁes the depth to which physical connectivity is extracted, default is 0. Only show in ﬂoorplan(FPV).
- • Device Connected: it is a table space where you can specify the terminal and vias width. Example 48.1


The example shows how to edit Device Connected.

1. Click the “+” to add a blank line, select a blank line and click the “-” to delete the selected blank line. Click the cell to input numbers directly, or double-click to enter edit mode.

![image 2435](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2435.png)

Figure 48.60 Device Connected Edit Example 1

- – Terminal: This is a user-deﬁned term that instructs the router to identify a speciﬁc lower-level instance.The instance is identiﬁed by the name string deﬁned in the ’terminal’ when setting the width.
- – Vias Width: the value is an integer value representing the number


of vias.

- • Trunk Width: speciﬁes the width of the main trunk in the trunk router, default is Bigger Pin.


![image 2436](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2436.png)

Figure 48.61 Trunk Width in Route Options Form

- – Bigger Pin: speciﬁes to use the maximum width of the pin.

∗ Times: speciﬁes the multiplier factor, which means the width is a multiple of the bigger pin’s width. Default is 1.

- – Smaller Pin: speciﬁes to use the minimum width of the pin.
- – Setup Rule: speciﬁes to use the set layer width.
- – Specify Width: speciﬁes to use the width.


∗ Vias Width: speciﬁes the width of the vias. The default value is 2 when the Trunk Width tab is selected, and 1 when Bus Width tab is selected.

- • Bus Width: speciﬁes the width of the main bus in the bus router, default is Bigger Pin.

![image 2437](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2437.png)

Figure 48.62 Bus Width in Route Options Form

- – Bigger Pin: speciﬁes to use the maximum width among the pins.
- – Smaller Pin: speciﬁes to use the minimum width among the pins.
- – Setup Rule: speciﬁes to use the width set for the layer.
- – Specify Width: speciﬁes to use the width.


∗ Vias Width: speciﬁes the width of the vias.

- • Use Pin Width To Separate I/V Nets Or Control Nets: speciﬁes to distinguish between IV nets and control nets. If not selected, key nets are identiﬁed based on user-deﬁned priority levels less than or equal to 4, symmetrical and diﬀerential pairs, or subsequent regular expression matching. When selected, it builds upon the unselected state by considering nets with pins wider than two via widths as key nets. Default is selected.
- • Bus Router Through Instance Or Pattern Group: speciﬁes that the bus router will pass through instances or pattern groups. If not selected, the router will not pass through. Default is selected.
- • Bus Router Near To Instance Or Pattern Group: speciﬁes that the bus router’s path will prioritize being adjacent to instances or pattern groups. If selected, the router will favor routes that are close to instances or pattern groups. If not selected, it will follow the shortest and most direct path.
- • Use “+” Mode When Nets Crossing: speciﬁes the mode to be used when nets intersect. If not selected, the “X” mode is used for intersections. If selected, the “+” mode is applied. Default is not selected.
- • Valid PurposeUse: this option is for conﬁguring the purpose of the layer(routing layer)in the techﬁle when it is not intended for drawing. If selected, the speciﬁed purpose is used to obtain the relevant routing layer. Default is selected and input area defaults to the drawing pin.


- • Save To...: saves the setting of this form.
- • Load From...: loads the settings to this form.


Trunk: speciﬁes the main conduit for signal routing.

![image 2438](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2438.png)

Figure 48.63 Trunk in Route Options Form

- • Trunk Mode: speciﬁes the mode for trunk routing. Default selection is Single Trunk.


- – : clicks the toolbar item to switch Single/Multiple Trunk quickly.

![image 2439](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2439.png)

- – Single Trunk: speciﬁes to use a single trunk for all connections.


- – Multiple Trunk: speciﬁes to use multiple trunks for connections.


- • Width Space Mode: speciﬁes the spacing and width conﬁguration for the trunk. Default selection is Width Space Group.

- – Width Space Group: speciﬁes the grouping of widths.
- – Width Space Pattern: speciﬁes the pattern of width distribution.


- • Density: speciﬁes the density of the trunk routing. Default selection is Medium.

- – High: speciﬁes high density trunk routing.
- – Medium: speciﬁes medium density trunk routing.
- – Low: speciﬁes low density trunk routing.


- • Experience Value Of Trunk Calculation: speciﬁes the value used to ﬁne-tune trunk calculation based on experience.


Common: speciﬁes common settings used during routing.

![image 2440](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2440.png)

###### Figure 48.64 Common in Route Options Form

- • Process Via Conﬂict Automatically: speciﬁes whether to automatically handle via conﬂicts.
- • Display Route Report: speciﬁes whether to display the routing report after the routing process is completed.


# Part V Layout Editor

# Chapter 49 Introduction

Aether -LE is a full-function layout editor, oﬀering the capability to easily create and edit shapes such as rectangle, polygon, path, bus, circle, arc, etc. It supports parametrized cells such as Pycell, allowing users to create and modify a device layout easily and quickly. The system supports advanced functions such as real-time DRC. The integrated parasitic resistance and capacitance extraction engine allows users to extract point-to-point, pin-to-pin, or whole net resistance on the ﬂy. The in-house Argus silicon-proven physical veriﬁcation tool is integrated into Aether , and other third-party physical veriﬁcation tools can be seamlessly integrated as well.

## 49.1 Layout Editor Window

The following is Aether Layout Editor Window.

![image 2441](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2441.png)

Figure 49.1 Layout Editor Window

- 1. Command Menu This tool supports tear oﬀ line menu. If you want to use one or more commands of a menu frequently, you can click left mouse button on the dashed line, the menu will change to a menu window. Click on the menu window, you can select command directly.


49.2. Starting Layout Editor Window

![image 2442](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2442.png)

Figure 49.2 Command Menu in Layout Editor

- 2. Icon Menu


The Icon Menu locates at the top of the working area. It includes frequently used commands. Click LMB on the Icon Menu, you can execute the command directly.

Besides, you can change the location of icon menu and modify the frequently used commands by yourself in Toolbar.

## 49.2 Starting Layout Editor Window

Click layout view from Aether Design Manager to start the Aether -LE.

## 49.3 Using Command

- 1. Mouse Button Commands


This tool supports standard 3-button mouse. In general, button assignments are the following.

![image 2443](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2443.png)

Figure 49.3 Mouse

- • Left Mouse Button (LMB): Object selection.
- • Right Mouse Button (RMB): Wake up the last command or command stroke.


- 2. Command Form

A form is a window that appears when you use a command. You use the form to change command settings. For example, in the Create Path form, you can change the Width Mode to any of the options listed.

![image 2444](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2444.png)

Figure 49.4 Create Path Form

There are two types of forms in the layout editor:

- • Standard form lets you change command settings before you execute commands. They appear automatically when you start a command.
- • Options form lets you change command settings while you are running commands. Options forms do not appear automatically if you turn oﬀ the Auto Popup form if so, you must press F3 to pop up the form.


- 3. Form Buttons There list some buttons on the command form.


![image 2445](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2445.png)

- Figure 49.5 Form Button List
- 4. Stroke

Aether provides the stroke operation. Holding the right mouse button and moving the cursor, you can execute some basic commands, such as, magnify/minify the image, moving the image toward left/right/top/down etc.

![image 2446](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2446.png)

Figure 49.6 Stroke

- 5. Pan


The arrow keys on the keypad let you pan the cellview in direction of left/right/top/down.

![image 2447](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2447.png)

Figure 49.7 Pan

- 6. Exactly Select Overlapped Object


Sometimes, objects are overlapped each other, which will take trouble to exactly select one of the objects. Aether -LE lets you press a key to select an object. The system sets the key V as default, you can also modify it by Key Mapping command.

To exactly select an overlapped object, you should

- • Slide the cursor in overlap area, it will automatically highlight the nearest object from the cursor.
- • Press V key to switch the highlighted object you want to select.
- • Click the left mouse button to select the highlighted object. The following ﬁgure illustrates the process of selection the overlapped object. The order of highlighting object obeys the layer number from low to high.


![image 2448](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2448.png)

Figure 49.8 Select Overlapped Object by V

- 7. Precise Locating


When creating an object, you can set the location precisely by inputing the coordinates in layout window.

To do it, you should

- • Press F9 to pop up an entry form in layout window before invoke edit command.
- • Enter the coordinates in it. An absolute coordinate can be speciﬁed by using one of the following syntax.

- – (x y), or (x, y), or (x:y)
- – [x y], or [x,y], or [x:y]
- – {x y}, or {x,y}, or {x:y}
- – <x y>, or <x,y>, or <x:y>
- – ‘x y’, or ‘x,y’, or ‘x:y’


- • Multiple points can be separated by Spaces or ‘,’, such as, ‘(1 2) (3.5 4)’, or ‘(1 2), (3.5 4)’
- • Press Enter to ﬁnish this operation, and press Esc to cancel it.

In EIP and Descend command, Aether will not reopen the already opened design. If autosave data has already been opened, Aether will open the autosave data for

EIP or Descend. If original data has already been opened, Aether will open the original data for EIP or Descend.

If user has already opened the autosave data, then execute Discard Edits, Aether will close the autosave data and open the original data for users, but the autosave data will not be removed from disk.

This option is valid in Advance Aether.

##### Add To Recently:

- 1. Add a currently open design at the position 1 of Open Recently list.
- 2. Add all viewtypes supported by Aether , including netlist. However, it supports up to 10 records, and the excess will be discarded.
- 3. The list of Open Recently is displayed in the File menu and expanded in a tiled manner.
- 4. For the design opened by binding, record in the default opening order.
- 5. Design won’t be added to Open Recently list, if the design fails to open or is unsupported by Aether . Record Edit Mode:


- 1. Open Recently will record the read or write edit mode when opening for the ﬁrst time and exiting design.
- 2. If you use Make Editable to change a readonly design to editable, and open the design again from the Open Recently list without closing the current


50.18. Close

design, the modiﬁed status will not take eﬀect. It can only take eﬀect after closing design.

##### From Open Recently:

- 1. The design will be opened in the recently edit mode and it will be updated to the position 1 of Open Recently list. The window which is opened from Open Recently list will be raised to the top.
- 2. Design will be removed from Open Recently list, when the design fails to open.

51.17. Background

Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the design to be set as a background. You can select the design by Browse button. Any of the Schematic, Symbol or Layout view can be selected. The default is empty.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the design. View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the design. X: speciﬁes origin X coordinate. The default value is 0. Y: speciﬁes origin Y coordinate. The default value is 0.

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 2576](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2576.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.
- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for


![image 2577](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2577.png)

![image 2578](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2578.png)

##### MX.

• MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation

of 90 degrees. Display: display the design as the background. The default value is on. Dilute: display the design as diluted which makes the display diﬀerent from the editing design. The default value is oﬀ. Unset: unset the background and reset all options to default.

## 52.3 Path

Menu: Create -> Path

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2590](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2590.png)

This command is used to create path in layout view.

![image 2591](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2591.png)

Figure 52.7 Create Path Form

There are some hide options. If you expand these options, the form will be as follows:

![image 2592](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2592.png)

Figure 52.8 Create Path

Net Name: speciﬁes a net name for the current path. The created path is added to the speciﬁed net. A new net is created if the speciﬁed one does not exist. Bundle name or bus name is not acceptable.

Probe Nets: creates probes for the speciﬁed net. Width Mode: speciﬁes how to select width of path. Default is Fixed Width.

- • Default Width: speciﬁes the width of path. Width is equal to minimum width * ratio if minimum width of current layer is deﬁned in technology ﬁle, or Aether will use manufacturing grid as minimum width.

– Ratio: speciﬁes ratio of default width.

- • Fixed Width: speciﬁes the width of path. Width is equal to minimum width of current layer if it is deﬁned in technology ﬁle. Otherwise, if the value of width has not been edited, Aether will use manufacturing grid


* 2 as the default value of width, or Aether will use the value that user

inputs.

- • Fixed Current: speciﬁes appropriated width according to rmsACCurrentDensity of current layer in technology ﬁle. If there is no rule in technology ﬁle, Aether will use 0.5mA/um as default value.


– Current(mA): speciﬁes current of path. Aether will calculate the

width of path according to Current(mA) and rmsACCurentDensity.

Note: The RMS AC current density attribute has the value which returns a ﬂoat that represents the RMS AC current density in mA/µm, where the distance refers to the width of the path.

Width: speciﬁes path width. : resets path width.

![image 2593](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2593.png)

Width Step: speciﬁes step of path width. When you press [ or ], Aether will increase or decrease width of path by Width Step.

Connect Path: merge paths automatically when two paths connected. These two paths must be:

- • same layer.
- • same width.
- • head-tail are same.


![image 2594](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2594.png)

![image 2595](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2595.png)

(a) Turn oﬀ (b) Turn on

Figure 52.9 Connect Path

Note: If you use Edit -> Advanced -> Merge on the left ﬁgure, Aether will merge the paths as the right ﬁgure.

Auto Detect Edge: Aether will calculate the width of path according to the edge of shape. If the path is detected, the width will be the same as the path. If the shape is not path, the half length of edge of detected will be adopted, but if the length cannot be divided exactly by 2, the approximation will be used.

##### Note:

- • If there are more than two shapes overlap, you can press V to switch shapes.
- • Aether support shapes under the diﬀerent hierarchy.
- • You can press F7 to turn on/oﬀ it.


With Same Layer: only detect the shape on the same layer. It is on only when Auto Detect Edge is on.

Auto Detect Via Center: only detect the via center. Aether will calculate the width of path according to the center of via.

Detect Via Width: If the via is detected, the width will be the same as the via width. It is on only when Auto Detect Via Center is on.

Real Time MC: If it is checked, program will measure capacitance when you create path. But you need to set Tech File(.etf), RC Table(.table), Layer Map(.map) in RCExplorer-> RC Setup... before you use it.

![image 2596](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2596.png)

Figure 52.10 Show Capacitance When Creating Path

Real Time MR: If it is checked, program will measure resistance when you create path. But you need to set sheet resistance in Technology Manager before you use it.

![image 2597](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2597.png)

Figure 52.11 Show Resistance When Creating Path

More Options for Path: speciﬁes more options for path.

- • End Type: speciﬁes the type of path.


- – truncate: this style results in no extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.
- – extend: this style results in a one-half width extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.


- – round: this style results in an octagonal extension with 3 edges which extend one-third the path width.
- – antiESD: this style can have an extension and corner for the path. Only paths with this style may have a Corner and End.

∗ Corner: sets the corner extension. Valid value is from zero to width.

∗ End: sets the beginning/ending extension. Valid value is from zero to half of width.

- – variable: this style can have a beginning extension diﬀerent from the ending extension. Only paths with this style may have a Begin and End set.


∗ Begin: sets the beginning extension. ∗ End: sets the ending extension.

![image 2598](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2598.png)

Figure 52.12 Path Type

- • Snap Mode: speciﬁes how to draw path.


- – AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- – Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- – Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- – XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis.
- – YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- – L45: draw wire along X-axis or Y-axis ﬁrst, then along 45-degrees direction.
- – 45L: draw wire along 45-degrees direction, then along X-axis or Yaxis.


![image 2599](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2599.png)

- Figure 52.13 Snap Mode
- – Acute Angle: only draws path in acute angle.


- • Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes the mouse position on the path’s point list.


- – Left: if move the path from bottom to up, mouse pointer is located the left of middle line. more information see following ﬁgure. Start is the ﬁrst point of path, the small rectangle is mouse pointer.

![image 2600](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2600.png)

Figure 52.14 Justiﬁcation: Left

- – Center: mouse pointer is always on the middle line of path.
- – Right: if move the path from bottom to up, mouse pointer is located the right of middle line. more information see following ﬁgure. Start is the ﬁrst point of path, the small rectangle is mouse pointer.


![image 2601](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2601.png)

Figure 52.15 Justiﬁcation: Right

- • Oﬀset: speciﬁes oﬀset of the mouse pointer.
- • Convert Non-orthogonal Path to Polygon on Grid: converts the non-orthogonal path to polygon, and snap polygon to grid.


Shield Path: creates shield path.

- • Width: speciﬁes width of shield path.
- • Space: speciﬁes space between shield paths.
- • Mode: speciﬁes how to place shield paths. Default is Entire Bus.


- – Every Path: speciﬁes to set shield path among every path.


![image 2602](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2602.png)

- Figure 52.16 Every Path


- – Entire Bus: speciﬁes to set shield path among the entire bus.


![image 2603](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2603.png)

- Figure 52.17 Entire Bus


- • Top/Bottom Path: speciﬁes whether create top/bottom layer path when creating shield path. This option only can be operated after checked Shield Path. The default is checked.


More Options for Via: speciﬁes more options for via.

- • Change To: speciﬁes which layer to switch. These layers must be deﬁned in via rule. + and - are short-cuts to switch layer.
- • Via Rule: speciﬁes which via rule to use when switching layer. These via rules must be deﬁned in Technology Manager.
- • Via Type: speciﬁes rows and columns of via.

– Max: speciﬁes rows and columns of via in the path at most. The

calculation is applied automatically.

– User: speciﬁes rows and columns of via by user self. In this mode,

Double Via can not be set. ∗ Rows: speciﬁes rows of via, valid is from 1 to 200, default is 1. ∗ Cols: speciﬁes columns of via, valid is from 1 to 200, default is

1.

- • Corner Via Align: speciﬁes how to align via when switch layer.


![image 2604](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2604.png)

- – : aligns via in horizontal center.


- – : aligns via in horizontal.

![image 2605](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2605.png)

![image 2606](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2606.png)

![image 2607](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2607.png)

- • Extend Path At Layer Jumping: extend path when switching layer.

More Options for Bus: speciﬁes more options for bus.

- • Number: speciﬁes path number of bus. Default is 1, valid is from 1 to 10000.
- • By: speciﬁes space or pitch to use.

Net Name: speciﬁes a net name for the current wire. The created wire is added to the speciﬁed net. A new net is created if the speciﬁed one does not exist. Bundle name or bus name is not acceptable.

Probe Nets: creates probes for the speciﬁed net. Width Mode: speciﬁes how to select width of wire. Default is Fixed

##### Width.

- • Default Width: speciﬁes the width of wire. Width is equal to minimum width of current layer that is deﬁned in Technology File. Note that width is not allowed to edit.
- • Fixed Width: speciﬁes the width of wire. Width is equal to minimum width of current layer if it is deﬁned in Technology File. If the value of width has not been deﬁned, Aether will use manufacturing grid * 2 as the default value of width, or Aether will use the value that user inputs. Width is allowed to edit, and value must be even multiple number of manufacturing grid.


Width: speciﬁes the current wire width. : resets wire width as minimum width.

Auto Detect: detects an object’s layer and attributes when clicking the ﬁrst end of a wire automatically. When clicking for creating a wire, the attributes of the creating wire can be determined from a detected object, such as a wire, a via, or another pin in layer view.

- • Detect Layer: sets wire’s layer as the layer of a detected object automatically. Simultaneously, when detected object is wire, wire style can be adjusted to smooth turning structure.

Begin Style: speciﬁes the begin extension of wire. End Style: speciﬁes the end extension of wire. You can create a wire with two diﬀerent styles.

- • End Type: speciﬁes the type of path.


- – truncate: this style results in no extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.
- – extend: this style results in a one-half width extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.
- – round: this style results in an octagonal extension with 3 edges which extend one-third the path width.
- – antiESD: this style can have an extension and corner for the path. Only paths with this style may have a Corner and End.

∗ Corner: sets the corner extension. Valid value is from zero to width.

∗ End: sets the beginning/ending extension. Valid value is from zero to half of width.

- – variable: this style can have a beginning extension diﬀerent from the ending extension. Only paths with this style may have a Begin and End set.


∗ Begin: sets the beginning extension. ∗ End: sets the ending extension.

Net Name: speciﬁes the net names for creating a wire bus. The net names could be speciﬁed in one of the following ways:

- • By specifying a bundle name, such as netA, netB<0>, netC<1>, netD, where the net names are separated by commas.
- • By specifying a bus name, such as net<0:2>. If you specify a bus name, the bus name expands to display individual net names, such as net<0>, net<1>, net<2>, in the Net Name when you move the cursor to another ﬁeld in the form. The number in the Number also updates based on the number of nets speciﬁed in the Net Name. For example, the Number updates to 3 for the bus name net<0:2>.
- • By specifying a bus base name, such as netA or netB, and additionally setting the bus cardinality in the Number. The bus base name expands to display individual net names in the Net Name only after you start creating the wire bus. For example, if you start creating a bus by specifying the bus base name as netA and setting the Number to 6, the wire


bus creation begins with 6 wires that are assigned to netA<0>, netA<1>, netA<2>, netA<3>, netA<4>, net<5> nets.

New nets are created if the ones speciﬁed do not already exist. If you start creating a wire bus from existing pins, the net names are automatically picked from the net of the pins. If you create the wire bus in blank area without specifying net names, the wire bus created is not assigned to any net and therefore, does not have any connectivity.

Probe Nets: creates probes for the speciﬁed net. Refer To Schematic: ﬁlls Net Name with names of selected nets of Aether schematic when invoke this command.

Width Mode: speciﬁes how to select the width of Wire Bus. Default is Fixed Width.

- • Default Width: speciﬁes the width of Wire Bus. Width is equal to minimum width of current layer that is deﬁned in Technology File. Note that Width is not allowed to edit.
- • Fixed Width: speciﬁes the width of Wire Bus for current layer. Width is equal to minimum width of current layer if it is deﬁned in Technology File. If the value of width has not been deﬁned, Aether will use manufacturing grid * 2 as the default value of width, or use the value that user inputs. Width is allowed to edit, and value must be even multiple number of manufacturing grid.
- • Same Width: speciﬁes the width of Wire Bus for all layer. Width is equal to minimum width of current layer if it is deﬁned in Technology File. If the value of width has not been deﬁned, Aether will use manufacturing grid * 2 as the default value of width, or use the value that user inputs. Width is allowed to edit, and value must be even multiple number of manufacturing grid.


Space Mode: speciﬁes how to select the space of Wire Bus. Default is Fixed Space.

- • Default: speciﬁes the space of Wire Bus. Space is equal to minimum space of current layer that is deﬁned in Technology File. Note that Space is not allowed to edit.
- • Fixed: speciﬁes the space of Wire Bus. Space is equal to minimum space of current layer if it is deﬁned in Technology File. If the value of space has not been deﬁned, Aether will use manufacture 0 as the default value of space, or use the value that user inputs. Space is allowed to edit.
- • Source: speciﬁes the space of Wire Bus space with selected object. Space is allowed to edit.


Width: speciﬁes the current Wire Bus width.

: resets Wire Bus width as mininum width. Space: speciﬁes the current Wire Bus space. : resets Wire Bus space as mininum space.

Menu: Create -> Bus ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

Net Name: speciﬁes the net names for creating a bus. The net names could be speciﬁed in one of the following ways:

- • By specifying a bundle name, such as netA, netB<0>, netC<1>, netD, where the net names are separated by commas.
- • By specifying a bus name, such as net<0:2>. If you specify a bus name, the bus name expands to display individual net names, such as net<0>, net<1>, net<2>, in the Net Name when you move the cursor to another ﬁeld in the form. The number in the Number also updates based on the


- number of nets speciﬁed in the Net Name. For example, the Number updates to 3 for the bus name net<0:2>.
- • By specifying a bus base name, such as netA or netB, and additionally setting the bus cardinality in the Number. The bus base name expands to display individual net names in the Net Name only after you start creating the bus. For example, if you start creating a bus by specifying the bus base name as netA and setting the Number to 6, the bus creation begins with 6 paths that are assigned to netA<0>, netA<1>, netA<2>, netA<3>, netA<4>, net<5> nets.


New nets are created if the ones speciﬁed do not already exist. Probe Nets: creates probes for the speciﬁed net. Snap Mode: speciﬁes how to draw bus.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis.
- • YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- • L45: draw wire along X-axis or Y-axis ﬁrst, then along 45-degrees direction.
- • 45L: draw wire along 45-degrees direction, then along X-axis or Y-axis.

![image 2765](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2765.png)

Figure 52.137 Snap Mode

- • Acute Angle: only draws path in acute angle.


Real Time MR: If it is checked, program will measure resistance when you create bus. But you need set sheet resistance in Technology Manager before you use it.

![image 2766](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2766.png)

- Figure 52.138 Show Resistance When Creating Bus

Real Time MC: If it is checked, program will measure capacitance when you create bus. But you need to set Tech File(.etf), RC Table(.table), Layer Map(.map) in RCExplorer-> RC Setup... before you use it.

![image 2767](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2767.png)

- Figure 52.139 Show Capacitance When Creating Bus


End Type: speciﬁes the type of path in bus.

- • truncate: this style results in no extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.
- • extend: this style results in a one-half width extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.
- • round: this style results in an octagonal extension with 3 edges which extend one-third the path width.
- • antiESD: this style can have an extension and corner for the path. Only paths with this style may have a Corner and End.


– Corner: sets the corner extension. Valid value is from zero to width. – End: sets the beginning/ending extension. Valid value is from zero

to half of width.

- • variable: this style can have a beginning extension diﬀerent from the ending extension. Only paths with this style may have a Begin and End set.


- – Begin: sets the beginning extension.
- – End: sets the ending extension.


![image 2768](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2768.png)

Figure 52.140 Path Type

Number: speciﬁes path number of bus. Default is 1, valid is from 1 to 10000. Negative: speciﬁes space or pitch is negative or not.

![image 2769](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2769.png)

![image 2770](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2770.png)

(a) Turn Oﬀ (b) Turn On

Figure 52.141 Negative

Note: notice the small rectangle in ﬁgure above. Reverse Order At Corner: speciﬁes reverse order at every corner of bus.

![image 2771](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2771.png)

![image 2772](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2772.png)

(a) Turn Oﬀ (b) Turn On

Figure 52.142 Reverse Order at Corner

Width: speciﬁes bus width. It can be 0.5 0.2. It means the width of ﬁrst path is 0.5, the second is 0.2, the third is 0.5 again, and so on.

Width Step: speciﬁes step of path width. By: speciﬁes space or pitch to use.

- • Space: speciﬁes distance between edges of paths. It can be set as 0.3 0.2.
- • Pitch: speciﬁes distance between center line of paths. It can be set as 0.3 0.2.
- • Space Step: speciﬁes step of space or pitch.


Increment of 45◦: speciﬁes spaces between the paths at the 45◦ segment. It is only valid when Snape Mode is Diagonal, L45, 45L. Space is equal to Space + Increment of 45◦. For example, we set Space to 0.2, Increment of 45◦ to 0.2 too, the space should be 0.4. But because the segment at 45 is oﬀ grid, we can measure it only in approximation.

![image 2773](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2773.png)

Figure 52.143 Increment of 45◦

Multiple of MinSpace: speciﬁes the multiple of min space. Space is equal to MINYSPACE * multiple. Minspace is deﬁned in technology.

Auto Update Space: speciﬁes update space automatically. If it turns on, Multiple of MinSpace can work.

Multi-Layer: speciﬁes which layers to create bus. The paths in bus may be in diﬀerent layers.

## 52.8 Instance

Menu: Create -> Instance ToolBar: BindKey: I Tcl Command: None

![image 2776](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2776.png)

This command is used to create instance. An instance is a reference to a design, representing the inclusion of that design as a part of the contents of a diﬀerent design. The referenced design is the master of the instance. Designer can design a hierarchy circuit by Create Instance.

![image 2777](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2777.png)

Figure 52.146 Create Instance

Library Name: speciﬁes library. Cell Name: speciﬁes cell. View Name: speciﬁes view. Instance Name: speciﬁes instance name. The instance name must be unique among all instances.

- • Preﬁx of instance Name is referenced from:

- – system property named InstName Preﬁx in Design Property.
- – Device Type in Device Deﬁne.
- – Default preﬁx is I_ followed by an arbitrary integer.


- • Instance names could be separated by space, for example, I0 I1 I2.
- • I<0> and I<0:10> are valid.


Magnify: speciﬁes instance magnify.

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 2778](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2778.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees.
- • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees.
- • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.


![image 2779](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2779.png)

- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for MX.

![image 2780](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2780.png)

- • MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


At Origin: speciﬁes the origin of instance. Where the origin of the instance’s master is located relative to the coordinate system of the parent design in which the instance is placed. By this option, instance’s origin coincides with origin of master of instance. It is mutual exclusive with Justiﬁcation.

Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes how to locate the original point of object. Aether calculates the original point based on the Justiﬁcation and the object’s bounding box.

- • LeftBottom
- • CenterBottom
- • RightBottom
- • LeftCenter
- • CenterCenter
- • RightCenter
- • LeftTop
- • CenterTop
- • RightTop Now we use labels to explain it. Please notice the little cross near the labels.


![image 2781](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2781.png)

Figure 52.147 Justiﬁcation Example

Array: speciﬁes array of instances.

- • Rows: speciﬁes row number of array instance. Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- • Cols: speciﬁes column number of array instance. Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.
- • Manual: speciﬁes distance between instances by manual.
- • Snap: speciﬁes snap mode of array instance in Manual.

- – AnyAngle: places array instance at any angle.
- – Diagonal: places array instance at X/Y direction and 45-degree


direction.

– Orthogonal: places array instance at X/Y direction only.

- • Pitch: speciﬁes distance between instances by pitch.

– Y-Pitch: speciﬁes sum of distance between instances and length of

boundary of instance in Y direction.

– X-Pitch: speciﬁes sum of distance between instances and length of

boundary of instance in X direction.

– : calculates the Y-Pitch automatically. – : calculates the X-Pitch automatically.

![image 2782](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2782.png)

![image 2783](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2783.png)

- • Space: speciﬁes distance between instances by space.

- – Y-Space: speciﬁes distance between instances in Y direction.
- – X-Space: speciﬁes distance between instances in X direction.
- – : calculates the Y-Space automatically.

![image 2784](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2784.png)

- – : calculates the X-Space automatically.


![image 2785](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2785.png)

- • Auto Update Pitch/Space: speciﬁes distance between instances by pitch.


Parameters: speciﬁes parameters of instance. If master is a parametrized cell, you should specify its parameters when creating instance of it. Parameters are diﬀerent when you create diﬀerent instance.

• Reset All: resets all parameters to default value.

Show Instance Contents: shows contents of instance in cartoon. It is useful to align instance with some shapes. Space can turn on/oﬀ this option.

: clears contents of Label quickly. Expand Bus Label: switches on the parser for bus label.

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.
