Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes how to locate the original point of object. Aether calculates the original point based on the Justiﬁcation and the object’s bounding box.

- • LeftBottom
- • CenterBottom
- • RightBottom
- • LeftCenter


- • CenterCenter
- • RightCenter
- • LeftTop
- • CenterTop
- • RightTop Now we use labels to explain it. Please notice the little cross near the labels.


![image 2811](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2811.png)

Figure 52.164 Justiﬁcation Example

Method speciﬁes the method to create label.

- • Step: creates labels one by one. It is default.
- • Serial: creates the serial labels as a sequence or a matrix, when there is more than one label deﬁned in Label.


- – Snap: speciﬁes snap mode when creating labels. ∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. ∗ XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. ∗ YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- – Array: speciﬁes expanding method.


∗ Checked: creates the bus labels as a matrix whose ﬁrst dimension length is deﬁned in Rows. The ﬁrst of all labels and the oﬀsets of both dimensions will be determined with sequential LBM-Click for three times. However, it will be created as a sequence while the labels are not suﬃcient.

∗ Unchecked: creates the labels as a sequence. The ﬁrst label and the oﬀset will be speciﬁed by LBM-Click successively.

- – Rows: speciﬁes ﬁrst dimension length while the Array is checked.


- • Batch: creates more labels at one time. You should specify the space between the labels.

– X Spacing: speciﬁes the space align x-direction. – Y Spacing: speciﬁes the space align y-direction.

- • Line: creates more labels when you draw a line overlap shapes.

- – Snap: speciﬁes snap mode when creating labels. ∗ AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle. ∗ Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle. ∗ Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. ∗ XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. ∗ YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.
- – Auto Rotate: Aether will rotate the label according to direction of line.
- – Selected Objects Only: only creates labels on shapes which ∗ overlaps with line. ∗ is selected.
- – Skip Width > =: skips the shapes which width is greater than or equal to speciﬁed width.


- • Whole: speciﬁes to create one label even if there are spaces between them. For example, A B C D, Aether will create only one label ‘A B C D’ when Whole is selected. And Expand Bus Label is invalid too.
- • Label Layer: speciﬁes which layer to create label.


- – Auto: speciﬁes layer according rule Label Layer in Technology Manager.
- – Active Layer: speciﬁes active layer as label layer.
- – Select Layer: speciﬁes the layer of label.


Attach To Shape: attaches the label to speciﬁed shape. After attached, label should be copied/moved/deleted when attached shape is copied/moved/deleted. It is valid when Method is Step, Line, Whole. Default is oﬀ.

Keep Last Label: keeps the last label in Label when there is no label left. Default is oﬀ

##### Convert To Polygon Text: converts label to polygon.

- • Non45: does not allow 45 degree segment.
- • Snap Grid: snap points of polygon to grid.
- • Space: speciﬁes distance between labels.
- • Polygon Width: speciﬁes the width of edges of polygon. It should be an even. And you can set cd-font-path in section Options of aether.rc by custom deﬁned font.


Auto: selects Auto mode. Label can be created by automation.

![image 2812](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2812.png)

Figure 52.165 Create Auto Label

- • From Pin/Net: sets pin and shape that can be created label from net name. If state is unchecked, pin and shape cannot be created label. The default state is checked.
- • From Instance: sets instance that can be created label from instance name or cell name. If state is unchecked, instance cannot be created label. The default state is checked.
- • Instance Name: sets instance that can be created label from instance name. The default state is checked.
- • Cell Name: sets instance that can be created label from cell name. The default state is unchecked.

## 52.13 Pin

Menu: Create -> Pin

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2850](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2850.png)

This command is used to create pin. Pin represents the physical connections of terminals to nets. A terminal can have multiple pins where multiple physical connections can correspond to one logical connection.

![image 2851](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2851.png)

Figure 52.197 Create Pin Form

##### Mode: switches Manual or Auto mode.

- • Manual: creates pin by manual mode. This option is default.
- • Auto: creates pin by auto mode.


Manual: speciﬁes Manual mode to create pin.

![image 2852](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2852.png)

###### Figure 52.198 Create Pin Form

Pin Names: speciﬁes pin names. It supports bus names.

- • X-Pitch: speciﬁes the distance between pins in x-direction. It is valid when you create bus pin, for example, A< 1:10> .
- • Y-Pitch: speciﬁes the distance between pins in y-direction. It is valid when you create bus pin, for example, A< 1:10> .


Pick Nets: picks nets from schematic view or ﬁle. Aether will treat nets as pins.

![image 2853](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2853.png)

Figure 52.199 Pick Nets

- • From Schematic: picks nets from schematic view. It is default.

- – Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of schematic view.
- – Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of schematic view.
- – View Name: speciﬁes the view name of schematic view.
- – : short-cut to pop up browser to select schematic view.

![image 2854](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2854.png)

- – : reloads nets from schematic view.

![image 2855](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2855.png)

- – Exclude Default Nets: removes the default nets from nets in schematic view.
- – Pin Only: lists the pins in Nets & Pins.
- – Select: selects the name from the edit box below.
- – Split Bus Net: lists the bus net in bit form, such as bus net A< 0:2> will be split into A< 0> ,A< 1> and A< 2> .
- – Nets & Pins: lists the nets and pins in schematic view.
- – : adds selected nets and pins to Pin Names.


![image 2856](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2856.png)

- • From File: picks nets from speciﬁed ﬁle. Aether will add the nets’ name to Pin Names automatically. There should be only one word per line in the ﬁle.


- Net1

- Net2


- Net3


Overbar: adds overline on the pin name. Aether implements overline by underscore(_). For example, when you specify pin name as a_bc_d, the eﬀect is as follows:

Figure 52.200 Overbar for Create Pin

Keep First Name: keeps the ﬁrst name to used as pin name always. Auto Arrange: arranges pins automatically. It is valid when you create bus pin, for example, A<1:10>.

Create Label: speciﬁes the generated pin label mode when creating pin, you can use the Manual mode to place the label on the speciﬁed location or use the Auto mode to generate pin label automatically.

- • Manual: creates pin label by manual mode.
- • Auto: creates pin label by auto mode. This option is selected by default. More Options: speciﬁes more options.

## 52.14 P and R Objects

### 52.14.1 Boundary

Menu: Create -> P&R Objects -> Boundary ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2902](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2902.png)

This command is used to create boundary in current design view.

Boundary Type: speciﬁes create boundary type.

- • P&R: in digital circuit design, P&R boundary is applications that limit the scope of the place and route of the block boundaries. Only one P&R boundary is allowed per cellview.


![image 2903](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2903.png)

Figure 52.238 P&R Boundary

- • Snap: snap boundary is an application that supports the design of any line macro or standard cell. Snap boundary must be rectangular, and snap boundary is needed to snap cells with straight (non-rectangular) P&R boundary. As P&R boundary, only one snap boundary is allowed per cellview.

![image 2904](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2904.png)

Figure 52.239 Snap Boundary

- • Area: area boundary is used for physical block, it is used to indicate an area of the block, and it is used for various purposes deﬁned by the design method. Each area boundary has a unique name.


![image 2905](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2905.png)

Figure 52.240 Area Boundary

Create Method: speciﬁes create method which method is used to create the boundary objects.

- • Select From Layout: selects the objects you need from current design. Once you have selected the objects, use the OK or Hide button to create the boundary.
- • Rectangle: creates a rectangle area for the boundary. Press OK or Hide button and draw a rectangle on the design.
- • Polygon: speciﬁes a polygon area for the boundary. In the P&R boundary type and Area boundary type, valid snap modes are any angle, diagonal, orthogonal, xﬁrst, yﬁrst.


Example 52.31

The example shows how to create an area boundary.

- 1. Select the objects from layout, as follows:

![image 2906](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2906.png)

Figure 52.241 Create Area Boundary Result

- 2. Choose Create -> P&R Objects -> Boundary. From the Boundary Type choose Area. In the Boundary Name ﬁeld, type the name of the library you want to create, such as test. From the Create Method choose Select From Layout, as follows:

![image 2907](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2907.png)

Figure 52.242 Form Settings

- 3. Press OK. The area of the selected objects shows a yellow boundary, as follows:


![image 2908](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2908.png)

Figure 52.243 Create Area Boundary Result

### 52.14.2 Blockage

Menu: Create -> P&R Objects -> Blockage ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2909](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2909.png)

This command is used to create blockage in current design view.

![image 2910](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2910.png)

Figure 52.244 Create Blockage Form

Blockage Type: selects the type of blockage to create.

- • Placement: in this area, you cannot place instances.
- • Routing: in this area, you cannot create vias or routes for a wire.
- • Pin: in the blockage area and layer, you cannot created pins.
- • Screen: only when nets reach the maximum density speciﬁed on the blockage can nets be created in the blockage area.


- • Slot: in the blocked area on its layer, you cannot create slotting.
- • Fill: in the blocked area on its layer, you cannot create ﬁll.
- • Wiring: in the blockage area on the given layer, you cannot create wires, except for stacked vias.
- • Feedthru: in the blockage area, you cannot create feedthrus.


Material: selects is the material of blockage. However, there are some special types of blockages that cannot select the material. When Blockage Type is Placement, the Material ﬁeld will be grayed out.

![image 2911](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2911.png)

Figure 52.245 Material’s Choose Area

Layer: selects the layer based on the selected material. The layers displayed are those with one of the above materials, which are deﬁned in the technology ﬁle. The default material is all . When Blockage Type is Placement, the Layer ﬁeld will be grayed out.

Max Density: When Blockage Type is Placement or Screen, you can set maximum percentage of the total design area that the metal may occupy.

Attach To Owner: according to the type of blockage, an instance or a cluster is designated as the owner of the blockage.

Snap Mode: selects mode to use when you enter points.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. • YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.

### 52.14.3 Track

Menu: Create -> P&R Objects -> Track ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2914](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2914.png)

This command is used to create track in layout view.

![image 2915](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2915.png)

Figure 52.248 Create Track Form

Layer Filter: ﬁlters the created track which according to the choose conditionse. Default is ALL .

Direction: speciﬁes track’s direction. Default is Horizontal.

- • Horizontal: creates track’s direction is Horizontal.
- • Vertical: creates track’s direction is Vertical. Layer: speciﬁes the layer to create the track. Width: speciﬁes the range of desirable widths for wire creation. Speacing: speciﬁes the distance between two tracks. Default is 0.005. Count: speciﬁes the number of tracks. Default is 1. Create In Entire Design Area: creates Track in the entire draw area.


Origin Oﬀset: if Direction is Horizontal, the bottom track y coordinate will be set up. if Direction is Vertical, the most left track x coordinate will be set up. Default is 0.

Name: speciﬁes the name to create the track.

### 52.14.4 Row

Menu: Create -> P&R Objects -> Boundary ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2920](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2920.png)

This command is used to create row in layout view.

![image 2921](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2921.png)

Figure 52.253 Create Row Form

Base Name: speciﬁes the name for each row objects created. Row Orientation: speciﬁes the row orientation as Horizontal or Vertical. Default is Horizontal. Site Rotation: speciﬁes the rotation mode. Default value is R0. Flip Every Other Row: speciﬁes the ﬂip mode. Flip every other row in the site.

• Flip The First Row: speciﬁes the ﬂip mode. Flip the ﬁrst row in the site.

Abut: speciﬁes the abut mode. Detail settings are below:

- • Rows: speciﬁes the number of rows on abut mode. The number must be positive integer.
- • Abut Every Other: speciﬁes every other row on abut mode
- • Abut The First Row: speciﬁes the ﬁrst and second rows on abut mode


Row Spacing: speciﬁes the row spacing between rows created. The number

can be ﬂoating-point. This row spacing value is overridden if specifying the abut mode.

Filter By Site Deﬁnition: speciﬁes the ﬁlter mode for site deﬁnitions. Core mode for core site deﬁnitions, Pad mode for pad site deﬁnitions and All mode for all the site deﬁnitions.

- • Site Template: shows all site deﬁnition names. You can select one site name at a time.
- • Technology Library: shows the library which have been selected in the


##### Site Template option.

• Site Information: shows all the type of site deﬁnitions that is the current site in the Site Template option. This information contains the type (core or pad), the width and height of the site deﬁnition, and three types of symmetry.

Method: speciﬁes the create method. There are two methods: Assisted and Area Fill, default is Assisted method.

- • Assisted: speciﬁes the Assisted method to create speciﬁed number of rows and sites.

- – Rows: speciﬁes the number of rows to create. The number should be greater than or equal to 1.
- – Sites: speciﬁes the number of sites in a row. The number should be greater than or equal to 1, default value is 1.


- • Area Fill: speciﬁes the Area Fill method to create rows in the giving area.


- – Type: speciﬁes the area build type. See details below.

∗ Rectangular: speciﬁes the rectangular build type. Create a rectangular area in which as many sites possible will ﬁt.

∗ Rectilinear: speciﬁes the rectilinear build type. Create a polygon area with rows that follow the edges of the polygon.

∗ Partition: speciﬁes the partition build type. Create rows within a pre-deﬁned areas.

- – Oﬀset: speciﬁes the oﬀset value between area and created rows. The diﬀerent oﬀset values can place asymmetrical rows in the area. There are four oﬀset values in four directions listed below.


∗ Top: speciﬁes the top oﬀset value between top of the area and created rows.

∗ Bottom: speciﬁes the bottom oﬀset value between bottom of the area and created rows.

∗ Left: speciﬁes the left oﬀset value between left of the area and created rows.

∗ Right: speciﬁes the right oﬀset value between right of the area and created rows.

Example 52.34 The example shows the diﬀerent rows created on diﬀerent options.

- 1. Choose Create -> P&R Objectes -> Row. Set the Row Spacing to 0.5, set the Rows to 4 and set the Sites to 2. The rows created in diﬀerent Row Orientation are as follows:

Name: sets a new wsp name or speciﬁes an existing wsp name. Layer: speciﬁes track’s layer. Direction: speciﬁes track’s direction.

- • Horizontal: creates track’s direction is Horizontal.
- • Vertical: creates track’s direction is Vertical. Period Oﬀset: speciﬁes oﬀset of the ﬁrst period. Auto Compute Period: speciﬁes width of every period, if was checked, the width will be computed automatically. Allowed Repeat Mode: speciﬁes allowed repeat mode.
- • Any: every mode of Default Repeat Mode is useable.
- • None: only None mode of Default Repeat Mode is useable.
- • Stepped Only: only Stepped mode of Default Repeat Mode is useable.


##### • Flipped Only: Flipped Starts With Odd and Flipped Starts WithEven mode of Default Repeat Mode are useable.

Default Repeat Mode: speciﬁes default repeat mode.

- • None: only creates data, but doesn’t use it any time.
- • Stepped: all the periods are same.
- • Flipped Starts With Odd: ﬂippeds every odd periods.
- • Flipped Starts With Even: ﬂippeds every even periods. Repeat Oﬀset: speciﬁes repeat oﬀset mode.
- • All Periods: speciﬁes the ﬁrst track’s oﬀset of every periods.
- • First Period Only: speciﬁes the ﬁrst track’s oﬀset of the ﬁrst period. Track Color: speciﬁes track color mode.
- • Alternate: starts from the ﬁrst track’s color, and alternates every tracks’s color.
- • As Speciﬁed: user speciﬁes every track’s color.
- • As Speciﬁed With Period Shift: user speciﬁes every track’s color of


the ﬁrst period, and alternates the track’s color in every period. First Track Oﬀset: speciﬁes the oﬀset of ﬁrst track. Preview: shows preview by settings. Create: creates a new wsp by settings. Update: updates current wsp by settings. Delete: deletes current wsp. Clear: sets all items to default. Close: closes form, and exists command.

![image 2934](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2934.png)

Figure 52.260 WSP Manager Import Form

Library Name: sets the library name of the imported design. Cell Name: sets the cell name of the imported design. View Name: sets the view name of the imported design. Width Spacing Patterns: shows all wsp from the imported design. Tracks: shows all tracks of the selected wsp. Preview: shows preview by selected wsp. Import All: imports all wsp. Import Select: imports the selected wsp. Close: closes form, and exists command.

## 52.15 Flexible Path

Menu: Create -> Flexible Path ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2945](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2945.png)

This command is used to create a ﬂexible path. A ﬂexible path consists of a master path and several subparts. The master path is similar to path and there are three types of subparts: Oﬀset Subpath, Enclosure Subpath, and Subrectangle. All subparts are related to the master path, but independent of each other. Every kind of subpart can have multiple independent items.

![image 2946](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2946.png)

Figure 52.271 Create Flexible Path Form

Template: speciﬁes the template used to create a ﬂexible path. Template Name: shows the name of the ﬂexible path template. Technology Library: speciﬁes the technology library that contains ﬂexible path templates.

Keep Default Layer: if this option is checked, the ﬁled object layer in option Layer will synchronize correspondingly with the layers selected in LSW.

Drawing Type: speciﬁes the drawing mode of ﬂexible path. Path: draws a ﬂexible path like a path. Rectangular: draws a ﬂexible path around border box of selected shape(s). Rectilinear: draws a ﬂexible path around outline of selected shape(s).

Parameter: shows the parameters of the master path. Layer: speciﬁes the layer name of the master path. Width: speciﬁes the width of the master path.

Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the master path to the mouse point. A positive value means the master is on the left side of the mouse point, and a negative value means it is on the right side.

Choppable: if this option is checked, the master path can be chopped. If the master path is choppable, the subparts must be choppable. If the master path is not choppable, the subparts can be choppable or not.

End Type: speciﬁes the type of master path. If the type of master path is truncate, extend or round, the sub-paths will follow it. If the type of master path is variable, the type of sub paths will become truncate.

truncate: this style results in no extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.

extend: this style results in a one-half width extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the path.

round: this style results in an octagonal extension with 3 edges which extend one-third of the path width.

variable: this style can have a beginning extension diﬀerent from the ending extension. Only paths with this style may have a Begin Extension and End Extension set.

Begin Extension: sets the beginning extension. End Extension: sets the ending extension.

![image 2947](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2947.png)

Figure 52.272 End Type

Enclose By: speciﬁes the distance between the ﬂexible path and the objects that the ﬂexible path will surround.

Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes the reference side on the master path. Left: speciﬁes the left edge of the master path as reference side. Center: speciﬁes the centerline of the master path as reference side. Right: speciﬁes the right edge of the master path as reference side.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes snap mode to create ﬂexible path. Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle. Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.

Subpart: clicks the button to launch parameters setting form of subparts.

![image 2948](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2948.png)

Figure 52.273 Subpart Form

Conﬁguration: shows the parameters of subparts.

![image 2949](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2949.png)

Figure 52.274 Subpart - Conﬁguration Form

Add: clicks the button to add a subpart. Del: clicks the button to delete a subpart. Edit: clicks the button to apply the modiﬁed parameters to the selected subpart. Oﬀset Subpath: speciﬁes the parameters of oﬀset subpaths.

![image 2950](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2950.png)

Figure 52.275 Subpart - Oﬀset Subpath Tab

Layer: speciﬁes the layer name of the subpath. Choppable: if this option is checked, the subpath can be chopped. Begin Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the start of the subpath to the start of the master path. End Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the end of the subpath to the end of the master path. Width: speciﬁes the width of the subpath. Separation: speciﬁes the distance from the subpath to Justiﬁcation. Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes the reference side on the master path for the subpath alignment.

Left: speciﬁes the left edge of the master path as reference side. The right edge of the subpath is separated from the left edge of the master path.

Center: speciﬁes the centerline of the master path as reference side. The centerline of the subpath is separated from the centerline of the master path.

Right: speciﬁes the right edge of the master path as reference side. The left edge of the subpath is separated from the left edge of the master path.

Enclosure Subpath: speciﬁes the parameters of enclosure subpaths.

![image 2951](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2951.png)

Figure 52.276 Subpart - Enclosure Subpath Tab

Layer: speciﬁes the layer name of the subpath. Choppable: if this option is checked, the subpath can be chopped. Begin Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the start of the subpath to the start of the master path. End Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the end of the subpath to the end of the master path.

Enclosure: speciﬁes the enclosure value of the subpath relative to the master path. The calculating formula is Width of Enclosure Subpath = Width of Master Path - 2 * Enclosure.

Subrectangle: speciﬁes the parameters of subrectangles.

![image 2952](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2952.png)

Figure 52.277 Subpart - Subrectangle Tab

Layer: speciﬁes the layer name of the subrectangles. Choppable: if this option is checked, the subrectangles can be chopped. Diagonal: if this option is checked and Width = Length, subrectangles can be created on diagonal segments of the path. Begin Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the start of the ﬁrst subrectangle to the start of the master path. End Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the end of the last subrectangle to the end of the master path. Begin Segment Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the start of the ﬁrst subrectangle to the start of the master path in a segment. End Segment Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the end of the last subrectangle to the end of the master path in a segment. Width: speciﬁes the length of the rectangle which is perpendicular to the centerline of the master path.

Length: speciﬁes the length of the rectangle which is parallel to the centerline of the master path.

Space: speciﬁes the minimum distance between adjacent rectangles. Separation: speciﬁes the distance from the subrectangles to Justiﬁcation. Gap: speciﬁes how the rectangles are distributed.

distribute: places rectangles as evenly as possible in each segment, while keeping the spacing no less than Space.

minimum: places rectangles with the value of Space in each segment.

Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes the reference side on the master path for the subrectangle alignment.

Left: speciﬁes the left edge of the master path as reference side. The right edge of the subrectangle is separated from the left edge of the master path.

Center: speciﬁes the centerline of the master path as reference side. The centerline of the subrectangle is separated from the centerline of the master path.

Right: speciﬁes the right edge of the master path as reference side. The left edge of the subrectangle is separated from the right edge of the master path.

Auto Fill: if check this option, Automatically calculate the number of rows of subrectangle that can be placed at the overlapping layers by using the parameters in the Subrectangle interface. According to the layers set in Master Path, Oﬀset Subpath, Enclosure Subpath and Subrectangle, match with the layers in StdVia interface parameters set in Technology Manager.

![image 2953](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2953.png)

Figure 52.278 Subrectangle - Auto Fill Form

||Note: If check this option, Add and Separation are grayed out and unavailable.|
|---|
|
|---|


- Layer1: if check the option of GetParam, display the layer which match with the Layer1 set in StdVia interface.
- Layer2: if check the option of GetParam, display the layer which match with the Layer2 set in StdVia interface.


Rows: the number of rows of subrectangle that can be placed at the overlapping area of Layer1 and Layer2.

GetParam: if check the option, automatically calculate and display the Layer1, Layer2 and Rows. Rows = Overlap of Layer1 and Layer2 - 2 * Max (Begin Oﬀset, End Oﬀset ) / ( Space + Width ) of Subrectangle .

![image 2954](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2954.png)

- Figure 52.279 Calculate Rows


||Note: If costom click this option multiple times, it will be displayed according to the lastest setting, regradless of whether it has been added to subrectangle list. Be careful not to add it repeatedly.|
|---|
|
|---|


Add: adds the checked corresponding list to the subrectangle Conﬁguration list by row, and automatically calculate the separation of each row.

![image 2955](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2955.png)

- Figure 52.280 Result of Auto Fill

||Note: Before using this function, custom need to set the Master Path, Oﬀset Subpath, Enclosure Subpath and Subrectangle ﬁrst otherwise the function cannot ﬁnd the area that can be ﬁlled with subrectangle according to the layer relationship.|
|---|
|
|---|


![image 2956](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2956.png)

![image 2957](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2957.png)

- Figure 52.281 Expand Menu Form


Help: clicks it to show the manual. Default: clicks it to default parameters.

Save Multi Template: saves multiple templates, whether the templates are from technology ﬁle, load templates or newly created with name not “New”.

![image 2958](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2958.png)

Figure 52.282 Save Multi Template Form

Select: uses to help customs quickly select the template names ﬁltered by keywords.

## 52.16 Guard Ring

Menu: Create -> Guard Ring ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 2969](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2969.png)

This command is used to create diﬀerent type of Guard Ring. A Guard Ring references a Guard Ring deﬁnition from the technology that corresponds to the design where the Guard Ring exists.

![image 2970](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2970.png)

Figure 52.293 Create Guard Ring Form

Guard Ring Template: shows existing guard ring, which is deﬁned in TM. Top Layer: shows the top layer of guard ring, which will be abled when Contact Mode=Stack Via. Contact Mode: shows contact modes, there are Normal and Stack Via modes. Contact Pattern: shows contact alignment mode.

Center Align: if the minimum via spacing is greater than the contact spacing, the contact spacing and guard ring body will be enlarged.

Max: if choose this option, the via spacing will be ﬁlled as far as possible.

Contact Rows: speciﬁes the contact rows number of guard ring, the default value is 1.

Body Width: speciﬁes the width of body layer, The Body Width and Contact Rows is alternative.

Contact Size: speciﬁes the contact size which is deﬁned in both direction of GuardRing expanding (W) and the perpendicular direction of GuardRing expanding (H) as in Technology Manager.

Contact Spacing: speciﬁes the contact spacing of adjacent contact layers which is deﬁned in both direction of GuardRing expanding (W) and the perpendicular direction of GuardRing expanding (H) as in Technology Manager.

Chamfer Amount: speciﬁes the side of cutting corner.

Metal Width=Body: The width of Metal1 will be the same as the width of body layer. It is enabled to switch and means checked while Contact Mode=Normal.

Same Metal Width: All of metal layers will be enlarged as same as the largest metal layer while checked. It is enabled to switch and means checked while Contact Mode=Stack Via.

Corner Contact: It will be ﬁlled with contacts at the corners while checked. It is checked as default. The 2-dimension deﬁnition of contact will disable it. It means unchecked while disabled no matter if it is checked or disabled before.

Implant Filled: if this option is on, the Implant layer is polygon, otherwise, it will be donut.

Well Filled: if this option is on, the Well layer is polygon, otherwise, it will be donut.

Type: speciﬁes the drawing mode when creating guard ring. There are three types.

Line: create linear type guard ring. When this option is on, Keep Min Met[CO] option appears, as shown below.

![image 2971](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2971.png)

Figure 52.294 Keep Min Met[CO] Option

Start: keeps minCon2MetalEnc rule at the start of guard ring. End: keeps minCon2MetalEnc rule at the end of guard ring.

![image 2972](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2972.png)

Figure 52.295 The Sketch of Keep Min Met[CO] Option

Line: create linear type guard ring. End Style option appears, as shown below.

![image 2973](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2973.png)

Figure 52.296 Create linear type guard ring With Truncate/Extend Style

Tuncate: this style results in no extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the guard ring

![image 2974](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2974.png)

Figure 52.297 Truncate Style

Extend: this style results in a one-half width extension beyond the beginning and ending points for the guard ring

![image 2975](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2975.png)

Figure 52.298 Extend Style

Polygon: create polygon type guard ring.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes snap mode to create guard ring. There are three mode Orthogonal, XFirst and YFirst.

##### Justiﬁcation: align the contact on either Left, Center or Right.

Oﬀset: speciﬁes oﬀset value. The default value is 0. Auto: create guard ring by Generate button.

Layer Spacing Rules: if this option is on, the minimum spacing rules will be used for creating guard ring.

Boundary Spacing: speciﬁes the spacing between instance boundary and guard ring boundary.

Rectangular: automatically create rectangular type guard ring. Rectilinear: automatically create rectilinear type guard ring. Generate!: the button is used to create guard ring automatically.

This command is used to create Advanced Guard Ring.

Figure 52.302 Create Advanced Guard Ring Form

Type: speciﬁes the mode when creating Advanced Guard Ring. There are four types.

Wrap: creates the Advanced Guard Ring around the selected objects. It supports pre-select and select in between the creating action. Click at any position in design and get the Advanced Guard Ring around the selected objects created.

Path: creates path type of Advanced Guard Ring. Rectangle: creates rectangle type of Advanced Guard Ring. Polygon: creates polygon type of Advanced Guard Ring.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes snap mode to create Advanced Guard Ring. It is enabled to switch and means checked while Type=Path or Type=Polygon.

- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XFirst: draws wire along X-axis ﬁrst, then along Y-axis. • YFirst: draws wire along Y-axis ﬁrst, then along X-axis.


Wrap Mode: speciﬁes wrap mode to create Advanced Guard Ring. There are two modes, Rectangular and Rectilinear. Rectangular means wrapping with a rectangle shape. Rectilinear means wrapping with the boundary’s shape. It is enabled to switch and means checked while Type=Wrap.

Technology: shows technology ﬁle name of present library. Device: speciﬁes AGR Pcell when creating Advanced Guard Ring. NetName: speciﬁes net name when creating Advanced Guard Ring.

Spacing: speciﬁes the spaceing between selected objects and Advanced Guard Ring. It is enabled to switch while Type=Wrap. There are two types.

Layer Spacing: if this option is on, the minimum spacing rules will be used for creating Advanced Guard Ring.

Boundary Spacing: speciﬁes the spacing between selected objects’ boundary and Advanced Guard Ring.

Parameters: user-deﬁned parameters. They can be edited in CDF Editor. Reset All: resets all parameters below. Poly Length: speciﬁes the poly length when creating Advanced Guard Ring. Poly Space: speciﬁes the poly space when creating Advanced Guard Ring. Fingers: speciﬁes the ﬁngers when creating Advanced Guard Ring. Fins: speciﬁes the ﬁns when creating Advanced Guard Ring. Top Metal: speciﬁes the top metal when creating Advanced Guard Ring. Voltage Type: speciﬁes the voltage type when creating Advanced Guard Ring.

## 52.18 Via

Menu: Create -> Via ToolBar: BindKey: O Tcl Command: None

![image 2984](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2984.png)

This command is used to create via. A via represents a physical connection between two adjacent route paths that are on diﬀerent layers. A via references a via deﬁnition from the technology that corresponds to the design where the via exists.

A via may be either a standard via or a custom via. A standard via has a predeﬁned set of via parameters that can be tailored to create a variety of vias to cover a variety of connections. The standard via references a standard via deﬁnition.

A custom via is very much like an instance where, through its custom via deﬁnition, another design is referenced. Custom vias often include a set of parameter values that can be used to tailor the master for each speciﬁc via.

A via can represent complex pin ﬁgures although vias are normally associated with routes.

![image 2985](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2985.png)

Figure 52.306 Create Via_Manual Form

Mode: speciﬁes how to create via. There are four modes: Manual, Stack, Auto and Fast Edit, default is Manual.

- • Manual: this option is used to create via manually.


- – Generate From: there are four types for creating via, below for more details.

∗ Array: creates array via by specifying rows and columns. ∗ Size: creates size via by specifying width and height. ∗ Shape: creates vias by selected shape. ∗ Area: creates area via by drawing rectangle and polygon.

- – Constraint Group: speciﬁes the constraint group for via creation.
- – Via Deﬁnition: lists the Standard Via and Custom Via types, which are deﬁned in Technology Manager.
- – Via Type/Tech: displays the via type that is corresponding to the selected via in the Via Deﬁnition, whether it is Standard Via or


- Custom Via, and the name of the current Technology Library. If the selected via in Via Deﬁnition is Standard Via, the text ﬁeld displays Standard Via/TechLib; If the selected via is Custom Via, the text ﬁeld displays Custom Via/TechLib.
- – Rows/Columns: speciﬁes the rows and columns for via. You can click to exchange both Rows and Columns values. And, more remarkable, if user selects the direct via in Via Deﬁnition, the Rows and Columns will change into Width and Height.

![image 2986](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2986.png)

- – Reset Parameters To...: resets the Size, Space and Enclosure values in the form to the technology database values. Which item is set according to the deﬁnition in Options-> Settings-> Route-> Parameters Calculator. When checking Calculate, the drop-down list will also have the following options: Min Rules And ViaDef, Minimum Rules, Minimum Rule Enclosures. When unchecking Calculate, the drop-down list will add ViaDef Defaults and ViaDef Default Enclosures.
- – Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degrees counter-clockwisete, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

∗ R0: represents no change in orientation. ∗ R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. ∗ R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. ∗ R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. ∗ MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. ∗ MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a

rotation of 90 degrees. ∗ MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. ∗ MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a

rotation of 90 degrees.

- – System: speciﬁes the parameters of standard via. It is valid when via type is StdVia.


![image 2987](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2987.png)

Figure 52.307 System Parameters

∗ Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes how to locate the original point of object. Aether calculates the original point based on the Justiﬁcation and the object’s bounding box.

· LeftBottom · CenterBottom · RightBottom · LeftCenter · CenterCenter · RightCenter · LeftTop · CenterTop · RightTop

Now we use labels to explain it. Please notice the little cross near the labels.

![image 2988](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2988.png)

Figure 52.308 Justiﬁcation Example

∗ Oﬀset By CenterCenter: speciﬁes calculate the original point of via from center-center.

· X: speciﬁes oﬀset to center-center of via in x-direction. · Y: speciﬁes oﬀset to center-center of via in y-direction.

∗ Cut: sets the Size and Space of cut layer. · X Size: speciﬁes cut size in x-direction. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.

· Y Size: speciﬁes cut size x-direction. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition. You can click to exchange both X Size and Y Size values.

![image 2989](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2989.png)

- · X Space: speciﬁes distance of cuts in x-direction. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.
- · Y Space: speciﬁes distance to cuts in y-direction. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition. You can click to exchange both X Space and Y Space values.


![image 2990](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2990.png)

· Cut Class: speciﬁes the cut class. The cut classes in the drop-down list are mapped according to the deﬁnition of cutClasses in technology ﬁle.

∗ Parameters: sets the Enclosure values.

· Calculate: if this option is checked, the following Enclosure values are automatically set, checked, and corrected based on the Reset Parameters To.

Left: speciﬁes distance that the cut must be enclosed by layer 1 at left side. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.

Right: speciﬁes distance that the cut must be enclosed by layer 1 at right side. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.

Top: speciﬁes distance that the cut must be enclosed by layer 1 at top side. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.

Bottom: speciﬁes distance that the cut must be enclosed by layer 1 at bottom side. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.

: clicks to exchange both Left/Right and Top/Bottom values.

![image 2991](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2991.png)

![image 2992](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2992.png)

- Implant X: speciﬁes distance that the implant must be enclosed by layer 1 at x-direction. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.
- Implant Y: speciﬁes distance that the implant must be enclosed by layer 1 at y-direction. Default value is deﬁned in via deﬁnition.


- – User Deﬁned: speciﬁes the parameters of custom via. It is valid when via type is CustomVia. The interface is diﬀerent according to the custom via deﬁnition.

![image 2993](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2993.png)

Figure 52.309 User Deﬁned

- – Cut Pattern: speciﬁes the cut pattern of standard via. It is valid when via type is StdVia and Rows or Columns is not 1.


![image 2994](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2994.png)

Figure 52.310 Cut Pattern

∗ Cut Pattern Size: speciﬁes the size of pattern. · Row: speciﬁes the row of pattern. Default is 1. Valid is from 1 to Rows in System. · Col: speciﬁes the column of pattern. Default is 1. Valid is from 1 to Columns in System.

![image 2995](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2995.png)

![image 2996](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2996.png)

(a) Pattern Size (b) Via

Figure 52.311 Cut Pattern Size 2 X 2

- • Stack: speciﬁes the bottom layer and top layer to create stack via. The layer selected in the Bottom Layer list does not appear in the Top Layer list


![image 2997](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2997.png)

Figure 52.312 Create Via_Stack Form

- – Bottom Layer: speciﬁes bottom layer to create via.
- – Top Layer: speciﬁes top layer to create via.
- – Top Rows/Columns: speciﬁes top rows and columns to create via. When Generate From is Size, it will convert to Width and Height.
- – Via Table: if the Bottom Layer and the Top Layer are set, the order of metal Connections, and their corresponding Via Deﬁnitions and Cut Class are listed in this table. As shown in the following ﬁgure.


![image 2998](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2998.png)

Figure 52.313 Stack Via Table

- • Auto: creates via automatically by Point or Area mode.


![image 2999](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile2999.png)

Figure 52.314 Create Via_Auto Form

- – Generate From: speciﬁes the modes to generate via. ∗ Point: creates via by clicking on the shapes.

∗ Area: creates via by drawing a rectangular or polygonal area on the overlapped shapes.

- – Use Entire Overlap: if this option is checked, the entire overlap area is used to create via.
- – Cut Class: speciﬁes the cut class types, which have been deﬁned in technology ﬁle.
- – Class Orientation: speciﬁes the cut class direction.
- – Layer Settings From...To...: speciﬁes the selected layer range of the vias.


- – Min Number Of Cuts: speciﬁes the minimum number of cuts when creating vias automatically for overlapping area.
- – Same Net Only: only creates vias on the bottom layer and top layer which are in same net.
- – Fill Polygon Overlap: speciﬁes how to create via on the polygonal overlapped area.

∗ Fully: ﬁlls the polygonal overlapped area. ∗ Partially: creates via partially. ∗ Align Cut: speciﬁes the alignment of cuts, which is enabled

when checking Fully option.

- – Options: clicks the button, the form appears, as shown below.


![image 3000](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3000.png)

Figure 52.315 Create Via_Options Form

∗ Extend Enclosure Beyond Overlap: if this option is checked, the via creating will exceed the overlap area in Auto mode.

∗ Fill Overlap With Enclosure: if this option is checked, the whole Overlap area needs to be ﬁlled in Auto mode.

∗ Consider Blockage: if this option is checked, the blockage will be considered when creating via.

∗ Use Top Two Layers Only: if this option is checked, the only top two layers will be used to create via, even there are more than two layers in the overlap region.

∗ Connections: lists all the connections of the Standard Via and Custom Via which are deﬁned in technology ﬁle. You can select the wanted connections to create via, or check All to select all the connections.

∗ Via Deﬁnitions: lists the via deﬁnitions, which only allow the user to select, and the default value is the ﬁrst via that to be deﬁned in the two layers in Standard Via.

∗ Cut Class: corresponds to the Via Deﬁnition, the default value is Auto.

∗ Min Cut Spacing: speciﬁes the minimum cut spacing in X and Y directions for connections. You can check the check box to set the minimum cut spacing values in the text ﬁelds.

- – Via Alignment: speciﬁes the alignment mode. The following ﬁgure shows the alignment modes under diﬀerent relative positional relationships.


![image 3001](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3001.png)

Figure 52.316 Via Alignment Modes

∗ Auto: selects alignment mode automatically based on the position of current mouse point and corners of overlapped area.

∗ Top Left, Top Center, Top Right, Center Left, Center Center, Center Right, Bottom Left, Bottom Center, Bottom Right: speciﬁes the alignment mode as shown in the above ﬁgure directly.

- – Show Preview: turns on/oﬀ the Via Preview and Alignment function. This function previews via which can be created on current overlapped area and adjusts via rapidly about the via data and position. This function only works in Auto mode and Fast Edit mode. Some additional explanation about this function:

∗ Preview Lock: stores the row, column and cut class of via. When the Preview Lock is in a lock state, the data stored in Preview Lock will be used when creating a via. Pressing the Space key can unlock the Preview Lock

∗ Adjustment Work: adjustments do not work in some special situations:

- 1. Irregular overlapped area;
- 2. The original overlapped area contains three or more layers;
- 3. The combination of custom via in Stack Via or the combination of custom via and standard via in Stack Via;
- 4. The supplementary via;
- 5. Two or more overlapped areas on Fast Edit mode.


- – Show Hints: turns on/oﬀ the Via Preview Bindkeys window which you can get the basic operations:


![image 3002](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3002.png)

Figure 52.317 Via Preview Bindkeys

- 1. Scrolling the Scroll Wheel up/down while holding down the Ctrl key: increase/decrease the number of rows of via.


- 2. Scrolling the Scroll Wheel up/down while holding down the Shift key: increase/decrease the number of columns of via.
- 3. Pressing the Middle Mouse button: swap the rows and columns of via.
- 4. Pressing the Space key: if the Preview Lock is in an unlock state, get the data of via at current mouse position into the Preview Lock and lock it. Unlock the Preview Lock if it is in a lock state. More detailed information about the Preview Lock can be found below.
- 5. Dragging the Middle Mouse button: create vias in dragged area by lock or unlock status.


##### • Fast Edit: updates via by Point or Selected Vias mode.

![image 3003](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3003.png)

Figure 52.318 Create Via_Fast Edit Form

- – Generate From: speciﬁes the modes to update via. ∗ Point: updates via by clicking via in the overlapping area.

∗ Selected Via: updates via by selecting via in the overlapping area.

- – Cut Class: speciﬁes the cut class types, which have been deﬁned in technology ﬁle.
- – Min Number Of Cuts: speciﬁes the minimum number of cuts when updating via for overlapping area.
- – Class Orientation: speciﬁes the cut class direction.
- – Fill Polygon Overlap: speciﬁes how to update via on the polygonal overlapped area.


∗ Fully: ﬁlls the polygonal overlapped area. ∗ Partially: updates via partially.

∗ Align Cut: speciﬁes the alignment of cuts, which is enabled when checking Fully option.

##### – Options, Via Alignment, Show Preview, Show Hints: Thesefunctions in Fast Edit mode are the same as in Auto mode.

- • LeftBottom

## 53.3 Copy

Menu: Edit -> Copy ToolBar: BindKey: C Tcl Command: None

![image 3045](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3045.png)

This command makes duplicate(s) of you selected object(s). When you activate Copy and press F3, the form appears.

![image 3046](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3046.png)

Figure 53.4 Copy Form

To Layer: changes into another layer when copy shape(s). It’s invalid to Instance.

Resize: expands(+) or shrinks(-) each side of shape(s) by the Resize option. Default value is 0.

Synchronize Group: creates synchronized ﬁggroup for source object and new copied object if new copied object is the same as source object. The edits of source object will reproduce to new copied object, and vice versa. Default is unchecked.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes the angles along which you can move objects.

- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • XOnly: draws wire along X-axis only. • YOnly: draws wire along Y-axis only.


![image 3047](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3047.png)

Figure 53.5 Draw Mode/Method

Maintain Color While Copying: speciﬁes the source object lock state and color information to be copied verbatim to the newly generated object when Copy or MakeCell. Default is checked.

Chain Mode: chooses a chain mode for copy.

- • All: copies all devices in a chain.
- • Selected: copies only selected devices.
- • Expand To Left: copies the selected device and all devices to the left of the selected device in the chain.
- • Expand To Right: copies the selected device and all devices to the right of the selected device in the chain.


Maintain Map Relationship While Copying: copies the map relationship on the objects to the new objects. Default is unchecked. When this option is checked, Copy Connectivity is checked at the same time.

Copy Connectivity: copies the net on the object to the new object. Default is unchecked.

![image 3048](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3048.png)

Figure 53.6 Copy 2 Rectangles with Nets

Increment Bus Net Name: increments the bus bit on the object to the new object. The option is activated only when the Copy Connectivity option is checked.

![image 3049](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3049.png)

Figure 53.7 Increase Index of Bus Bit from 1 to 2

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 3050](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3050.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.
- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for


![image 3051](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3051.png)

![image 3052](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3052.png)

##### MX.

• MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.

Rows and Columns: let you copy objects to array objects. Default value is 1. For example, the following ﬁgure shows copying an instance to 3x3 objects.

![image 3053](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3053.png)

Figure 53.8 Copying a Shape to 3 Rows and 3 Columns

Y-Pitch and X-pitch: Indicate the horizontal and vertical distance between the center of shapes. These options are activated only when the Auto Arrange option is turned on. The default value depends on the User Units. The button after the text box restores the default value.

Delta X and Y: sets the pitch when copying objects. Default values are 0.

![image 3054](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3054.png)

Figure 53.9 Copy - Delta

Note: Delta with Array of Rows or Columns are supported only when either of row and columns is 1. or when both row and col are 1.

Show Instance Contents: display instance contents when executing copy.

Auto Change Instance Label Name: if the instance name label is created by Create Label By Instance and this option is checked, the instance will be ordered when executing copy.

![image 3058](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3058.png)

Figure 53.12 Repeat Copy Form

This command executes the copy again of you selected object(s). When you activate Repeat Copy and press F3, the form appears.

Release Direction: resets the paste direction and allows you to paste the copied object in any direction and distance relative to the previous paste object. After disabling this option, the direction of pasting objects is ﬁxed, which is the direction of the last pasted copied object. This checkbox is only available after placing the ﬁrst copy.

Keep Selected: keeps the copied object to the selected state. Default is unchecked.

To Layer: changes into another layer when copy shape(s). It’s invalid to Instance.

Resize: expands(+) or shrinks(-) each side of shape(s) by the Resize option. Default value is 0.

Synchronize Group: creates synchronized ﬁggroup for source object and new copied object if new copied object is the same as source object. The edits of source object will reproduce to new copied object, and vice versa. Default is unchecked.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes the angles along which you can move objects.

- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • XOnly: draws wire along X-axis only. • YOnly: draws wire along Y-axis only.


![image 3059](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3059.png)

Figure 53.13 Draw Mode/Method

Maintain Color While Copying: speciﬁes the source object lock state and color information to be copied verbatim to the newly generated object when Copy or MakeCell. Default is checked.

Chain Mode: chooses a chain mode for copy.

- • All: copies all devices in a chain.
- • Selected: copies only selected devices.
- • Expand To Left: copies the selected device and all devices to the left of the selected device in the chain.


- • Expand To Right: copies the selected device and all devices to the right of the selected device in the chain.


Maintain Map Relationship While Copying: copies the map relationship on the objects to the new objects. Default is unchecked. When this option is checked, Copy Connectivity is checked at the same time.

Copy Connectivity: copies the net on the object to the new object. Default is unchecked.

![image 3060](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3060.png)

Figure 53.14 Copy 2 Rectangles with Nets

Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 3061](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3061.png)

- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a shortcut for MY.
- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for


![image 3062](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3062.png)

![image 3063](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3063.png)

##### MX.

• MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.

Delta X and Y: sets the pitch when copying objects. Default values are 0.

![image 3064](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3064.png)

Figure 53.15 Copy - Delta

Show Instance Contents: display instance contents when executing copy.

Auto Change Instance Label Name: if the instance name label is created by Create Label By Instance and this option is checked, the instance will be ordered when executing copy.

Menu: Edit -> Move ToolBar: BindKey: M Tcl Command: None

To Layer: moves selected object(s) and changes into another layer. Resize: shrinks(-) or magniﬁes(+) the object(s) after moving.

Snap Mode: speciﬁes the angles along which you can move objects.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.
- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • XOnly: draw wire along X-axis only.
- • YOnly: draw wire along Y-axis only.
- • Stay: remains in the same place(not to move).

Chain Mode: chooses a chain mode for move.

- • Selected: moves only selected devices.
- • Expand To Left: moves the selected device and all devices to the left of the selected device in the chain.
- • Expand To Right: moves the selected device and all devices to the right of the selected device in the chain.


Rotate: speciﬁes rotate mode. Default value is R0. Aether will rotate 90degrees when clicking RMB, mirror X when holding Shift, mirror Y when holding Ctrl.

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a 90 degree rotation. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 3070](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3070.png)

- • MXR90: represents mirroring about the X axis then a 90 degree rotation.


Delta X and Y: sets the pitch when move objects. The default is not checked. Show Instance Contents: controls whether the instance’s content is displayed when moving instance.

## 53.8 Stretch

Menu: Edit -> Stretch ToolBar: BindKey: S Tcl Command: None

![image 3085](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3085.png)

This command stretches selected objects to another location. When you activate Stretch and press F3, the form appears.

![image 3086](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3086.png)

Figure 53.28 Stretch Form

Snap Mode: speciﬁes the angles along which you can move objects.

- • Orthogonal: speciﬁes 90-degrees angle.
- • Diagonal: speciﬁes 45-degrees angle.


- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.
- • XOnly: draws wire along X-axis only.
- • YOnly: draws wire along Y-axis only.


![image 3087](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3087.png)

Figure 53.29 Draw Mode/Method

Chain Mode: chooses a chain mode for stretch.

- • All: stretches all devices in a chain.
- • Selected: stretches only selected devices.
- • Expand To Left: stretches the selected device and all devices to the left of the selected device in the chain.
- • Expand To Right: stretches the selected device and all devices to the right of the selected device in the chain.


Via Mode: chooses a via mode for stretch.

- • Stretch Metal: stretches and ﬁlls the via in the new box.
- • Stretch Row/Col: stretches the via horizontally, the number of columns is invariant; or stretches the via vertically, the number of rows is invariant.


Lock Mode: sets the angle changing mode while stretching. Default value is Lock Angle.

- • Unlock Angle: selects this option, it will not prevent changing the object angles while stretching.
- • Lock Angle: prevents changing the object angles of a corner or edge while stretching.
- • Lock Shape: prevents the shape selected object(s) as you stretch it.


![image 3088](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3088.png)

Figure 53.30 Stretch-Lock Mode

Delta X and Y: sets the pitch when stretching objects. The default is not checked.

Show Instance Contents: controls whether the instance’s content is displayed when moving instance. This option is valid in Advance Aether. Keep Guard Ring Ends Connected: controls whether a guard ring with touching ends stays connected when stretching. Keep Wires Connected To: speciﬁes mode for stretching objects.

- • All Wires And Vias: all wires, paths and vias connected to the selected wires/paths/vias will be stretched.
- • Wires Only: only wires will be stretched. This item is selected by default.
- • No Wires Or Vias: no connected wires, paths or vias will be stretched.


Lock Unselected Vias: locks the vias which are not selected but connected to wires.

Keep Wires Connected To Shapes: keeps wires or paths connected to shape while stretching.

Snap: speciﬁes the stretch object which is pin or P&R boundary. The default state is unchecked.

- • Pins To Boundary: speciﬁes the pin will snap to the boundary after stretch. The default state is unchecked.


![image 3089](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3089.png)

![image 3090](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3090.png)

(a) Snap Before (b) Snap After

Figure 53.31 Pins To Boundary

- • Keep Pin Side: speciﬁes the pin will snap to the boundary according to pin side stretch. The default state is unchecked, but if yout check Pins To Boundary the state will be checked.


![image 3091](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3091.png)

![image 3092](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3092.png)

(a) Snap Before (b) Snap After

Figure 53.32 Keep Pin Side

Boundary: speciﬁes the stretch object is boundary. The default state is unchecked.

• Keep Area: speciﬁes the stretch object is rectangle P&R boundary, it will preserve the boundary area while stretching. The default state is checked.

![image 3093](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3093.png)

Figure 53.33 Keep Area

• Show Boundary Area: speciﬁes the stretch object is P&R boundary, it will show the boundary area while stretching and highlight it. The default state is checked.

![image 3094](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3094.png)

Figure 53.34 Show Boundary Area

To execute Rotate Left command in other commands, the fully selected objects must exist in the layout. The following table lists rotating objects criteria in other commands.

Table 53.1 Criteria Table of Rotating Object in Other Commands

|---|---|---|

By Axis Of: speciﬁes how to calculate the reference point when using Justiﬁcation.

- • Object: the boundary box of justiﬁcation is determined by object.
- • Selection Frame: the boundary box of justiﬁcation is determined by selection frame.

## 53.14 Align

Menu: Edit -> Align ToolBar: BindKey: A Tcl Command: None

![image 3154](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3154.png)

This command aligns ﬁgures including instance in current design. You could use Shift or Ctrl to add or remove object one by one, you also could use Backspace back to previous selection, and could use the F6 to change snap mode. After invoking Align command and F3 is pressed, the Align form appears with all default options:

![image 3155](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3155.png)

Figure 53.80 Align Form

Copy Reference: copies the full selected ﬁgures to the reference. Default is unchecked.

Spacing: speciﬁes the distance of aligned ﬁgures to the reference. Snap Target: speciﬁes the highlight mode of the target object or the reference object.

- • Edge And Point: highlights the object’s edges and point.
- • Edge: highlights the object’s edges.
- • Point: highlights the object’s points, edge’s middle point and object’s center point.


Snap Mode: chooses a snap mode for align, AnyAngle, XFirst, YFirst are options for snap mode.

- • AnyAngle: aligns by both X and Y directions.
- • XFirst: aligns by X direction ﬁrst, if X direction oﬀset is 0 and reference is line, align also by Y direction.
- • YFirst: aligns by Y direction ﬁrst, if Y direction oﬀset is 0 and reference is line, align also by X direction.


Chain Mode: chooses a chain mode for align.

- • All: aligns all devices in a chain.
- • Selected: aligns only selected devices.
- • Expand To Left: aligns the selected device and all devices to the left of the selected device in the chain.
- • Expand To Right: aligns the selected device and all devices to the right of the selected device in the chain.


Hide: hides the form. Cancel: cancels the align command.

## 53.15 Advanced Align

### 53.15.1 Distributed Align

Menu: Edit -> Advanced Align -> Distributed Align ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3181](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3181.png)

This command is used to distribute and align shapes in current design. After invoking Distributed Align command and pressing F3, the Distributed Align form appears.

![image 3182](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3182.png)

Figure 53.106 Distributed Align Form

Reference: speciﬁes the reference of alignment by setting the following options.

• Mode: speciﬁes the reference mode by selecting one of the following options.

- – Point: uses point as a reference to align.
- – Object: uses object as a reference to align and speciﬁes which type of objects to be used, the default is Instance.


∗ Instance: speciﬁes the reference object as instance. ∗ Any Shape: speciﬁes the reference object as any shape. ∗ Group: speciﬁes the reference object as group.

∗ Row: speciﬁes the reference object as row.

- – Layer: uses speciﬁc layer as a reference to align.


• Direction: speciﬁes the alignment direction of reference. The default is

##### Horizontal.

- – Horizontal: aligns selected shapes horizontally.
- – Vertical: aligns selected shapes vertically.


• Type: speciﬁes which edge or point of objects to be used for reference. It has diﬀerent types based on Reference Mode and Direction. It will be enabled if Reference Mode is Object or Layer, the default is Center. If the Direction is Horizontal, it includes:

- – Top Edge: sets to top edge alignment.
- – Center: sets to center alignment.
- – Bottom Edge: sets to bottom edge alignment.


##### If the Direction is Vertical, it includes:

- – Left Edge: sets the left edge alignment.
- – Center: sets the center alignment.
- – Right Edge: sets the right edge alignment.


##### And only if Reference Mode is Object Instance, it includes Origin.

– Origin: sets the origin alignment. Clear Reference: uses to clear reference line. Align: speciﬁes how to align shapes by setting the following options:

- • Mode: speciﬁes the align mode by selecting one of the following options:

- – Object: aligns shapes and speciﬁes which type of selected objects to be used, the default is Instance.

∗ Instance: speciﬁes the reference object as instance. ∗ Any Shape: speciﬁes the reference object as any shape. ∗ Group: speciﬁes the reference object as group. ∗ Row: speciﬁes the reference object as row.

- – Layer: aligns shapes by using speciﬁc layer.


- • Type: speciﬁes which edge or point of objects is used to align. It has diﬀerent types based on diﬀerent option settings. If Reference Mode is Point, the default is Bottom Left.


- – Top Left: sets the alignment to top to left.
- – Top Center: sets the alignment to top to center.
- – Top Right: sets the alignment to top to right.
- – Center Left: sets the alignment to center to left.
- – Center Center: sets the alignment to center to center.
- – Center Right: sets the alignment to center to right.
- – Bottom Left: sets the alignment to bottom to left.
- – Bottom Center: sets the alignment to bottom to center.
- – Bottom Right: sets the alignment to bottom to right.


##### If Reference Mode is Object or Layer, Align Type depends on Direction and the default is Center. If the Direction is Horizontal, it includes:

- – Top Edge: sets to top edge alignment.
- – Center: sets to center alignment.
- – Bottom Edge: sets to bottom edge alignment. If the Direction is Vertical, it includes:
- – Left Edge: sets the left edge alignment.
- – Center: sets the center alignment.
- – Right Edge: sets the right edge alignment.


##### Only if Align Mode is Object Instance, it includes Origin.

– Origin: sets the origin alignment. Distributed Type: distance calculating methods when distributing shapes.

- • Space: calculates distances by shapes boundaries of bounding boxes.
- • Pitch: calculates distances by shapes center of bounding boxes. If the reference line is horizontal, the distributed part will be below:

![image 3183](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3183.png)

Figure 53.107 Distributed Align Horizontal Type

- • : sets the distance in horizontal.

![image 3184](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3184.png)

- • Orthogonal: sets the distance in vertical direction.


– : the objects on the left of the reference object move down and

![image 3185](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3185.png)

the objects on the right of the reference move up.

– : the objects on the left of the reference object move up and the

![image 3186](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3186.png)

objects on the right of the reference move down. If the reference line is horizontal, the distributed part will be as follows:

![image 3187](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3187.png)

Figure 53.108 Distributed Align Vertical Type

- • : sets the distance in vertical direction.

![image 3188](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3188.png)

- • Orthogonal: sets the distance in horizontal direction.

– : the objects under the reference object move to the left and the

![image 3189](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3189.png)

objects above the reference moves to the right.

– : the objects under the reference object move to the right and the

![image 3190](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3190.png)

objects above the reference moves to the left.

- • Sort Objects By: speciﬁes sort object.

- – Instance Name: speciﬁes sort object by instance name.
- – Net Name: speciﬁes sort object by net name.


- • Reverse: sorts reversely.

- • LeftBottom
- • CenterBottom

- 53.18.14 Corner Smart Cut Menu: Edit -> More -> Corner Smart Cut


ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3330](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3330.png)

This command is used to modify a selected square or rectangular donut so its corner or corners are rounded and shapes which are inside this donut are cut so that a particular spacing is preserved between inner boundary of the donut and these shapes.

To start this command select Edit -> More -> Corner Smart Cut, this will pop up the form, as shown below.

![image 3331](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3331.png)

Figure 53.207 Corner Smart Cut Form

Inner Radius: sets the arc radius of inner boundary of a donut at the corner after it is cut.

Spacing: the spacing, which needs to be preserved, from the inner boundary of a donut to the inner shapes.

Segment: sets the number of straight segments of the arc of selected corner after it is cut.

Set the parameters in the form. The Inner Radius and Spacing parameters should be multiple of the minimum grid of the design. The Segment value should be in the range from 1 to 1024. After setting the parameters select the donut to be modiﬁed. If a donut is selected as a full ﬁgure then all 4 corners of this donut will be cut. Selecting a particular corner or corners of a donut will allow you to cut only selected corners. When a donut or its corners are selected, it is highlighted. The next step is to select the shapes which are inside the selected donut. When the inner shapes are selected then press Apply/OK form button to process the selected objects. Press F3 to show the form if the form was hidden during the selection.

Note that only donuts with equal side width are supported by this command. The example of such donuts could be the one created with command Create -> Donut or manually drawn with Create -> Path.

- Example 53.42


The example shows how to cut a donut corner or corners by this command.

###### 1. Activate the command Edit -> More -> Corner Smart Cut and set InnerRadius, Spacing and Segment like below.

![image 3332](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3332.png)

Figure 53.208 Settings in Corner Smart Cut Form

###### 2. Click on a donut to cut its corners, as shown below.

![image 3333](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3333.png)

- Figure 53.209 Donut selection and donut with all corners cut

3. Or click on a corner of a donut to cut it, as shown below.

![image 3334](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3334.png)

- Figure 53.210 Selecting and cutting one corner of a donut


###### 4. Or click on an edge of a donut to cut 2 corners, as shown below.

![image 3335](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3335.png)

- Figure 53.211 Selecting and cutting 2 corners of a donut


- 5. Or, while holding Shift key, click on 3 corners of a donut to cut them, as shown below.

![image 3336](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3336.png)

Figure 53.212 Selecting and cutting 3 corners of a donut

- 6. A donut will be highlighted with solid yellow line after selecting its corners or full shape, as shown below.

![image 3337](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3337.png)

Figure 53.213 Highlighted donut after selection

- 7. Press Apply or OK button to make cutting done or continue with selecting shapes inside the selected donut to make them also cut so that spacing is preserved between inner donut boundary and selected shapes. Then press Apply or OK button. This is shown below.


![image 3338](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3338.png)

Figure 53.214 Selecting and cutting shapes inside the selected donut

- Example 53.43


This example shows the case when Inner Radius is bigger than it is possible for a selected donut.

1. Suppose you have a square donut with length of hole edge equal to 0.08. We set Inner Radius to 0.05, as shown below.

![image 3339](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3339.png)

Figure 53.215 Inner Radius is bigger than it is possible

2. In this case, after clicking on the donut the following message with suggestion of new value will pop up:

![image 3340](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3340.png)

Figure 53.216 Message suggesting new value for Inner Radius

New value calculation involves Spacing and Segment, so it could diﬀer for diﬀerent Spacing and Segment values. Generally, the valid value of Inner Radius should be equal or less than a half of the length of a donut hole smallest edge.

3. To accept the suggested value press Yes button. This will alter Inner Radius value to 0.04 in this case. Then press Apply on the Corner Smart Cut form. This will modify the donut as shown below.

![image 3341](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3341.png)

Figure 53.217 Modiﬁed donut with suggested Inner Radius value.

- Example 53.44


This example shows the case when Spacing is bigger than it is possible for a selected donut.

- 1. Suppose you have a square donut with length of hole edge equal to 0.08. We set Spacing to 0.05, as shown below.

![image 3342](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3342.png)

Figure 53.218 Spacing is bigger than it is possible

- 2. In this case, after clicking on the donut the following message with suggestion of new value will pop up:


![image 3343](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3343.png)

Figure 53.219 Message suggesting new value for Spacing

Generally, the valid value of Spacing should be less than a half of the length of a donut hole smallest edge.

- 3. To accept the suggested value press Yes button. This will alter Spacing value to 0.035 in this case. Then press Apply on the Corner Smart Cut form. This will modify the donut as shown below.


![image 3344](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3344.png)

Figure 53.220 Modiﬁed donut with suggested Spacing value.

The white lines on the picture represent the boundary of the area where spacing between inner boundary of the modiﬁed donut and inner shapes is less than Spacing on the form. Thus, all shapes that overlap this area will be either cut or deleted to fulﬁll spacing criteria. Currently, only shapes of rectangle, polygon and path type are processed. Some polygons with more than two vertices whose bounding box completely overlaps the polygon are also not processed. Note that the outer boundary of this spacing area is coincident with outer boundary of the original donut. As you can see, 3 red square shapes were inside the spacing area and were deleted, while one is left as the spacing to it is greater or equal to 0.035.

### 53.18.16 Metal Fill

Menu: Edit -> More -> Metal Fill ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3353](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3353.png)

This command is used to ﬁll metal for your layout according to the rule deﬁned in Technology Manager -> Metal Fill.

![image 3354](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3354.png)

Figure 53.225 Metal Fill Form

Fill Mode: speciﬁes the mode you want to ﬁll. The default mode is Area.

• Area: does ﬁll to objects that satisfy the ﬁll rule in drawn area.

• Cell: does ﬁll to objects that satisfy the ﬁll rule in the whole cell.

##### Metal Fill Rule: lists rules deﬁned in Technology Manager -> Metal Fill.

Window Step: uses step mode to create metal ﬁll. Aether will divide the speciﬁed area into little areas. One little area is X multiple Y. This option is disabled unless Fill Mode -> Cell is selected.

• dX: speciﬁes width of step. • dY: speciﬁes height of step.

Fill Dummy Shape of Layer: shows dummy layer. This option is deﬁned in Technology Manager -> Metal Fill.

For The Coverage of Layer: shows coverage layer. This option is deﬁned in Technology Manager -> Metal Fill.

Ignore Coverage: ignore coverage or not. If you don’t ignore it, Aether will create metal ﬁll to meet from Min Ratio and Max Ratio, which is deﬁned in Technology Manager -> Metal Fill.

Filling Pattern Deﬁned By: speciﬁes ﬁlling pattern Rectangle or Instance.

With Fixed: speciﬁes ﬁxed type, Width, Height or Width and Height. This option is only for Rectangle ﬁlling pattern.

Space X: shows minimum x space of dummy. This option is editable. Space Y: shows minimum y space of dummy. This option is editable. Min Space to Existing Shapes and Keepouts: shows keep out space.

Aether will not create metal in Keep Out Space. This option is editable. Keepout Layer: speciﬁes keep out layer. Keepout Area: speciﬁes keep out area, you can specify multiple areas into box by Add or remove selected area by Delete. Save All Fill to CellName: save current dummy ﬁll as a cell. You can ﬁnd it in DM -> Cell.

- • AnyAngle: speciﬁes any angle.

- • Replace Itself: updates the selected object after executing.
- • Replace Itself with Active Layer: updates the selected object and changes its layer to the active drawing layer following the operating.
- • New Shape with Avtive Layer: generate a new object on the active drawing layer after the operation.
