### 53.19.4 Resize

Menu: Edit -> Advanced -> Resize ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3377](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3377.png)

This command is used to magnify or shrink selected shapes by resize operation.

![image 3378](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3378.png)

Figure 53.239 Resize Form

##### Select Mode: this command provides three mode Object, Area, Cell. Resize Mode: speciﬁes resize mode Size or Shrink/Grow.

![image 3379](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3379.png)

Figure 53.240 Resize Mode-Shrink/Grow

- • Size: speciﬁes size value. It is only displayed when Size is checked. If you type positive value, the selected shape will be enlarged. on the contrary, will be lessened.
- • Direction: speciﬁes size direction. It is only displayed when Size is checked.

- – Both X and Y: magniﬁes or shrinks the shapes along x and y direction.
- – X Only: magniﬁes or shrinks the shapes along x direction only.
- – Y Only: magniﬁes or shrinks the shapes along y direction only.


- • Left: speciﬁes shrinking/growing length value for the left side. It is only displayed when Shrink/Grow is checked.
- • Right: speciﬁes shrinking/growing length value for the right side. It is only displayed when Shrink/Grow is checked.
- • Bottom: speciﬁes shrinking/growing length value for the bottom side. It is only displayed when Shrink/Grow is checked.
- • Top: speciﬁes shrinking/growing length value for the top side. It is only displayed when Shrink/Grow is checked.


Truncate Value: speciﬁes truncate value. If you type truncate value is less than threshold value, the real acute truncate value will be the threshold value.

![image 3380](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3380.png)

Figure 53.241 Truncate Threshold Value Computing Method

- • Keep Orthogonal: controls whether the edge of corner cut is perpendicular to the orthogonal edge.
- • Absolute Value: speciﬁes the truncate value. If check this option, the truncate value = truncateValue, else, the truncate value = size*truncateValue.


To Another Layer: speciﬁes the generated layer. Size Shape One By One: speciﬁes to do resize one by one.

### 53.19.10 Pad Text

Menu: Edit -> Advanced -> Pad Text ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3429](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3429.png)

This command is used to create text for pad with the clockwise or counterclockwise according to the user-deﬁned ﬁle.

![image 3430](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3430.png)

Figure 53.284 Pad Text Form

Pad Layer: speciﬁes pad layer.

Auxiliary Layer: speciﬁes auxiliary layer for pad. Auxiliary layer and pad layer are used to deﬁne pad area.

Text Layer: speciﬁes the generated pad text layer. Text Height: sets the text height. Search Depth: speciﬁes the search depth between 0 and 50. The default value is 10.

First X Coord: speciﬁes the starting x coordinate of the ﬁrst pad. First Y Coord: speciﬁes the starting y coordinate of the ﬁrst pad. Input File: deﬁnes the pad text according to input ﬁle. In the ﬁle, you can

only type a string each line, such as:

|pad1 pad2 pad3 pad4 pad5 pad6 pad7 pad8 pad9<br><br>|
|---|


You can also deﬁne text by following grammar, like this.

|[5 :1 ] #5, 4 , 3 , 2 , 1; A<5 :2> #A5, A4, A3, A2; A<<5:2>> #A<5>, A<4>, A<3>, A<2>; A<[3 :10:3 ]>BUS #A<3>BUS, A<6>BUS, A<9>BUS; A<1 :2>B<1 :2> #A1B1, A1B2, A2B1, A2B2;<br><br>|
|---|


Report File: the report ﬁle has recorded the message of executing status. Set Area: speciﬁes the area where will generate or not generate. If you type

the coordinates, the yellow cartoon will appear. As shown below.

![image 3431](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3431.png)

Figure 53.285 The Yellow Cartoon Appears When Input Coordinates

- • Not To Generate Pad Text: sets the area not to generate pad text.
- • To Generate Pad Text: sets the area to generate pad text.
- • Left Bottom/Right Top: sets the coordinates of executing area.
- • Text Order: sets the sequence of pad text, Clockwise or Counterclockwise. Following are the detailed descriptions of pad arrangement:
- • Multilayer serrated conﬁguration of pad text clockwise order, as shown below.


![image 3432](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3432.png)

- Figure 53.286 Multilayer Serrated Conﬁguration of Pad Text Clockwise Order


• The pad text clockwise order in corner:

– Case 1: Text as “24” to be the distance from the center of the pad is 88005, the distance from the left side is 70.81, closer to the left, so, it will be included in the column on the left side of the pad.

![image 3433](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3433.png)

- Figure 53.287 The Case1 Shows the Pad Text Clockwise Order in Corner

– Case 2: Text as “25” to be the distance from the center of the pad is 88005, the distance from the left side is 121.7, closer to it, so, it will be included in the above list.

![image 3434](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3434.png)

- Figure 53.288 The Case2 Shows the Pad Text Clockwise Order in Corner


– Case 3: Text as “25” to be the distance from the left of the pad is 88005, the distance from above side is 88005, both of them are equal, it will be included in the above column when sorting. By the same token, the text of “24” center distance from the top and the left are 0, also included in the above columns to sort. When the corner of the pad in a similar position, sorting will give priority to bring into up and down, next are left and right.

![image 3435](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3435.png)

- Figure 53.289 The Case3 Shows the Pad Text Clockwise Order in Corner


### 53.19.11 Pad Report

Menu: Edit -> Advanced -> Pad Report ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3436](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3436.png)

This command is used to report the text of the pads in special layer. All the shapes whose layer are same as that speciﬁed in Pad Layer will be treated as pads and report them in this command.

![image 3437](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3437.png)

Figure 53.290 Pad Report Option Form

Pad Layer: speciﬁes the layer where pads located at. Auxiliary Layer: the text only placed on the overlap of Pad Layer and Auxiliary Layer will be reported.

Text Layer: speciﬁes the layers containing text. This option can be empty, if you do not specify it, it will report all pad but not ﬁnd any text. The input ﬁeld allows you to quickly ﬁnd the layer.

Search Depth: speciﬁes the search depth between 0 and 50. The default value is 15.

##### Report Order: reports the pads in Clockwise or Counter-clockwise order.

Pad Area Size: ﬁlters the pads with size constraint. Check this option, it will ask you to specify the area constraint, only pads that follow this constraint will be reported.

||Note: The conditional expression contains > =,> ,< =,< ,==.|
|---|
|
|---|


Add Preﬁx To Pad Name: adds a preﬁx name before the found names. This option can only work under the situation that pads have text layer, it will auto add preﬁx name to original text.

Deﬁne First Pad By Mouse: speciﬁes the ﬁrst pad with all the constraints above by mouse.

Merge By Same Layer: speciﬁes the pad boundary to merge by same layer. By Area: speciﬁes the area by drawing a rectangle or polygon as the area.

- • Rectangle: clicks the button to draw a rectangle area.
- • Polygon: clicks the button to draw a polygon area.
- • Clear All: clicks the button to clear all coordinate values.
- • Add Area: clicks the button to add one area.


Example 53.62 This example shows a typical ﬂow of pad report.

- 1. Activate the command Edit -> Advanced -> Pad Report.
- 2. Make the options speciﬁed as follow.

- 3. Click left mouse button to specify the ﬁrst pad.

![image 3439](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3439.png)

Figure 53.292 Specify the First Pad

- 4. Click the Apply button to report the pad texts, and click the Save Report... button to save the result, if demanded.

|xtrack <number>,<spacing> <step> , . . . , <spacing> <step>; ytrack <number>,<spacing> <step> , . . . , <spacing> <step>;<br><br>#Specify the spacing of instance array in X and Y direction . number: how many rules in x or y direction ; spacing: the distance between instances ; step: how many times the<br><br>spacing values will be used .<br><br>define row <number> to <number>; #Define the number of row .<br><br>vacancy <num>, <hex> , . . . ,<hex>;<br><br>#Speci fi e s the display position of each cell , the Num value i s euqal with the given group hex , and this group i s a hexadecimal number .<br><br>R90/R180/R270 <x/y> <number>, . . . , <number>; #According to the row or column counterclockwise Instance<br><br>90−degrees , 180 degrees , or 270 degrees . Mode i s equal to 1 , the x line rotate according to the row , and y rotate acording to column ; Mode i s equal to 0 , the y line rotate<br><br>according to the row , and the x rotate according to column . Then as the row number and column number , row and column count starting from 1. Xflip / Yflip /X90Flip/Y90Flip <x/y> <number>, . . . , <number><br><br>|

### 53.19.14 Create Pin By Label

Menu: Edit -> Advanced -> Create Pin By Label ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

Figure 53.309 Create Pin By Label Form

Hierarchical: checks this option, it will search all labels in all hierarchical design, otherwise it will only search labels in edit design. Default mode is unchecked.

Create Pin Name: checks this option, it will automatically display pin names after creating pins, otherwise pin names will be invisible after creating pins. Default mode is unchecked.

Auto Connect Net: checks this option, it will add net message to shapes which pins are created on, otherwise these shapes do not have net message after creating pins. Default mode is checked.

Selected: checks this option, it will only display selected labels by user, support pre selection and post selection. Default mode is checked.

Attach Label To Pin: checks this option, it will automatically attach an existing label to the newly generated pin. Default mode is checked.

All: checks this option, label items which are listed below will be all selected, it will do this command to the all labels.

None: checks this option, none of label items which are listed below will be selected.

| |Layer<br><br>|Pin Layer|Pin Length|Pin Width|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Check Box|Searched Label Layer|Speciﬁes generating pin layer<br><br>|Speciﬁes value for pin length|Speciﬁes value for pin width|


Table 53.5 Label Item List

Skipped Labels: Speciﬁes labels name which you do not want to generate pin by them.

- • Add: adds new label name in Skipped Labels.
- • Delete: deletes the selected label name in Skipped Label.

### 53.21.4 Create Voltage Labels/Markers From Simulation

Menu: Edit -> Labels -> Create Voltage Labels/Markers From Simulation ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3516](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3516.png)

This command is used to create voltage labels/Markers for min/max voltage of net in the layout.

![image 3517](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3517.png)

Figure 53.347 Create Voltage Labels And Markers From Simulation Form

Select Create Entry: the table shows all the instance names with the completed hierarchy path when the current cell was called,speciﬁes the called cell in the current layout to create the voltage label,the ﬁrst row is selected by default.

Update: updates voltage according to constraint ﬁle. Mode: speciﬁes how create labels/markers, default is Replace.

- • Replace: all labels/markers will be recreated.
- • Update: updates net voltage associated lables/markers, the update rule is:


– the minimum voltage needs to be updated, when the minimum volt-

age is lower than the corresponding existing label/marker.

– the maximum voltage needs to be updated, when the maximum volt-

age is higher than the corresponding existing label/marker.

- • Override Manual Voltage Inputs: if checked, it will overwrite the manually entered voltage with the simulation voltage.


Voltage Mode: indicate whether you are creating labels or a markers, default is Labels.

Voltage Labels: indicate the method used to create the layer and purpose for the label.

- • Auto: automatically sets the layer of the voltage label, default is selected.
- • Layer: manually sets the minimum and maximum layer of the voltage label.

– Max Voltage: speciﬁes the layer and purpose used to create the

maximum voltage labels.

– Min Voltage: speciﬁes the layer and purpose used to create the

minimum voltage labels.

- • Purpose: specify the purpose for creating the label.

– Max Voltage: speciﬁes the purpose used to create the maximum

voltage labels.

– Min Voltage: speciﬁes the purpose used to create the minimum

voltage labels.

- • Special Voltage LPP File: specify the layer and purpose for creating the label by reading the ﬁle.


Voltage Marker: speciﬁes the method used to create the voltage markers.

- • Voltage Purpose File: specify the layer and purpose for creating the marker by reading the ﬁle.
- • Net Voltage Mode: specify the mode for creating voltage markers.

- – maxVoltage: speciﬁes that only maximum voltage markers are to be created.
- – minVoltage: speciﬁes that only minimum voltage markers are to be created.
- – bothVoltage: speciﬁes that minimum and maximum voltage markers are to be created.


- • Voltage Rounding: specify the mode for voltage rouding.


- – roundOﬀ: specify rounding of the voltage.
- – ceiling: specify ceiling of the voltage.
- – ﬂoor: specify ﬂoor of the voltage.


Options: specify options to create labels/markers

- • Net Selection: specify which nets to create labels/markers

– External And Internal Nets: specify external and internale nets

to create labels/markers.

– Only External Nets: specify external nets to create labels/mark-

ers.

– Only Internal Nets: specify internal nets to create labels/mark-

ers.

- • Stop Level: speciﬁes the depth of the net to be searched to create the labels/markers.
- • Label/Markers Height: sets the height for the generated voltage labels/markers.
- • Precision Of Signiﬁcant Figures: speciﬁes the precision of the label value, default is 2.
- • Exclude Voltage: speciﬁes whether to exclude voltage labels/markers, default is false.


– if the condition is <, exclude labels/markers smaller than the condi-

tional value.

– if the condition is >, exclude labels/markers larger than the condi-

tional value.

## 53.22 Find/Replace

Menu: Edit -> Find/Replace ToolBar: BindKey: F2 Tcl Command: None

![image 3527](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3527.png)

This command is used to search objects in designs and then replace them.

![image 3528](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3528.png)

Figure 53.353 Find/Replace Form

Search For: sets the searching type. In: sets the searching scope.

- • Current Cellview: searches in the editing cellview.
- • Current To Bottom: searches from the current level to the bottom level in the cellview.
- • Current to Stop Level: searches from the current level to the stop level in the cellview.


Add Criteria: adds a line of ﬁelds in the form to allow users to search more speciﬁcally.

![image 3529](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3529.png)

Figure 53.354 Criteria of Find/Replace Form

Cyclic Field: sets option of searching for speciﬁc attributes, instances, libraries, view names, or properties for this type of object as Figure 53.355. Condition Cyclic Field: sets option of searching for character strings or numerals that are exactly matched (==) or are not matched (!=); to get matches that contain a string, a leading and/or trailing asterisk must be used. The symbols <, <=, >, >= are used where applicable. EXIST and !EXIST locate or exclude discrete blocks of information anywhere in the string.

Value Field: sets the value of the attribute or property to be used in the search. In the text ﬁeld, you can specify the search string using the wild card characters.

Delete: deletes this line of criteria from the form.

![image 3530](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3530.png)

Figure 53.355 Criteria of Find/Replace Form

Replace With: replaces the objects’ matching results with a new object, attribute value, or property value. The cyclic ﬁeld contains the frequently used properties. In the text ﬁeld, you can specify the value of the property with which you want to replace the original value.

• Add Criteria: adds a line of ﬁelds in the form to allow users to replace more speciﬁcally.

Search: sets more operations for searching conditions.

- • Match Method: sets the way of matching when there are multiple matching criteria.

– All Conditions: all criteria must be met when searching objects.

This is the default value of Match Method.

– Any Condition: at least one of the criteria must be met when

searching objects.

- • Search By: sets the area ﬁlter condition.


- – Cell: ﬁlters by the hole bbox of cell.
- – Screen: ﬁlters by the screen ﬁtting area.
- – Area: ﬁlters by selecting area. The drawn search area can be either a Rectangle or a Polygon, and the coordinates of the area’s vertices will be displayed in the box following the Area.


- • Search Method: ﬁlters by the positional relationship of ﬁgures .

– Enclosed Figures: This option ﬁlters out objects that are fully

contained within the screen or search area.

– Enclosed Figures and Crossed Figures: This option ﬁlters out objects that intersect with the screen or search area in any way, including those that are fully contained as well as those that partially overlap.

- • Zoom To: zooms to the centers the cellview around the current object in the search group when you click Find, Previous, or Next.
- • Case Sensitive: searches object with considering case sensitivity.
- • Wildcard Match: searches and ﬁnds object with wild card. Check it,


*, ?, . and [] are supported by Find, * and {} are supported by Replace and Replace All, else, regular expressions are supported. It is checked in AetherAdv by default. This option is valid in Advance Aether.

Table 53.7 Wildcard Illustrations

|Wildcard<br><br>|Parse Expression|
|---|---|


|*|Matches any sequence of zero or more characters when used by Find. Indicates the content of nth wild card character if current * is the nth * in replacing string when used by Replace or Replace All.|
|---|---|
|?<br><br>|Matches any single character. Only used by Find.|
|.|Matches any single character. Only used by Find.|
|[A-Z]|The 26 English letters and the range of letter is from A to Z. Only used by Find.|
|[0-9]|The 10 digits and the range of digit is from 0 to 9. Only used by Find.|
|[abc]<br><br>|The character is one of a, b or c. Only used by Find.|
|{n}<br><br>|Indicates the content of nth wild card character. Only used by Replace or Replace All.|


Table 53.8 Regular Expression

|Regular Expression<br><br>|Parse Expression|
|---|---|


|[A-Z]<br><br>|The 26 English letters and the range of letter is from A to Z.|
|---|---|
|A{1,3}<br><br>|The number of characters A within [1,3].|
|[0-9]{1,2}|The range of number is from 0 to 99.|
|\d|The range of number is from 0 to 9.|
|A?<br><br>|The range of character is A{0,1}, or character A.|
|\d?<br><br>|The range of number is from 0 to 9.|
|A|B|C<br><br>|Character A or B or C.|
|[^A]<br><br>|All single character or number except the character A.|
|A+<br><br>|The letter A combination of the string, such as: A, AA, AAA...|
|A{n}|Multiple character A.|
|A{n,}<br><br>|The number range of continuous character A is equal or greater than n.|
|A{n,m}|The number range of continuous character A is equal or greater than n and is equal or less than m.|


- • Current Figure: shows which object in the search group is highlighted as you click Previous or Next.
- • Figure Count: after clicking Find, show the number of objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Instance Count: after clicking Find, show the number of instance objects found by Find/Replace.
- • Auto Highlight Next After Replacing: after clicking Replace, auto highlight next object.
- • Stop Level: after selecting Current to Stop Level, set the stop level in the editing cellview.
- • Only Report Once For Duplicated Cells In Hierarchy: after clicking Find, instances referring to same cell will be fully traversed at most one time. Notice: instances which are partially traversed will be retraversed later if found any, and corresponding target objects will be found out in all traverses.


Search Results: sets more operations for ﬁnding results.

- • Add Select: selects the current object in the search group.
- • Select All: selects all objects found by Find/Replace.


- • Replace: edits or replaces the current object with the settings shown in the Replace ﬁeld.
- • Replace All: replaces all objects found by Find/Replace with the settings shown in the Replace ﬁeld.


Find: searches for objects matching the settings in the Find/Replace form. Previous: highlights the previous object in the search group. Next: highlights the next object in the search group. Cancel: closes the Find/Replace form.

- Example 53.82


The example shows how Only Report Once For Duplicated Cells In Hierarchy takes eﬀect.

- 1. Assume that there are 4 cells named A, B, C and D, with D containing 10 instances of cell A and B respectively, and 4 instances of cell C. There C contains 10 instances of B, and B contains 10 instances of A. If we ﬁnd all instances from Top to Bottom in D, with the option OFF, then 24 + (10x10+10)x4 +


10x10 = 564 instances will be found, and with the option ON, 24 + 10 + 10 = 44 instances will be found. There are 24 from D, 10 from C and 10 from B.

![image 3533](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3533.png)

![image 3534](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3534.png)

(a) OFF: found 564 instances (b) ON: found 44 instances

Figure 53.357 Results of Turn OFF and Turn ON

- 2. If Screen or Area is selected as search ﬁlter, some instances may be partially selected. So the ﬁnd result under such situation may vary according to the traverse order, but the found cell collections are the same.

Deselect: removes the selected items on the tree. Select: keeps the selected items on the tree. First: highlights the ﬁrst object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties. Previous: highlights the previous object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties. Next: highlights the next object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties. Last: highlights the last object in the group and resets the form to show that object’s properties. Apply: saves the edit and keeps the form opening. OK: saves the edit and closes the form. Cancel: aborts the edit and closes the form.

Trace Rules: deﬁnes connected layers.

- • Show All Rules: selects all rules in the list.
- • Exclude Poly Rule: disables the poly rules.

-> Block. Hide: hides the form and keeps the command. Cancel: closes the form and exits the command.

## 56.14 Navigator

Menu: Hierarchy -> Navigator ToolBar: BindKey: None

![image 3761](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3761.png)

Tcl Command: None

This command mainly displays the objects of the current design through Navigator form, and provides some quick commands by the right bottom menu of Navigator Tree Nodes.

Navigator Form: Navigator form displays relationships between the hierarchical objects. This is a useful system for manipulating large datasets, distinguishing diﬀerent objects by diﬀerent icons. This form will provide you some functions about search and classiﬁcation, so that you can use more eﬃciently.

![image 3762](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3762.png)

Figure 56.73 Navigator Form

Mode: speciﬁes the type to control the nodes displayed on the Navigator tree, the default model is All.

![image 3763](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3763.png)

Figure 56.74 Modes of layout

Modes(in layout): in layout view, there are nine diﬀerent modes, they are All, Instances, Nets, Pins, Nets And Pins, Ungenerated, Cells, FigGroups mode.

All: lists all types of objects on Navigator tree. At the same time, a certain depth of hierarchical relationship will be displayed when expand the FigGroups, Hierarchy Instance type node.

Instances: lists the existing hierarchy instances and ﬂattens instances of current design. At this mode, only hierarchy instance is expandable, the instance included in the hierarchy instance will be listed out, when expand them.

Nets: lists all the nets of current design, and lists those hierarchy instances which have nets.

Pins: lists all the pins of current design, and lists those hierarchy instances which have pins.

Nets And Pins: lists all the nets and pins of current design. This mode is composed of Nets and Pins, therefore, it will not be repeated here.

Ungenerate: this mode is available in layout with SDL relationship, otherwise the Navigator tree will be empty. In this mode, the ungenerate instances and pins of schematic will be listed.

Cells: lists all the Cell of current design, and the corresponding instances will be listed under the Cell node.

FigGroups: lists all ﬁggroup of current design, and every ﬁggroup node will contain all object it has.

Matching Groups: lists all matching groups of current design, and every matching group node will contain all object it has.

Pattern Groups: lists all pattern groups of current design, and every pattern group node will contain all object it has.

Clone Family: lists all clones of current design, and every clone node will contain all object it has.

Search: uses this wiget to control the displayed of objects in the Navigator tree, and it will temporarily remember previous search records until restart. At the same time, you can choose the query method, including ﬁnd method, matching method and case matching. Setting them through the menu by clicking the bottom on the right.

Path: displays current node path, you can copy the path by right bottom. Name(Tree): displays the contents corresponding to the current selected mode. Click the rightmost arrow to sort, and the sort rule is setting by Design Manager -> setting -> Sort Name By Numberical Order.

Navigator Right Button Menu: to help you operate the corresponding object directly throught the Navigator Tree Node, The Navigator tree provides

some right bottom menu, the speciﬁc menu is decide by the node type you click on. There might be some diﬀerences between diﬀerent versions.

![image 3764](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3764.png)

Figure 56.75 Navigator Right Button Menu

Open Instance(Read): this command is available for root node and instance node of both layout and schematic view. It is used to open the corresponding instance of selected node. The open mode is based on Design Manager -> Setting -> Open Design Mode.

Open CellView: this command is available for root node, instance node and cell node, it is used to open corresponding view of selected Cell.

![image 3765](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3765.png)

Figure 56.76 Open CellView Form

View Type: lists the existing views in CellView. Open Mode: speciﬁes the open mode. Default is Edit mode. Open In: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in which window. The default value is New Window.

- • New Tab: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in new tab.
- • Current Tab: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in current tab.
- • New Window: opens the corresponding view of selected Cell in new window.


Copy Path: puts the contents of the path column of the current node into the clipboard. This command which is available for all node.

Select All: selects all nodes on Navigator tree, which is available for all nodes.

Deselect All: deselects all nodes on Navigator tree, which is available for all nodes.

Expand All: expands all level of current node, which is available for all expandable nodes.

Collapse All: collapses all level of current node, which is available for all expandable nodes.

![image 3766](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3766.png)

Figure 56.77 Navigator Ungenerate Instance Menu

Generate Selected From Schematic: executes Generate Selected From Schematic command to generate pin and instance. This is available for layout with SDL relationship.

Edit In Place: executes Edit In Place command to the corresponding object of current selected node, and this command is only available for layout instance.

Hierarchy: executes Hierarchy related commands, they are:

![image 3767](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3767.png)

Figure 56.78 Navigator Hierarchy Menu

Make Cell: executes the Make Cell command to the selected object with make cell form.

Smash: executes the Smash command to the selected object with smash form.

Add Ignore: executes Add Ignore command to the selected node object. Remove Ignore: executes Remove Ignore command to the selected node object.

Update: is valid for layout instances with SDL relationship, there are two commands under the submenu containing Update related command. They are:

![image 3768](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3768.png)

Figure 56.79 Navigator Update Menu

Master: executes Update Master command to the corresponding instance of current selected instance node.

Layout Parameter: executes Update Layout Parameter command to the corresponding instance of current selected instance node.

Trace Net(Layout): executes layout Trace Net related commands. This command is available to the layout pin and net node. it has a submenu contains:

![image 3769](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3769.png)

Figure 56.80 Navigator Layout Trace Net Menu

Add Logic Trace: executes Logic Trace to the corresponding pins or nets of selected nodes.

Add Physical Trace: executes Physical Trace to the corresponding pins or nets of selected nodes.

Remove Trace: executes Remove Trace to the corresponding pins or nets of selected nodes.

Remove All Traces: executes Remove All Traces to clear all traces.

##### Signal Type: available to all nets, starts with Navigator Options form.

Zoom To Voltage Label/Marker: zoom to this net related voltage label/marker.

##### Min/Max Voltage: sets the net’s voltage.

![image 3770](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3770.png)

Figure 56.81 Min/Max Voltage Form

Net Name: need to set the net name of voltage. Min Voltage: sets the min voltage for this net. Max Voltage: sets the max voltage for this net.

Group: executes Group related commands, they are:

![image 3771](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3771.png)

Figure 56.82 Navigator Group Menu

Add To Group: executes Add To Group command, add the last selected object to the executed group.

Ungroup One Level: ungroups one level for the currently selected group node.

Ungroup All Level: ungroups all level for the currently selected group node.

Options...: available to all nodes, start with Navigator Options form. This form main function is to set the maximum number of diﬀerent type nodes to display. If the object number is more than the number speciﬁed here, a further node will replace all nodes of this type and point out the accurate number. Only positive integers are valid here, and the unit is one thousand.

![image 3772](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3772.png)

Figure 56.83 Navigator Options Form

Max Number Of FigGroups(K): controls the maximum number of ﬁggroup nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Instances(K): controls the maximum number of instance nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Nets(K): controls the maximum number of net nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Pins(K): controls the maximum number of pin nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Ungenerated Instances(K): controls the maximum number of ungenerated instance nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

Max Number Of Ungenerated Pins(K): controls the maximum number of ungenerated pin nodes in current design which will be displayed on Navigator tree.

### 57.4.6 Resistance

Menu: Query -> Measure -> Resistance ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3834](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3834.png)

This command is used to measure resistance of rectangle or polygon. This command calculates resistance according to formula as R=Rs*L/W. Here Rs is Sheet Resistance, L is length of shape, W is width of shape.

![image 3835](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3835.png)

Figure 57.42 Measure Resistance Form

Sheet Resistance: speciﬁes sheet resistance value.

Extension: speciﬁes extension value. If setting a value,you need to consider the option eﬀect while calculating resistance using formula. That is L should subtract Extension value.

##### Resistance Direction:

- • Horizontal: speciﬁes horizontal as current direction.
- • Vertical: speciﬁes vertical as current direction.

## 57.8 Trace Net

Menu: Query-> Trace net ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3855](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3855.png)

This command is used to trace nets in layout design, which doesn’t support logic operation in trace rules.

![image 3856](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3856.png)

Figure 57.58 Trace Net Form

Select Mode: selects the area of trace net cartoon.

- • Cell: highlights the nets in the whole cell block.
- • Screen: highlights the nets in the area of screen.
- • Area: highlights the nets in the area that selected in the design. Trace Options: oﬀers some operations when tracing a net.
- • Keep Trace Net: keeps the previous trace results when selecting next net.
- • Highligth Via: keeps highlight via when tracing a net.
- • Virtual Connections: only highlights the objects that have same logical


net information. Color: selects the color of trace net cartoon. Line Width: sets the lines’ width of cartoon. Trace Rules: deﬁnes connected layers.

• Show All Rules: enables all rules in the list. • Exclude Poly Rule: disables the poly rules. • Block Rules: disables connecting shape when the shape is overlap with

block shapes, these rules are set in Technology Manager -> Trace Rule

-> Block.

![image 3857](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3857.png)

Figure 57.59 Trace Rules

Trace Net Browser: oﬀers some operations for trace net results. Show all Records: highlights all nets that have been traced. Delete: deletes a record of selected net. Fit View: ﬁts the draw area according to selected nets. Zoom To: zooms to the highlighted nets. Clear All: clears all records. Hide: hides the form and keep the command. Cancel: closes the form and exits the command.

||Note: This command supports multithreading. The number of threads is automatically set according to the size of the data. You can also input setVarVal -group Options -name trace-thread-count -value threadNumber command in Design Manager to specify the number of threads. The threadNumber ranges from 0 to 100, where 0 indicates that the number of threads is automatically set. Other values indicate that the speciﬁed number of threads is used. The value isn’t saved when exiting Aether .|

This command is used to trace nets in layout design, which supports logic and physical operations in trace rules.

![image 3860](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3860.png)

Figure 57.61 Advanced Trace Net Form

Trace Mode: speciﬁes the mode for trace.

- • Physical Trace Net: traces and highlights the nets physically connected in the design.
- • Logic Trace Net: traces and highlights the nets which are connected in schematic.
- • From Net: traces and highlights the shapes which are physically connected on the same net.
- • Across Pycell: allows trace to pass through pycell.


Preview: sets preview options.

- • Show Preview: dynamically traces and highlights around the shapes which the pointer hovers over. It also displays layer name and net name.
- • Color: selects the color of trace net cartoon. cycle means the ﬁrst trace uses the color at the top of the list, the subsequent traces use the next colors in the sequence. In addition, chooses the color in the list to specify the color of all traces.


Trace Region: speciﬁes the region for traces.

• Hierarchy Range: speciﬁes the start level and stop level for trace.

- – Top To Bottom: traces will pass from level 0 to level 50.


- – Current To Bottom: traces will pass from current level to level 50.
- – Top To Current: traces will pass from level 0 to the current level.
- – Top To Stop Level: traces will pass from level 0 to the stop level which is speciﬁed in View -> Display Depth - > Set Display Depth.
- – Current To Stop Level: traces will pass from the current level to the stop level which is speciﬁed in View -> Display Depth - > Set Display Depth.
- – User Deﬁned: traces enable Start and Stop ﬁelds to specify the start level and the stop level. Traces will pass from the start level to the stop level.

∗ Start: speciﬁes the hierarchy level which the trace starts. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Hierarchy Range is set to User Deﬁne.

∗ Stop: speciﬁes the hierarchy level which the trace stops. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Hierarchy Range is set to User Deﬁne.

- – Area: speciﬁes the area that nets can be traced.


∗ Entire View: traces nets in entire view. This option is selected

by default. ∗ View Area: traces nets in current view area. ∗ By Area: traces nets in a rectangular or polygonal area which

is speciﬁed by user. Click Rectangle or Polygon button to specify the required shape for trace.

Connection Setup: chooses and sets the constraint group which is deﬁned in technology ﬁle to be used for trace.

- • Stack Layers: speciﬁes the Start Layer and End Layer for trace. It can narrow down the trace scope.

- – Start Layer: speciﬁes the start layer for trace. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Stack Layers is checked.
- – End Layer: speciﬁes the end layer for trace. This ﬁeld is editable only when the Stack Layers is checked.


- • Setup: speciﬁes the custom/custom_mt trace rule for trace. This ﬁeld can be manipulated when the Connection Setup is set to Custom/Custom _MT.


![image 3861](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3861.png)

![image 3862](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3862.png)

(a) Custom Setup Form (b) CustomMT Setup Form

Figure 57.62 Custom Options Form

In Custom Setup Form, the display format of each rule is Layer. In Custom MT Setup Form, the display format of each rule is Instance: Layer

- – Via Layers: uses this part to customize the via layers rules.


∗ Use Custom Via Layers: speciﬁes whether to use the via layers deﬁned in the table below. When this option is selected, the lists deﬁned in the table below are enabled. Conversely, all the via layers from the technology ﬁle are enabled.

∗ Via Layers Table: this table will display all via layers that you have added or all the via layers from the technology ﬁle. Use the individual check boxes to decide which one works when tracing.

∗ : adds a new item to the Via Layers Table. ∗ : deletes the items selected in the Via Layers Table. ∗ Reset To Default: deletes any via layers that you may have

![image 3863](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3863.png)

![image 3864](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3864.png)

added, and adds the via layers deﬁned in the technology ﬁle.

- – Connected Layers: uses this part to customize the connected layers rules.

∗ Use Connected Layers: speciﬁes whether to use the connected layers deﬁned in the table below. If the option is deselected, connected layers will not work when tracing.

∗ Connected Layers Table: this table will display all connected layers that you have added. Use the individual check boxes to decide which one works when tracing.

∗ : adds a new item to the Connected Layers Table.

![image 3865](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3865.png)

∗ : deletes the items selected in the Connected Layers Table. ∗ Reset To Default: deletes any connected layers that you may

![image 3866](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3866.png)

have added, and adds the connected layers deﬁned in the technology ﬁle.

- – Stop Layers: uses this part to customize those layers which will stop tracing a net. The Advanced Trace Net command stops tracing those connected shapes, which overlap the stopLayer shape.

∗ Use Stop Layers: speciﬁes whether to use the stop layers deﬁned in the table below. If the option is deselected, stop layers will not work when tracing.

∗ Stop Layers Table: this table will display all stop layers that you have added. Use the individual check boxes to decide which one works when tracing.

∗ : adds a new item to the Stop Layers Table. ∗ : deletes the items selected in the Stop Layers Table. ∗ Reset To Default: deletes any stop layers that you may have added, and adds the stop layers deﬁned in the technology ﬁle.

![image 3867](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3867.png)

![image 3868](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3868.png)

- – Exclude Purposes: uses this part to customize those layer purposes to be excluded for tracing.

∗ Use Exclude Purposes: speciﬁes whether to use the exclude layer purposes deﬁned in the browser ﬁeld for tracing.

- – Load/Save Options: this part provides settings for saving and loading.


∗ Via Layers: speciﬁes save (or load) via layer settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Connected Layers: speciﬁes save (or load) Connected layer settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Stop Layers: speciﬁes save (or load) Stop layer settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Exclude Purposes: speciﬁes save (or load) Exclude Purposes settings to (or from) ﬁle. If the option is selected, the corresponding part in ﬁle (or on form) will be covered when saving (or loading). Conversely, it will remain unchanged.

∗ Save As: speciﬁes the name and path of the ﬁle to save in, according to the option of Load/Save Options.

∗ Load From: uses this button to choose which setting ﬁle to be load, according to the option of Load/Save Options.

- – Load MT Connection: in Custom MT Setup form, use this button to load multi-tech trace rule.
- – Apply: uses this button to make the options on this form eﬀective when tracing, and save the setting on to the ﬁle in default path.
- – OK: uses this button to make the options on this form eﬀective when tracing, and save the setting on to the ﬁle in default path. And closes the form.
- – Cancel: closes the form.
- – Save: uses this button to save the options on this form to the ﬁle in default path, according to the option of Load/Save Options.


Hide: hides the form and keeps the command. Cancel: closes the form and exits the command.

### 57.9.2 Save

Menu: Query-> Advanced Trace Net -> Save ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3890](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3890.png)

![image 3891](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3891.png)

Figure 57.78 Save Traces Form

Library Name: the default value is the current library, and the drop-down box is all libraries with writable permissions.

Cell Name: the default value is the current cell, and the drop-down box shows all cells that have been created. You can ﬁll in any cell name you want.

View Name: the default value is _Net_Traces_X, X is a number starting from 1, each time you execute a command, take 1 and start to check whether the view already exists, if it exists, take the next number and continue to check until you ﬁnd a name that does not exist. The drop-down box is all views that have been created. You can ﬁll in any view name you want.

View Name: the default value is the largest number in the suﬃx of the view starting with _Net_Traces_ in the corresponding cell. If there is no view starting with _Net_Traces_, take out all view names in the current cell except yourself, sort by ASCII code, then take the ﬁrst one. You can ﬁll in any view name you want.

## 57.10 Short Locator

Menu: Query-> Short Locator

![image 3899](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3899.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to locate the shorted nets and add marks for breaking. The command requires you to select two points to highlight the short paths between the two points. Then you can select the short path to add a breaking mark on it.

![image 3900](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3900.png)

Figure 57.84 Short Locator Form

Select Mode: selects the area of short location cartoon.

- • Cell: highlights the short location in the whole cell block.
- • Screen: highlights the short location in the area of screen.
- • Area: highlights the short location in the area that selected in the de-


sign. Color: selects the color of short location cartoon. Debug Segment List: lists the mark of segments you select to break. See the following ﬁgure for an example.

![image 3901](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3901.png)

Figure 57.85 Short Locator Mark

Unmark Segment: cancels the mark you select in the list. Unmark All: cancels all the marks. Show All: highlights all the paths between two points. Blink: blinks the short mark. Zoom To: zooms to the highlighted paths. Line Width: sets the lines’ width of cartoon. Clear All: clears all cartoons to the original state of command. Break: removes the objects under the mark to really break the short path. Hide: hides the form and keeps the command. Cancel: closes the form and exits the command.

## 60.1 Generate All From Schematic

Menu: SDL - >Generate All From Schematic ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3939](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3939.png)

This command is used to generate all objects and their layout from Aether schematic, it has Generate, I/O Pins, PR Boundary tabs.

Generate: speciﬁes the objects generation mode and their layout.

![image 3940](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3940.png)

Figure 60.1 Generate Tab

- • Objects: a total group shows the control of the generation.

- – Instances: speciﬁes the generation of the Instance.
- – I/O Pins: speciﬁes the generation of I/O Pins.


∗ Except Global Pins: speciﬁes not generate the Global Pins while generating I/O Pins.

– PR Boundary: speciﬁes the generation of the PR Boundary.

- • Location: speciﬁes the location of Instance and Pins.

- – Minimum Space: speciﬁes the Minimum Space of objects. The default value is 1.
- – In Boundary: speciﬁes whether the objects are in PR Boundary.
- – Schematic To Layout Scale: speciﬁes the placement scale between instances while generating all schematic components. The default value is 100.


- • Binding: the objects user deﬁned.


##### – Preserve User-Deﬁned Bindings: speciﬁes whether to preserve

user deﬁned bindings.

- • Connectivity: the relationship of the objects.

– Extract Connectivity When Generation: speciﬁes whether to

show connections of objects when generation.

- • Sub Block: whether generate Sub Block in layout.


##### – Generate Sub Block’s Layout: speciﬁes generate sub objects in

generation.

I/O Pins: according to the options, they control the I/O Pins generation.

![image 3941](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3941.png)

Figure 60.2 I/O Pins Tab

- • All Pins: shows the options which can change the label list all items.


- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin label list which can apply to all items.
- – Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin label list which can apply to all items.


- – Height: speciﬁes the height of the pin label list which can apply to all items.
- – Num.: speciﬁes the num of the pin label list which can apply to all items.
- – Create: speciﬁes whether create of the pin label list which can apply to all items.
- – Apply: makes Layer, Width, Height, Num., Create apply to all items.


- • Selected Pins: shows the options which can change the label list selected item.

- – Search Net Name: a search lineedit is used to search Net Name in Pins Label List.
- – Net Name: shows selected pin’s net name of schematic.
- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin label list which can apply to the selected item.
- – Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin label list which can apply to the selected item.
- – Height: speciﬁes the height of the pin label list which can apply to the selected item.
- – Num.: speciﬁes the num of the pin label list which can apply to the selected item.
- – Create: speciﬁes whether to create the pin label list which can apply to the selected item.
- – Modify: makes Layer, Width, Height, Num., Create apply to the selected item.


- • Pins Label List: shows the all pins of schematic.

- – Net Name: shows pin’s net name of schematic.
- – Layer: shows the pin layer this action will create for each pin.
- – Width: shows the pin width this action will create for each pin.
- – Height: shows the pin height this action will create for each pin.
- – Num.: shows this action will generate how many nums for each pin.
- – Create: speciﬁes this action whether to generate the pin.


- • Pin Label: shows the options of pin label.


- – Create Label As: speciﬁes whether to create pin label.


- ∗ Label: creates pin label as label. ∗ Pin Name: creates pin label as pin name.
- – More Options: the more options setting for pin label. ∗ Height: speciﬁes the height of pin label. The default value 0.02.


∗ Auto: if this option is selected, the label will be created with

0.8 times of the pin’s height. ∗ Font: speciﬁes the font of pin label. ∗ Drafting: speciﬁes whether pin label drafting. ∗ Rotate: speciﬁes the orient of pin label. ∗ Justiﬁcation: is used to set the pin label’s justiﬁcation. ∗ Layer: speciﬁes on which layer the pin label will be used.

· Pin Layer: speciﬁes pin label layer same as pin layer. · Layer: speciﬁes which layer will be used by choosing layer.

PR Boundary: according to the options, control the PR Boundary generation.

![image 3942](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3942.png)

Figure 60.3 PR Boundary Tab

• Shape: selects to generate rectangle boundary or polygon boundary.

- – Rectangle Origin(x y): speciﬁes the lower left point of the rectangle PR Boundary which is generated by Area Estimation settings.
- – Polygon Points List((x1 y1)(x2 y2)...): speciﬁes points of the


polygon PR Boundary.

• Area Estimation: when generating rectangle PR Boundary, set how to generate.

##### – Estimator Mode: speciﬁes the method of calculation between PRBoundary and BBox Based.

∗ PR Boundary Based: speciﬁes the method of calculation is to use PR Boundary.

∗ BBox Based: speciﬁes the method of calculation is to use BBox Based.

###### – LA Combox: has 4 selection Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H),Height, Width, but you only can choose 3 of it because LB Com-

boBox will have one. ∗ LA Line Edit: speciﬁes the LA ComboBox parameter.

- – LB Combox: has 4 selection Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width, but you only can choose 3 of it because LA ComboBox will have one.


∗ LB Line Edit: speciﬁes the LB ComboBox parameter.

## 60.3 Clones

### 60.3.1 Generate Clones

Menu: SDL -> Clones -> Generate Clones ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 3970](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3970.png)

This command is used to replicate the layout while maintaining the schematic correspondence and inheriting connection information.

![image 3971](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3971.png)

###### Figure 60.30 Clone Source

Clone Source: displays the devices to be used as the clone source. Selecting the clone source is a prerequisite for enabling other parts.

- • Layout CellView: lists those designs with sdl relationship.
- • Schematic Instances: displays the schematic name of the clone source, which has been bound to corresponding layout devices.
- • Layout Instances: displays the names of layout clone source devices.


![image 3972](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3972.png)

Figure 60.31 Search

Search: provides option settings for you to set the scope and conditions of the search target. After the settings are completed, click Search to start the search.

- • View Type: speciﬁes the search scope, the default value is Schematic.


- – Layout: searches all layout device to ﬁnd same structures target.


- – Schematic: searches all schematic device, except those devices already generated, to ﬁnd same structures target.


- • Selected Only: speciﬁes the scope of the clone search. This conﬁguration can be combined with View Type, to qualify the target devices as part of the layout or schematic.
- • Allowed Permutation: speciﬁes whether to consider pin permutability in searching process, if there is an appropriate permute rule deﬁned for the device to be matched.
- • Exact Parameters: speciﬁes whether to require that the parameters value on the target device is exactly same to the corresponding clone source device.
- • Exact Connectivity: speciﬁes whether to search target with diﬀerent connectivity. When switched on the searching engine will search for those matches with same connectivity structures as the clone source’s. Conversely, those matches with diﬀerent structures will also be considered, but it will spend signiﬁcantly more time than exact searching.
- • More Options For Search: speciﬁes the conﬁguration of inexact search.

- – Allow Partial Net Names: speciﬁes those names of nets in clone source that are allowed to be unmatched in the target structure. Those nets that are not included need to maintain the same structure as the clone source. Meanwhile the wildcard * is already supported.
- – Maximum Partial Net Matches: speciﬁes the maximum number of target structure which is unmatched to the clone source.
- – Maximum Found Matches: speciﬁes the maximum number of target matches in inexact search.


- • Search: starts the search engine with this button


Create: speciﬁes the types of clones to be created.

![image 3973](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile3973.png)

###### Figure 60.32 Create Clone

- • Clone Mode: speciﬁes the clone mode.

- – Synchronized Family: generates the clone source and each clone target as groups in the layout, and set them to same synchronized family.
- – Grouped Objects: generates the clone source and each clone target as groups in the layout.
- – Free Objects: generates the clone source and each clone target as free objects.


- • Justiﬁcation: sets the justiﬁcation for generating clones.
- • Update Layout Parameters: updates generated instances’ paramaters to match their counterparts in the schematic. When switched oﬀ, the parameters are same to clone source.
- • Show Flight Lines: shows the ﬂight lines while generating clones. When switched oﬀ, doesn’t show ﬂight lines.
- • Rotate: rotates generating clones.
- • Rotate 90: rotates it by 90-degrees counterclockwise.

– Mirror X: ﬂips clones according to the X axis. – Mirror Y: ﬂips clones according to the Y axis.

- • Place Clone As Array: generates all selected clones together.
- • More Options For Array: array’s more options.

- – Rows: the count of rows while generating clones.
- – Columns: the count of columns while generating clones.
- – X Space: horizontal spacing between 2 clones.
- – Y Space: vertical spacing between 2 clones.


- • Clone Found: shows found clones, and selects to be created.


- – Clone Found List: shows all found clones as list.
- – Select All: selects all the found clones to be created.
- – Edit: edits the correspondence between the instances in source and target structures.


∗ Source Instances: the instances of clone source. ∗ Target Instances: the instances of selected clone target from

clone found list. ∗ Move To Top: moves the selected instance to top.

∗ Move Up: moves the selected instance up. ∗ Swap: swaps 2 selected instances. ∗ Move Downward: moves the selected instance down. ∗ Move To Bottom: moves the selected instance to bottom.

## 60.5 Update

### 60.5.1 From Schematic

Menu: SDL->Update ->Form Schematic ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4024](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4024.png)

This command is used to update layout based on Aether schematic. It may update the diﬀerences of instances, pins, connectivity, etc., which includes Update, I/O Pins, PR Boundary tabs.

Update: speciﬁes the update options on existing layout components and whether to generate new layout components.

![image 4025](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4025.png)

Figure 60.77 Update Tab

- • Update: speciﬁes the update options and decide to change or remove the existing layout components.


- – Update Selected Layout Components Only: updates the selected instances and pins in layout only. Checking this option will automatically disable the generation of new components in Object group. if Update Instance Master Mode Replacing or Creating is enabled and set to Creating, you can set the Minimum Space value. Uncheck this option, the generation of new components options will be restored to the previous settings.
- – Update Nets And Instance Name Mismatches Only: speciﬁes only update connectivity, instance name, terminal name, pin name. If this option checked, it will automatically disable all other options on this form, except Update Selected Layout Components Only. Uncheck this option, all other options except Update Selected Layout Components Only will be restored to the previous settings.


- – Update Instance Master Mode: speciﬁes whether to update an incorrect master instance to the correct master. The default update mode is Replacing.

∗ Replacing: this mode will replace the incorrect instance, at the same place, with the correct instance with correct master.

∗ Creating: this mode will generate a marker on the incorrect master instance, and rename this instance with suﬃx _old. Then create the correct master instance below the incorrect one. When renaming the incorrect instance, if the new name has been used, the new correct master will not be generated.

- – Update Layout Parameters: speciﬁes whether to update the parameters on layout instances based on their counterparts components on corresponding schematic.
- – Update Net Signal Type: speciﬁes whether to update the signal type of net.
- – Delete Unmatched Pins: deletes layout pins that are not matched in the schematic. Redundant nets and terminals from the layout view are not deleted at the same time. When this option is disabled, the unmatched pins in the layout view will not be deleted, while a marker will be put on it.
- – Delete Unmatched Instances: deletes layout instances that are not matched in the schematic. When this option is disabled, the unmatched instances in the layout view will not be deleted, while a marker will be put on it.
- – Minimum Space: speciﬁes the minimum space between instances to all others objects.


- • Objects: speciﬁes whether to generate ungenerate layout components.


- – Instances: speciﬁes the generation of the Instance. Checking this option will automatically enable the I/O Pins Tab, on the contrary, it will disable the I/O Pins Tab.
- – I/O Pins: speciﬁes the generation of I/O Pins. Checking this option will automatically enable the PR Boundary Tab, on the contrary, it will disable the PR Boundary Tab.

∗ Except Global Pins: speciﬁes not generating the Global Pins while generating I/O Pins.

- – PR Boundary: speciﬁes the generation of the PR Boundary.


I/O Pins: according to the options, they control the I/O Pins generation.

![image 4026](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4026.png)

Figure 60.78 I/O Pins Tab

- • All Pins: this part is used to modify all the Pins Table List items.


- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer which will be used to generate pins. Its optional list is determined according to the following conditions:

- 1. if the constraint group is set by Options->SDL Options >Connectivity, the list will contain those valid layers deﬁned in the constraint group, whose function is Poly, Li, Metal.
- 2. if there are no valid layers deﬁned in constraint group or without constraint group, then the list will contain all layers deﬁned in technical ﬁle whose function is Poly, Li, Metal.
- 3. if the above two situations are not satisﬁed, then the list will contain all layers deﬁned in LSW.


- – Width: speciﬁes the width for generating pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Height: speciﬁes the Height for generating pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle.


- Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Num.: speciﬁes the number of pins to generate. The default value is 1, any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Create: speciﬁes whether to generate pins.
- – Apply: makes the settings of Layer, Width, Height, Num., Create applies to all items in Pins Table List.


- • Selected Pins: this part is used to modify the selected items in Pins Table List.

- – Search Net Name: a search lineedit is used to search Net Name in Pins Table List.
- – Net Name: displays the selected pin’s net name of schematic.
- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer of each selected pins. It is an optional list which is the same as the All Pins ->Layer.
- – Width: speciﬁes the width of each selected pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Height: speciﬁes the height of each selected pins. The default is the minWidth value according to the current layer in the technology ﬁle. Any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Num.: speciﬁes the number of each selected pins. The default value is 1, any input value should be greater than the default value, otherwise it will be restored to the previous value.
- – Create: speciﬁes whether to create for each selected pins.
- – Modify: makes the settings of Layer, Width, Height, Num., Create applies to the selected items in Pins Table List.


- • Pins Table List: shows the ungenerate pins of schematic.


- – Net Name: shows pin’s net name of schematic.
- – Layer: shows the pin layer this action will create for each pin.
- – Width: shows the pin width this action will create for each pin.
- – Height: shows the pin height this action will create for each pin.
- – Num.: shows this action will generate how many nums for each pin.


- – Create: speciﬁes this action whether to generate the pin.


- • Pin Label: shows the options of pin label.


- – Create Label As: speciﬁes whether to create pin label. ∗ Label: creates pin label as label. ∗ Pin Name: creates pin label as pin name.
- – More Options: the more options setting for pin label.


∗ Height: speciﬁes the height of pin label. The default value of 0.02.

∗ Auto: if this option is selected, the label will be created with

0.8 times of the pin’s height. ∗ Font: speciﬁes the font of pin label. ∗ Drafting: speciﬁes whether to draft the pin label. ∗ Rotate: speciﬁes the orient of pin label. ∗ Justiﬁcation: is used to set the pin label’s justiﬁcation. ∗ Layer: speciﬁes on which layer the pin label will be used.

· Pin Layer: speciﬁes pin label layer same as pin layer. · Layer: speciﬁes which layer will be used by choosing layer.

PR Boundary: according to the options, control the PR Boundary generation.

![image 4027](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4027.png)

Figure 60.79 PR Boundary Tab

• Shape: selected to generate rectangle boundary or polygon boundary.

- – Rectangle Origin(x y): speciﬁes the lower left point of the rectangle PR Boundary and generated based on Area Estimation settings.
- – Polygon Points List((x1 y1)(x2 y2)...): speciﬁes points of the


polygon PR Boundary.

• Area Estimation: sets estimation method and Calculation factors of generating PR Boundary.

##### – Estimator Mode: speciﬁes the method of calculation between PR Boundary and BBox Based.

∗ PR Boundary Based: speciﬁes the method of calculation to use PR Boundary.

∗ BBox Based: speciﬁes the method of calculation to use BBox Based.

– Area Estimation options: this part will determine area calculation result, it contains 4 selections Utilization(%), Aspect Ratio(W/H), Height, Width. Use the two comboxes to set diﬀerent combinations.

∗ Utilization(%): speciﬁes the percentage of the design area in the cell boundary area. The default is 50.

∗ Aspect Ratio(W/H): speciﬁes the ratio between width and

height. The default is 1. ∗ Height: speciﬁes the design boundary height. The default is 10. ∗ Width: speciﬁes the design boundary width. The default is 10.

### 60.5.4 Binding

Menu: SDL->Update ->Binding ToolBar:

![image 4067](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4067.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to update and establish the corresponding relationship between layout instances and schematic instances, and ensure the consistency of the connection information of instances in layout and schematic.

![image 4068](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4068.png)

Figure 60.116 Binding Form

Scope: speciﬁes the scope for updating the binding relationship of instances.

Current Level: speciﬁes whether to only update the binding relationship of the instances in the current level or the substrate level.

Name Only: speciﬁes whether to update the binding relationship of layout instances only according to the name of instances between layout and schematic.

All CellViews In Design: speciﬁes whether to update the binding relationship from the top level to the bottom in layout.

Hierarchy: speciﬁes whether to update the binding relationship of instances in all levels between layout and schematic, and it will ﬂatten hierarchy instances in layout after binding.

Bind Mode: speciﬁes the way of updating the binding relationship of instances.

None: speciﬁes that the binding relationship of instances are updated by using the consistency of the connection information of instances in layout and schematic.

Binding: speciﬁes that the binding relationship of instances are updated by using Binding File.

Binding File: speciﬁes the path of Binding File.

PVS: speciﬁes that the binding relationship of instances are updated by using Cross Reference File and Extracted Netlist File.

Cross Reference File: speciﬁes the path of Cross Reference File.

Extracted Netlist File: speciﬁes the path of Extracted Netlist File.

Input Scale: speciﬁes the precision value when run LVS.

Flatten Instances: speciﬁes whether to ﬂatten hierarchy instances in layout.

Synchronized Family: the ﬂatten hierarchy instances are divided into group based on the cell, the group will become clone family if it satisﬁes the condition of clone family.

Grouped Objects: the ﬂatten hierarchy instances are divided into group based on the cell.

Free Objects: only ﬂatten hierarchy instances, don’t gather them into group or clone.

Connectivity: speciﬁes the processing of connection relationship when binding.

Clear: whether to clear the logic information in layout. Extract To Level: speciﬁes the depth to extract physical connections. Extract Connectivity When Binding: whether to execute Extract Layout after binding. Across Pycell: whether to allow the physical trace to pass through pycell before binding.

Use Physical Bindings: whether the master cell of the layout instance must be the speciﬁed master cell of the schematic instance.

Preserve: whether to keep the existing binding relationship of instances when binding.

User-Deﬁned Bindings: whether to keep the binding relationship of instances established through Reuse Block.

Existing Bindings: whether to keep the existing binding relationship of instances in layout.

## 60.6 Extract Layout

Menu: SDL - >Extract Layout ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4109](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4109.png)

This command is used to extract layout net status (open, short or illegal) and set the connectivity for layout objects.

![image 4110](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4110.png)

Figure 60.143 Current CellView Form

Current CellView: extracts all ﬁgures(including pin ﬁgures) of the top-level and pin ﬁgures of top-level instantiated masters of the current editing design.

![image 4111](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4111.png)

Figure 60.144 Hierarchy CellViews Form

Hierarchy CellViews: extracts either an entire hierarchical design or selected lower-level cellviews from the current editing design.

##### • Settings:

- – Selected Instances: speciﬁes whether to check the instance is selected in current editing design.
- – Edited Only: checks whether the design has been modiﬁed after the last extracting operation.
- – Search Depth: speciﬁes the depth to ﬁnd from the current editing design.
- – Library Cell View: lists all available instances found according to settings.


∗ Library: shows library name of instance. ∗ Cell: shows cell name of instance.

∗ View: shows view name of instance. ∗ Number: number of lib/cell/view selected. ∗ Refresh: refreshes lib/cell/view list in the form. ∗ Select All: selects all lib/cell/view in the form. ∗ Deselect All: deselects all lib/cell/view in the form.

- – Selected By: selection ﬁlter settings, supports wildcards. ∗ Library: ﬁlters the name of libraries. ∗ Cell: ﬁlters name of cells. ∗ View: ﬁlters name of views.
- – Save Extracted CellViews: speciﬁes whether to save the design after extracting.


![image 4112](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4112.png)

Figure 60.145 Extract By Area Form

By Area: speciﬁes the area of the design in which objects will be extracted. You can enter the coordinates in the following formats:

- • X1 Y1 X2 Y2 • X1,Y1,X2,Y2 • (X1, Y1) (X2, Y2)
- • (X1 Y1) (X2 Y2) • (X1 Y1),(X2 Y2)


Select Area: uses the rectangle area drawn in the design.

## 60.7 Reuse Block

Menu: SDL -> Reuse Block ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4131](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4131.png)

This command is used to view and change the instances or terminals relationship between schematic and layout design.

![image 4132](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4132.png)

Figure 60.164 Reuse Block Form

##### Filter: this option includes four types: All Instances, All Terminals, Unmapped Instances and Unmapped Terminals.

- • All Instances: shows all of instances in current design.
- • All Terminals: shows all of terminals in current design.
- • Unmapped Instances: shows unmatched instances.
- • Unmapped Terminals: shows unmatched terminals. Schematic: lists instances or terminals in schematic design. Layout: lists instances or terminals in layout design. Update Layout Instance: this option includes Name and Parameters.
- • Name: uses the schematic instance name to update the corresponding layout instance name when this option is checked.
- • Parameters: uses the schematic instance parameters to update the corresponding layout instance parameters when this option is checked.


Map: this button is used to map these instances or terminals which lose matching relation. If the terminal of layout instance is mismatched with corresponding schematic instance, Assign Net To Terminal form pops up automatically.

Unmap: this button is used to remove matching relation of instances or terminals.

Deselect All: clicks this button, the selected instances and terminals will be discarded.

Assign Net To Terminals: this form pops up when layout instance mapped schematic instance with mismatch terminals.

![image 4133](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4133.png)

Figure 60.165 Assign Net To Terminals Form

- • Select Terminal To Assign: this table lists layout instance terminals information.
- • Instance: lists instance names.
- • Terminal: lists instance terminal names.
- • Net: lists the net names that attached to instance terminals.
- • Select Net: lists the nets which is attached to correponding instance in schematic, also lists all of global nets.
- • Assign Instance Terminal: clicks this button to attach the net in Select Net to the instance terminal which is selected in Select Terminal To Assign.

## 60.8 Group Device

Menu: SDL -> Group Device

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4142](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4142.png)

This command is used to make devices as a group. The diﬀerence between this command and Edit -> Group is that this command can not only make devices as a group, but can adjust devices position, do some align operation.

![image 4143](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4143.png)

Figure 60.171 Group Device Form

Placement: adjusts the placement of devices after making them as one group.

- • Use Existing Placement: selects this option, which will make devices as one group and keep their placement. Default mode of this option is unselected.
- • Auto Place And Align: selects this option, it will align devices according to some certain placement ﬁrst, then make these devices as a group. Default mode of this option is selected.


- – Side By Side Placement: ∗ Top: aligns vertically selected devices to the top. ∗ Bottom: aligns vertically selected devices to bottom.
- – End To End Placement: ∗ Left: aligns horizontally selected devices to the left. ∗ Vcenter: aligns horizontally selected devices to the center. ∗ Right: aligns horizontally selected devices to the right.


Spacing: speciﬁes the spacing of aligned devices, this option is enabled when Auto Place And Align is selected.

Create Common Bulk Port: checks this option, and speciﬁes Select Layer, it will create rectangle with speciﬁed layer to overwrite the group devices.

• Select Layer: selects the layer used to create common bulk port, this option is enabled when Create Common Bulk Port is checked. The layers list here are the common layer of selected devices.

Add Dummy: checks this option, it will create dummy devices in make selected devices as a group. Note: This option is enabled when selected devices are the same type. For example, if you select one mos and one resistance, this option can not be checked. Only when selected devices are all mos, all resistance and so on, this option can be checked.

Merge Transistors: checks this option, when you select transistors to make a group, it will merge these transistors ﬁrst, then make them as a group. Note: When this option is checked, Spacing becomes not editable and Auto Remove Contacts Without Pin can be checked.

• Auto Remove Contacts Without Pin: checks this option, it will delete contacts without pin after merging transistors.

Example 60.16 The example shows how to group devices, including the using way of form option.

- 1. Open a layout view ,active the command SDL -> Group Device, select three moses in layout, select Use Existing Placement, keep other options as default, press OK to ﬁnish grouping device.


Figure 60.172 Group Device with Use Existing Placement Mode

![image 4146](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4146.png)

- Figure 60.173 Group Device with Auto Place And Align Mode


- 3. Press OK to ﬁnish grouping device.


- Figure 60.174 Group Device with Auto Place And Align Mode

Figure 60.175 Group Device with Create Common Bulk Port

- 5. Press OK to ﬁnish grouping device.

- 6. Select three moses in layout, select Auto Place And Align, check Add Dummy, keep other options as default.

## 60.10 Device Matching

Menu: SDL -> Device Matching ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4164](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4164.png)

This command is used to do device matching. Patterns: speciﬁes matching patterns for device matching. Add Pattern: adds user-deﬁned pattern to pattern list for device matching. Delete Pattern: deletes user-deﬁned pattern from pattern list. Fold Number: speciﬁes the fold number to fold device in device matching. Row: speciﬁes row to ﬁlter patterns when some pattern row less than this number. Label Height: speciﬁes height of label to show device name or net name. Snake mode: speciﬁes snake mode or not for resistor matching. Swap Column: swaps instance column with speciﬁed two columns. Devices: shows devices information.

- • Alias: shows alias name, this name can be renamed.
- • Device Name: shows device name, this name is device name in schematic.


- • Multiplier: shows device numbers.
- • Total_Width: shows total width for mos.
- • Width: shows width for mos.
- • Length: shows length for mos.
- • R_total: shows total length for resistor.
- • R_unit: shows length for resistor.
- • R_width: shows width or resistor.


Rename Alias: applies rename alias.
