## 60.13 Adjust Under

### 60.13.1 SD Connection

Menu: SDL -> Adjust Under -> SD Connection ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4232](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4232.png)

This command is used to adjust the distance of two mos devices which the one’s gate is connected to the other one’s source or drain in layout view which is started by Schematic Driven Layout.

||Note: Only mos device satisfy the following situation, these mos devices are needed to be adjusted distance:<br><br>• The gate of one mos is connected to the other one’s source or drain.<br>• The distance of two mos devices is less than Ratio*minSpacing.<br>|
|---|
|
|---|


![image 4233](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4233.png)

Figure 60.223 SD Connection Form

Rule: speciﬁes rule, if the distance of two mos devices is less than Ratio*minSpacing, these two mos devices need to be adjusted. Here minSpacing is selected in drop-list of Rule. And the drop-list is according to Technology Manager-> Constraint.

Ratio: speciﬁes the ratio value of minSpacing, the default value is 2. The value should be positive integer.

Zoom To: zooms to the centers of the cellview around the current object in the search group when you click Find, Previous, or Next.

Find: searches mos devices which violate speciﬁed rule. Previous: highlights the previous group of mos devices which violate speciﬁed rule. Next: highlights the next group of mos devices which violate speciﬁed rule. Adjust: adjusts the distance of found and highlighted mos devices.

60.13. Adjust Under

Adjust All: adjusts the distance of all found mos devices.

Example 60.30 The example shows how to adjust the distance of mos devices which violate rule.

- 1. Opens a layout view which is started by SDL. There exist two mos devices that satisfy connection relationship and the distance is less than Ratio*minSpacing.

![image 4234](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4234.png)

Figure 60.224 Group of MOS in Layout

- 2. Activate SD Connection, select minSpacing SN 0.440 in Rule. Set Ratio value is 2. As following:

![image 4235](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4235.png)

Figure 60.225 Form Setting of SD Connection

- 3. Click Find, the mos devices found are highlighted. And it would also highlight the position after adjusting. As following:


![image 4236](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4236.png)

Figure 60.226 The Highlight Cartoon

- 4. Click Adjust, the right mos would adjust to the position of highlight cartoon shows. And the distance of these mos devices is equal to Ratio*minSpacing=2*0.440.


![image 4237](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4237.png)

Figure 60.227 After Adjusting

## 60.14 Conﬁgure Physical Hierarchy

Menu: SDL - >Conﬁgure Physical Hierarchy ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4238](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4238.png)

This command controls how the physical hierarchy is generated from your logical design, including which logical components are to be ignored in the physical implementation and which physical views are used to implement the logical components.

![image 4239](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4239.png)

Figure 60.228 PhysConﬁg Editor

Save: saves changes to the ﬁle, it can only be used when window is changed. Make Read Only: makes window not editable. When it pressed, it will change to Make Editable.

Discard Edit: discards edit, it can only be used when window is changed.

Import Floorplan File...: loads the Soft Block Parameters from the ﬁle exported by Export Floorplan File..., and deﬁnes the parameters into instances according to the binding physical Lib/Cell/View.

Export Floorplan File...: exports Soft Block Tab data to Floorplan ﬁle. Close: clicks it to close the window. Help: clicks it to show the manual.

Occurrence Entry: controls occurrence mode. When the icon is pressed, you are working in occurrence mode. In this mode, all changes in instance table or attribute table only inﬂuence the instances that you edited. Otherwise, these changes will replicate to all other identical instances. As shown in following ﬁgure, without occurrence mode, changes of M1:A in instance table or attribute table also applied to M2:A, but not to M3:A, because M1 and

M2 have same cellviews, M3 has diﬀerent cellviews. With occurrence mode, changes of M1:A only applied to M1:A.

![image 4240](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4240.png)

Figure 60.229 Simple Example for Occurrence Mode

Hierarchy Conﬁguration: shows the information and settings of the instance.

![image 4241](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4241.png)

Figure 60.230 Hierarchy Conﬁguration Tab

- • Logical Top Cell: shows the physconﬁg binding schematic.

- – Set/Remove Force Descend: sets or clears force descend for instance, it has the lowest priority among Set/Clear Stop Point and Set/Remove Hierarchical Force Descend. Generation will skip this instance and generate hierarchy instance when instance has force descend.

Patterns: speciﬁes patterns for instance placement.

- • Rows: speciﬁes row to generate pattern.

Label Height: speciﬁes the height of net name and device name. Display Net: speciﬁes whether to display net name and device name. Dummy: speciﬁes whether to generate dummy device.

- • Right: speciﬁes whether to generate the right dummy device.
- • Top: speciﬁes whether to generate the top dummy device.
- • Bottom: speciﬁes whether to generate the bottom dummy device. Map: speciﬁes the correspondence between pattern and device.


- • Mapped To: shows pattern name, this name can be renamed.
- • Instance Name: shows device name, this name is device name in schematic.
- • Instance Number: shows device number. Remap: applies rename pattern. OK: generates device into layout design, will use the origin of instance in the lower left corner. Cancel: closes the form and exits the command.

## 61.3 Pin Alignment

Menu: FloorPlan -> Pin Alignment ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4294](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4294.png)

This command is used to align pins in top cell or soft block instance. First, you should choose the reference pins from top cell, normal instance or soft block instance, then choose the alignment pins in top cell or soft block instance, the cell containing the alignment pins must have the P&R boundary otherwise this command would do nothing. After these two steps, the alignment pins will be aligned to reference pins which have the same net name.

![image 4295](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4295.png)

Figure 61.11 Pin Alignment Form

Update Layer/Purpose To Reference Pin: if this option is selected, this command can update the layer and purpose of alignment pin to those of reference pin.

![image 4296](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4296.png)

![image 4297](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4297.png)

(a) Oﬀ (b) On

Figure 61.12 Update Layer/Purpose To Reference Pin Option

Update Label Layer To Reference Pin: if this option is selected, this command can update the layer of alignment pin’s label to that of reference

pin. Keep unchanged if the purpose of alignment pin’s label doesn’t match to that of reference pin.

![image 4298](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4298.png)

![image 4299](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4299.png)

(a) Oﬀ (b) On

Figure 61.13 Update Label Layer To Reference Pin Option

Update Size: if this option is selected, the following option Match With Reference Pin will be automatically selected as default. This command can update the bounding box size of alignment pin to that of reference pin according to Match With Reference Pin or Match With The Direction. Keep unchanged if the shape of alignment pin is polygon.

- • Match With Reference Pin: this option makes the bounding box size of alignment pin update to be the same length and width as reference pin.

![image 4300](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4300.png)

(a) Oﬀ (b) On

![image 4301](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4301.png)

Figure 61.14 Match With Reference Pin Option

- • Match With The Direction: this option makes the side of alignment pin update to be the same length or width as reference pin. It depends on which side of alignment pin will be aligned to reference pin.

## 61.4 Convert To FloorPlan

Menu: FloorPlan -> Convert To FloorPlan ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4325](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4325.png)

This command is used to convert the current layout design into a ﬂoorplan. The conversion applies only to Pin and P&R Boundary. The form is shown in the ﬁgure below.

![image 4326](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4326.png)

Figure 61.38 Convert To FloorPlan Form

Boundary: speciﬁes the conversion boundary.

- • P&R Boundary: speciﬁes the P&R Boundary as the conversion boundary. If there is no P&R Boundary in the design, the cell box is used as the conversion boundary. The default is P&R Boundary.
- • Boundary Layer: speciﬁes the layer as the conversion boundary. If there is no shape in the speciﬁed layer, the cell box(without labels) is used as the conversion boundary.


Library Name: speciﬁes the library name. The default value is current library.

Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name. The default value is current cell. View Name: speciﬁes the view name. The default value is ﬂoorplan.

Layer Map File: speciﬁes a layer mapping ﬁle to be used during conversion. You can specify the ﬁle name with a full or relative path. You can choose a Layer Map File by button.

![image 4327](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4327.png)

The format for the map ﬁle is:

<Current Lib Layer Name> <Current Lib Layer Purpose> <Target Lib Layer Name> <Target Lib Layer Purpose>

If you specify a layer mapping ﬁle, Aether will convert objects from the layer name and purpose name in the current library technology to the layer name and purpose name in the target library technology.

If Aether cannot ﬁnd the layer name or purpose name in the technology library, that line of information will be ignored.

By default, if you do not specify a mapping ﬁle, Aether converts objects using the current library technology.

Lines in the layerMap ﬁle that are blank and lines beginning with the comment character # are ignored.

Table 61.1 Layer Mapping File of Convert To Floorplan

|Current Lib Layer Name|Current Lib Layer Purpose<br><br>|Target Lib Layer Name<br><br>|Target Lib Layer Purpose|
|---|---|---|---|
|M1<br><br>|pin|ME1<br><br>|pin|
|M1<br><br>|text|MnTXT<br><br>|M1|
|M1<br><br>|drawing|ME1<br><br>|drawing|


Convert Mode: speciﬁes the convert mode.

- • Cell View: converts objects in current level. The default is Cell View.
- • Hierarchy: converts objects in all levels.
- • To Level: converts objects in a speciﬁed level. Convert Options: speciﬁes the convert options.
- • Generate Blockage: speciﬁes whether to generate blockage in the subcell during conversion. The default is Checked.

If Check the Generate Blockage check box, it will generate blockages within the boundary area of the sub-cell.

A metal blockage(routing) is generated below the metal layer of the pin. Some metal blockage (routing) is generated above the metal layer of the pin for the area of the hierarchy pin, and these blockages are placed in the corresponding group. Note that no blockages are generated in the top-cell.

- • Convert Unbound Label: speciﬁes whether to convert unbound label and generate pin during conversion. The default is Unchecked. If this option is checked, the label options are shown in the ﬁgure below.


![image 4328](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4328.png)

Figure 61.39 Convert Unbound Label Options

- – All: Checking this option will select all label items listed below, it will convert all labels.
- – None: checks this option, none of the label items listed below will be selected.

Table 61.2 Label Item List

| |Label Layer<br><br>|Pin Layer<br><br>|Pin Length<br><br>|Pin Width|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Check Box<br><br>|Searched Label Layer|Speciﬁes generating pin layer<br><br>|Speciﬁes value for pin length|Speciﬁes value for pin width|


- – Skipped Labels: Speciﬁes labels name which you do not want to generate pin by them during conversion.


∗ Add: adds new label name in Skipped Labels. ∗ Delete: deletes the selected label name in Skipped Label.

Open Converted View: determines how to open the converted view.

• Open For: opens the design in edit or read mode. The default value is

##### Edit.

- – Edit: opens the design with edit mode.
- – Read: opens the design with read mode.


• Open In: opens the design in which window. The default value is New

##### Tab.

- – New Tab: opens the design in new tab.
- – Current Tab: opens the design in current tab.
- – New Window: opens the design in new window.


||Note:<br><br>• If you specify the existing design, the message will be displayed to conﬁrm your real intention.|
|---|
|
|---|

## 61.5 Paper Convert

Menu: FloorPlan -> Paper Convert ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4338](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4338.png)

This command is mainly used to convert the component into a real device. applies only to the following components: Bump, Pad, Pin, Block, Inductor and ESD. Before starting the conversion, ensure that the active FloorPlan or Layout is associated with the corresponding Schematic via an SDL relationship.

![image 4339](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4339.png)

Figure 61.46 Paper Convert Form

Bump: sets the default value for the Bump Component conversion.

- • Library Name: sets the library name of the device associated with the Bump Component.
- • Cell Name: sets the cell name of the device associated with the Bump Component.
- • View Name: sets the view name of the device associated with the Bump Component.
- • Pin Width: sets the width of the pin corresponding to the Bump Component.
- • Pin Length: sets the length of the pin corresponding to the Bump Component.
- • Pin Layer: sets the layer where the pin corresponding to the Bump Component is located.


- • Pin Label Layer: sets the layer where the label of the pin corresponding to the Bump Component is located.


Pad: sets the default value for the Pad Component conversion.

- • Library Name: sets the library name of the device associated with the Pad Component.
- • Cell Name: sets the cell name of the device associated with the Pad Component.
- • View Name: sets the view name of the device associated with the Pad Component.
- • Pin Width: sets the width of the pin corresponding to the Pad Component.
- • Pin Length: sets the length of the pin corresponding to the Pad Component.
- • Pin Layer: sets the layer where the pin corresponding to the Pad Component is located.
- • Pin Label Layer: sets the layer where the label of the pin corresponding to the Pad Component is located.


Block/Inductor/ESD: sets the default value for the Block, Inductor and ESD Component conversion.

- • Reference Libraries: speciﬁes the relevant list of libraries. When the component does not specify a Lib/Cell/View, it will search for the speciﬁed cell in the library in the list.
- • Block Name Mapping File: speciﬁes the mapping ﬁle between the component and cell name. The cell name in the mapping ﬁle will serve as the basis for the search mentioned above.


Pin: sets the default value for the Pin Component conversion.

- • Top/Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the Pin Component that is attached to the bottom or top side of the component.
- • Top/Bottom Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the label for the Pin Component that is attached to the bottom or top side of the component.
- • Left/Right Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the Pin Component that is attached to the left or right side of the component.
- • Left/Right Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the label for the Pin Component that is attached to the left or right side of the component.

## 61.6 Global Options

Menu: FloorPlan - >Global Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4353](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4353.png)

This command is used to set the FloorPlan options for SDL.

![image 4354](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4354.png)

Figure 61.58 Global Options Form

##### Global Options: sets the FloorPlan options.

- • Soft Block Macro Color: displays soft block instance color.
- • Generate Physical Hierarchy: The settings will aﬀect the default values of same options in SDL ->Generate All From Schematic, SDL

- >Generate Selected From Schematic, FloorPlan ->Generate Physical Hierarchy, SDL ->Update.

- – Instance: sets whether to generate the instance.
- – Pin: sets whether to generate the pin.
- – PR Boundary: sets whether to generate the PR Boundary.


- • Pin Label: shows the options of pin label.


– Create Label As: speciﬁes whether to create pin label.

∗ Label: creates pin label as label.

∗ Pin Name: creates pin label as pin name. – More Options: shows more options for pin label.

∗ Height: speciﬁes the height of pin label. The default value is 0.02.

∗ Font: speciﬁes font. Default value is stick. Aether supports the

following fonts: · euroStyle · gothic · math · roman · script · stick · ﬁxed · swedish · milSpec

![image 4355](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4355.png)

Figure 61.59 Font

∗ Drafting: Aether will display labels in a human-readable direction even if the note text is rotated 180/270 degrees.

∗ Rotate: speciﬁes rotation mode. Default value is R90. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degree counter-clockwise, and mirror X while holding Shift, or mirror Y while holding Ctrl.

· R0: represents no change in orientation.

· R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees. is a shortcut for R90.

![image 4356](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4356.png)

· R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. · R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. · MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis. is a

![image 4357](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4357.png)

shortcut for MY. · MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees. · MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis. is a shortcut for MX. · MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.

- • Design CG: this section deﬁnes the individual design constraint group (wire constraint group) for each net. It mainly deﬁnes the layer, layer direction, width, space, via, and cut number of the net. For nets that belong to the same group (Symmetry, Diff Pair, Bus, Bundle), when only one is deﬁned, the other nets in the same group will also simultaneously have a design constraint group added. Example 62.3 The example shows how Equal Length works.

1. If no net pins are selected, equal nets in the same group will be guaranteed to be exactly equal in length. As shown in Equal Length Example 1, the ﬁrst row of net OUTA<1> is redundant in the fourth column after net. Similarly, OUTA<2> is alse redundant except for the left of the second column, which is above the second column. These redundancies are to ensure equal length.

![image 4398](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4398.png)

Figure 62.33 Equal Length Form Example 1

![image 4399](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4399.png)

Figure 62.34 Equal Length Example 1

2. If two pairs of net pins are selected, only the selected net will be guaranteed to be of equal length. As shown in Equal Length Example 2, the endpoints of the middle four columns are the selected net pins, and the OUTA<2> vertical nets extends part way up in order to maintain equal length. The diﬀerence from example 1 is that the yellow nets don’t need to be rqual length.

.

Coloring Method: speciﬁes how to color, this option only works if Color Engine is checked On. Default is Interactive.

- • Interactive: checks this option, it will automatically colorize the connected graphics on the same layer. And the toolbar is .

![image 4434](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4434.png)

- • Managed: checks this option, it will both automatically colorize the connected graphics on the same layer, but also on the same layer which violates the constraint rule. And the toolbar is .


![image 4435](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4435.png)

Shape Assignment: speciﬁes how to color a graph, this option only works for isolated graphs which unlocked when Color Engine is checked On. Default is Random.

• Random: checks this option, it will colorize the graph randomly according to the layer’s mask color. Mainly for gray graphics or in the region of color violation graphics.

64.1. Multiple Patterning Options

- • ASIS: checks this option, it will keep the original color when editing graphics.
- • LayerDefault: checks this option, it will keep the original color when creating graphics.
- • Gray: checks this option, it will not colorize the graphics.


Display color: speciﬁes whether to display mask color. Default is Show.

• Show: checks this option, it will display mask color. And the toolbar is

.

![image 4436](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4436.png)

• Hide: checks this option, it will not display mask color. And the toolbar is .

![image 4437](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4437.png)

Maintain Color While Copying: speciﬁes the source object lock state and color information to be copied verbatim to the newly generated object when Copy or MakeCell. Default is checked.

Propagate Locks While Locking: speciﬁes that lock information is automatically passed to the connected layer graph. Default is checked.

• Override Locked Color: checks this option, it passes the lock information automatically to the connected layer lock graph. Default is not checked, it only takes eﬀect when Propagate Locks While Locking is checked.

Propagate Locks: speciﬁes the design which is created or edited to automatically pass the lock information to the same layer lock graph that is connected, when Color Engine is opened. Default is not checked.

Coloring Stop Level: speciﬁes the hierarchy level of the colored graph. Valid is from 0 to 50. Default is 0.

Auto Recolor When Turning On Color Engine: speciﬁes how to recolor when color engine turns from oﬀ to on.

- • Never: checks this option, it will not recolor.
- • Always Ask: checks this option, a dialog will pop up when shapes in current cellview need to be recolored. You can choose whether to recolor or not.
- • Always: checks this option, it always needs to recolor.


Only Report Once For Duplicated Color Conﬂict Cells: speciﬁes whether only report once for duplicated color conﬂict cells or not.

Color Locking Check Rule: speciﬁes which rule needs to be checked.

• HCL Over HCL In Hierarchy: checks this option, this rule will be checked.

- • HCL Over DbLock Shape In Hierarchy: checks this option, this rule will be checked.
- • Uncolored: checks this option, this rule will be checked.
- • Unlocked: checks this option, this rule will be checked.

## 64.4 Color Locking Check

Menu: MPT->Color Locking Check ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4473](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4473.png)

This command is used to check the color conﬂict of the Multiple Patterning Technology. The speciﬁc rules are classiﬁed as follows:

Table 64.1 Color Locking Check Rule

|Diﬀ Color - HCL Over HCL In Hierarchy<br><br>|The shape in an instance is colored with the diﬀerent color by multiple Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|---|---|
|Same Color - HCL Over HCL In Hierarchy<br><br>|The shape in an instance is colored with the same color by multiple Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|Diﬀ Color - HCL Over DbLock Shape In Hierarchy<br><br>|The shape in an instance has been colored and locked, but at the same time is colored with the diﬀerent color by Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|Same Color - HCL Over DbLock Shape In Hierarchy|The shape in an instance has been colored and locked, but at the same time is colored with the same color by Hierarchy Color Lock(HCL), so there is a color conﬂict.|
|Uncolored<br><br>|The shape is uncolored.|
|Unlocked<br><br>|The shape is unlocked.|


Which rule will be checked and whether to report once for duplicated color conﬂict cells or not are conﬁgured in Multiple Patterning Options. The check result is displayed in the Window -> Annotation Assistant. The check result will generate a marker on the corresponding shape, as follows:

![image 4474](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4474.png)

Figure 64.22 Color Locking Check Marker

64.5. Delete Color

||Note: Color Locking Check only checks 1000 markers by default. When the 1000th mark is checked, the check is stopped, and the following information is prompted on the DM: Not all conﬂicts are detected. There are 1000 markers of color locking check; Aether supply to set PANDA_COLORCHECK_LIMIT environment variable, this environment variable can be set to deﬁne the upper limit of the Color Locking Check check. The input value of this environment variable is an integer from 1 to 4000, If the value is invalid, the default value of 1000 is used. If the value is greater than 4000, the upper limit is set to 4000.|
|---|
|
|---|

## 66.4 Area And Density Calculator

Menu: ToolBox -> Area And Density Calculator ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4521](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4521.png)

This command is used to calculate the area and density according to the speciﬁed objects.

![image 4522](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4522.png)

Figure 66.19 Area And Density Calculator Form

Object: speciﬁes objects All or Selected to calculate the area and density.

All: speciﬁes that all objects will be considered for area and density calculation. The default is All.

Selected: speciﬁes that only the selected objects will be considered for area and density calculation.

Layer: speciﬁes the wanted layer to calculate the area and density. In the ﬁrst line selection ﬁeld, the layers can be selected by drop-down button, and in the second line, the boolean operation will be supported, the syntax format is as below.

Single Layer: behaves similarly to the ﬁrst line that selects one layer. Example:M1.drawing.

Multiple Layers: behaves similarly to the ﬁrst line that selects multiple layers. Example:M1.drawing M2.drawing M3.drawing.

All Purpose: In this mode(just input one layer name), all of the diﬀerent purposes with the same layer name will be merged. Example:M1.

Boolean: supports the input of the logical command for boolean operation, currently only supports OR, AND and NOT. Example:M1.drawing OR GT.drawing AND NW.drawing.

Hierarchy Range: the design data is considered with hierarchical calculation.

Current Cell View: the design date only is considered in the current cell view.

Current to Bottom: the design date is considered from the current view level to the bottom level.

Current to Stop Level: the design date is considered from the current view level to the stop level.

Region: speciﬁes the calculation region.

Entire Cell View: speciﬁes the entire cell view as the area and density calculation.

A Selected Boundary: selects a boundary as the area and density calculation. The option is activated only when the All is selected.

By Area: speciﬁes the area by drawing a rectangle or polygon as the area and density calculation.

Rectangle: clicks the button to draw a rectangle area. Polygon: clicks the button to draw a polygon area.

Window: this option will be activated when clicking Rectangle button. By default, both the w and l settings are null, which means that the entire drawing region will be considered, you can only set w or l, which means that the area and density calculation will be considered as dividing according to speciﬁed values. The option is supported only in Rectanle region.

## 66.8 Create Barcode

Menu: ToolBox -> Create Barcode ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4538](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4538.png)

This command is used to create barcode. For now, Aether can only create barcode whose rule is Code39.

- • The characters supported by Code39 are:"A-Z", "0-9", "$", "+", "-", "/", ".", "%", "Space".
- • The characters a-z will be treated as A-Z.
- • Code39 supports character *, but it’s the Start and Stop character in Code39 and does not have Check Number.


Figure 66.32 Create Barcode Form

Barcode: speciﬁes the barcode text. If you input the characters which are not supported by Code39, Aether will give error message to remind you and cannot create barcode.

Reset: clears contexts of Barcode quickly. Height: speciﬁes the Barcode height value. Rotate: rotate the Barcode direction. Space Between Characters: speciﬁes the space value between characters. Wide Bar And Space Width: speciﬁes the wide bar and space value. Narrow Bar And Space Width: speciﬁes the narrow bar and space value. Options: Barcode options.

Generate Start And Stop Characters: speciﬁes whether to create start and stop character * or not. The default mode is checked.

Add Check Number: speciﬁes whether to create check number or not.The default mode is unchecked. If you check this option, it will add the character which is corresponding check number after generating character speciﬁed in Barcode.

Bar-Space-Reverse: if this option is checked, the reverse barcode will be generated. As shown below.

![image 4540](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4540.png)

Figure 66.33 Sketch of Bar-Space-Reverse Option

Generate Silence Zone: speciﬁes whether to generate silence zone or not. The default mode is unchecked. If you check this option, it will add silence zones before and after barcode. And the space between silence zone and barcode is equal to Space Between Characters.

Silence Width: speciﬁes silence width value.

Make Barcode As Cell: speciﬁes whether to make Barcode as cell. The default mode is unchecked. If you check this option, cell name is asked to be speciﬁed.

Barcode Label: Creates label options.

Create Barcode Label: speciﬁes whether to create barcode label or not. The default mode is unchecked.

Height: speciﬁes barcode label height. Font: chooses barcode label font. Convert To Polygon Text: speciﬁes whether to convert barcode label to polygon or not. The default mode is unchecked. Position: speciﬁes barcode label’s position. The default mode is upperleft.

Load: loads an existing barcode settings ﬁle to the Create Barcode form. Save: stores the current settings to a .bar ﬁle.

## 66.11 Connect Bus

Menu: ToolBox -> Connect Bus ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4556](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4556.png)

This command creates a bundle of paths to connect two groups of selected paths, wires, rectangles or polygons.

![image 4557](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4557.png)

Figure 66.46 Connect Bus Form

Mode: speciﬁes the connect path mode.

- • : connects two groups of paths in orthogonal mode.

![image 4558](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4558.png)

- • : connects two groups of paths in nonorthogonal mode. The two groups of paths extension center line by original direction must have intersection point.


![image 4559](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4559.png)

Connect Order: speciﬁes connect order Same(default), Reverse or By Net Name. The connect order is only valid when connect mode is Orthogo-

![image 4560](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4560.png)

nal(default). When Mode is set to , Connect Order is set to By Net Name, an additional Auto option will be displayed in Corner Via Align.

![image 4561](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4561.png)

Figure 66.47 Connect Bus Results with Diﬀerent Connect Order

![image 4562](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4562.png)

Figure 66.48 Connect Bus Form When Set to By_Net_Name

Cut Class: speciﬁes the cut class types, which have been deﬁned in technology ﬁle.

Min Number Of Cuts: speciﬁes the minimum number of cuts of via. Corner Via Align: speciﬁes how to align via when switch layer.

- • : aligns via in horizontal center.

![image 4563](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4563.png)

- • : aligns via in vertical center.

![image 4564](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4564.png)

- • : aligns via in horizontal.

![image 4565](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4565.png)

- • : aligns via in vertical.

![image 4566](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4566.png)

- • Auto: When Mode is set to , Connect Order is set to By Net Name, and Corner Via Align is set to Auto, Auto mode will be activated, automatically resolving via conﬂicts.


![image 4567](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4567.png)

![image 4568](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4568.png)

Figure 66.49 Connect Bus Auto Form

- – Width: sets the width of each transition path.


∗ Same To Pin: the transition path width is calculated from the two groups of selected objects and matches the narrowest width within the selected objects.

∗ Specify: speciﬁes a ﬁxed value for the transition path width.

- – Space: sets the spacing between transition paths.

∗ Same To Pin: the transition path spacing is calculated from the two groups of selected objects and matches the minimum spacing within the selected objects.

∗ Specify: speciﬁes a ﬁxed value for the transition path spacing.

- – Layer: speciﬁes the layer selection mode for transition paths. ∗ Specify: sets the layer selection mode to Specify mode.


· Horizontal Layer: speciﬁes the available layer(s) for horizontal transition paths.

· Vertical Layer: speciﬁes the available layer(s) for vertical transition paths.

∗ Range: sets the layer selection mode to Range mode. · Top Layer: speciﬁes the highest available layer for transition paths. · Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the lowest available layer for transition paths.

![image 4569](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4569.png)

Figure 66.50 Connect Bus Form When Set to Layer_Range

- – Backup Layer: when via conﬂicts cannot be resolved using only the speciﬁed layers, backup layers are used to attempt to resolve them.

∗ Horizontal Layer: speciﬁes the available backup layer(s) for horizontal transition paths.

∗ Vertical Layer: speciﬁes the available backup layer(s) for vertical transition paths.

- – Routing Target: controls whether routing aims for an optimal track reuse solution or a minimum crossings solution.


∗ Minimize Area Utilization: sets the Routing Target to the optimal track reuse scenario, with optimal area utilization as the routing objective.

· Zero-Spaced Track: editable only when Minimize Area Utilization is selected. When checked, allows for zero spacing for traces on the transition layer.

∗ Minimize Crossings: sets the Routing Target to the minimum crossings scenario, aiming for the fewest trace crossings as the routing objective.

- – Routing Scenario: deﬁnes whether routing is for a Bus Joint mixed-line scenario or a Connect Bus scenario.


∗ Bus Joint: in the Bus Joint mixed-line scenario, wire sequencing and via handling are performed. Routing must be completed within the area deﬁned by the Pins; if it exceeds the valid routing area, a pop-up error will appear.

∗ Connect Bus: in the Connect Bus scenario, routing will proceed even if it extends beyond the valid routing area.

Pick Multi-Layer: speciﬁes which paths to connect according to the option.

- • All: picks all selected paths no matter what the paths’ layer is.
- • Active Layer: picks the paths with speciﬁc layer selected in the LSW.
- • Selected: the Layer List window pops up to select the layers when the two groups of selected paths are in diﬀerent layers.


![image 4570](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4570.png)

Figure 66.51 Layer List Window

Transition Layer: speciﬁes the layer of transition path. Width: speciﬁes the width of transition path. Space: speciﬁes the space of transition path.

## 66.13 Bridge

Menu: ToolBox - > Bridge ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4656](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4656.png)

This command is used to replace the layer of the path/wire between the ﬁrst and second selection line on the router with the setting layer, and then auto create vias at the intersections of the replacement layer and the original layer. Any original via on the router between the ﬁrst selection line and the second selection line will be removed.

![image 4657](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4657.png)

Figure 66.112 Bridge Form

Layer: sets the layer that will be used for bridge.

Mode: ﬁlters out the valid path/wire by the serial numbers, based on the result of Pick Multi-Layer.

All: all paths/wires highlighted can be used for bridge. Odd: ﬁlters out the highlighted path/wire that the serial number is odd. Even: ﬁlters out the highlighted path/wire that the serial number is even.

Min Number Of Cuts: speciﬁes the minimum number of cuts when creating any vias automatically at the intersections of the selection line and path/wire.

Pick Multi-Layer: ﬁlters out the valid path/wire according to the option. All: all path/wire to bridge. Active Layer: only the path/wire to bridge which the layer is the same as the active layer in LSW.

Selected: determines which layer to be operated, the layer list form will be shown after the ﬁrst selection line ﬁnished, and selects a part of layers to bridge from all available layers listed on the layer list form.

![image 4658](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4658.png)

Figure 66.113 Layer List Form

Example 66.18 The example shows how to use bridge function:

- 1. Activate the command ToolBox -> Bridge, then, press F3 to open the bridge form and deﬁne the following settings.


![image 4659](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4659.png)

Figure 66.114 Bridge Settings

- 2. Press Hide, and draw the ﬁrst line to select a path/wire.
- 3. When the target layer for bridge is set, the path/wire that matches bridge setting will be highlighted and the serial numbers will be auto assigned, as shown below.

![image 4660](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4660.png)

Figure 66.115 After the First Selection Line

- 4. Draw the second line to select path/wire. The result is as follows.


![image 4661](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4661.png)

Figure 66.116 Second Selection Line

- 5. All common paths/wires between the ﬁrst and the second selection lines will be found, and the valid path/wire will be ﬁltered according to Mode.
- 6. To each path/wire, the sections between the ﬁrst and the second selection lines will be replaced, and vias will be created at the intersections of the selection line and path/wire.
- 7. Finally, any vias that crossed the common path/wire will be removed, the last result as shown below.

## 66.21 Generate Array On Shape

Menu: ToolBox -> Generate Array On Shape ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4700](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4700.png)

This command generates arrays on the selected shape. The shape of this function supports to select is Circle, Ellipse, Rectangle, Polygon, Donut. Path, Label, Instance cannot be selected, and it only allows you to select one shape once.

![image 4701](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4701.png)

Figure 66.140 Generate Array On Shape Form

Origin Oﬀset-X/Origin Oﬀset-Y: speciﬁes the X/Y oﬀset between the center of the shape and origin of the ﬁrst generated instance.

X-Pitch/Y-Pitch: speciﬁes the horizontal/vertical distance between the centers of adjacent instances.

X-Space/Y-Space: speciﬁes the horizont:al/vertical space between adjacent instances.

Outline Layer: if this option is checked, it will use the speciﬁed shape boundary as array instance’s boundary. As shown below.

![image 4702](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4702.png)

Figure 66.141 Generate Array On Shape by Specifying Outline Layer

Generate Array By Row: if this option is checked„ it will place array instances with row mode.

Keep Instance Which Overlapped On Shape Ratio: speciﬁes the smallest ratio of the area whose instance’s boundary is overlapped with selected shape. The instance will be generated only when the ratio is larger than the speciﬁed value.

Smash Instance Which Overlapped On Shape: when this option is on, these generated instances of overlapped on shape boundary will be smashed into one level. However, these smashed instances or shapes that are overlapped with the select area will not be considered.

Add Dummy Cell When dx < =X Pitch: if the distance between the intersection of shape and instance and the outermost part of instance is less than or equal to ratio X Pitch, the edge of instance will be added to a dummy cell.

Make Arrays As A Cell: makes the generated arrays as a whole new cell. Generate Report: generates a report about the arrays.

## 66.22 Convert Shapes To Array

Menu: ToolBox -> Convert Shapes To Array

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4716](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4716.png)

This command converts a group of same shapes to one array instance. It only allows you to select Polygon, Rectangle, Path, Donut, Circle, Ellipse in this command. The operation steps are:

- • Select one or a group of shapes. You can select shapes before or after activating command. Invalid objects will be deselected if you have selected them before the command starts.
- • Point at the second shape, Aether will calculate the X/Y-Pitch between the boundary box of the ﬁrst group shape and the second group.
- • Aether will search in X,Y direction and ﬁnd all the shapes that are exactly same as the ﬁrst group of shapes, including same number, same shape, same X/Y-Pitch from previous group.

||Note: Searching direction is X/Y-Positive or X/Y-Negative depends on X/Y-Pitch got by the ﬁrst step. For example, if X/Y-Pitch is positive, Aether will search shapes in X/Y-Positive direction.|
|---|
|
|---|


- • After ﬁnding all shapes, Aether will make the ﬁrst group shapes as the basic cell, then expand basic cell to array. The cell name is speciﬁed at Cell in the form.


||Note: The row and column number of array is based on how many exact same groups of shapes Aether ﬁnds in X,Y direction.|
|---|
|
|---|


![image 4717](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4717.png)

Figure 66.155 Convert Shapes To Array Form

Library: speciﬁes the library name which array instance is generated. Cell: speciﬁes the cell name which array instance is generated. View: speciﬁes the view name which array instance is generated. Filter: set ﬁlter for selecting library or cell or view.

Delete Original Shapes: the default mode is unchecked. If check this option, it will delete original shapes which have been already converted to array instance.

Example 66.29 The example shows how to use the function of convert shapes to array.

- 1. Activate the command and ﬁll options ToolBox -> Convert Shapes To Array, specify the cell name as array.


![image 4718](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4718.png)

- Figure 66.156 Activate the command and ﬁll options
- 2. Select ﬁrst group of shapes, you can also select one shape.

![image 4719](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4719.png)

Figure 66.157 Select ﬁrst shapes

- 3. Point at the second shape, Aether will calculate the X/Y-Pitch.


![image 4720](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4720.png)

Figure 66.158 X/Y-Pitch

- 4. Aether searches shapes in X/Y direction and ﬁnds all exact shapes, then convert them to array. In this case, Aether ﬁnds 5 exact groups of shapes in X-Positive direction and 8 groups in Y-Positive direction. So ﬁnally, it generated 5*8 array whose cell name is array.

![image 4721](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4721.png)

Figure 66.159 Convert to one array instance

- 5. Display array instance content.


![image 4722](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4722.png)

Figure 66.160 Display array instance content.

## 66.25 Check Instance Orientation

Menu: ToolBox -> Check Instance Orientation ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4737](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4737.png)

This command is used to check the instance orientation from the top cell, it can help user to make sure the correctness/accuracy of some sub cells’ orientation.

![image 4738](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4738.png)

Figure 66.173 Check Instance Orientation Form Library Name: speciﬁes library name of sub cell. Cell Name: speciﬁes cell name of sub cell. View Name: speciﬁes view name of sub cell. Rotate: speciﬁes checking orientation

- • R0: represents no change in orientation.
- • R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. • R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. • MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.
- • MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- • MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.
- • MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.


Report: speciﬁes whether to generate the checking report after operation, the format of report is as follows:

66.25. Check Instance Orientation

Lib/Cell/View:LayerSet/rotate/layout Rotate !=R270 The boundary of instances which violate rule are following:

1. (0,0)(1,1) 2. (3,3)(4,4)

## 66.31 Smart Fill Dummy Pattern

Menu: ToolBox -> Smart Fill Dummy Pattern ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4799](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4799.png)

This command ﬁlls as many cells as possible in the selected areas, including Circle, Ellipse, Rectangle, Polygon, Donut.

![image 4800](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4800.png)

Figure 66.215 Smart Fill Dummy Pattern Form

Dummy Cell: speciﬁes the lib/cell/view of placing cell. BBox: when BBox is checked, bounding box of cell is set as cell’s outline. Layers: when Layers is checked, boundary of some layers of objects in cell is set as cell’s outline. X-Space: speciﬁes the x space of two adjacent cells. Y-Space: speciﬁes the y space of two adjacent cells. Placing Region: speciﬁes the placing region. By Layer: speciﬁes the layers of the placing region. By Area: form will disappear after Draw is clicked, and you can select a polygon area by cartoon in draw area as the placing region. Space To Region Edge: speciﬁes the min space between cell and the region edge. Avoid Cells: speciﬁes the cells to avoid. BBOX: when BBox is checked, bounding box of cell is set as avoid boundary. Layers: when Layers is checked, boundary of some layers of objects in cell is set as avoid boundary.

: clicks this tool button to delete a line in Avoid Cells. : clicks this tool button to add a new line in Avoid Cells.

![image 4801](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4801.png)

![image 4802](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4802.png)

Avoid layers: speciﬁes the boundary of some layers of objects as avoid boundary.

Space To Avoid Pattern: speciﬁes the min space between cell and the avoid edge.

Smash Overlapped Instance: checks on this checkbox, smash cells one level which overlapped the placing region, delete the sub cells outside of space to region edge, and keep the sub cells within the placing region.

Keep Array: checks on this checkbox, keep array in each placing region. Save As Cell: checks on this checkbox, then all the placing cell will be stored in a cell, which will be assigned a name followed. Message: shows warning/error and other log information during command execution. Stopped: the program will be stopped after Stop is clicked. Preview: previews the placing cell by cartoon. Apply: ﬁnishes placing, without exiting the form. OK: ﬁnishes placing, and exits the form. Cancel: cancels this command.

## 67.10 Component List

Menu: Window -> Component List ToolBar:

![image 4864](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4864.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is mainly used to create components. There are diﬀerent types of components: Bump/Pad, Pin, Channel, Inductor,Block, Domain and ESD.

Bump/Pad: speciﬁes the option settings of Bump/Pad Component. It has three diﬀerent shapes: circle, square, octagon.

![image 4865](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4865.png)

Figure 67.5 Component List: Bump

![image 4866](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4866.png)

Figure 67.6 Create Bump Component Form

• Component Type: speciﬁes the type of Component. Default is Bump.

- – Bump: speciﬁes the Component type is Bump.
- – Pad: speciﬁes the Component type is Pad.


• Signal Type: speciﬁes the signal type of created Bump/Pad Component. Default is None.

- – None: speciﬁes the signal type is None.
- – Power: speciﬁes the signal type is Power.
- – Ground: speciﬁes the signal type is Ground.
- – Signal: speciﬁes the signal type is Signal.


• Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation mode. Default value is R0 and this option will be enabled when Mode is Center Radius and Speciﬁed Size is checked. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degrees counterclockwisete.

- – R0: represents no change in orientation.
- – R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. – R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. – MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.
- – MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.
- – MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a


rotation of 90 degrees.

• Mode: speciﬁes the mode to create Bump/Pad Component.

– Center Radius: speciﬁes the Bump/Pad Component will be cre-

ated by center radius.

– Boundary: speciﬁes the Bump/Pad Component will be created by

boundary.

– Bump/Pad Ring: speciﬁes the Bump/Pad Component will be cre-

ated as ring.

- • Bump Diameter: speciﬁes the diameter of Bump/Pad Component if the option is checked. The default value is 60 and this option will be not enabled when Mode is Boundary.
- • Speciﬁed Size: speciﬁes the width and height of Bump/Pad Component if the option is checked. This option is mutually exclusive with Bump Diameter and will be not enabled when Mode is Boundary.
- • Width: speciﬁes the width of Bump/Pad Component.
- • Height: speciﬁes the height of Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Names: speciﬁes the pin name of Bump/Pad Component.


- • Create In Group: speciﬁes whether created Bump/Pad Components in group. The option will be enabled if the number of Bump/Pad Components is more than 1.
- • Array: speciﬁes the array of Bump/Pad Components.


– Cols: speciﬁes the column number of Bump/Pad Component array.

Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.

– X-Pitch: speciﬁes the length of distance between Bump/Pad Com-

ponent centers in X direction.

– Rows: speciﬁes the row number of Bump/Pad Component array.

Default value is 1, minimum is 1, maximum is 32767.

– Y-Pitch: speciﬁes the length of distance between Bump/Pad Com-

ponent centers in Y direction.

– Delta: speciﬁes whether needs to be oﬀset. ∗ X: speciﬁes the oﬀset between diﬀerent rows. ∗ Y: speciﬁes the oﬀset between diﬀerent cols.

• Ring: speciﬁes the option settings of the ring of Bump/Pad Components. The following options will be shown and enabled if Mode is Bump/Pad Ring.

– Rows: speciﬁes the row number of the ring of Bump/Pad Compo-

nent. Default value is 1, maximum is 2.

– Generate Method: speciﬁes the generate method.

∗ Inside: speciﬁes the ring will be generated inside the select rectangle shape.

∗ Outside: speciﬁes the ring will be generated outside the select rectangle shape.

– Location: speciﬁes which location of the ring of Bump/Pad Com-

ponents will be generated. Default is all.

- – Space to Shape: speciﬁes the space between shape and row1.
- – Array Pitch: speciﬁes the pitch of the same rows of the ring.
- – X-Oﬀset: speciﬁes the oﬀset relative to the array growth direction.
- – Y-Oﬀset: speciﬁes the oﬀset of the diﬀerent rows of the ring.


- • Library Name: speciﬁes the library name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Cell Name: speciﬁes the cell name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.


- • View Name: speciﬁes the view name of the device associated with the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Length: speciﬁes the length of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Pin Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.
- • Label Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin label corresponding to the Bump/Pad Component.


Pin: speciﬁes the option settings of Pin Component.

![image 4867](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4867.png)

Figure 67.7 Component List: Pin

![image 4868](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4868.png)

Figure 67.8 Create Pin Component Form

- • Pin Names: speciﬁes the name of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Space: speciﬁes the spacing between the corresponding instantiated pins of the Pin Component when the Pin Names is bus name.
- • Pin Width: speciﬁes the width of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.


- • Pin Length: speciﬁes the length of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Pin Layer: speciﬁes the layer of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Label Layer: speciﬁes the label layer of the pin corresponding to the Pin Component.
- • Order: speciﬁes the placement order of the pins corresponding to the Pin Component. Default is In Order.


– In Order: speciﬁes pin placement in order according to Pin Names. – Reverse Order: speciﬁes pin placement in reverse order according

##### to Pin Names.

• Separate: speciﬁes the interval mode when Pin Names is bus name. Default is None.

- – None: speciﬁes no interval.
- – Odd-Even: speciﬁes Odd-Even interval. – Even-Odd: speciﬁes Even-Odd interval. – Two-Bits: speciﬁes Two-Bits interval.
- – Three-Bits: speciﬁes Three-Bits interval.


• Cross: speciﬁes whether the placement of the pins corresponding to the Pin Component should be interleaved. Default is None.

- – None: speciﬁes no cross.
- – Cross: speciﬁes cross.


Channel: speciﬁes option settings of Channel Component and it has three diﬀerent shapes.

![image 4869](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4869.png)

Figure 67.9 Component List: Channel

![image 4870](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4870.png)

(a) Create Rectangle/Polygon Channel Component Form

![image 4871](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4871.png)

(b) Create Path Channel Component Form

Figure 67.10 Create Channel Component Form

- • Channel Name: speciﬁes which modules are connected to the Channel Component.
- • Net Names: speciﬁes which nets are included in the Channel Component. If you have already selected pins, the names of selected pins are automatically ﬁlled into this option.
- • Channel Width: speciﬁes the width of Channel Component. The option is displayed only when creating path shape Channel Component. Default value is 2 * manufacturing grid.
- • Pin: speciﬁes whether the routing width and spacing in the Channel Component are consistent with the pins.


– Width: speciﬁes routing width in the Channel Component. Default

is Same to Pin. ∗ Same to Pin: speciﬁes generating routing based on the width of the pins. ∗ Specify: speciﬁes the width of the generated routing.

– Space: speciﬁes routing space in the Channel Component. Default

is Same to Pin. ∗ Same to Pin: speciﬁes generating routing based on the space of the pins. ∗ Specify: speciﬁes the space of the generated routing.

• Layer: speciﬁes layer for routing. Default is Specify.

– Specify: if this option is checked, Horizontal Layers and Vertical Layers will be shown. Please choose the same number of horizontal

and vertical layers. ∗ Horizontal Layers: speciﬁes the layers for horizontal routing. ∗ Vertical Layers: speciﬁes the layers for vertical routing.

##### – Range: if this option is checked, Top Layer and Bottom Layer

will be shown. ∗ Top Layer: speciﬁes the top layer of routing range. ∗ Bottom Layer: speciﬁes the bottom layer of routing range.

Inductor: speciﬁes option settings of Inductor Component and it has two diﬀerent shapes.

- • Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation mode. Default value is R0. Clicking RMB will rotate the objects 90-degrees counter-clockwisete.


- – R0: represents no change in orientation.
- – R90: represents a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – R180: represents a rotation of 180 degrees. – R270: represents a rotation of 270 degrees. – MY: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis.
- – MYR90: represents mirroring relative to the Y axis and then a rotation of 90 degrees.
- – MX: represents mirroring relative to the X axis.
- – MXR90: represents mirroring relative to the X axis and then a


rotation of 90 degrees.

- • Speciﬁed Size: speciﬁes the width and height of Inductor Component if the option is checked.
- • Width: speciﬁes the width of Inductor Component.
- • Height: speciﬁes the height of Inductor Component.

## 67.11 LSW

Menu: Window -> LSW ToolBar: BindKey: None

![image 4897](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4897.png)

Tcl Command: None This command is used to show/hide LSW window. Note: If you close LSW, the Component in schematic editor and None in symbol editor are closed too. If you open it, the other two panels are opened too.

### 67.11.1 LSW Introduction

LSW means layer select window. You can modify the layer in LSW without changing technology.

![image 4898](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4898.png)

Figure 67.35 Layer Select Window

When layout is opened in MT mode, you can modify the die layer in LSW independently without changing technology.

![image 4899](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4899.png)

Figure 67.36 Layer Select Window in MT mode

Menu: there is a menu item for LSW, Edit. Technology Library Name: lists the technology library name.

Layer Status List: switches layer status. You can set status as you want ﬁrst, then you save status to A, B, C or D. If necessary, you can switch layer status from A to B quickly.

![image 4900](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4900.png)

Figure 67.37 Layer Checkbox

Layer Checkbox: ﬁlters the display of layers by their attributes, Valid, Used, Routing and MPT (only shown with MPT Support selected.)

![image 4901](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4901.png)

Figure 67.38 Active LPP

Active LPP: shows the active layer-purpose pair. Popup menu records the LPPs used recently.

Set Fill/Visible/Selectable: sets layer status: ﬁll/visible/selectable.

![image 4902](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4902.png)

Figure 67.39 All Visible

- • AV: sets all layers visible. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. AV as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; AV-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; AV-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • NV: sets all layers invisible, except for active LPP. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. NV as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; NV-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; NV-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • AS: sets all layers selectable. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. AS as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; AS-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; AS-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • NS: sets all layers unselectable. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. NS as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; NS-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; NS-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.


AF and NF only display, when Show Fill Buttons item in Edit -> Options is selected.

- • AF: sets all layers ﬁlled. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. AF as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; AF-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; AF-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.
- • NF: sets all layers unﬁlled. The 3 actions in the popup menu have diﬀerent scopes. NF as the default action, acts on layers currently shown in the table; NF-Layer Set acts on layers in the table, and takes the layers ﬁltered by Filter into consideration; NF-Tech File acts on all layers in the technology.


Die Table: show in MT mode. Display or control all layers of dies.

![image 4903](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4903.png)

Figure 67.40 Die Table

• Inst Name: display Inst Name of die, top cell will be displayed with

##### Top.

- • V: sets all layers of die visible or invisible.
- • S: sets all layers of die selectable or unselectable.


Find/Filter: ﬁnds or ﬁlters layers by input string. Click Find/Filter button to switch between ﬁnd mode and ﬁlter mode. The popup menu at the right shows the setups for ﬁnd and ﬁlter mode. To see more details, LSW-> Find/Filter

Layer Set: lists the layer set. Layer set is a set of layers. Default layer sets include All, System. You can specify your own layer set by LSW -> Edit -> Layer Set.

Layer Table Header: lists the layer-purpose pairs’ information as column name. Now Aether supports 9 columns Icon, Layer Name, Purpose Name, Color, GDS Number, Visible, Selectable, Validity, and Member with 5 displayed by default.

![image 4904](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4904.png)

Figure 67.41 Layer-Purpose Pair

- • Icon: layer-purpose pair icon
- • Layer Name: layer name of layer-purpose pair
- • Purpose Name: purpose name of layer-purpose pair
- • Color: color icon of layer-purpose pair
- • GDS Number: GDS number of layer-purpose pair
- • Visible: visible state of layer-purpose pair
- • Selectable: selectable state of layer-purpose pair
- • Validity: valid state of layer-purpose pair
- • Member: member state of layer-purpose pair
- • Inst Name: display Inst Name of die in MT mode


![image 4905](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4905.png)

- Figure 67.42 Inst Name

- 67.11.2 Find/Filter This command has 2 modes, Find and Filter, Default: Find.


![image 4906](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4906.png)

- Figure 67.43 Find/Filter Bar


Find/Filter Button: The mode can be switched by clicking this button. Input ComboBox: inputs strings for Find/Filter. Press Enter to record strings in ComboBox popup list. Setup Popup Menu: selects items to set up the conﬁg for Find or Filter mode.

![image 4907](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4907.png)

Figure 67.44 Setup Popup Menu

- • Find With: the items listed in the Find With section are used to specify the search operator for Find/Filter: And(All Of The Words), Or(Any Of The Words), Exactly(The Exact Phrase), and Not(None Of The Words).
- • Match Word: the items listed in the Match Word section are used to specify the matching mode for a word: Substring, Preﬁx, Exactly, Suﬃx.
- • Using Case: the Using Case section is used to specify the case insensitivity of Find/Filter operation.


In Find mode, searching operation is used to ﬁnd an active Layer-Purpose Pair(LPP), according to the input words. The ﬁrst LPP that matches the search criteria becomes the active LPP. Find Operation just acts on LPPs in the current Layer Table. If Used checkbox is selected, the un-used LPPs will not be found by this operation.

In Filter mode, only the LPPs that match the search criteria are displayed in the Layer Table. Active LPP doesn’t change.

### 67.11.3 Layer Table Header

The Layer Table display status indicates the layer-purpose pair’s information, such as visibility, selectability, validity, and ﬁll state.

- • Icon Display: if the layer-purpose pair is invisible, the icon will be hidden.
- • Icon Fill: if the layer-purpose pair is unﬁlled, the icon will be unﬁlled.

- • Left Mouse Button: clicking and dragging on left mouse button to change an active LPP.
- • Middle Mouse Button: clicking and dragging on middle mouse button to change the visibility of LPP. Ctrl+ middle mouse click to start Display Resource Editor.
- • Right Mouse Button: clicking and dragging on right mouse button to change the selectability of LPP.
- • Mouse Hover over: hovering over a LPP to display the tip information of the LPP.

### 67.11.10 Layer Set Manager

The Layer Set Manager in the LSW lists all the layer sets that are available in the current design window.

![image 4934](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4934.png)

###### Figure 67.61 Layer Set Manager

Layer Set Manager Table: lists the layer set information. Now Aether supports three columns: Name, Visibility, and Selectability.

- • Name: layer set name.
- • Visibility: sets visibility state of layer-purpose pairs in layer set.
- • Selectability: sets selectability state of layer-purpose pairs in layer set. • +: sets layer-purpose pairs listed in the Layer Table and in corresponding


layer set at the same time to visible or selectable.

• -: sets layer-purpose pairs listed in the Layer Table and in corresponding layer set at the same time to invisible or deselectable.

All layer sets selected in the Layer Set Manager are considered active and a layer-purpose pair is listed in the Layer Table if it is a member of at least one of the selected layer sets.

Example 67.6

The example shows how to select one or more layer sets and turn on or oﬀ the visibility and selectability.

## 67.13 Annotation Assistant

Menu: Window -> Annotation Assistant ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 4940](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4940.png)

This command is used to display marker information reported by SDL -> Extract layout, SDL -> Check From Schematic and MPT -> Color Locking Check operations. It has Connectivity, CFS, CLCR tabs. The form is shown in Figure 67.66 .

![image 4941](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4941.png)

Figure 67.66 Annotation Assistant

Zoom To Markers: allows you to magnify the marker from results and show it in the center of window. Default value is 2.

Tree: check result tree. Connectivity: displays the result of command SDL -> Extract Layout.

- • Illegal Connections: displays illegal connections.
- • Incomplete Nets: displays if there aren’t physical connections between objects belonging to the same net in the current cell view.
- • Shorts: displays if there are physical connections between objects belonging to diﬀerent nets in the current cell view.
- • Visible: if you check it, all the child markers are shown in current window.


CFS: displays the result of command SDL -> Check From Schematic.

- • Connectivity: displays the result of connectivity.
- • Dummy Instances: displays the result of dummy instances.
- • Masters: displays the result if masters are diﬀerent between layout and schematic.
- • Names: displays the result if names are diﬀerent between layout and schematic.


- • Parameters: displays the result if parameter value is diﬀerent between layout and schematic.
- • Unbound: displays the result of instances, pin and net, which is in layout but not in schematic.
- • Ungenerated: displays the result of instances, pin and net, which is in schematic but not in layout.
- • Visible: if you check it, all the child markers are shown in current window.
- • Color: you can choose diﬀerent color to highlight the corresponding instance,pin or net in schematic or layout.


CLCR: displays the result of command MPT -> Color Locking Check.

- • Color locking check rules: displays diﬀerent check results according to diﬀerent check rules.
- • Visible: if you check it, all the child markers are shown in current window, on the contrary, markers are not showed in current window.


Delete: deletes the marker which you choose in the tree. Delete parent in tree, all the child markers will be deleted. Support multiple selection.

Delete All: deletes all markers. Description: shows the speciﬁc information of the marker which you choose

.

# Chapter 68 Options

## 68.1 Settings

Menu: Options -> Settings ToolBar: BindKey: E Tcl Command: None

![image 4962](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4962.png)

This command is used to set options for Aether-LE. It has Display, Editor, Measure, Gravity and Route. Especially, Route is valid in AetherAdv.

Display: sets display settings for Aether-LE, which decides how to display layout view.

2395

![image 4963](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4963.png)

###### Figure 68.1 Display in Settings Form (in Aether)

![image 4964](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4964.png)

Figure 68.2 Display in Settings Form (in AetherAdv)

- • Grid: speciﬁes how to draw the grid in layout editor.


- – Minimum Resolution: manufacturing grid.
- – Minor Spacing: speciﬁes space between minor grid.
- – Major Step: speciﬁes step between major grid, the space between major grid is multiple of minor spacing and major step.


- – X Snap Spacing: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves in the x direction.
- – Y Snap Spacing: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves in the y direction.
- – Type: speciﬁes grid type, default is Dot. ∗ None: doesn’t show grid. ∗ Dot: shows grid in dot. ∗ Line: shows grid in line.
- – Snap Cursor To Minor Ratio: speciﬁes snap spacing which mouse moves. Aether deﬁnes snap spacing as multiple of minor spacing if the checkbox is checked, or the snap spacing is equal to manufacturing grid.
- – Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of grid dot(50 ~255). Default is 80.


- • Instance: speciﬁes how to draw instance in layout editor.


– Show: speciﬁes how to show instance’s attributes. ∗ Inst Name: speciﬁes whether to show instance name or not. ∗ Cell Name: speciﬁes whether to show cell name of instance or

not. ∗ Origin: speciﬁes whether to show origin of instance or not. ∗ F-Style: speciﬁes whether to show instance in F-Style or not.

F-Style illustrates the rotation of instance.

![image 4965](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile4965.png)

∗ display: this mode displays all design elements in a standard view format.

- – Full: if checked, no object will be ﬁltered when Filter Level is set to 0. This option is disabled when Filter Level is set from 1 to 6.
- – Fuzzy Ratio: speciﬁes fuzzy ratio for instances or vias or shapes. The ratio is bigger, the performance is better but the quality is lower.


- Valid is from 0 to 100, default is 100.
- – Fuzzy Mode: speciﬁes fuzzy mode for instances or vias or shapes. Min means using the shorter side to deal fuzzy. Max means using the longer side to deal fuzzy. The performance is better but the quality is lower with Min. Default is Min.
- – Drag Limit: speciﬁes upper limitation to display objects which are dragged. Valid is from 1 to 10000, default is 200.
- – Shape Brightness: speciﬁes brightness of shapes displayed in LE. Valid is from 0 to 200 in percentage, default is 100, the same as LSW shows.

- • Wire Editing: speciﬁes the behavior of wire editing.


- – Wire Snapping: speciﬁes the behavior of wire snapping mode, the combination mode of options Off Grid, Manufacturing Grid, Routing Grid, Track Pattern, Snap Pattern may be used to create wire. When selecting Track Pattern, the Detect Track option is enabled.


∗ Oﬀ Grid: does not snapping. ∗ Manufacturing Grid: snaps the wire to the manufacturing

grid.

∗ Routing Grid: snaps the wire and the via to the routing grid. ∗ Track Pattern: snaps the wire and the via to the track pattern. ∗ Snap Pattern: snaps the wire to the snap pattern.

- – Detect Track: if selected, snaps the wire to the centerline of the track pattern. Also, the wire inherits the width of the active width spacing pattern and the direction in which the wire is created is the same as the direction of the track pattern.
- – Wire Constraint Group: speciﬁes the wire constraint group.

∗ foundry: this option applies design contraints based on speciﬁc fabrication rules provided by the foundry.

∗ default: this option uses a set of general constraints suitable for common design practices.

- – Parameters Calculator: speciﬁes parameters calculator for wire.

∗ Min Rules And ViaDef: this option calculates wire parameters based on both minimum design rules and via deﬁnitions to ensure compliance with basic fabrication standards.

∗ Minimum Rules: this option calculates wire parameters based on the minimum design rules to ensure compliance with basic fabrication standards.

∗ Viadef Defaults: this option evaluates wire connection parameters using default via deﬁnitions to ensure optimal electrical performance.

- – Merge Wires: if this option is checked, the generated wire will be merged.


- • Create Via: speciﬁes the behavior of creating via.


- – Constraint Group: speciﬁes the constraint group for creating via.

∗ Same As Wire: this option applies the same constraint group settings that are currently used for wire routing.

∗ default: this option uses a set of general constraints suitable for common design practices.

∗ foundry: this option applies design contraints based on speciﬁc fabrication rules provided by the foundry.

- – Parameters Calculator: speciﬁes parameters calculator for creating via.


∗ Min Rules And Viadef: this option calculates via parameters based on both minimum design rules and default via deﬁnitions.

∗ Minimum Rules: this option applies only the minimum design rules to calculate via parameters.

∗ Viadef Defaults: this option evaluates via parameters using default via deﬁnitions.

Save/Load Mode: speciﬁes the mode for save and load.

- • File: speciﬁes ﬁle mode. Press Save, options will be saved to the ﬁle speciﬁed in lineedit at rightside. Press Load, it will load options from the speciﬁed ﬁle.
- • Library: speciﬁes library mode. Press Save at Display tab, display options will be saved to current library’s data.dm. Press Load at Display tab, will load options from current library’s data.dm. Switching to other tabs, Library checkbox will be hidden. Press Save at other tabs, display options will be saved to data.dm, other options will be saved to speciﬁed ﬁle. The behavior of load is similar.
- • Tech Library: speciﬁes tech library mode. Press Save, display options will be saved to data.dm of current library’s techlib. Press Load, will load options from data.dm of current library’s techlib. Switching to other tabs, Tech Library checkbox will be hidden. Behavior of Save and Load, please refer to Library mode.

Sometimes, you need to take snapshot, but default background is in black, which will result in a bad eﬀect in snapshot. Using this command, you can set Background to white. It will be much better than in black. And you can save your modiﬁcation in order to use next time.
