If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Line Style: shows line Style to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Fill: shows ﬁll Color to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Outline: shows outline Color to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Fill Style: shows ﬁll style to use. It cannot be modiﬁed here. If you want to modify it, please do it in Display Resource Editor. Load: loads user color setting from rc ﬁle. Save As: saves the current color setting as a rc ﬁle. Apply: applies the setting to current section, current project or current user.

- • Apply the setting to current section: the setting is only valid during the current AetherMW event period
- • Apply the setting to current project: the setting is only valid for the current project


• Apply the setting to current user: the setting is only valid for the current user

Default: restores the default color scheme of Layout Editor.

## 68.7 DRD

Menu: Options -> DRD ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5111](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5111.png)

This command is used to set options for DRD. DRD is design rule driven. When you create, modify object which disobeys the design rule, Aether will prompt a message. Aether will adjust the appropriate way automatically sometimes.

![image 5112](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5112.png)

Figure 68.91 DRD Form

DRD Mode: speciﬁes drd mode, default disable it.

- • Notify: Aether only notices user.
- • Enforce: Aether not only notices user, but also adjusts the object to appropriate position.


1. If distance is less than 1/2 of rule, Aether will snap to zero.

2. If distance is greater than 1/2 of rule and less than rule, Aether will snap to value of rule.

![image 5113](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5113.png)

![image 5114](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5114.png)

(a) Distance < Half of Rule (b) Distance > Half of Rule

Figure 68.92 Enforce Mode

3. If distance is greater than rule, Aether will snap to value of rule by

##### Rebounding Radius.

- • Hierarchy Depth: speciﬁes the hierarchy depth for DRD. Valid is from 0 to 50, default is 0.

Note: If you set it to 50, Aether will spend more time and memory doing DRD.

- • Category: speciﬁes which design rule Aether uses.


- – All: speciﬁes to all design rules.
- – Spacing: Aether will use spacing(minSpacing) rule in technology to do DRD. The red message shows spacing error, the white message shows width warning which is closer to the width rule.


![image 5115](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5115.png)

Figure 68.93 Spacing Rule

- – Width: Aether will use width(minWidth) rule in technology to do DRD. The red message shows width error, the white message shows warning which width is closer to the width rule.


![image 5116](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5116.png)

Figure 68.94 Width Rule

- – Overlap: Aether will use overlap(minExtension) rule in technology to do DRD.

![image 5117](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5117.png)

Figure 68.95 Overlap Rule

- – Enc: Aether will use enclosure(minEnclosure) rule in technology to do DRD.


![image 5118](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5118.png)

- Figure 68.96 Enc Rule
- – Area: it is invalid now.
- – Edge Length: it is invalid now.
- – Misc: it is invalid now.


Text Height: speciﬁes text height of message. Character ‘s’ is for spacing, ‘w’ is for width, ‘o’ is for overlap and ‘e’ is for enc in messages.

Rebounding Radius: speciﬁes the boundary radius which is used to query object. Valid is from 0 to 10000 pixels, default is 40 pixels. Aether will use maximum between Rebounding Radius and Max Threshold.

Ruler Displaying Radius: speciﬁes the radius which Aether shows messages.

Max Threshold: speciﬁes maximum threshold which is used to query object, default is 1 um. Aether will use minimum value between Rebounding Radius and Max Threshold.

![image 5119](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5119.png)

Figure 68.97 Rebounding Radius and Max Threshold

## 68.8 Route Options

Menu: Options -> Route Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5120](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5120.png)

This command is used to set options for Aether-Route. It has Pin, Trunk and Common. You can set the following options.

##### Pin: provides a setting interface for Clock, Power and Ground, Label Pin, Prefer Pin, Device Connected, Trunk Width, Bus Width, etc.

![image 5121](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5121.png)

###### Figure 68.98 Pin in Route Options Form

- • Clock Included When Nets Are Selected Automatically: speciﬁes to include the clock when nets are selected automatically, default is selected.
- • Power And Ground Included When Nets Are Selected Automatically: speciﬁes to include power and ground when nets are selected automatically, default is not selected.
- • Identify Label Pin: speciﬁes to identify the label pin, default is not selected.
- • Extract Pin: speciﬁes how pins and nets are to be connected, default is Pin Shape Or Net Shape Only.


##### – Pin Shape Or Net Shape Only: speciﬁes to connect only pin or

net shape.

– Net Through Same Layer: speciﬁes to connect shapes on the

same layer as the pin.

##### – Whole Net On Routing Layers: speciﬁes to connect the entire

net on the routing layer associated with the pin.

- • Connect All Pins When Multiple Pins Of Supply: speciﬁes to connect all pins of the same net when there multiple pins for the same supply in a pattern group or instance. The default is not selected and the pins will be connected according to the priority of the highest metal, the widest pin, and the nearest pin. If there are multiple nets with the same signal, signal net automatically selects the connection pin based on the shortest path.
- • Prefer Pin: speciﬁes the priority for pin identiﬁcation, default is Pin


##### Layer.

- – Pin Layer: speciﬁes to prioritize the identiﬁcation of the highest metal layer pin within a pattern group. If there are multiple pins in the higher layer, then speciﬁes to prioritize those with a larger width.
- – Pin Width: speciﬁes to prioritize the identiﬁcation of the widest metal pin within a pattern group. If there are multiple pins of the same width, then speciﬁes to prioritize those in higher layer levels.


- • Update Connectivity When Routing: speciﬁes to update physical connectivity. Default is not selected.
- • Extract Connectivity To Level: speciﬁes the depth to which physical connectivity is extracted, default is 0. Only show in ﬂoorplan(FPV).
- • Device Connected: it is a table space where you can specify the terminal and vias width. Example 68.1


The example shows how to edit Device Connected.

1. Click the “+” to add a blank line, select a blank line and click the “-” to delete the selected blank line. Click the cell to input numbers directly, or double-click to enter edit mode.

![image 5122](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5122.png)

Figure 68.99 Device Connected Edit Example 1

- – Terminal: This is a user-deﬁned term that instructs the router to identify a speciﬁc lower-level instance.The instance is identiﬁed by the name string deﬁned in the ’terminal’ when setting the width.
- – Vias Width: the value is an integer value representing the number


of vias.

• Trunk Width: speciﬁes the width of the main trunk in the trunk router, default is Bigger Pin.

![image 5123](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5123.png)

Figure 68.100 Trunk Width in Route Options Form

– Bigger Pin: speciﬁes to use the maximum width of the pin.

∗ Times: speciﬁes the multiplier factor, which means the width is a multiple of the bigger pin’s width. Default is 1.

- – Smaller Pin: speciﬁes to use the minimum width of the pin.
- – Setup Rule: speciﬁes to use the set layer width.
- – Specify Width: speciﬁes to use the width.


∗ Vias Width: speciﬁes the width of the vias. The default value is 2 when the Trunk Width tab is selected, and 1 when Bus Width tab is selected.

• Bus Width: speciﬁes the width of the main bus in the bus router, default is Bigger Pin.

![image 5124](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5124.png)

Figure 68.101 Bus Width in Route Options Form

- – Bigger Pin: speciﬁes to use the maximum width among the pins.
- – Smaller Pin: speciﬁes to use the minimum width among the pins.
- – Setup Rule: speciﬁes to use the width set for the layer.
- – Specify Width: speciﬁes to use the width.


∗ Vias Width: speciﬁes the width of the vias.

- • Use Pin Width To Separate I/V Nets Or Control Nets: speciﬁes to distinguish between IV nets and control nets. If not selected, key nets are identiﬁed based on user-deﬁned priority levels less than or equal to 4, symmetrical and diﬀerential pairs, or subsequent regular expression matching. When selected, it builds upon the unselected state by considering nets with pins wider than two via widths as key nets. Default is selected.
- • Bus Router Through Instance Or Pattern Group: speciﬁes that the bus router will pass through instances or pattern groups. If not selected, the router will not pass through. Default is selected.
- • Bus Router Near To Instance Or Pattern Group: speciﬁes that the bus router’s path will prioritize being adjacent to instances or pattern groups. If selected, the router will favor routes that are close to instances or pattern groups. If not selected, it will follow the shortest and most direct path.
- • Use “+” Mode When Nets Crossing: speciﬁes the mode to be used when nets intersect. If not selected, the “X” mode is used for intersections. If selected, the “+” mode is applied. Default is not selected.
- • Valid PurposeUse: this option is for conﬁguring the purpose of the layer(routing layer)in the techﬁle when it is not intended for drawing. If selected, the speciﬁed purpose is used to obtain the relevant routing layer. Default is selected and input area defaults to the drawing pin.


- • Save To...: saves the setting of this form.
- • Load From...: loads the settings to this form.


Trunk: speciﬁes the main conduit for signal routing.

![image 5125](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5125.png)

Figure 68.102 Trunk in Route Options Form

• Trunk Mode: speciﬁes the mode for trunk routing. Default selection is

##### Single Trunk.

![image 5126](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5126.png)

– : clicks the toolbar item to switch Sin-

gle/Multiple Trunk quickly.

– Single Trunk: speciﬁes to use a single trunk for all connections.

– Multiple Trunk: speciﬁes to use multiple trunks for connections.

• Width Space Mode: speciﬁes the spacing and width conﬁguration for the trunk. Default selection is Width Space Group.

- – Width Space Group: speciﬁes the grouping of widths.
- – Width Space Pattern: speciﬁes the pattern of width distribution.


• Density: speciﬁes the density of the trunk routing. Default selection is

##### Medium.

- – High: speciﬁes high density trunk routing.
- – Medium: speciﬁes medium density trunk routing.
- – Low: speciﬁes low density trunk routing.


##### • Experience Value Of Trunk Calculation: speciﬁes the value used to

ﬁne-tune trunk calculation based on experience. Common: speciﬁes common settings used during routing.

![image 5127](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5127.png)

###### Figure 68.103 Common in Route Options Form

- • Process Via Conﬂict Automatically: speciﬁes whether to automatically handle via conﬂicts.
- • Display Route Report: speciﬁes whether to display the routing report after the routing process is completed.


## 68.9 SDL Options

Menu: Options -> SDL Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5128](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5128.png)

This command is used to set options for Aether-SDL. It includes General, Connectivity, Generation and Parameters.

General: provides setting interface for Flight Lines, Net, synchronize between SE and LE, Schematic Open mode. The ﬁrst part Show Flight Lines speciﬁes the Flight Lines display rules. The second part Power/Ground Nets assigns the name of Power and Ground which belong to Power Net or Ground Net. The third part is composed of a single check box which determines whether to synchronize SE and LE. And the ﬁnal part Schematic Opening Option is mainly responsible for the open mode of corresponding schematic.

![image 5129](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5129.png)

Figure 68.104 General in SDL Options Form

- • Show Flight Lines: speciﬁes how to display Flight Lines.

– Show Distance Connections: speciﬁes whether to display all

Flight Lines.

– Hide Global/Power/Ground Nets: speciﬁes whether to display

the Flight Lines of Global Net, Power Net and Ground Net.

– Use Colors: speciﬁes whether to display Flight Lines in diﬀerent

colors.

- • Power/Ground Nets: speciﬁes Power and Ground Nets.

- – Power Name: speciﬁes the Power Net Name.
- – Ground Name: speciﬁes the Ground Net Name.


- • Probe Nets During Object Creation: speciﬁes whether nets that are speciﬁed during object creation are highlighted in the layout canvas.
- • Cross Selection: speciﬁes whether to synchronize SE and LE.
- • Schematic Opening Option: speciﬁes the options to open the corresponding Schematic.


- – Open With Schematic: if this option is selected, when opening Layout the corresponding Schematic will also be opened.
- – Open Corresponding Schematic During EIP Or Descend: speciﬁes whether to open the corresponding Schematic when EIP or Descend in Layout enter the lower unit, default is Open In New Window.

∗ Open In New Window: when this option is selected, the corresponding Schematic will be opened in new window.

∗ Open In New Tab: when this option is selected, the corresponding Schematic will be opened in new tab.

∗ Open In Current Tab: when this option is selected, the corresponding Schematic will be opened in current tab if top Schematic exists, otherwise opened in new tab.

- – No Schematic: speciﬁes to open Layout without its corresponding Schematic.


Connectivity: speciﬁes settings for Connectivity information and Net information.

![image 5130](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5130.png)

Figure 68.105 Connectivity in SDL Options Form

- • Settings: speciﬁes settings of Connectivity.


- – Extract Layers From Constraint Group: you can select the Constraint Group instead of edit. If no any valid Layer in Constraint Group, this select box will be invalid and be set to None.
- – Report: pops up the report window and prints the Constraint Group information according to the selection in Extract Layers From Constraint Group. If there is without any valid Layer in Constraint Group, this botton will be invalid.
- – Extract Connectivity To Level: speciﬁes the level of Connectivity Export. The value range is [0, 50], default is 0.
- – Update Connectivity When Design Is Modiﬁed: speciﬁes whether to update Connectivity in real time.
- – Enable Substrate Veriﬁcation And Set Well Layers As Soft: speciﬁes whether to report substrate.
- – Use : To Deﬁne Net As Virtually Connected: speciﬁes whether to use ":" to deﬁne virtual connection Net.


- – Across Pycell: speciﬁes whether to allow trace to pass through pycell.


- • Assignment: speciﬁes settings of Net information.

– Keep Shape Assignment: speciﬁes whether to keep the Net in-

formation of Shape.

– Connect Unassign Instance Pin: speciﬁes whether to connect

the Instance Pin without Net information.

– Assign Shapes From Attach Labels: speciﬁes whether to assign

Net information to those shapes which have attached to labels.

– Assign Shapes From Overlapping Labels Deﬁned By StampLabelLayers: speciﬁes whether to assign Net information to those shapes which contain the labels created by StampLabelLayer.

![image 5131](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5131.png)

Figure 68.106 Annotations in SDL Options Form

- • Annotations Types: speciﬁes annotations setting of connectivity.


– Incomplete Nets(Opens): speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete

nets in the annotation form.

– Invalid Instance Pins: speciﬁes whether to list the invalid instance

pins in the annotation form.

- • Signal Types: sets the speciﬁed signal types of incomplete nets to be listed.

- – All: speciﬁes whether to list all incomplete nets.
- – None: speciﬁes whether to list none of incomplete nets.
- – Signal: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Signal.
- – Power: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Power.
- – Ground: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Ground.
- – Clock: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Clock.
- – Scan: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Scan.
- – Reset: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Reset.
- – Analog: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of Analog.
- – TieOﬀ: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of TieOﬀ.
- – TieHigh: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of TieHigh.
- – TieLow: speciﬁes whether to list the incomplete nets of TieLow.


- • Illegal Overlaps For Stopped Colored Shapes: speciﬁes whether to list the overlap shapes in the annotation form.
- • Illegal Hierarchical Connections: speciﬁes whether to list the hierarchical connections in the annotation form.


![image 5132](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5132.png)

- Figure 68.107 Connectivity Limits in SDL Options Form
- • Limit: speciﬁes limits of connectivity.


- – Maximum Number Of Opens By Net: limits the maximum number of open markers to display by net.
- – Maximum Number Of Opens By CellView: limits the maximum open markers number to display in the entire cellView.
- – Maximum Number Of Shorts By Net: limits the maximum number of short markers to display by net.
- – Maximum Number Of Shorts By CellView: limits the maximum illegal markers number to display in the entire cellView.
- – Maximum Number Of illegal Connections By CellView: limits the maximum number of illegal markers to display of the entire cellView.
- – Maximum Number Of Flyline By Net: limits the maximum number of ﬂylines to display by net.


- – Maximum Number Of Flyline By CellView: limits the maximum ﬂyline numbers to display in the entire cellview.


Generation: speciﬁes the settings of generation.

![image 5133](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5133.png)

Figure 68.108 Generation in SDL Options Form

- • Split mFactored Devices: speciﬁes whether to generate multiple devices when encountering the mFactor parameter.
- • Split sFactored Devices: speciﬁes whether to generate multiple devices when encountering the sFactor parameter.
- • Split Fingered Devices: speciﬁes whether to generate multiple devices when Finger parameter is not one.
- • Device Rotate: speciﬁes the rotation direction of the device. Now Aether provides the following options. default is R0.


- – Preserve
- – R0
- – R90


- – R180
- – R270
- – MY
- – MYR90
- – MX
- – MXR90


- • IO Pin Layer List: speciﬁes the default Layer when Generate Pin.
- • Search Cell From Libraries: speciﬁes which Library to use when Generate Cell.


Parameters: speciﬁes the parameters and settings when Generate, Check, and Update check. The ﬁrst part Check/Ignore speciﬁes the parameters which will inﬂuence the behavior of Generate, Check and Update check. The second part Schematic Parameters clariﬁes the inconsistent parameters between Schematic and Layout. The third part Parameter Check/Generation/Update speciﬁes the options for Parameter Check/Generation/Update. The ﬁnal part Component Description Format controls the format of component.

![image 5134](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5134.png)

Figure 68.109 Parameters in SDL Options Form

- • Check/Ignore: speciﬁes the parameters and settings of Generate, Check and Update check, default is Check Parameters.


- – Check Parameters: when this option is selected, if no parameter is speciﬁed here, the function of Check From Schematic will check the consistency of all displayed CDF Parameter between Schematic Instance and the corresponding Layout Instance.
- – Ignore Parameters When Check: when this option is selected, if no parameter is set here, the behavior of Check From Schematic will be same as Check Parameters. Conversely, if Check Parameters is empty, Check From Schematic will ignore the parameters set here; if there are same parameters both in here and Check Parameters, Check From Schematic will not ignore those parameters.
- – Ignore Parameters When Generation And Update: when this option is selected, if no parameter is set here, the CDF Parameters in Schematic of the Instance which are generated by Generate All From Schematic or Generate Selected From Schematic, should apply to Layout, and all inconsistent parameter values need to be updated


- when Update. Conversely, those parameters set here do not need to use the value in Schematic when Generate All From Schematic or Generate Selected From Schematic, and Update will Ignore those parameters. At same time those parameters will be added to Ignore Parameters When Check, so the inconsistency of these parameters will be ignored when Check From Schematic.
- – Ignore Objects With Properties When Check: when this option is selected, if no parameter is set here, Check From Schematic will check whether all Instances both in the current Layout and the Schematic. The property name is usually set to:lvsIgnore, nlAction, ignore, lxRemoveDevice. If Properties is set and the value are compliant, Check From Schematic will ignore those Instance with any one of these Properties, and does not check the consistency in the following situations:

∗ nlAction must be string type and its value must be equal to ignore.

∗ all Properties except nlAction must be of type boolean and their values are true.

- – Ignore Objects With Properties When Generation And Update: when this option is selected, if no property is set here, the Generate and Update action which is executed by Generate Selected From Schematic, Generate Selected From Schematic and Update, can apply to any Instance. The property name is usually set to: nlAction, ignore, lxRemoveDevice. If Properties are set here and the value are compliant, Generate Selected From Schematic, Generate Selected From Schematic and Update will ignore the Instance with any one of those Properties in the following situations:


∗ Properties must be boolean type and its value is true.

The Properties set here will be added to Ignore Objects With Properties When Check, so the Instance with these Properties will be ignored when Check From Schematic.

- • Schematic Parameters: this item is used to set those special parameters which will inﬂuence the behavior of Generate Selected From Schematic, Generate Selected From Schematic and Update. Now Aether provides the following options. Default is mFactor.


- – mFactor: sets Multiple Parameter, which is the parallel parameter of Devices, default value is: m, M.
- – sFactor: sets the Serial Parameter, which is the serial parameter of Devices, default value is: s, S.


- – Transistor Width: sets the Width Parameter name of Transistor, default value is: w, W.
- – Capacitance: sets the Capacitance Parameter name of Capacitance, default value is: c, C.
- – Resistance: sets the Resistance Parameter name of Resistance, default value is: r, R.
- – Inductance: sets the Segment Parameter name of Resistance, default value is: l, L.
- – Fingers: sets the Finger Parameter name of MOS, default value is: ﬁngers, ﬁnger, numFingers, numFinger.
- – Segments: sets the Segment Parameter name of Resistance, default value is: segments.


- • Parameter Check/Generation/Update: speciﬁes options for Parameter Check, Generation and Update.

- – Consider Parameters Only: when this option is selected, Check From Schematic and Update will check the inconsistent value of CDF Parameters and Design Property between Schematic and Layout.
- – Consider Parameters And Properties: when this option is selected, Check From Schematic and Update will check the inconsistent value of CDF Parameters, Design Property and User Property between Schematic and Layout.
- – Ignore Missing Parameters Or Properties: speciﬁes whether to ignore missing Parameters or Properties.
- – Always Consider Properties For Generation: speciﬁes whether to consider Properties when generation.
- – Update Schematic Parameters Expression With Evaluated Value: speciﬁes whether to update the circuit parameter expression.
- – Tolerance: speciﬁes the redundancy of inspection.
- – Update Based On Parameters To Ignore For: speciﬁes which to ignore when Update, Check Parameter or Generate Parameter.


- • Component Description Format: speciﬁes the format of Component.


- – Evaluate CDF Callbacks During Generation And Update: speciﬁes whether to Evaluate CDF Callback during Generate or Update.
- – Signiﬁcant Digits When Calculating Parameter Values: speciﬁes the eﬀective value of the calculation parameter. The value range


is [1, 14], default is 14.

Conﬁgure: speciﬁes the settings of conﬁgure.

![image 5135](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5135.png)

Figure 68.110 Conﬁgure in SDL Options Form

- • All: checks all options.
- • None: unchecks all options.
- • Open With Schematic: if this option is selected, when open layout the corresponding schematic will also be opened.

– Open Corresponding Schematic During EIP Or Descend: speciﬁes whether to open the corresponding schematic when EIP or Descend in layout to enter the lower unit, default is Open In New Window.

- • Update Connectivity When Design Is Modiﬁed: speciﬁes whether to update connectivity in real time.
- • Show Flight Lines: speciﬁes how to display ﬂight lines.
- • Net Name Display: speciﬁes whether to show net name and terminal name, the default is checked.


Default: clicks Default to reload the default settings. Load From: clicks Load From button, then, selects a conﬁguration ﬁle, the SDL Options will use the values in the ﬁle. Save To: clicks Save To button to save settings to a conﬁguration ﬁle. Apply: clicks this Apply button, the settings in the form will take eﬀect. OK: clicks OK to save the settings, and the form exits at the same time. Cancel: clicks this Cancel button, the settings you modiﬁed will be canceled and the form exits at the same time.

Auto Unit: processes diﬀerent PCell units between schematic and layout for related SDL functions like Generate All. This function is implemented through a conﬁguration ﬁle which is not supported on the SDL Options form.

• Work Flow: the basic workﬂow is shown in the following ﬁgure.

1. set parameters mapping relationship through Cell Mapping or CPH. 2. write the Auto Unit conﬁguration ﬁle and load it by pressing Load

##### From button on SDL Options form.

3. do SDL generate functions.

![image 5136](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5136.png)

Figure 68.111 Auto Unit Process Flow

• Conﬁguration File Format: the following code deﬁnes the format of conﬁguration ﬁle: [AutoUnit] lib = param1.u1 param2.u2 lib/cell = param1.u3 add a new section named AutoUnit which has following rules:

- 1. every line should be in the format of Key=Values, no extra equal sign <=> in the Key and Value.


- 2. Key has two rules: (a) a single lib, represents all the cells in this lib.

(b) lib/cell (both slash and backslash are acceptable), represents a speciﬁc cell in this lib.

||Note: this rule has higher priority than the former.|
|---|
|
|---|


- 3. Value is composed of one or more param-unit pairs separated by spaces. A Decimal separator <.> is used to separate parameter from unit.
- 4. the parameter with the same name that appears later will overwrite the former.

# Part VI

# Mixed-signal Design Environment(MDE)

# Chapter 69Introduction

MDE seamlessly integrates with the Alps SPICE simulator and iWave waveform viewer. It allows users to easily set up pre- and post-layout simulation environments and simulation control, check simulation results through iWave , back annotate voltage and current to schematics, and perform cross probing between schematics and waveform viewer. MDE is designed to be easy to use and signiﬁcantly improves designer productivity. Where needed, third-party simulators can also be integrated with MDE.

If you want to know the netlist format, please see Alps manual. ALPS_User_Manual

Include Simulation Files: speciﬁes what ﬁles to include for analog simulator. It will create a “.inc” statement in spice top netlist.

Include Digital Files: speciﬁes what ﬁles to include for verilog simulator. It will create a “.include” statement in top verilog.

Include Vector Files: speciﬁes vector ﬁles. It will create a “.vec” statement in spice top netlist.

## 71.6 Stimuli

Menu: Setup -> Stimuli ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5209](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5209.png)

This command is used to set up stimuli of the input ports or global sources.

![image 5210](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5210.png)

Figure 71.12 Setup Stimuli

Stimuli Type: specify stimuli type, which can be an input port or a global source.

Enable: specify whether an input port or a global source signal is ON or OFF. If a signal is ON or enabled, this signal is generated in the spice netlist, otherwise, it is not generated.

Function: choose the appropriate function for the selected signal.

- • dc: direct current.
- • pulse: pulse waveform.
- • sin: sinusoidal waveform.
- • exp: exponential waveform.
- • pwl: piecewise linear waveform.


Type: select the type of a signal from the list box, which can be voltage or current.

Note: Arguments listed here will change according to the signal function and type.

Figure 71.13 Setup Stimuli-dc

- 2. set the pulse source as Figure 71.14. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vvin vin gnd DC 1.8 PULSE( 0 1.8 10n 1n 1n 5n 20n)” .

Figure 71.14 Setup Stimuli-pulse

- 3. set the sinusoidal source as Figure 71.15. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vv3 v3 gnd DC 1.8 SIN( 0 100u 100M 10n 0 0 )” .

Figure 71.15 Setup Stimuli-sin

- 4. set the exponential source as Figure 71.16. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vv2 v2 gnd DC 1.8 EXP( 0 1.8 10n 1 20n 2 )” .

![image 5214](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5214.png)

Figure 71.16 Setup Stimuli-exp

- 5. set the piecewise linear source as Figure 71.17. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vv4 v4 gnd DC 1.8 PWL( 10n 0.9 R=10n TD=1n )” .

## 71.7 NoteText Simulation

Menu: Setup -> NoteText Simulation ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5216](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5216.png)

Sometimes a user may like to write the simulation statements directly. This command allows a user to write simulation statements manually by using the NoteText editor.

![image 5217](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5217.png)

Figure 71.18 Setup NoteText Simulation

Only Use NoteText To Run Simulation: ignore all simulation settings in MDE, and use only the settings in NoteText to generate the spice top netlist.

Search Key: NoteText statements are written in sections (See “Create NoteText” ). Each section has a unique name. Search key lists all the sections and allow you to select. If you select a section, the content of that section is used to generate the spice top netlist.

- • Find: search user-deﬁned sections.
- • Show All: show all sections.
- • Name List: lists all the sections, and allows you to select one or more sections.


Text Browser: show the content of the selected section for review. See Also: Schematic Editor -> Create -> Note Text 11.13

### 72.3.1 Interactive

Menu: Mixed-Signal -> Display Partition -> Interactive ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5227](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5227.png)

This command is used to highlight analog, digital, mixed or unknown views using diﬀerent colors in schematic. The options of this command are described as follows.

![image 5228](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5228.png)

Figure 72.8 Display Partition Form

Partition Name: sets the highlighted color of analog, digital, mixed, unknown views in schematics

- • Analog: the highlighted color of the analog view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.
- • Digital: the highlighted color of the digital view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.


- • Mixed: the highlighted color of the mixed-signal view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.
- • Show View Found: display the text of the found view type in schematics using the selected color. The default mode is checked
- • Unknown: the highlighted color of the unknown view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.


Display Level: hierarchical or leaf instances is considered to highlight if Hierarchical Blocks or Primitives is checked.

- • Hierarchical: if this option is unchecked, the hierarchical instances are ignored, otherwise, the hierarchical instances are highlighted in schematics. The default mode is checked
- • Primitive: if this option is unchecked, the leaf instances are ignored, otherwise, the leaf instances are highlighted in schematics. The default mode is checked


Display IO:: whether to highlight nets in schematics

- • Nets: highlights nets in schematic, default mode is checked
- • None: does not highlight nets in schematic, default mode is unchecked


Blink: highlights views and nets under blink mode, and the default mode is unchecked

Zoom To: sets the zoom factor for the highlighted area, the range of this option is 1 to 10, default value is 1

Line Width: sets the width of the highlighted lines, and the range of this option is 2 to 10, default value is 2

Clear All: clears all highlights in schematics Fit View: zooms to ﬁt for the schematics Note: This function distinguishes which views are analog or digital or mixed according to the settings of view to use in Aether Sim View Editor

## 72.4 IE Manager

Menu: Mixed-Signal -> IE Manager ToolBar:

![image 5234](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5234.png)

BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to add, delete and modify library or cell interface element parameters, the options are shown as follows.

![image 5235](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5235.png)

Figure 72.12 IE Manager Form

Scope: switches library or cell IE. • Library: shows library IE.

- • Cell: shows cell IE, this option is selected by default. Library/Cell IE List: shows library or cell IE parameters.
- • Add: adds current conﬁg library IE parameters or selects cell from Aether Schematic.
- • Delete: deletes IE parameters from the selected in IE List. A2D Parameter: sets a2d device parameter’s values.
- • a2d_tx: delay time before digital state changes to unknown state. The default value is 1m.


- • a2d_v0: The threshold voltage for digital state is 0. The default value=1.5.
- • a2d_v1: The threshold voltage for digital state is 1. The default value=3.5.
- • dynamic_mod: sets a2d dynamic mode value. The default is unchecked.


- – ref_source: sets reference source net. The default value is empty.
- – oﬀ_region: sets Non-operation region. The default value is 0.
- – vh_ratio: sets High threshold radio of ref source. The default value is 0.5.
- – vl_ratio: sets Low threshold radio of ref source. The default value is 0.3.


D2A Parameter: sets d2a device parameter’s values.

- • d2a_tf: transfer time when digital state changed from 1 to 0. The default value=2n.
- • d2a_tr: transfer time when digital state changed from 0 to 1. The default value=3n.
- • d2a_vh: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is 1. The default value=5.
- • d2a_vl: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is 0. The default value=0.
- • d2a_vx: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is unknown state. The default value is empty.
- • d2a_vz: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is high impedance state. The default value is empty.
- • d2a_ron: the output impedance when digital state is 0, 1 or unknown state. The default value=100.
- • d2a_rz: the output impedance when digital state is high impedance state. The default value is empty.
- • d2a_tz: transfer time when digital state changed from 0, 1 or unknown to high impedance state. The default value is empty.
- • dynamic_mod: sets d2a dynamic mode value. The default value is not checked.


– ref_source: sets reference source net. The default value is empty.

## 73.1 Add Analysis

Menu: Analysis -> Add Analysis ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5250](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5250.png)

You may use this command to set simulation analysis options, such as .tran, .dc, .ac, .op, .noise. And below parameters are necessary to set before running the actual simulation:

2533

![image 5251](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5251.png)

Figure 73.1 Add Analysis Form

### 73.1.1 Tran

Menu: Analysis-> Add Analysis -> TRAN ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5252](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5252.png)

You may use this command to set tran simulation analysis options, And below parameters are necessary to set before running the actual simulation:

![image 5253](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5253.png)

Figure 73.2 Add Analysis Form - TRAN

Start: deﬁnes the simulation starting time in seconds. The default value is 0 if this parameter is not deﬁned

Stop: deﬁnes the simulation stop time in seconds, which can be speciﬁed as a parameter or as an expression

Step: deﬁnes the time increment in seconds for plotting and printing simulation results

UIC: deﬁnes whether the you want to calculate the initial condition before transient analysis or not, which is unchecked by default. If UIC is checked in the form or deﬁned in .tran statement, Alps skips the initial DC operating Point calculation and starts transient analysis directly. At time zero of the transient analysis, the node values are determined in this order: from .ic statements, then .NODESET values, otherwise set as as 0V voltage Wave Format:FSDB: makes the output wave in FSDB format

Accuracy Level: deﬁnes the simulation accuracy. It has three levels: conservative, moderate and liberal. Where conservative is the most accurate but the slowest, and liberal is the fastest and the least accurate. The default level is moderate.

Monte Carlo: deﬁnes the number of random samples for Monte Carlo analysis. Monte Carlo settings will appear when the option is checked and

the user needs to specify the corresponding parameters for Monte Carlo:

• Type: speciﬁes whether it is fast or traditional Monte Carlo method. • Sampling Method: speciﬁes the sampling method of Monte Carlo, it

can be lhs, sobol or srs.

![image 5254](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5254.png)

- Figure 73.3 Add Analysis Form - Traditional Monte Carlo Settings for TRAN Analysis


- • Number Of Runs: speciﬁes the number of random samples for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • First Run: speciﬁes the ﬁrst run parameter in the samples from which Monte Carlo analysis starts.
- • List: speciﬁes the sample lists for Monte Carlo analysis. Note: Number Of Runs and List are mutually exclusive.


![image 5255](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5255.png)

Figure 73.4 Add Analysis Form - Fast Monte Carlo Settings for TRAN Analysis

For fast Monte Carlo, it has the following user settings.

- • Max Num. Of Runs: speciﬁes the max running number for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • Target Setting: When running fast Monte Carlo, if it satisﬁes the user speciﬁed target, it will stop running without regarding to the maximal running number.

In analysis form, you can specify at most 5 targets. The target is speciﬁed by .measure statement. The following is the description of every item of the target deﬁned in the GUI.

- • Name: The target name. It is the measurement name deﬁned in the

.measure statement

- • Type: The statistics type of the target. It can be sigma or mean. For example, If using sigma, the target is related with the standard deviation of the target.
- • Error Boundary: The value of the error boundary of the target.


Save Recovery: deﬁnes settings for tran save/recovery. When this option is checked, Save Recovery settings will appear:

![image 5256](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5256.png)

Figure 73.5 Add Analysis Form - Save Recovery Settings for Tran Analysis

- • Save Clock: speciﬁes the real time interval to save state for Save Recovery
- • Save Period: speciﬁes the transient simulation time interval to save state for Save Recovery
- • Save Time: speciﬁes the time points to save state for Save Recovery
- • Save Path: speciﬁes the path to save state ﬁle for Save Recovery
- • Recovery Path: speciﬁes the path to recover the saved state ﬁle for Save Recovery
- • @: speciﬁes the time point to recover the saved state ﬁle for Save Recovery.


More Option: deﬁnes settings for sweep, second sweep and third sweep tran analysis. When this option is checked, Sweep Variable, Sweep Range, Second Sweep settings will appear:

![image 5281](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5281.png)

Tran Statement: this option is used to place tran analysis statement by the manual input mode, and to assign parameter values for user to achieve multiple scanning.

- Example 73.1


The example shows how to set tran analysis, including Monte Carlo simulation and UIC simulation

- 1. Select the command Analysis-> Add Analysis -> TRAN, the Add Analysis form appears with TRAN analysis option checked


![image 5282](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5282.png)

Figure 73.31 Tran Monte Carlo And UIC Settings

- 2. Set Start value as 1n
- 3. Set Stop value as 10u
- 4. Set Step value as 1n
- 5. Check UIC option
- 6. Check Monte Carlo option
- 7. Set Number of Runs value as 20.
- 8. Set First Run value as 15.
- 9. Press Apply or OK button, the tran setting message appears in MDE form as below:


![image 5283](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5283.png)

Figure 73.32 Tran Settings In MDE Form

- 10. Click Netlist And Run, The tran analysis statement will be generated in the simulation ﬁle as: .tran 1n 10u 1n uic sweep monte=20 firstrun=15.


- Example 73.2


The example shows how to set tran analysis, including Save Recovery.

- 1. Select the command Analysis-> Add Analysis -> TRAN, the Add Analysis form appears with TRAN analysis option checked


![image 5284](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5284.png)

Figure 73.33 Tran Save Recovery Settings

- 2. Set Start value as 1n
- 3. Set Stop value as 10u
- 4. Set Step value as 1n
- 5. Check Save/Recovery option
- 6. Set Save Clock value as 0.5.
- 7. Set Save Path directory as /home/savefile by directly inputting or using the browser.
- 8. Set Recovery Path directory as /home/savefile by directly input or using the browser.
- 9. Set Recovery Time as auto.
- 10. Press Apply or OK button, the tran setting message appears in MDE form as below:


![image 5285](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5285.png)

Figure 73.34 Tran Settings In MDE Form

- 11. Click Netlist And Run, The tran analysis statement will be generated in the simulation ﬁle as: .tran 1n 10u 1n saveclock=0.5 savefile=/home/savefile recover=/home/savefile@auto.


- Example 73.3


The example shows how to set tran sweep analysis, including Second Sweep simulation.

- 1. Select the command Analysis-> Add Analysis -> TRAN, the Add Analysis form appears.


![image 5286](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5286.png)

Figure 73.35 Tran Sweep And Second Sweep Settings

- 2. Set Start value as 1n
- 3. Set Stop value as 10u
- 4. Set Step value as 1n
- 5. Check More Option option
- 6. Set Sweep Variable as Temperature
- 7. Set Sweep Range-> Start value as 27
- 8. Set Sweep Range-> Stop value as 100
- 9. Set Sweep Range mode as Linear
- 10. Set Sweep Range-> Linear-> Step Size value as 20.
- 11. Check Second Sweep option
- 12. Set Second Sweep-> Sweep Variable as Parameter and the Name as vout_cp.
- 13. Set Second Sweep-> Sweep Range-> Start value as 1.
- 14. Set Second Sweep-> Sweep Range-> Stop value as 5.
- 15. Set Second Sweep-> Sweep Range mode as Linear.


- 16. Set Second Sweep-> Sweep Range-> Linear-> Number Of Points value as 5
- 17. Press Apply or OK button, the tran setting message appears in the MDE form as below:

![image 5287](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5287.png)

Figure 73.36 Tran Setting Message In MDE Form

- 18. Click Netlist And Run, the tran analysis statement will be generated in the simulation ﬁle as follows: .tran 1n 10u 1n sweep temp 27 100 20 sweep vout_cp lin 5 1 5.


- Example 73.4


The example shows how to perform transient Temperature Sweep analysis.

- 1. Select the command Analysis-> Add Analysis -> TRAN, the Add Analysis form appears with TRAN analysis option checked.


![image 5288](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5288.png)

###### Figure 73.37 Tran Temperature Sweep Settings

- 2. Set Start value as 1n
- 3. Set Stop value as 20u
- 4. Set Step value as 1n
- 5. Check moderate option
- 6. Check Temperature Sweep option
- 7. Set Tempvec value as 0 27 10n 20 20n 30 30n 40.
- 8. Check and set Tempstep value as 5n.
- 9. Press Apply or OK button, the tran setting message appears in MDE form as below:

![image 5289](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5289.png)

Figure 73.38 Temperature Sweep Settings In MDE Form

- 10. Click Netlist And Run, The tran analysis statement will be generated in the simulation ﬁle as: .tran 1n 20n 1n tempvec=(0 27 10n 20 20n 30 30n 40) tempstep=5n.

.measure statement

# Chapter 74Simulation

## 74.1 Options

Menu: Simulation -> Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5368](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5368.png)

This command is used to control the accuracy, speed and convergence for Alps or other simulators by setting diﬀerent options. These options are classiﬁed into Algorithm, Component, Output, Job and Misc. To invoke option menu, select Simulation -> Options.

2601

![image 5369](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5369.png)

Figure 74.1 Simulation Options - Main Tab

Main: Tolerance Setting: sets tolerance variable for simulation.

- • Reltol: sets the relative error tolerance for current and voltage from iteration to iteration. The default value is 0.001.
- • Abstol: sets the absolute current error tolerance. The default value is 1e-09. Min value is 1e-25; Max value is 10. Option Abstol is the same as Absi.
- • Absv: sets the absolute voltage error tolerance. The default value is 5e-06.


Temperature: sets temperature related options.

• Tnom: this option is used to set the model reference temperature. The default value is 27.

Netlist Compatible: the option controls whether Aether outputs spectre netlist and Alps supports the parse of Spectre ModelCard in sp ﬁle. Possible values are:

- • Hspice: supports hspice model.
- • Spectre: supports spectre model.


Netlist View List: speciﬁes the views order for searching when creating netlist. This view list requires a particular sequence. If design of MDE is Conﬁg View, this option is enabled

Stop View List: speciﬁes the views to identify the stopping view when creating netlist. This view list does not require a particular sequence. If design of MDE is Conﬁg View, this option is enabled.

##### Algorithm:

![image 5370](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5370.png)

Figure 74.2 Simulation Options - Algorithm Tab

Homotopy: the homotopy method for solving convergence problems. Possible methods are gminDC ramping, gmin ramping, source ramping, dptran, ptran. If you select one of the above methods, the simulator will try this method directly. If you select All, the simulator tries all above methods one by one until a DC solution is found. The order is GMIN Ramping, GMINDC Ramping, Source Ramping, DPTRAN, PTRAN. The default is All.

Gmin: adds minimum conductance to all PN junctions for TRAN. The default value is 1e-12.

Gmindc: adds minimum conductance to all PN junctions for DC. The default value is empty.

Gdcpath: adds conductance to the nodes which have no DC path to ground. The default value is empty.

Delmax: sets the maximum allowable time step size for TRAN. The default value is empty.

ltl1: sets the maximum number of DC iterations. The default value is 200.

ltl4: sets the maximum iterations for a convergent solution in transient analysis. If Alps does not get convergence within itl4 iterations, it rejects present time step and selects a new one which is reduced by 0.25. The default value is 8.

Method: sets the integration method for transient analysis. The default value is None.

- • TRAP: trapezoidal integration method.
- • GEAR: gear integration method.
- • BE: back euler integration method.
- • None: Aether will not export method option to the *.sp ﬁle. Component:


![image 5371](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5371.png)

Figure 74.3 Simulation Options - Component Tab

Scale: sets the instance scaling factor. The default value is 1. Scalm: sets the model scaling factor. The default value is 1.

##### Output:

![image 5372](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5372.png)

Figure 74.4 Simulation Options - Output Tab

Post: saves simulation results. Probe: only saves output variables speciﬁed in .PROBE and .PRINT statements for post processing.

Postlvl: when schematic has hierarchy, this tells the simulator to write simulation results for n-levels in the schematic, where n=0, 1, 2,...,n, to the waveform ﬁle. Default value of n is 0.

Posttop: when schematic has hierarchy, this tells the simulator to write simulation results for top n-levels in the schematic, where n=0, 1, 2,...,n, to the waveform ﬁle. . Default value of n is 0.

Ingold: this option controls whether Alps prints output in exponential form or engineering notation. Possible values are: 0 - Engineering Format 1 - G Format (ﬁxed and exponential) 2 - E Format (exponential SPICE)

Measﬁle: this option controls whether the measure information outputs to a single or multiple ﬁles when an .ALTER command is present in the netlist.

Autostop: stops a transient analysis after the simulator ﬁnishes calculating all measurement functions.

History Number: the purpose of this option is to store several simulation result ﬁles, such as, .sp ﬁle, wave ﬁle, netlist ﬁle, netlist map, and so on. If this option is checked and assigned a number, before simulation, Aether MDE will create new folders which sort by Arabic numerals under $ProjectNetlistDirectory/Lib_Cell_View_Alps/ for storing simulation results, the generated maximum quantity of new folders will be consistent with the assigned value of History Number. The default value is 3, and it allows you to enter any value from 1 to 100. If not checked, it will store one simulation result ﬁle.

##### Job:

![image 5373](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5373.png)

Figure 74.5 Simulation Options - Job Tab

Mode: speciﬁes whether to run simulation in distributed mode or not. Local: all simulation jobs run locally (without network read/write). LSF: Load Sharing Facility. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via LSF. OGE: Oracle Grid Engine. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via OGE. Donau: Donau Engine. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via Donau.

Job Name: job name of LSF, OGE or Donau. Default value is jHHMMSS(H is hour, M is minute, S is second). Its length should be from 1 to 10 characters. Because Aether MDE uses it as key name for simulation and waveform postprocessing, the user had better provide a meaningful name.

Queue Name: Queue name of LSF, OGE or Donau. Aether MDE loads the queue names of LSF, OGE or Donau when the user launches it for the ﬁrst

time. Aether MDE does not update it if queue names have been changed by administrator.

Misc: other options for LSF, OGE or Donau.

||Note: We suggest using LSF, OGE or Donau when you run multicorner simulations. But using LSF, OGE or Donau, there are some requirements:<br><br>• LSF, OGE or Donau must be installed.<br>• All directories and ﬁles have the same name on all servers.<br>• All directories and ﬁles must be accessed by user on all servers. The following directory may be not valid, /home/userA. Because /home/userA on diﬀerent servers are diﬀerent.<br>|
|---|
|
|---|


Max Job Number: speciﬁes the max job number for simulation, the value range is [2,20], the default value is 20.

||Note: If environment variable AETHER_MDE_MAX_JOB is set, the value will be used as the max job number for simulation.|
|---|
|
|---|


##### Misc:

![image 5374](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5374.png)

Figure 74.6 Simulation Options - Misc Tab

Other Options: speciﬁes INCLUDE options used by .sp ﬁle. Command Options of Alps: speciﬁes INCLUDE options used by Alps.

Command Options of Alps-MS: speciﬁes INCLUDE options used by AlpsMS.

## 75.13 Output Setting

Menu: Outputs -> Output Setting ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5432](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5432.png)

This command is used to set outputs, including signals and expressions.

![image 5433](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5433.png)

Figure 75.30 Output Setting

Name: lists the signal name or expression name in Output List. Type: lists the output type which is selected in Output List. It can be Signal or Expression. Expression/Signal: lists the contents of expression or signal. If it’s normal signal, this option is the same as Name. Operate: sets the operation for the selected output.

- • Save: enables or disables saving.
- • Plot: enables or disables plotting.


New expression: edits a new expression. The form will change to Figure 75.31

Output List: lists the outputs. Delete: deletes selected output in Output List. Modify: modiﬁes selected output in Output List. Close: closes the form.

Note: The form will change according to the selection in the Output List. If you select a signal, the form will change to Figure 75.30. Otherwise if user click New Expression or select an expression, the form will change to Figure 75.31.

![image 5434](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5434.png)

Figure 75.31 Output Setting Expression

Name: speciﬁes the alias of the expression.

||Note: It is optional to set a alias on an expression. The entire expression will be displayed and plotted if the alias has not been speciﬁed. The alias of a trivial signal but an expression will be ignored.|
|---|
|
|---|


Expression: editor for the expression. It is recommended to add signals by Signal or Parameter and get mathematical operators and functions from the Expression Table below although all of them can be input by literally typing.

||Note: The cursor will move automatically when user is editing an expression and selected signals. For example, when select a function which need two parameters, the cursor will move to the ﬁrst parameter’s location. After selecting the ﬁrst parameter, cursor will move to the second location.|
|---|
|
|---|


Signal: opens a schematic window to allow you to select signals. Parameter: pops up parameter list to allow you to select parameters.

![image 5435](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5435.png)

Figure 75.32 Parameter Form

Parameter: shows all parameters which are deﬁned in MDE-> Parameter. It only allows you to select one parameter in this list.

OK: adds the selected parameter to Expression Table and the parameter will be display as par(ParameterName).

##### Cancel: exits Parameter form.

MP: opens a schematic window to allow you to select model parameter. See Also: Outputs -> Save Options 85.13.

Expression Table: selects the functions. Operate: sets the plot operation. Add: adds the edited output to Output List. Clear: clears the Expression. Cancel: exits expression editing form. Note: A signal with wild card cannot be plotted. The expression cannot be saved.

# Chapter 76Results

## 76.1 Direct Plot

### 76.1.1 Main Form

Menu: Results -> Direct Plot -> Main Form ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5447](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5447.png)

This command is used to display signal waveforms in iWave immediately, such as TRAN, DC, AC.

Note: This command should be used after simulation ﬁnishes.

![image 5448](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5448.png)

Figure 76.1 Main Form

Selection Mode: select a corner ﬁle or all ﬁles to display.

- • Selected: specify a corner ﬁle to display.
- • All: specify to display all ﬁles.


2651

Corner: speciﬁes which corner ﬁle is selected. This option is enabled only when Selection Mode is Selected.

Analysis: specify which analysis result is plotted. Note: The Analysis types displayed are based on the setting in MDE -> Analysis -> Add Analysis.

- • TRAN: speciﬁes to plot tran analysis simulation result of signal.

![image 5449](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5449.png)

Figure 76.2 Main Form - Tran Form

- – Function: specify signal types to be plotted, such as voltage or current.

∗ Voltage: plots voltage of signal. ∗ Current: plots current of signal. ∗ Auto: plots voltage of net when user selects net in schematic, and plots current of port when user selects port in schematic.

- – FFT: displays the FFT result of signals.
- – Clip: speciﬁes the starting and stopping points to clip the waveform.
- – With Calculator: activates iWave’s calculator after selecting nets or ports in schematic. This option is enabled only when Selection Mode is Selected.


- • DC: plots dc analysis simulation result.


![image 5450](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5450.png)

Figure 76.3 Main Form - DC Form

– Function: speciﬁes types of signals to be plotted, such as voltage or

current. ∗ Voltage: plots voltage of signals. ∗ Current: plots current of signals. ∗ Auto: plots voltage of nets when a user selects nets in schematic,

and plots current of ports when a user selects ports in schematic.

– With Calculator: activates iWave’s calculator after selecting nets or ports in schematic. This option is enabled only when Selection Mode is Selected.

- • AC: plots ac analysis simulation result.


![image 5451](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5451.png)

Figure 76.4 Main Form - AC Form

- – Function: speciﬁes types of signals to be plotted, such as voltage or current.


∗ Voltage: plots voltage of signals. ∗ Current: plots current of signals.

∗ Auto: plots voltage of nets when a user selects nets in schematic, and plots current of ports when a user selects ports in schematic.

- – Modiﬁer: speciﬁes which ac simulation result is plotted. ∗ Magnitude: plots magnitude of signals. ∗ Phase: plots phase of signals. ∗ dB20: plots dB20 result of signals. ∗ Gain: plots the gain of signals.
- – With Calculator: activates iWave’s calculator after selecting nets or ports in schematic. This option is enabled only when Selection Mode is Selected.

78.3. Outputs

![image 5548](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5548.png)

Figure 78.5 MDE Analog Output Panel

Analog: shows analog output signals, Output Panel displays this table by default mode.

Name: lists the analog signal name or expression name in Output List. Type: lists the output type which is selected in Output List. It can be Signal or Expression.

Expression/Signal: lists the contents of expression or signal. If it’s normal signal, this option is the same as Name.

Save: enables or disables saving. Plot: enables or disables plotting. S+: clicks this button to execute Select From Design, it can add normal signals to output panel. E+: clicks this button to execute Output Setting, it can add expression to output panel.

: deletes the output signals or expressions from Output Panel.

![image 5549](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5549.png)

![image 5550](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5550.png)

Figure 78.6 MDE Digital Output Panel

Digital: shows digital output signals.

- • Name: lists the digital signal name in Output List.
- • Save: enables or disables saving.


- • : clicks this button to execute Select From Module Tree, it can add digital signal from module tree to output panel.

![image 5551](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5551.png)

- • : deletes the output signals or expressions from Output Panel.


![image 5552](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5552.png)

Plotting Mode: speciﬁes the way of opening waves in iWave. Default mode is Append.

- • Append: opens waves by append mode, it would not close the waves which are already opened in iWave.
- • Replace: opens waves by replace mode, it will close the waves which are opened ﬁrst, then open the new waves.


## 78.4 Results

Menu: Window -> Results ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5553](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5553.png)

This command is used to display or hide the results dock in MDEL2 form. By default, it is below the outputs dock. MDEL2 shows simulation results on the dock automatically after a successful simulation. Type of Results contains waves of outputs signal, waves of expression and value of expression.

![image 5554](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5554.png)

Figure 78.7 MDEL2 Detailed Results Table

Corner Information: shows corner information including model ﬁle, parameter and temperature. Contents are same as Show Full Corner Table

• Parameter: lists model ﬁles name, parameters name and temperature. • Nominal: displays conditions of nominal including section of model,

value of parameter and value of temperature.

• Corner Name: displays conditions of corner including section of model,

value of parameter and value of temperature. Simulation Results: shows simulation results.

- • Output: lists outputs name which you set in output panel.
- • Nominal: displays simulation results of nominal.
- • Min: displays minimum value of output across all corners.
- • Max: displays maximum value of output across all corners.
- • Corner Name: displays simulation results of corner.
- • Key Word: many key words will be shown in results tab. It is shown as follows:


Table 78.1 Type Of Results

|Key Words<br><br>|Representation|
|---|---|


|sim_err|Simulation Failed.|
|---|---|
|running<br><br>|The corner is simulating.|
|none|Waiting for simulation.|
|canceled<br><br>|The Simulation was killed.|
|![image 5555](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5555.png)|Simulation result is a wave. If you click it, the wave will be displayed in a wave viewer.|
|value<br><br>|It is a result of measurement.|
|eval_err|Failed to evaluate it. It may be caused by wrongly expression or no date.|


- • Shortcut Menu: right-click on simulation results tab to show shortcut menu


Table 78.2 Shortcut Menu

|Command<br><br>|Subcommand|Function|
|---|---|---|


|Show Log File| |The simulation log will be displayed.|
|---|---|---|
|Show SP File| |The whole of netlist will be displayed.|
|Plot| |Plot selected waves.|
|Plot Across Corners| |Plot all of waves across corners.|
|Histogram| |Plot all of MP’s numerical results.|
|Direct Plot| |See Also: Results -> Direct Plot 86.7.|
|Annotate|Transient Node Voltages and Currents<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> Transient Node Voltages and Currents 76.2.1.|
| |DC Voltage<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> DC Operating Point -> All Voltage 76.2.3.1.|
| |DC Current<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> DC Operating Point -> All Current 76.2.3.2.|
| |DC Operating Point<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> DC Operating Point -> All Device Status 76.2.3.3.|
| |Model Parameters<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> Model Parameters ??.|
| |Tran Voltage<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> Tran Operating Point -> All Voltage 76.2.4.1.|
| |Tran Operating Point<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> Tran Operating Point -> All Device Status 76.2.4.2.|


| |Annotate Options|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> Annotate Options 86.8.9.|
|---|---|---|
|Print|DC Operating Point<br><br>|See Also: Results -> Annotate -> DC Operating Point -> Select from Schematic ??.|
| |Model Parameters|See Also: Results -> Print -> Model Parameters 86.9.4.|

# Part VII Advanced Mixed-signal Design Environment

# Chapter 80Introduction

Advanced MDE is modern circuit simulation platform that uses direct methods to simulate analog and digital circuits. In addition to the baseline simulation functionalities, supports Spectre options simulations, and it seamlessly integrates with the Alps simulator and iWave waveform viewer. It allows users to easily set up pre- and post-layout simulation environments and simulation control, check simulation results through iWave , back annotate voltage and current to schematics, and perform cross probing between schematics and waveform viewer. MDE is designed to be easy to use and signiﬁcantly improves designer productivity. Where needed, third-party simulators can also be integrated with MDE.

Paths/Files: speciﬁes the search paths and include ﬁles.

- • Include Paths: speciﬁes the search path for all include ﬁles of the analog simulator. It will create a .option search statement in spice top netlist.
- • Include Simulation Files: includes the contents of another ﬁle into current netlist. .inc is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in spice top netlist.
- • Include Digital Files: includes the content of another digital ﬁle into current netlist. .include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in top verilog.
- • Include Pspice Files: includes the content of another pspice ﬁle into current netlist. pspice_include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in current netlist.
- • Include DSPF Files: includes the content of another DSPF ﬁle into current netlist. dspf_include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in current netlist.


– DSPF Options: speciﬁes the dspf ﬁles options.

∗ Port Order: speciﬁes the port order of dspf ﬁles. sch means take the port order from pre-layout schematic netlist, spf means

take the port order from dspf ﬁle deﬁnition.

∗ Extra Port: speciﬁes the extra port of dspf ﬁles. true means extra ports in dspf ﬁle will change to inner nodes, false means the port number in dspf ﬁle and schematic is same.

∗ Case Sensitivity: speciﬁes the case sensitivity of dspf ﬁles. true means the dspf ﬁle is case-sensitive, false means the dspf ﬁles is case insensitive.

∗ Black Box: speciﬁes the instances which to be considered as

blackboxes. Click Select button to choose black box in schematic. ∗ Bus Delimiter: speciﬁes the bus delimiter of dspf ﬁles to map

with schematic. ∗ Other Options: speciﬁes any dspf_include options that not supported in this form of dspf ﬁles.

Vector Files: speciﬁes the content of vector ﬁles.

• Include Vector Files: includes the content of another vector ﬁle into current netlist. .vec is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in spice top netlist.

## 82.7 Stimuli

Menu: Setup -> Stimuli ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 5620](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5620.png)

This command is used to set up stimuli of the input ports or global sources.

![image 5621](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5621.png)

Figure 82.15 Setup Stimuli

Stimuli Type: specify stimuli type, which can be an input port or a global source.

Enable: specify whether an input port or a global source signal is ON or OFF. If a signal is ON or enabled, this signal is generated in the spice netlist, otherwise, it is not generated.

Function: choose the appropriate function for the selected signal.

- • dc: direct current.
- • pulse: pulse waveform.
- • sin: sinusoidal waveform.
- • exp: exponential waveform.
- • pwl: piecewise linear waveform.


Type: select the type of a signal from the list box, which can be voltage or current.

Note: Arguments listed here will change according to the signal function and type.

Example 82.2 This example shows how to set up a source

###### 1. set the dc source as Figure 82.16. The spice top netlist will have a statement“Vin (in gnd) vsource dc=1.8 mag=1 phase=0 type=dc” .

![image 5622](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5622.png)

Figure 82.16 Setup Stimuli-dc

###### 2. set the pulse source as Figure 82.17. The spice top netlist will have a statement“Vin (in gnd) vsource delay=10n fall=1n period=20n rise=1n val0=0 val1=1.8phase=0 dc=1.8 width=5n mag=1 type=pulse” .

![image 5623](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5623.png)

Figure 82.17 Setup Stimuli-pulse

###### 3. set the sinusoidal source as Figure 82.18. The spice top netlist will have astatement “Vin (in gnd) vsource delay=10n freq=10M ampl=100u sinedc=0phase=0 dc=1.8 mag=1 type=sine” .

![image 5624](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5624.png)

Figure 82.18 Setup Stimuli-sin

- 4. set the exponential source as Figure 82.19. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vin (in gnd) vsource delay=1n val0=0 tau1=1 val1=1.8 tau2=2 td1=10n td2=20n phase=0 dc=1.5 mag=1 type=exp” .

![image 5625](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile5625.png)

Figure 82.19 Setup Stimuli-exp

- 5. set the piecewise linear source as Figure 82.20. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vin (in gnd) vsource wave=[10m 1.6 ] mag=1 oﬀset=2n delay=1n phase=0 dc=0.8 type=pwl” .

# Chapter 84 Simulation

## 84.1 Options

Menu: Simulation -> Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 6053](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6053.png)

This command is used to control the accuracy, speed and convergence for Alps or other simulators by setting diﬀerent options. These options are classiﬁed into Algorithm, Component, Check, Annotation, Misc, Netlist, Job and Plotting. To invoke option menu, select Simulation -> Options.

2917

![image 6054](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6054.png)

Figure 84.1 Simulation Options - Main Tab

Main: Tolerance Setting: sets tolerance variable for simulation.

- • reltol: speciﬁes the relative error tolerance for current and voltage from iteration to iteration. The default value is 1e-3.
- • trtol: speciﬁes the value of trtol. The default value is 1e-3.
- • maxvoltage: speciﬁes the value of maxvoltage. The default value is 1e-3.
- • residualtol: speciﬁes the tolerance ratio for multiplies reltol.
- • vabstol: speciﬁes the absolute voltage error tolerance. The default value is 1e-6.
- • iabstol: speciﬁes the absolute current error tolerance. The default value is 1e-12.


Temperature: sets temperature related options.

- • temp: speciﬁes the value of temperature. The value is synchronized with the main form setting.


- • tnom: this option is used to set the model reference temperature. The default value is 27.
- • tempeﬀects: speciﬁes the value of tempeﬀects. Possible values are vt, tc and all.


Noise Options: sets noise options.

- • Noise Contribution: speciﬁes the value of noise contribution. Possible values are on and oﬀ. One of them is checked, Instance List can be speciﬁed, otherwise, it can not be speciﬁed.
- • Instance List: speciﬁes the value of instances.
- • Select: clicks Select button, it is easy to select instances from schematic.
- • Clear: clicks Clear button, the instances in Instance List will be cleared.
- • noiseon_type: speciﬁes the value of noiseon_type. Possible values are thermal, ﬂicker, shot, ign and all.
- • noiseoﬀ_type: speciﬁes the value of noiseoﬀ_type. Possible values are thermal, ﬂicker, shot, ign and all.


##### Algorithm:

![image 6055](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6055.png)

Figure 84.2 Simulation Options - Algorithm Tab

Convergence Options: speciﬁes values of convergence options.

- • homotopy: the homotopy method for solving convergence problems. Possible methods are gmin, source, dptran, ptran. If you select one of the above methods, the simulator will try this method directly. If a user selects none, the simulator will try without method directly. If a user selects All, the simulator tries all above methods one by one until a DC solution is found. The order is none, gmin, source, dptran, ptran, all.
- • limit: speciﬁes the value of limit. Possible values are delta, log, dev.
- • gmethod: speciﬁes the value of gmethod. Possible values are dev, node, both.
- • dptran_gmethod: speciﬁes the value of dptran_gmethod. Possible values are dev, node, both.
- • try_fast_op: speciﬁes the value of try_fast_op. Possible values are yes and no.
- • convdbg: speciﬁes the value of convdbg. Possible values are none, status and detailed.
- • icpriority: speciﬁes the value of icpriority. Possible value are netlist and ﬁle.
- • nonconv_topnum: speciﬁes the value of nonconv_topnum.
- • gmin: speciﬁes the value of gmin.
- • gmin_check: speciﬁes the value of gmin_check. Possible value are no, max_v_only, max_only and all.
- • gmindc: speciﬁes the value of gmindc.
- • gshunt: speciﬁes the value of gshunt.
- • rforce: speciﬁes the value of rforce. The default value is 1.
- • rthresh: speciﬁes the value of rthresh.
- • rabsclamp: speciﬁes the value of rabsclamp.
- • rclamp: speciﬁes the value of rclamp.
- • rabsshort: speciﬁes the value of rabsshort.


Maxtrix Parameter Options: speciﬁes values of maxtrix parameter options.

- • pivotdc: speciﬁes the value of pivotdc. Possible values are yes and no.
- • dc_pivot_check: speciﬁes the value of dc_pivot_check. Possible values are yes and no.
- • pivrel: speciﬁes the value of pivrel. The default value is 1e-3.


- • pivabs: speciﬁes the value of pivabs.
- • preorder: speciﬁes the value of preorder. Possible values are partial and full.
- • rebuild_matrix: speciﬁes the value of rebuild_matrix. Possible values are yes and no.

Nport Options: speciﬁes values of nport options.

Model Options: speciﬁes values of model options.

##### . Job:

![image 6061](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6061.png)

Figure 84.8 Simulation Options - Job Tab

Mode: speciﬁes whether to run simulation in distributed mode or not. Local: all simulation jobs run locally (without network read/write). LSF: Load Sharing Facility. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via LSF. OGE: Oracle Grid Engine. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via OGE.

Donau: Donau Engine. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via Donau.

Job Name: job name of LSF, OGE or Donau. Default value is jHHMMSS(H is hour, M is minute, S is second). Its length should be from 1 to 10 characters. Because Aether MDE uses it as key name for simulation and waveform postprocessing, the user had better provide a meaningful name.

Queue Name: Queue name of LSF, OGE or Donau. Aether MDE loads the queue names of LSF, OGE or Donau when the user launches it for the ﬁrst time. Aether MDE does not update it if queue names have been changed by administrator.

Misc: other options for LSF, OGE or Donau.

||Note: We suggest using LSF, OGE or Donau when you run multicorner simulations. But using LSF, OGE or Donau, there are some requirements:<br><br>• LSF, OGE or Donau must be installed.<br>• All directories and ﬁles have the same name on all servers.<br>• All directories and ﬁles must be accessed by user on all servers. The following directory may be not valid, /home/userA. Because /home/userA on diﬀerent servers are diﬀerent.<br>|
|---|
|
|---|


Max Job Number: speciﬁes the max job number for simulation, the value range is [2,20], the default value is 20.

||Note: If environment variable AETHER_MDE_MAX_JOB is set, the value will be used as the max job number for simulation.|
|---|
|
|---|
