## 84.8 Run Monte Carlo

Menu: Simulation -> Run Monte Carlo ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 6079](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6079.png)

This command is used to spectre netlist format simulation. This feature has been added into only MDE L2 version.

![image 6080](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6080.png)

Figure 84.18 Run Monte Carlo Form

Statistical Variation: deﬁnes statistical variation, to be used with a Monte Carlo analysis.

- • Process: speciﬁes the input process statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • Mismatch: speciﬁes the input mismatch statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • All: speciﬁes both process and mismatch statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.


Sampling Method: speciﬁes the method of statistical sampling to apply.

- • Random: generates statistical variation random numbers according to the speciﬁed distributions.
- • LHS: generates statistical variation using Latin Hypercube Sampling(LHS). When this option is selected, the Number Of Bins is enabled.


- • LDS: generates statistical variation using Latin Discrepancy Sampling(LDS).


Number Of Points: sets the number of Monte Carlo points you want to simulate. The minimum value is 1, default is 10.

Number Of Bins: sets the number of bins (subdivisions) in the text ﬁeld for LHS method. The minimum value is 1, default is 10.

Monte Carlo Seed: sets the seed for the Monte Carlo analysis. The minimum value is 1, default is 12345.

First Point: sets the ﬁrst point for the Monte Carlo analysis. The minimum value is 1, default is 1.

Netlist Options: sets the netlist options for the Monte Carlo analysis. The default value is empty.

Save Simulation Data: whether to save simulation directory for the Monte Carlo analysis. If the checkbox is checked, save the simulation directory, otherwise delete simulation dirctory. The default value is not checked.

Save Statistical Data: whether to save montecarlo directory for the Monte Carlo analysis. If the checkbox is checked, save the montecarlo directory, otherwise delete montecarlo dirctory. The default value is not checked.

##### Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo(Unspeciﬁed): clicks this button to show the form Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo.

Default: clicks this Default button, the form will reload the default settings. Run: clicks this Run button, the operation will be executed. OK: clicks this OK button, the operation will be saved and the form escapes at the same time. Cancel: clicks this Cancel button, the operation will be canceled and the form escapes at the same time.

This form Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo speciﬁes instances for Monte Carlo analysis.

![image 6081](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6081.png)

Figure 84.19 Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo

Statistical Variation: deﬁnes statistical variation, its same as Statistical Variation to the Run Monte Carlo form.

Selected: speciﬁes the value for Selected, the default value is Process. Unselected: speciﬁes the value for Unselected, the default value is Process. Instances Speciﬁcation: speciﬁes instances from schematic or subcircuit.

• Schematic: speciﬁes instances from schematic.

##### – Select From Schematic: clicks this Select From Schematic but-

ton to select instances from schematic.

– Select List: shows the instances selected from schematic.

• Subcircuit: speciﬁes instances from subcircuit.

![image 6082](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6082.png)

Figure 84.20 Instances Speciﬁcation Subcircuit

- – Cell: speciﬁes cell, selects instances from Select List and clicks Add button to add instances.
- – Select List: shows all instances in the Cell. Default: clicks this Default button, the form will reload the default settings. OK: clicks this OK button, the operation will execute. Cancel: clicks this Cancel button, the operation will be canceled and the form escapes at the same time.


- Example 84.4


The following is the netlist format for the Monte Carlo analysis:

- 1. When Sampling Method=Random: mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=mismatch {...}
- 2. When Sampling Method=LHS, check the Number Of Bins option, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=process sampling=lhs numbins=0 {...}

- 3. When Sampling Method=LHS, uncheck the Number Of Bins option, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows: mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all sampling=lhs {...}
- 4. When Sampling Method=LDS, First Point=3, Netlist Options=itl4=200, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all sampling=lds itl4=200 ﬁrstrun=3{...}

- 5. When Sampling Method=Random, uncheck the Number Of Bins option, set Selected=Process Unselected=No Variation, the syntax is like


following or the syntax is as follows: mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=process ignoremode=nominal {...}

##### 6. When Sampling Method=Random, uncheck the Number Of Bins op-tion, set Selected=No Variation Unselected=Mismatch, the syntax islike following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=mismatch ignore=[...] {...}

##### 7. When Sampling Method=Random, uncheck the Number Of Bins op-tion, set Selected=All Unselected=No Variation, the syntax is like fol-lowing or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all dut=[...] ignoremode=nominal {...}

###### 8. When Sampling Method=Random, check the Save Statistical Data thesyntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

## 85.13 Save Options

Menu: Outputs -> Save Options ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 6153](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6153.png)

This form is used to conﬁgure simulation options. To invoke option form, select Outputs -> Save Options.

![image 6154](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6154.png)

Figure 85.43 Save Options Form

Basic: speciﬁes basic options.

- • save: this option is used to generate voltage information ﬁles. The default value is allpub checked.
- • pwr: this option is used to generate power information ﬁles. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • nestlvl: this option is used to set the number of stages of the output subckt. This options is valid when save is lvlpub or lvl. The default value is empty.
- • currents: this option is used to generate current information ﬁles. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • useprobes: this option is used to select AC terminal currents. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • subcktprobelvl: this option is used to control up to how many levels deep will current probes be added to subcircuits.
- • saveahdlvars: this option is used to select AHDL variables. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • Circuit Options: speciﬁes circuit options for output. The default values are modelParameter, element, designParamVals, subckts and < Click To Add > . Click < Click To Add > to add a row. Popup context menu and click the Delete action to delete the selected rows.


- – Name: speciﬁes name value.
- – What: speciﬁes what value. The values of this option are none, inst, models, parameters, subckts and oppoint. The default value is none.
- – Where: speciﬁes where value. The values of this option are file, logfile, nowhere and rawfile. The default value is rawfile.
- – File: speciﬁes ﬁle. The default value is empty.
- – Extremes: speciﬁes extreme value. The values of this option are no, yes and only.
- – Others: speciﬁes other value. The default value is empty.
- – Enabled: speciﬁes whether the row is enabled. If Enabled is checked, the row is enabled.


- • Output Options: speciﬁes options for output.


- – Output Format: speciﬁes the format of output. The default value is ps.
- – History Number: speciﬁes the number of history. If the number of history is speciﬁed as 1, the Overwrite Directory checkbox is automatically checked.
- – Overwrite Directory: speciﬁes directory to be overwritten. If the Overwrite Directory is checked, it will auto overwrite the directory when running simulation.
- – Save Simulation Data: speciﬁes whether the simulation saves data. If it is checked, the simulation data will be saved, otherwise it will not save simulation data. The default status is checked.


Save By Subckt: speciﬁes subckt options.

![image 6155](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6155.png)

Figure 85.44 Save By Subckt

- • Subckts: speciﬁes information.


- – Instance: selects a subckt.
- – V[depth]: speciﬁes voltage depth. The default value is empty and checked.
- – I[depth]: speciﬁes current depth. The default value is empty and unchecked.
- – Pwr[depth]: speciﬁes power depth. The default value is empty and unchecked.
- – Compress: speciﬁes whether compression is enabled. The default value is unchecked.
- – Filter RC: speciﬁes whether the ﬁlter is rc. The default value is unchecked.
- – Ports: speciﬁes whether ports are enabled. The default value is unchecked.
- – Exclude: speciﬁes exclude value. The default value is empty and unchecked.
- – Sigtype: speciﬁes sigtype. The values of this option are node, dev, subckt and all. The default value is all.
- – User Options: speciﬁes user options. The default value is empty.


- • Add: the button can add a row.
- • Delete: the button can delete selected rows.

Menu: Outputs -> Output Setting ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

Signal: shows signal content. Open a schematic window to allow you to select net or terminal by clicking Signal button.

Type: shows signal type. It can be current or voltage. Operate: sets the operation for the selected output.

- • Save: saves the output. The default is checked.
- • Plot: plots the output. The default is checked. Output List: lists the outputs.
- • Name: lists the signal name or expression name in Output List.
- • Type: lists the output type in Output List. It can be Signal or Expression.
- • Expression/Signal: lists the contents of expression or signal in Output List.


- • Save: saves the output.
- • Plot: plots the output.


Add: adds the edited output to Output List. Delete: removes the selected output from Output List. Modify: modiﬁes the selected output in Output List. New expression: clicks this button to create a new expression, the form likes this Figure 85.46 OK: modiﬁes the selected output and then the form exites. ∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for Current function.Select item in harmonic number table.

- – Power: selects the Power function type of the ENVLP analysis.


![image 6832](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6832.png)

Figure 86.642 Main Form - Power - Function

![image 6833](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6833.png)

Figure 86.643 Select

∗ Select: speciﬁes select mode for Power function. ∗ Modiﬁer: speciﬁes modiﬁer for Power function. · Magnitude: selects magnitude of modiﬁer. · dB10: selects dB10 of modiﬁer. · dBm: selects dBm of modiﬁer.

∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for Power function. Select item in harmonic number table.

- – ACPR: selects the ACPR function type of the ENVLP analysis.


![image 6834](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6834.png)

Figure 86.644 Main Form - ACPR - Function

![image 6835](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6835.png)

Figure 86.645 Select

∗ Select: speciﬁes select mode for ACPR function. ∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for ACPR func-

tion. Select item in harmonic number table.

∗ Method: speciﬁes method type for ACPR function. · Power: selects power of method type. · Power Density: selects power density of method type.

∗ Channel Deﬁnitions(Default Custom): speciﬁes channel definitions for ACPR function.

∗ Main Channel Width: speciﬁes main channel width for ACPR function.

∗ Add: appends the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) in the text boxes into the table above.

∗ Modify: modiﬁes the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) of the selected record in the table and update it with the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) in the text boxes.

∗ Delete: deletes the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) currently selected in the table.

∗ From: speciﬁes the lower bound of the ﬁltering range for ACPR function.

∗ To: speciﬁes the upper bound of the ﬁltering range for ACPR

function. ∗ Strobe Period: speciﬁes strobe period for ACPR function. ∗ Window Size: speciﬁes window size for ACPR function. De-

fault is 64. ∗ Repetitions: speciﬁes repetitions for ACPR function. Default is 2. ∗ Resolutions BandWidth: speciﬁes resolutions bandwidth for ACPR function. ∗ Windowing(Default Rectangle): speciﬁes windowing for ACPR function.

- – Main Channel Power: selects the Main Channel Power function type of the ENVLP analysis.


![image 6836](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6836.png)

Figure 86.646 Main Form - Main Channel Power - Function

![image 6837](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6837.png)

Figure 86.647 Select

∗ Select: speciﬁes select mode for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for Main Chan-

nel Power function. Select item in harmonic number table. ∗ Main Channel Width: speciﬁes main channel width for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Reference Resistor: speciﬁes reference resistor for Main Channel Power function. Default is 50. ∗ From: speciﬁes the lower bound of the ﬁltering range for Main Channel Power function. ∗ To: speciﬁes the upper bound of the ﬁltering range for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Strobe Period: speciﬁes strobe period for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Window Size: speciﬁes window size for Main Channel Power function. Default is 64. ∗ Repetitions: speciﬁes repetitions for Main Channel Power function. Default is 2.

∗ Resolutions BandWidth: speciﬁes resolutions bandwidth for Main Channel Power function.

∗ Windowing(Default Rectangle): speciﬁes windowing for Main Channel Power function.

– Rms Voltage: selects the Rms Voltage function type of the ENVLP

analysis.

### 86.9.10 NOISE Summary

Menu: Context menu -> Print -> NOISE Summary ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 6992](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6992.png)

This command is used to print the NOISE Summary, which supports NOISE/PNOSIE/HBNOISE analysis.

![image 6993](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6993.png)

###### Figure 86.768 NOISE Summary Form

Data From: speciﬁes the simulation data. Type: deﬁnes the method of computing noise.

• Spot Noise: selects this option, it will use the given frequency to computing noise.

![image 6994](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6994.png)

Figure 86.769 Spot Noise

– Frequency Spot(Hz): speciﬁes the frequency of Spot Noise. • Integrated Noise: selects this option, it will produce a noise summary

integrated over a frequency range.

![image 6995](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6995.png)

Figure 86.770 Integrated Noise

- – From(Hz): speciﬁes the starting value of Integrated Noise.
- – To(Hz): speciﬁes the ending value of Integrated Noise. Noise Unit: speciﬁes the unit for this noise summary.


- • V^2: speciﬁes noise summary unit as V^2.
- • V: speciﬁes noise summary unit as V.


Hierarchy Level: selects the hierarchy level from the drop-down list, the device from top level to hierarchy level will be computed. Changes the hierarchy level, all the device types from top level to hierarchy level will be listed in the list box, you can select these types by Shift or Ctrl. The default is empty.

Select All: selects all the device types in the list box below. Select None: deselects all the device types in the list box below. Include Instances: lists instances to include.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to include from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all included instances.


Exclude Instances: lists instances to exclude.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to exclude from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all excluded instances.


Truncate: limits the number of devices in the noise summary according to noise contribution, the default is By Number.

- • None: selects this option, there will be no limit for noise summary.

![image 6996](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6996.png)

Figure 86.771 Truncate - None

- • By Number: selects this option, only shows the Top number of the highest noise contribution in the noise summary.

![image 6997](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6997.png)

Figure 86.772 Truncate - By Number

– Top: sets the value of Top, the default value is 3.

- • By Relative Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices in which the percentage of noise contribution is greater than Noise%.

![image 6998](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6998.png)

Figure 86.773 Truncate - By Relative Threshold

– Noise%: sets the value of By Relative Threshold, the default

value is 50.

- • By Absolute Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices in which the noise contribution is greater than Noise Value.


![image 6999](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile6999.png)

Figure 86.774 Truncate - By Absolute Threshold

##### – Noise Value: sets the value of By Absolute threshold, the de-

fault value is 0.

Sort By: deﬁnes the order of the noise summary, the default is Noise Contribution.

- • Noise Contribution: sorts by the noise contribution from large to small.
- • Composite Noise: sorts by the total noise contribution of each device from large to small. The same device is in the same group.
- • Device Name: sorts by ASCII of the each device name. The same device is in the same group.


Consolidate Iterated Instances: checks this option which will combine the noise contributions of iterated instances to one.

Suﬃx Notation: checks this option which will convert scientiﬁc notation to suﬃx notaion.

Absolute Noise Precision: sets absolute noise precision, the default is 6. Relative Noise Precision: sets relative noise precision, the default is 2.

Parametric Variable: selects a sweep variable combination. This table only appears when PSS analysis has Sweep checked or HB analysis has Sweep/Loadpull checked.

Example 86.45

This example shows how to print NOISE Summary by Context menu -> Print -> NOISE Summary.

- 1. Set NOISE analysis, as follows:


![image 7000](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7000.png)

- Figure 86.775 NOISE Analysis Setting
- 2. Click Netlist And Run to run simulation.
- 3. After simulation, invoke Context menu -> Print -> NOISE Summary.


![image 7001](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7001.png)

Figure 86.776 NOISE Summary

- 4. The default value of Type is Spot Noise and the default value of Frequency Spot(Hz) is the value of At Frequency in NOISE analysis. When Sweep Variable in NOISE analysis is not Frequency, Type and Frequency Spot(Hz) are not allowed to modify. VDD is the Variable Name in NOISE analysis and its default value is the minimum value of Sweep Range.
- 5. Specify the Hierarchy Level to 1, the types of all devices in layer 0~1 will be displayed in the list box. Click Select All to select all types in the list box. Set the Inlucde Instances and Exclude Instances list (Wildcards are supported).


![image 7002](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7002.png)

Figure 86.777 NOISE Summary - Filter

###### 6. Select None from Truncate drop-down list, and check Noise Contribution.

![image 7003](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7003.png)

Figure 86.778 NOISE Summary - Truncate And Sort

###### 7. Click Apply, the noise summary information appears as follows:

![image 7004](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7004.png)

Figure 86.779 Simulation Results - Noise Contribution

###### 8. Check Composite Noise, and click Apply, the noise summary informationappears as follows:

![image 7005](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7005.png)

Figure 86.780 Simulation Results - Composite Noise

- 9. Check Device Name, and click Apply, the noise summary information appears as follows:


![image 7006](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7006.png)

Figure 86.781 Simulation Results - Device Name

##### 10. Check Noise Contribution, Composite Noise, Consolidate Iterated In-stances and Suﬃx Notation. Set Absolute Noise Precision to 4 and setRelative Noise Precision to 3. Click Apply, the noise summary informa-tion appears as follows:

![image 7007](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7007.png)

Figure 86.782 Simulation Results - Noise Contribution and Composite Noise

### 86.9.11 DCMATCH Summary

Menu: Context menu -> Print -> DCMATCH Summary ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 7008](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7008.png)

This command is used to print the DCMATCH Summary, which only is just for DCMATCH analysis.

![image 7009](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7009.png)

Figure 86.783 DCMATCH Summary Form

Filter: shows all the device types in the list box, you can select these types by Shift or Ctrl. The default is empty.

Select All: selects all the device types in the list box below. Select None: selects all the device types in the list box below. Include Instances: lists instances to include.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to include from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all included instances.


Exclude Instances: lists instances to exclude.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to exclude from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all excluded instances.


Device Type: selects device type from drop-down list. The variations from the device type will be listed in the list box, you can select these variations by Shift or Ctrl. The default is empty.

Select All: selects all the variations in the list box below. Select None: selects all the variations in the list box below.

Truncate: limits the number of devices in the DCMATCH summary, the default is By Relative Threshold.

- • None: selects this option, it will no limit for DCMATCH summary.

![image 7010](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7010.png)

Figure 86.784 Truncate - None

- • By Number: selects this option, only shows the Top number of devices in the DCMATCH summary.

![image 7011](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7011.png)

Figure 86.785 Truncate - By Number

– Top: sets the value of Top, the default value is 3.

- • By Relative Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices in which the absolute value of Contribution or sigmaOut is greater than Threshold multiplied by the largest absolute value of Contribution or sigmaOut in all devices.

![image 7012](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7012.png)

Figure 86.786 Truncate - By Relative Threshold

– Threshold: sets the value of By Relative Threshold.

- • By Absolute Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices in which the absolute value of Contribution or sigmaOut is greater than Mismatch.


![image 7013](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7013.png)

Figure 86.787 Truncate - By Absolute Threshold

##### – Mismatch: sets the value of By Absolute threshold.

Sort By: deﬁnes the order of the DCMATCH summary, the default is Output Variation.

- • Output Variation: sorts by the Contribution or sigmaOut from large to small. If same values of Contribution or sigmaOut appeared, it will sort by Device Name.
- • Device Name: sorts by ASCII of each device name.


Suﬃx Notation: checks this option which will convert scientiﬁc notation to suﬃx notation.

Absolute Precision: sets absolute precision, the default is 6. Relative Precision: sets relative precision, the default is 2.

When specify Sweep Variable in DCMATCH analysis, the DCMATCH Summary form expands as shown below.

![image 7014](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7014.png)

Figure 86.788 DCMATCH Summary Form

Print Summary At Temperature Spot(C): sets the point to print DCMATCH summary result. The points generated by Sweep Range, Sweep Type and Add Speciﬁc Points in DCMATCH analysis, and set the minimum point into Print Summary At Temperature Spot(C), such as 0.5.

## 86.11 Data History

Menu: Results -> Data History ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 7033](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7033.png)

This command is used to load the latest simulation results. The latest results are saved in the Project Directory, which is set in Setup -> Netlist/Directory. This command is only supported in MDE Level2 and Advanced MDE.

- • Delete: deletes the selected simulation results.
- • Rename: renames the selected simulation results.
- • View: only shows the selected simulation results in results tab, do not change the current setting state.
- • Load: loads the latest simulation results.

: checks this item, it will participate simulation.

Parameter: clicks drop-down box to select a design parameter. This option is not editable.

Value: As long as the Parameter is selected, the corresponding value will be loaded also. This option is not editable.

##### Range Type: speciﬁes a range type. It includes four types: Start-Stop, Center-Span, Center-Span% and Add Speciﬁc Points.

Start-Stop: speciﬁes start and stop of sweep values, both of them are used together to specify sweep limits.

Center-Span: speciﬁes center and span of sweep, both of them are used together to specify sweep limits. The calculation formula is as follows,

center − 0.5 ∗ span,center + 0.5 ∗ span

Center-Span%: speciﬁes center and span of sweep, both of them are used together to specify sweep limits. The calculation formula is as follows,

center − 0.5 ∗ span% ∗ center,center + 0.5 ∗ span% ∗ center

##### Add Speciﬁc Points: speciﬁes values only by Inclusion List and Exclusion List.

Step Mode: speciﬁes a step mode to check analysis point information. It includes seven modes: Auto, Linear Steps, Linear, Decade, Octave, Logarithmic, Times.

Table 88.1 The Formula Illustrations of Step Modes

|Step Mode<br><br>|Title For Setting|Formula|
|---|---|---|


|Auto|Total Steps<br><br>|![image 7094](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7094.png)|
|---|---|---|
|Linear Steps<br><br>|Step Size|f(n)=f(n-1)+$step_size|
|Linear|Total Steps<br><br>|f(n)= ($stop-$start)/($steps-1)+f(n-1)|
|Decade<br><br>|Steps/Decade<br><br>|![image 7095](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7095.png)|
|Octave|Steps/Octave<br><br>|![image 7096](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7096.png)|
|Logarithmic|Total Steps<br><br>|![image 7097](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7097.png)|
|Times<br><br>|Multiplier<br><br>|f(n)=$multiplier* f(n-1)|


||Note: Both $start and $stop are the starting value and the termination value of the actual value range.|
|---|
|
|---|


Inclusion List: this input box is used to add additional analysis points, which can be outside or inside the range of sweep point.

Exclusion List: this input box is used to skip the speciﬁed analysis points.

If you keep the default value empty, it will not skip any analysis points.

Continue: continue the suspended process in the current tab. This button is invisible if the process is not suspended by the Pause.

![image 7138](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7138.png)

Figure 89.4 MDEL2 Analog Outputs Panel

Analog: shows analog output signals, Outputs panel displays this table by default mode.

Name: lists the analog signal name or expression name. Type: lists the output type. It can be Signal or Expression. Expression/Signal: lists the contents of expression or signal. If it’s normal signal, this option is the same as Name. EvalType: sets evaluate type. It can be Point, Corners, Sweeps, All. The default value is Point.

- • Point: calculates the expression for every point.
- • Corners: calculates the expression across all corners.
- • Sweeps: calculates the expression across all sweep points.
- • All: calculates the expression across all corners and sweep points. Save: enables or disables saving. Plot: enables or disables plotting. Spec: clicks to deﬁne the speciﬁcation. The speciﬁcation of evaluate rule when simulating is shown in table below.
- • none: no speciﬁcation.
- • <: inputs target value, if the simulation result is less than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • >: inputs target value, if the simulation result is greater than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • range: inputs lower bound and upper bound, if the simulation result falls between the boundary values, the pass status will be returned.
- • tolerance: inputs target value and percentage deviation, if the simulation result is within the percentage deviation of the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • minimize: inputs target value as the target of the minimization result, if the simulation result is less than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • maximize: inputs target value as the target of the maximization result, if the simulation result is greater than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • info: no evaluation.


Table 89.1 Rule of Evaluate Speciﬁcation

|Type|Status<br><br>|Evaluate Rule|
|---|---|---|
|<|pass<br><br>|<targetValue|
| |near|[targetValue, targetValue×(1+10%)]|
| |fail<br><br>|>targetValue×(1+10%)|
|>|pass<br><br>|>targetValue|
| |near<br><br>|[targetValue×(1-10%), targetValue]|
| |fail<br><br>|<targetValue×(1-10%)|
|range<br><br>|pass<br><br>|(lowerBound, upperBound)|
| |near|[lowerBound×(1-10%), lowerBound] or [upperBound, upperBound×(1+10%)]|
| |fail|(-∞, lowerBound×(1-10%)) or (upperBound×(1+10%), +∞)|
|tolerance<br><br>|pass<br><br>|[targetValue×(1-tol%), targetValue×(1+tol%))|
| |near|[targetValue×(1-tol%)(1-10%), targetValue×(1-tol%)) or [targetValue×(1+tol%), targetValue×(1+tol%)(1+10%)]|
| |fail|(-∞, targetValue×(1-tol%)(1-10%)) or (targetValue×(1+tol%)(1+10%), +∞)|
|minimize|pass<br><br>|<targetValue|
| |near<br><br>|[targetValue, targetValue×(1+10%)]|
| |fail|>targetValue×(1+10%)|
|maximize<br><br>|pass|>targetValue|
| |near|[targetValue×(1-10%), targetValue]|
| |fail<br><br>|<targetValue×(1-10%)|
|info| |no evaluation|


Note: 10% in table above is Near Tolerance Of Speciﬁcation. See Also: Results -> Annotate -> Annotate Options 86.8.9.

Weight: sets the weight of speciﬁcation. S+: clicks this button to execute Select From Design, it can add normal signals to Outputs panel. E+: clicks this button to execute Output Setting, it can add expression to Outputs panel.

- Example 89.1


The example shows how to deﬁne speciﬁcation.

- 1. Click spec column of the expression, and select none in the drop-down list as Figure 89.7 :

![image 7147](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7147.png)

- 2. Press Enter or change mouse focus, the speciﬁcation deﬁned successfully.

Figure 89.8 After Deﬁne Spec None

- 3. Click spec column of the expression, and select <, >, minimize or maximize in the drop-down list, and input target value in the text ﬁeld. The target value can be a number or an expression.

![image 7149](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7149.png)

Figure 89.9 Deﬁne Spec Less

- 4. Press Enter or change mouse focus, the speciﬁcation deﬁned successfully.
- 5. Click spec column of the expression, and select range in the drop-down list, and input lower bound and upper bound in the two text ﬁelds. The lower


bound and upper bound can be a number or an expression. If lower bound and upper bound are both numbers, then lower bound must be less than upper bound, otherwise the speciﬁcation returns to the last valid value or none.

Figure 89.10 Deﬁne Spec Range

The target value can be a number or an expression. If percentage deviation is not positive number, the speciﬁcation returns to the last valid value or none.


![image 7151](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7151.png)

- Figure 89.11 Deﬁne Spec Range
- 8. Press Enter or change mouse focus, the speciﬁcation deﬁned successfully.

![image 7152](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7152.png)

## 89.3 Results

Menu: Window -> Results ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 7155](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7155.png)

This command is used to display or hide the results dock in MDEL2 form. By default, it is below the outputs dock. MDEL2 shows simulation results on the dock automatic after a successful simulation. Type of Results contains waves of outputs signal, waves of expression and value of expression.

![image 7156](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7156.png)

Figure 89.15 MDEL2 Detailed Results

Corner Information: shows corner information including model ﬁle, parameter and temperature. Contents are same as Show Full Corner Table

• Parameter: lists model ﬁles name, parameters name and temperature. • Nominal: displays conditions of nominal including section of model,

value of parameter and value of temperature.

• Corner Name: displays conditions of corner including section of model,

value of parameter and value of temperature. Simulation Results: shows simulation results.

- • Output: lists outputs name that you set in Outputs panel.
- • Nominal: displays simulation results of nominal. If the corner has speciﬁcation, it will return four status(pass, near, fail, error) after simulating. See Also: Window -> Outputs 95.2.5.


- – pass: means the simulation result is within the limits deﬁned by speciﬁcation, displayed with a green background.
- – near: means the simulation result is no more than Near Tolerance Of Speciﬁcation outside the target value of the speciﬁcation, displayed with a yellow background.


- – fail: means the simulation result is greater than Near Tolerance Of Speciﬁcation outside the target value of the speciﬁcation, displayed with a red background.
- – error: means the expression given in the speciﬁcation failed to evaluate, displayed with a crimson background.


- • Spec: displays outputs speciﬁcation.

- – overridden: means one or more corner speciﬁcation is overridden.
- – disabled: means all the corners’ speciﬁcations are disabled.
- – speciﬁcation: means all the corners’ speciﬁcations are same as the


global speciﬁcation.

- • Weight: displays output weight.
- • Pass/Fail: displays a pass, near, fail or error status for each output.

- – pass: means the simulation results of all the corners have a pass status.
- – near: means the simulation result of one or more corners have a near status.
- – fail: means the simulation result of one or more corners have a fail status.
- – error: means the simulation result of one or more corners have an error status.


- • Min: displays minimum value of output across all of corners.
- • Max: displays maximum value of output across all of corners.
- • Corner Name: displays simulation results of corner. If the corner has speciﬁcation, it will return four status(pass, near, fail, error) after simulating. See Also: Window -> Outputs 95.2.5.
- • Key Word: many key words will be shown in results tab. It is shown as follows:

|value|It is a result of measurement.|
|---|---|
|eval_err|Failed to evaluate it. It may be caused by wrong expression or no date.|

Output: lists outputs name which is double value for Detailed Results. Min: displays minimum value of output across all of values. Max: displays maximum value of output across all of values. Mean: displays mean value of output across all of values. Median: displays median value of output across all of values. Std Dev: displays standard deviation value of output across all of values. Spec: displays outputs speciﬁcation.

- • overridden: means one or more corner speciﬁcation is overridden.
- • disabled: means all the corners’ speciﬁcations are disabled.
- • speciﬁcation: means all the corners’ speciﬁcations are same as the global speciﬁcation.


Pass/Fail: displays a pass, near, fail or error status for each output.

- • pass: means the Min and Max have a pass status. • near: means the Min and Max have a near status. • fail: means the Min and Max of one or more have a fail status.
- • error: means the Min and Max of one or more have a error status. Pass Ratio: displays the pass ratio. Save: saves summary results to a CSV ﬁle.


Display statistical information during multiple iterations of the same corner after the expression is simulated and calculated using "Run Monte Carlo". First level node row: displays the statistical situation of all corners of the corresponding output in multiple iterations. Second level node row: displays the statistical situation of each corner of the corresponding output in multiple iterations.

![image 7159](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7159.png)

Figure 89.17 MDEL2 Yield Results

Output: lists the output and corner names that participate in MC iterations and have EvalType as Point or Corners and simulation results as scalars.

Yield: displays the pass rate of several iterations of the corresponding corner for each output. The pass rate of the ﬁrst level node summary is the smallest among all the corner pass rates.

Min: displays the minimum value among all iteration results of the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the minimum values of all corners under the current output in all iteration results.

Max: displays the maximum value among all iteration results of the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the maximum values of all corners under the current output in all iteration results.

Mean: displays the average of all iteration results for the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the average of all iteration results for all corners under the current output.

Std Dev: displays the standard deviation of all iteration results for the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the standard deviation of all iteration results for all corners under the current output.

Spec: displays the spec values of the current Output and Corner.

- • overridden: means one or more corner speciﬁcation is overridden.
- • disabled: means all the corners’ speciﬁcations are disabled.


- • speciﬁcation: means all the corners’ speciﬁcations are same as the global speciﬁcation.

# Part VIII Mixed-signal Design Environment Platform

# Chapter 92 Introduction

MDE Platform oﬀers a comprehensive suite of tools and features designed to cater to every aspect of the circuit design process. From schematic capture to layout implementation, Platform simulator provides a seamless and intuitive environment for crafting even the most intricate designs. Harness the full potential of user’s designs with Platform’s advanced simulation capabilities. Otherwise, from transient analysis to Monte Carlo simulations, Platform simulator empowers user to explore the behavior of circuits with unprecedented depth and insight.

# Chapter 93 Multiple Tests

Multiple Tests can simultaneously running multiple testbenches, conducting cosimulations, and debugging multiple circuit modules within a single top cell to meet overall design objectives. It primarily features:

- 1. Managing multiple testbench simulations.
- 2. Batch modifying simulation settings for multiple testbenches.
- 3. Post-processing simulation results and generating comprehensive reports.

### 93.3.5 Load Setup StateMenu: File -> Load Setup State

Figure 93.7 Load Setup State

States Name: selects the name of the state to be loaded. Description: shows the description of the selected state. What To Load: speciﬁes which options to load. • Select: selects or deselects setup options.

- – Select All: selects all setup options.
- – Select None: deselects all setup options.


• Options: lists all setup options.

- – Tests: whether to load all tests and all settings belonging to the tests.


- – Outputs: whether to load output information.
- – Global Parameters: whether to load global parameters information.
- – Corner Setup: whether to load corner setup information.
- – Run Setup: whether to load run setup information.
- – Job Setup: whether to load job setup information.
- – Save Options: whether to load results save options information.
- – Filter Setting: whether to load ﬁlter information.


Mode: speciﬁes mode for loading state

- • Retain: keeps all the rows on the option panel, and only loads the row with non-duplicate name in loaded state and option panel.
- • Merge: keeps the row on the option panel which is not the same name as that in loaded state, deletes the row on the state panel which has the same name as that in loaded state, and loads all the rows in loaded state.
- • Overwrite: clears all the rows on the option panel and loads all the rows in the loaded state.

## 93.5 Simulation

- 93.5.1 Job Setup Menu: Simulation -> Job Setup


![image 7244](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7244.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to specify simulation job mode. To invoke option menu, select Simulation -> Job Setup.

![image 7245](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7245.png)

Figure 93.10 Job Setup Form

Mode: speciﬁes whether to run simulation in distributed mode or not. Local: all simulation jobs run locally (without network read/write).

- Figure 93.11 Job Setup Form-LSF

LSF: Load Sharing Facility. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via LSF.

![image 7247](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7247.png)

- Figure 93.12 Job Setup Form-OGE


OGE: Oracle Grid Engine. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via OGE.

- Figure 93.13 Job Setup Form-Donau


Donau: Donau Engine. If you select it, all simulation jobs run in the distributed mode (with network read/write) via Donau.

Job Name: job name of LSF, OGE or Donau. Default value is jHHMMSS(H is hour, M is minute, S is second). Its length should be from 1 to 10 characters. Because MDE Platform uses it as key name for simulation and waveform post-processing, the user had better provide a meaningful name.

Queue Name: Queue name of LSF, OGE or Donau. MDE Platform loads the queue names of LSF, OGE or Donau when the user launches it for the ﬁrst time. MDE Platform does not update it if queue names have been changed by administrator.

Misc: other options for LSF, OGE or Donau. Tests with Local jobPolicy: lists the names of all tests that utilize the Local job policy.

Turn Oﬀ Test Job Setup: clicking this button will prompt a dialog asking for conﬁrmation. If Yes is clicked, the Global job setup will be applied to all tests.

||Note: We suggest using LSF, OGE or Donau when you run multicorner simulations. But using LSF, OGE or Donau, there are some requirements:<br><br>• LSF, OGE or Donau must be installed.<br>• All directories and ﬁles have the same name on all servers.<br>• All directories and ﬁles must be accessed by user on all servers. The following directory may be not valid, /home/userA. Because /home/userA on diﬀerent servers are diﬀerent.<br>|
|---|
|
|---|


Max Job Number: speciﬁes the max job number for simulation, the value range is [1,30000], the default value is 20. The minimum value is 2 when using LSF, OGE or Donau.

||Note: If environment variable AETHER_MDE_MAX_JOB is set, the value will be used as the max job number for simulation.|
|---|
|
|---|

- 93.5.4 Run Monte Carlo Menu: Simulation -> Run Monte Carlo


![image 7253](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7253.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to run Monte Carlo simulation for all checked tests.

![image 7254](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7254.png)

Figure 93.16 Run Monte Carlo Form

Statistical Variation: deﬁnes statistical variation, to be used with a Monte Carlo analysis.

- • Process: speciﬁes the input process statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • Mismatch: speciﬁes the input mismatch statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • All: speciﬁes both process and mismatch statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.


Sampling Method: speciﬁes the method of statistical sampling to apply.

- • Random: generates statistical variation random numbers that according to the speciﬁed distributions.
- • LHS: generates statistical variation using Latin Hypercube Sampling(LHS). When this option is selected, the Number Of Bins is enabled.
- • LDS: generates statistical variation using Latin Discrepancy Sampling(LDS).


Number Of Points: sets the number of Monte Carlo points you want to simulate. The minimum value is 1, default is 10.

Number Of Bins: sets the number of bins (subdivisions) in the text ﬁeld for LHS method. The minimum value is 1, default is 10.

Monte Carlo Seed: sets the seed for the Monte Carlo analysis. The minimum value is 1, default is 12345.

First Point: sets the ﬁrst point for the Monte Carlo analysis. The minimum value is 1, default is 1.

Netlist Options: sets the netlist options for the Monte Carlo analysis. The default value is empty.

Save Simulation Data: whether to save simulation directory for the Monte Carlo analysis. If the checkbox is checked, save the simulation directory, otherwise delete simulation dirctory. The default value is not checked.

Save Statistical Data: whether to save montecarlo directory for the Monte Carlo analysis. If the checkbox is checked, save the montecarlo directory, otherwise delete montecarlo dirctory. The default value is not checked.

##### Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo(Unspeciﬁed): clicks this button to show the form Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo [Global].

Default: clicks this Default button, the form will reload the default settings. OK: clicks this OK button, the operation will be saved and executed. Cancel: clicks this Cancel button, the operation will be canceled and the form escapes at the same time. This form Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo [Global] speciﬁes instances for Monte Carlo analysis.

![image 7255](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7255.png)

Figure 93.17 Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo [Global]

##### Statistical Variation: deﬁnes statistical variation, its same as Statistical Variation to the Run Monte Carlo form.

Selected: speciﬁes the value for Selected, the default value is Process. Unselected: speciﬁes the value for Unselected, the default value is Process.

Test: shows the name of enable tests. If all of tests are disabled, it will be set No Test Enabled.

Instances Speciﬁcation: speciﬁes instances from schematic or subcircuit.

• Schematic: speciﬁes instances from schematic.

##### – Select From Schematic: clicks this Select From Schematic

button to select instances from schematic.

Example 93.3 The following is the netlist format for the Monte Carlo analysis:

- 1. When Sampling Method=Random: mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=mismatch {...}
- 2. When Sampling Method=LHS, check the Number Of Bins option, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=process sampling=lhs numbins=0 {...}

- 3. When Sampling Method=LHS, uncheck the Number Of Bins option, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows: mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all sampling=lhs {...}
- 4. When Sampling Method=LDS, First Point=3, Netlist Options=itl4=200, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all sampling=lds itl4=200 ﬁrstrun=3{...}

- 5. When Sampling Method=Random, uncheck the Number Of Bins option, set Selected=Process Unselected=No Variation, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=process ignoremode=nominal {...}

- 6. When Sampling Method=Random, uncheck the Number Of Bins option, set Selected=No Variation Unselected=Mismatch, the syntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:


mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=mismatch ignore=[...] {...}

##### 7. When Sampling Method=Random, uncheck the Number Of Bins op-tion, set Selected=All Unselected=No Variation, the syntax is like fol-lowing or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all dut=[...] ignoremode=nominal {...}

###### 8. When Sampling Method=Random, check the Save Statistical Data thesyntax is like following or the syntax is as follows:

mc1 montecarlo numruns=200 seed=4321 variations=all saveprocessparams=yes processparamﬁle="../monteCarlo/processParam" processscalarﬁle="../monteCarlo/processData" savemismatchparams=yes dumpdependency=mismatch dependencyscalarﬁle="../monteCarlo/compactmismatchdata" dependencyparamﬁle="../monteCarlo/compactmismatchparam" {...}

Project Directory: speciﬁes the working directory of simulation. $(HOME) will be replaced by your home directory, and $(USER) will be replaced by the user name.

History Number: speciﬁes the number of history. If the number of history is speciﬁed as 1, the Overwrite Directory checkbox is automatically checked.

Overwrite Directory: speciﬁes directory to be overwritten. If the Overwrite Directory is checked, it will auto overwrite the directory when run simulation.

Save Simulation Data: speciﬁes whether the simulation save data. If it is checked, the simulation data will be saved, otherwise it will not save simulation data. The default status is checked.

History Name Preﬁx: speciﬁes a history name preﬁx string for the upcoming simulation runs. A separate preﬁx can be conﬁgured for each simulation run mode. For example, if sweepcorner is set for Sweeps & Corners run mode, the 1st upcoming run of Sweeps & Corners type will be named as sweepcorner.1 and the 2nd will be named as sweepcorner.2. If a preﬁx string is left as an empty string, PlatRun will be used by default. This conﬁguration only aﬀects the history names created in Multiple Tests mode. In Single Test mode, it does not take eﬀect.

Menu: Window -> Outputs

ToolBar:

This command is used to display or hide the outputs dock in MDE Platform.

![image 7324](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7324.png)

![image 7325](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7325.png)

(a) Display (b) Hide

Figure 93.62 MDE Platform Window Outputs

![image 7326](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7326.png)

Figure 93.63 MDE Platform Analog Outputs Panel

Analog: shows analog output signals, Outputs panel displays this table by default mode.

Test: lists which test this output belongs to. Name: lists the analog signal name or expression name.

Type: lists the output type. It can be Signal or Expression. Expression/Signal: lists the contents of expression or signal. If it’s normal signal, this option is the same as Name. EvalType: sets evaluate type. It can be Point, Corners, Sweeps, All. The default value is Point.

- • Point: calculates the expression for every point.
- • Corners: calculates the expression across all corners.
- • Sweeps: calculates the expression across all sweep points.
- • All: calculates the expression across all corners and sweep points. Save: enables or disables saving. Plot: enables or disables plotting. Spec: clicks to deﬁne the speciﬁcation. The rule of evaluate speciﬁcation when simulating as shown in table below.
- • none: no speciﬁcation.
- • <: inputs target value, if the simulation result is less than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • >: inputs target value, if the simulation result is greater than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • range: inputs lower bound and upper bound, if the simulation result falls between the boundary values, the pass status will be returned.
- • tolerance: inputs target value and percentage deviation, if the simulation result is within the percentage deviation of the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • minimize: inputs target value as the target of the minimization result, if the simulation result is less than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • maximize: inputs target value as the target of the maximization result, if the simulation result is greater than the target value, the pass status will be returned.
- • info: no evaluation.


Table 93.3 Rule of Evaluate Speciﬁcation

|Type|Status<br><br>|Evaluate Rule|
|---|---|---|
|<|pass<br><br>|<targetValue|
| |near|[targetValue, targetValue×(1+10%)]|
| |fail<br><br>|>targetValue×(1+10%)|
|>|pass<br><br>|>targetValue|
| |near<br><br>|[targetValue×(1-10%), targetValue]|
| |fail<br><br>|<targetValue×(1-10%)|
|range<br><br>|pass<br><br>|(lowerBound, upperBound)|
| |near|[lowerBound×(1-10%), lowerBound] or [upperBound, upperBound×(1+10%)]|
| |fail|(-∞, lowerBound×(1-10%)) or (upperBound×(1+10%), +∞)|
|tolerance<br><br>|pass<br><br>|[targetValue×(1-tol%), targetValue×(1+tol%))|
| |near|[targetValue×(1-tol%)(1-10%), targetValue×(1-tol%)) or [targetValue×(1+tol%), targetValue×(1+tol%)(1+10%)]|
| |fail|(-∞, targetValue×(1-tol%)(1-10%)) or (targetValue×(1+tol%)(1+10%), +∞)|
|minimize|pass<br><br>|<targetValue|
| |near<br><br>|[targetValue, targetValue×(1+10%)]|
| |fail|>targetValue×(1+10%)|
|maximize<br><br>|pass|>targetValue|
| |near|[targetValue×(1-10%), targetValue]|
| |fail<br><br>|<targetValue×(1-10%)|
|info| |no evaluation|


Note: 10% in table above is Near Tolerance Of Speciﬁcation. Corner Information: shows corner information including model ﬁle, parameter and temperature, and group according to test.

value of parameter and value of temperature. Simulation Results: shows simulation results.

- – pass: means the simulation result is within the limits deﬁned by speciﬁcation, displayed with a green background.
- – near: means the simulation result is no more than Near Tolerance Of Speciﬁcation outside the target value of the speciﬁcation, displayed with a yellow background.


- – fail: means the simulation result is greater than Near Tolerance Of Speciﬁcation outside the target value of the speciﬁcation, displayed with a red background.

error status.

Display statistical information during multiple iterations of the same corner after the expression is simulated and calculated using "Run Monte Carlo".

- • First level node row: displays which test the output below belongs to.

Test: lists the names of the tests to which the output belongs Output: lists the output and corner names that participate in MC iterations and have EvalType as Point or Corners and simulation results as scalars.

Yield: displays the pass rate of several iterations of the corresponding corner for each output. The pass rate of the ﬁrst level node summary is the smallest among all the corner pass rates.

Min: displays the minimum value among all iteration results of the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the minimum values of all corners under the current output in all iteration results.

Max: displays the maximum value among all iteration results of the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the maximum values of all corners under the current output in all iteration results.

Mean: displays the average of all iteration results for the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the average of all iteration results for all corners under the current output.

Std Dev: displays the standard deviation of all iteration results for the current Output and Corner. At the ﬁrst level node row, displays the standard deviation of all iteration results for all corners under the current output.

Spec: displays the spec values of the current Output and Corner.

### 93.9.4 Jobs

Menu: Window -> Jobs ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 7360](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7360.png)

This command is used to display or hide the jobs dock in MDE Platform form. Jobs dock dynamically displays the information of all jobs called by the simulation currently underway on the MDE Platform. For jobs that complete normally, their information will be cleared after 5 seconds of successful execution. For jobs that exit abnormally, by default, their information will remain on the Jobs dock.

![image 7361](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7361.png)

Figure 93.78 Jobs Dock in Default Style

![image 7362](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7362.png)

Figure 93.79 Jobs Dock in Distributor Style

Default Style: displays the following information about the job: Job ID, Job Policy, Host, CPU%, State, History, Test, Sweep, Corner, Submit Time, Start Time, Running Time.

Distributor Style: on top of the information displayed in the default style, add the following information about the job: Distributor Job ID, Load%, Reason, Submit Time Cost.

: if you click this button, the data in the jobs dock will be restored to its original order, sorted in ascending order by Job ID. Job ID: displays the job number, increasing sequentially from 1. Job Policy: displays the mode in the Job Setup form corresponding to the job. It currently supports four types: Local, LSF, OGE, and Donau. Distributor Job ID: local mode: displayed as "–"; other modes: displays the ID assigned by the scheduler for the job. Host: displays the server name where the job is located. Load%: displays the load of the computing node where the current job is located. CPU%: displays the CPU usage of the job on the computing node where it is located. State: displays the current status of the job. Reason: displays the reason why the job is in this state. History: displays the result name corresponding to the job. Test: displays the test name of the job. Sweep: displays the sweep parameters of the job. Corner: displays the corner name of the job. Submit Time: displays the time of job submission. Start Time: displays the time when the job started running on the server.

![image 7363](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7363.png)

Submit Time Cost: displays the time waiting for the job from submission to start running, which is equal to the time diﬀerence between Start Time and Submit Time.

Running Time: displays the time used by the job since it started running, equal to the time diﬀerence between the current time and the start Time. Refresh the display every 5 seconds until the job ends and exits.

# Chapter 94 Single Test

Run a single testbench to simulate and debug an individual bottom-level circuit to meet design objectives. The interactive Test includes the following characteristics:

- 1. Perform parameter scanning, analyze and debug the circuit.
- 2. Conduct Corner and MC simulations.
- 3. Utilize result GUI to check if the speciﬁcations are met.

Figure 94.8 Select Load Options

Select: selects the options to be loaded from the loaded state.

• Select All: all setup options are selected. • Select None: no setup option is selected.

Options: speciﬁes options to load.

- • Analysis: whether to load analysis information.
- • Model Setup: whether to load model information.
- • Parameters: whether to load parameter information.
- • Outputs: whether to load output information.
- • Simulation Options: whether to load simulation option information.
- • Convergence Setup: whether to load convergence information.
- • Simulation Files: whether to load simulation ﬁles information.
- • Stimuli: whether to load stimuli information.
- • Note Text: whether to load note text information.
- • Corner Setup: whether to load corner information.
- • Run Setup: whether to load Monte Carlo information.
- • MMSIM: whether to load mixed simulation information.


Mode: speciﬁes mode for loading state.

• Overwrite: clears all the rows on the option panel and loads all the rows in the loaded state.

- 94.4.1 Design Menu: Setup -> Design


ToolBar:

Hide Category: hides “category” panel. Show Schematic View: shows the “schematic” view Library: selects the corresponding library of top design. Cell: selects the corresponding cell of top design. View: selects the corresponding view of top design.

![image 7395](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7395.png)

![image 7396](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7396.png)

Figure 94.10 MDE Platform Setup Simulator

Simulator: speciﬁes simulation tool.

- • Alps: Alps analog simulator.
- • Hspice: Hspice analog simulator.
- • Alps-MS: Alps-MS mixed-signal simulator.
- • Alps-CS: Alps-CS co-simulation simulator.


Thread Number: speciﬁes the number of threads used for simulation, the thread number should be an integer from 1 to 99.

Use Job CPUs As MT: speciﬁes the job CPUs as the multiple threads used for simulation.

### 94.4.3 High Performance

Menu: Setup -> High Performance

![image 7397](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7397.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to provide the high performance simulation for spectre.

![image 7398](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7398.png)

Figure 94.11 High Performance Form

Simulation Performance Mode: speciﬁes the simulation performance mode. Possible values are None, Baseline, Turbo, Advanced. The default value is Baseline. This option is controlled by the environment variable SLE_MDE_HIGH_PERFORMANCE_MODE.

General: speciﬁes the general options.

- • Error Preset: sets the accuracy level. Possible values are Not Override, Liberal, Moderate, Conservative. The default value is Not Override
- • Processor Aﬃnity: speciﬁes the value of processor aﬃnity. The values cannot be repeated.
- • Use Boost Mode: speciﬁes the value of use boost mode. The default value is not checked.
- • Use Cis: speciﬁes the value of use cis. The default value is not checked.


Post-Layout Setting: speciﬁes the post layout setting options.

- • Enable Post Layout Simulation: speciﬁes the level of simulation accuracy and speed. If it is checked, Post-Layout Preset Mode, Enable Fmax Control will be enabled. The defalut value is not checked.

- – Post-Layout Preset Mode: speciﬁes the post simulation level. If the simulation performance mode is None, Baseline or Turbo, Possible values are Level1(Liberal Mode), Level2, Level3(Moderate Mode), Level4, Level5(Conservative Mode). The default value is Level3(Moderate Mode). If the simulation performance mode is Advanced, Possible values are LA(Accurate Mode), LB(Balance Mode), LP(Performance Mode), LS(Super Mode), LU(Ultra Mode), LX(Extreme Mode).The default value is LS(Super Mode).
- – Enable Fmax Control: sets whether Circuit Internal Net Maximum Frequency(GHz) is valid. If it is checked, Circuit Internal Net Maximum Frequency(GHz) will be enabled. The default value is not checked.
- – Circuit Internal Net Maximum Frequency(GHz): speciﬁes the max frequency for post circuit simulation. The defalut value is empty.


- • Instance Preservation: speciﬁes the preservation instance. Possible values are None, Select, All. If you select the Select button, Selected Instances will be enabled. The default value is None.
- • Selected Instances: speciﬁes the instances. If you clicks the Select button, you can select instance. If you clicks the Clear button, the selected instances will be cleared.

- 94.4.6 Simulation Files Menu: Setup -> Simulation Files


![image 7408](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7408.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to set up simulation-speciﬁc ﬁles and directory paths.

![image 7409](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7409.png)

###### Figure 94.17 Simulation Files Form

![image 7410](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7410.png)

###### Figure 94.18 Simulation Files Form

Paths/Files: speciﬁes the search paths and include ﬁles.

- • Include Paths: speciﬁes the search path for all include ﬁles of the analog simulator. It will create a .option search statement in spice top netlist.
- • Include Simulation Files: includes the contents of another ﬁle into current netlist. .inc is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in spice top netlist.
- • Include Digital Files: includes the content of another digital ﬁle into current netlist. .include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in top verilog.
- • Include Pspice Files: includes the content of another pspice ﬁle into current netlist. pspice_include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in current netlist.
- • Include DSPF Files: includes the content of another DSPF ﬁle into current netlist. dspf_include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in current netlist.


– DSPF Options: speciﬁes the dspf ﬁles options.

∗ Port Order: speciﬁes the port order of dspf ﬁles. sch means take the port order from pre-layout schematic netlist, spf means take the port order from dspf ﬁle deﬁnition.

∗ Extra Port: speciﬁes the extra port of dspf ﬁles. true means extra ports in dspf ﬁle will change to inner nodes, false means the port number in dspf ﬁle and schematic is same.

∗ Case Sensitivity: speciﬁes the case sensitivity of dspf ﬁles. true means the dspf ﬁle is case-sensitive, false means the dspf ﬁles is case insensitive.

∗ Black Box: speciﬁes the instances which to be considered as

blackboxes. Click Select button to choose black box in schematic. ∗ Bus Delimiter: speciﬁes the bus delimiter of dspf ﬁles to map

with schematic. ∗ Other Options: speciﬁes any dspf_include options that are

not supported in this form of dspf ﬁles. Vector Files: speciﬁes the content of vector ﬁles.

• Include Vector Files: includes the content of another vector ﬁle into current netlist. .vec is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in spice top netlist.

### 94.4.7 Stimuli

Menu: Setup -> Stimuli

![image 7411](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7411.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to set up stimuli of the input ports or global sources.

![image 7412](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7412.png)

Figure 94.19 Setup Stimuli

Stimuli Type: specify stimuli type, which can be an input port or a global source.

Enable: specify whether an input port or a global source signal is ON or OFF. If a signal is ON or enabled, this signal is generated in the spice netlist, otherwise, it is not generated.

Function: choose the appropriate function for the selected signal.

- • dc: direct current.
- • pulse: pulse waveform.
- • sin: sinusoidal waveform.
- • exp: exponential waveform.
- • pwl: piecewise linear waveform.


Type: select the type of a signal from the list box, which can be voltage or current.

Note: Arguments listed here will change according to the signal function and type.

Example 94.2 This example shows how to set up a source

- 1. set the dc source as Figure 94.20. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vin (in gnd) vsource dc=1.8 mag=1 phase=0 type=dc” .

![image 7413](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7413.png)

Figure 94.20 Setup Stimuli-dc

- 2. set the pulse source as Figure 94.21. The spice top netlist will have a statement “Vin (in gnd) vsource delay=10n fall=1n period=20n rise=1n val0=0 val1=1.8 phase=0 dc=1.8 width=5n mag=1 type=pulse” .


![image 7414](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7414.png)

Figure 94.21 Setup Stimuli-pulse

###### 3. set the sinusoidal source as Figure 94.22. The spice top netlist will have astatement “Vin (in gnd) vsource delay=10n freq=10M ampl=100u sinedc=0phase=0 dc=1.8 mag=1 type=sine” .

![image 7415](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7415.png)

Figure 94.22 Setup Stimuli-sin

###### 4. set the exponential source as Figure 94.23. The spice top netlist will have astatement “Vin (in gnd) vsource delay=1n val0=0 tau1=1 val1=1.8 tau2=2td1=10n td2=20n phase=0 dc=1.5 mag=1 type=exp” .

![image 7416](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7416.png)

Figure 94.23 Setup Stimuli-exp

###### 5. set the piecewise linear source as Figure 94.24. The spice top netlist will have astatement “Vin (in gnd) vsource wave=[10m 1.6 ] mag=1 oﬀset=2n delay=1nphase=0 dc=0.8 type=pwl” .

![image 7417](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7417.png)

Figure 94.24 Setup Stimuli-pwl

### 94.4.8 NoteText SimulationMenu: Setup -> NoteText Simulation

![image 7418](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7418.png)

Sometimes a user may like to write the simulation statements directly. This command allows a user to write simulation statements manually by using the NoteText editor.

![image 7419](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7419.png)

Figure 94.25 Setup NoteText Simulation

Only Use NoteText To Run Simulation: ignore all simulation settings in MDE Platform, and use only the settings in NoteText to generate the spice top netlist.

Search Key: NoteText statements are written in sections (See “Create NoteText” ). Each section has a unique name. Search key lists all the sections and allow you to select. If you select a section, the content of that section is used to generate the spice top netlist.

- • Find: search user-deﬁned sections.
- • Show All: show all sections.
- • Name List: lists all the sections, and allows you to select one or more sections.


Text Browser: show the content of the selected section for review.

### 94.5.3 Display Partition

##### 94.5.3.1 Interactive

Menu: Mixed-Signal -> Display Partition -> Interactive

![image 7428](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7428.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to highlight analog, digital, mixed or unknown views using diﬀerent colors in schematic. The options of this command are described as follows.

![image 7429](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7429.png)

Figure 94.32 Display Partition Form

Partition Name: sets the highlighted color of analog, digital, mixed, unknown views in schematics

- • Analog: the highlighted color of the analog view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.
- • Digital: the highlighted color of the digital view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.
- • Mixed: the highlighted color of the mixed-signal view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.
- • Show View Found: display the text of the found view type in schematics using the selected color. The default mode is checked
- • Unknown: the highlighted color of the unknown view. It can be selected from the drop-down list. The default is checked.


Display Level: hierarchical or leaf instances is considered to highlight if Hierarchical Blocks or Primitives is checked.

- • Hierarchical: if this option is unchecked, the hierarchical instances are ignored, otherwise, the hierarchical instances are highlighted in schematics. The default mode is checked
- • Primitive: if this option is unchecked, the leaf instances are ignored, otherwise, the leaf instances are highlighted in schematics. The default mode is checked


Display IO: whether to highlight nets in schematics

- • Nets: highlights nets in schematic, default mode is checked
- • None: does not highlight nets in schematic, default mode is unchecked


Blink: highlights views and nets under blink mode, and the default mode is unchecked

Zoom To: sets the zoom factor for the highlighted area, the range of this

- option is 1 to 10, default value is 1 Line Width: sets the width of the highlighted lines, and the range of this
- option is 2 to 10, default value is 2 Clear All: clears all highlights in schematics Fit View: zooms to ﬁt for the schematics


Note:This function distinguishes which views are analog or digital or mixed according to the settings of view to use in Aether Sim View Editor

Example 94.5

### 94.5.4 IE Manager

Menu: Mixed-Signal -> IE Manager

![image 7435](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7435.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to add, delete and modify library or cell interface element parameters, the options are shown as follows.

![image 7436](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7436.png)

Figure 94.36 IE Manager Form

Scope: switches library or cell IE. • Library: shows library IE.

- • Cell: shows cell IE, this option is selected by default. Library/Cell IE List: shows library or cell IE parameters.
- • Add: adds current conﬁg library IE parameters or selects cell from Aether Schematic.
- • Delete: deletes IE parameters from the selected in IE List. A2D Parameter: sets a2d device parameter’s values.
- • a2d_tx: delay time before digital state changes to unknown state. The default value is 1m.


- • a2d_v0: The threshold voltage for digital state is 0. The default value=1.5.
- • a2d_v1: The threshold voltage for digital state is 1. The default value=3.5.
- • dynamic_mod: sets a2d dynamic mode value. The default is unchecked.


- – ref_source: sets reference source net. The default value is empty.
- – oﬀ_region: sets Non-operation region. The default value is 0.
- – vh_ratio: sets High threshold radio of ref source. The default value


is 0.5.

– vl_ratio: sets Low threshold radio of ref source. The default value

is 0.3.

D2A Parameter: sets d2a device parameter’s values.

- • d2a_tf: transfer time when digital state changed from 1 to 0. The default value=2n.
- • d2a_tr: transfer time when digital state changed from 0 to 1. The default value=3n.
- • d2a_vh: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is 1. The default value=5.
- • d2a_vl: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is 0. The default value=0.
- • d2a_vx: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is unknown state. The default value is empty.
- • d2a_vz: the stable voltage of analog driver when digital state is high impedance state. The default value is empty.
- • d2a_ron: the output impedance when digital state is 0, 1 or unknown state. The default value=100.
- • d2a_rz: the output impedance when digital state is high impedance state. The default value is empty.
- • d2a_tz: transfer time when digital state changed from 0, 1 or unknown to high impedance state. The default value is empty.
- • dynamic_mod: sets d2a dynamic mode value. The default value is not checked.


– ref_source: sets reference source net. The default value is empty.
