- 5. In the Digital Library Directories(-y) ﬁeld, click button Add, specify the digital library directories, such as ./dir1 ./dir2. Click button Delete, the directory can be deleted.
- 6. In the Digital Library Extension(Only For -y) ﬁeld, specify the digital library extention, such as path.
- 7. In the Digital Library Files(-v) ﬁeld, click button Add, specify the digital library ﬁles, such as ./file1 ./file2. Click button Delete, the ﬁle can be deleted.


![image 7450](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7450.png)

Figure 94.48 Netlist Options Form

- 8. In the Options Files(-f) ﬁeld, click button Add, specify the option ﬁles, such as File1 File2. Click button Delete, the ﬁle can be deleted.
- 9. In the Verilog File Paths(+incdir) ﬁeld, click button Add, specify the verilog ﬁle paths, such as path1 path2. Click button Delete, the path can be deleted.
- 10. Press the Apply or OK button to store the parameters in MDE.
- 11. Click Netlist And Run, the ﬁles and paths in Netlist Options will be added into arguments for Alps simulation. Generate to this section will be shown in Zterm, as follows:


Listing 94.1: Alps Command in ZTerm

|Command Args : alpsMS −y " ./ dir1 " −y " ./ dir2 " +libExt " path " −v " ./ f i l e 1 " −v " ./ f i l e 2 " −f " ./ File1 " −f " ./ File2 " +incdir+" ./ Path1 " +incdir+" ./ Path2 "<br><br>|
|---|


## 94.6 Analysis

### 94.6.1 Add/Modify Analysis

This command make the Add/Modify Analysis form show up. The Add/Modify Analysis works exactly as its counterpart in MDE L2, except that each form belongs to a speciﬁc test.

![image 7451](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7451.png)

Figure 94.49 Add Analysis Form

- 94.6.1.1 TRAN Menu: Analysis -> Add/Modify Analysis -> TRAN


![image 7452](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7452.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

You may use this command to set tran simulation analysis options, and below parameters are necessary to set before running the actual simulation:

![image 7453](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7453.png)

Figure 94.50 Add/Modify Analysis Form - TRAN

Stop: deﬁnes the simulation stop time in seconds, which can be speciﬁed as a parameter or as an expression

Accuracy Level: deﬁnes the simulation accuracy. It has three levels: conservative, moderate and liberal. Where conservative is the most accurate but the slowest, and liberal is the fastest and the least accurate. The default level is moderate.

Transient Noise: deﬁnes noise for transient analysis. Click this checkbox to show more options. As shown below.

![image 7454](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7454.png)

Figure 94.51 Transient Noise Options

- • Noise Fmax: speciﬁes noise fmax.
- • Noise Fmin: speciﬁes noise fmin.
- • Noise Seed: speciﬁes noise seed.
- • Noise Scale: speciﬁes noise scale.
- • Noise Tmin: speciﬁes noise tmin.
- • Noise Update: speciﬁes noise update types.


- • Multiple Runs: speciﬁes the number of parallel processing.
- • Number Of Runs: When Multiple Runs is checked, Number Of Runs is editable.
- • Noise Contribution: speciﬁes noise contribution mode.
- • Instance List: When Noise Contribution is on, Instance List is editable.


Dynamic Parameter: deﬁnes dynamic parameter for transient analysis. Click this checkbox to show more options. As shown below.

![image 7455](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7455.png)

Figure 94.52 Dynamic Parameter Options

• Parameter: chooses this option when only one parameter is to be conﬁgured.

![image 7456](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7456.png)

Figure 94.53 Parameter Option

- – Parameter Name: speciﬁes parameter name, which can be either a built-in parameter (e.g. errpreset, method) or a user-deﬁned parameter.
- – Parameter File: speciﬁes to conﬁgure the dynamic parameter setting through a ﬁle.

![image 7457](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7457.png)

Figure 94.54 Parameter File

- – Parameter Vector: speciﬁes to conﬁgure the dynamic parameter setting by ﬁlling a vector table.


![image 7458](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7458.png)

Figure 94.55 Parameter Vector

• Parameter Set: chooses this option when more than one parameters are to be conﬁgured.

![image 7459](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7459.png)

Figure 94.56 Parameter Set Option

– Add: clicks the Add button to add a parameter into the vector

table.

![image 7460](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7460.png)

Figure 94.57 Parameter Set Vector

Options: deﬁnes settings for more analysis. As shown below.

![image 7461](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7461.png)

Figure 94.58 Time Step Options

- • start: deﬁnes the simulation starting time in seconds. The default value is 0 if this parameter is not deﬁned
- • outputstart: deﬁnes the output time for simulation starting time in seconds. The default value is 0 if this parameter is not deﬁned
- • step: deﬁnes the time increment in seconds for plotting and printing simulation results.


- • maxstep: speciﬁes the max step.
- • minstep: speciﬁes the min step.


Algorithm: deﬁnes settings for large circuits. As shown below.

![image 7462](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7462.png)

Figure 94.59 Algorithm Options

- • ic: speciﬁes ic match analysis types. ic includes four types: dc,node, dev, all.
- • skipdc: speciﬁes skipdc types. skipdc includes two types: yes, no.
- • readic: speciﬁes readic ﬁle.
- • readns: speciﬁes readns ﬁle.
- • cmin: speciﬁes cmin value.
- • method: speciﬁes integration method, integration method includes six types, euler, trap, traponly, gear2, gear2only, trapgear2.
- • relref: speciﬁes accuracy types, accuracy includes four types, pointlocal, alllocal, sigglobal, allglobal.
- • iteratio: speciﬁes iteratio value.
- • maxiters: speciﬁes maxiters value.


State File: speciﬁes state ﬁle to use as an estimate in the next analysis or subsequent simulations. As shown below.

![image 7463](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7463.png)

Figure 94.60 State File

- • write: speciﬁes the write parameter.
- • writeﬁnal: speciﬁes the writeﬁnal parameter.
- • save clock(hour): speciﬁes the saveclock time points to save the state.
- • save period(s): speciﬁes the saveperiod time points to save the state.
- • save time(s): speciﬁes the savetime time points to save the state.
- • save path: speciﬁes the path for save ﬁle.
- • recover path: speciﬁes recover path for spectre simulation.


Output: speciﬁes output message from spectre during generation of log ﬁle. As shown below.

![image 7464](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7464.png)

Figure 94.61 Output

• save: speciﬁes save message types, save includes ﬁve types: selected,

##### lvlpub, lvl, allpub, all.

- • nestlvl: speciﬁes the level of subcircuit to output.
- • Strobing Parameters: speciﬁes parameters for strobing.


- – skipstart: speciﬁes the skipstart time for strobing.
- – skipstop: speciﬁes the skipstop time for strobing.
- – skipcount: speciﬁes the skipcount for strobing.
- – strobeperiod: speciﬁes the strobeperiod for strobing.
- – strobeoutput: speciﬁes the strobeoutput types: none, strobeonly, all.
- – strobedelay: speciﬁes the strobedelay for strobing.


- • Save Final OP Pt: checks this option will save ﬁnal OP point parameter into log ﬁle.
- • Infotimes Settings: speciﬁes the settings of infotimes.


- – infotimes: speciﬁes the times when the analysis speciﬁed by infonames are performed.
- – infotime pair: speciﬁes the correspondence between the values in-


fonames and infotimes. The default value is no.

– infoname: speciﬁes the infonames.

– tran info other params: speciﬁes other parameters of tran infor-

mation.

• ACtimes Settings: speciﬁes the settings of actimes.

– actimes: speciﬁes the times when the analysis speciﬁed by acnames

are performed.

– actime pair: speciﬁes the correspondence between the values ac-

names and actimes. default is no – acnames: speciﬁes the acnames.

Misc: deﬁnes misc settings. As shown below.

![image 7465](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7465.png)

Figure 94.62 Misc

- • annotate: speciﬁes annotate types.
- • additionalparams: speciﬁes the additional parameters for the transient analysis, such as vth=1u.


Enable: speciﬁes the state for analysis. This option will be checked when analysis modiﬁed. If this option is unchecked, the analysis will not run a simulation.

## 94.7 Simulation

### 94.7.1 Job Setup

Menu: Simulation -> Job Setup

![image 7881](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7881.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to specify simulation job mode. To invoke option menu, select Simulation -> Job Setup.

![image 7882](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7882.png)

Figure 94.457 Job Setup Form

Job Policy: speciﬁes whether to run the simulation in Global mode or Tests mode. When Global is selected, this test follows the setup conﬁgured in the Global job setup for simulation; when Tests is chosen, it simulates according to its own job setup.

See Also: Multiple Tests -> Simulation -> Job Setup 93.5.1.

### 94.7.2 Options

Menu: Simulation -> Options

![image 7883](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7883.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to control the accuracy, speed and convergence for Alps or other simulators by setting diﬀerent options. These options are classiﬁed into Algorithm, Component, Check, Annotation, Misc, Netlist and DSPF. To invoke option menu, select Simulation -> Options.

![image 7884](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7884.png)

Figure 94.458 Simulation Options - Main Tab

Main: Tolerance Setting: sets tolerance variable for simulation.

- • reltol: speciﬁes the relative error tolerance for current and voltage from iteration to iteration. The default value is 1e-3.
- • trtol: speciﬁes the value of trtol. The default value is 1e-3.


- • maxvoltage: speciﬁes the value of maxvoltage. The default value is 1e-3.
- • residualtol: speciﬁes the tolerance ratio for multiplies reltol.
- • vabstol: speciﬁes the absolute voltage error tolerance. The default value is 1e-6.
- • iabstol: speciﬁes the absolute current error tolerance. The default value is 1e-12.


Temperature: sets temperature related options.

- • temp: speciﬁes the value of temperature. The value is synchronize with the main form setting.
- • tnom: this option is used to set the model reference temperature. The default value is 27.
- • tempeﬀects: speciﬁes the value of tempeﬀects. Possible values are vt,


##### tc and all. Noise Options: sets noise options.

- • Noise Contribution: speciﬁes the value of noise contribution. Possible values are on and oﬀ. One of them is checked, Instance List can be speciﬁed, otherwise, it can not be speciﬁed.
- • Instance List: speciﬁes the value of instances.
- • Select: clicks Select button, it is easy to select instances from schematic.
- • Clear: clicks Clear button, the instances in Instance List will be cleared.
- • noiseon_type: speciﬁes the value of noiseon_type. Possible values are thermal, ﬂicker, shot, ign and all.
- • noiseoﬀ_type: speciﬁes the value of noiseoﬀ_type. Possible values are thermal, ﬂicker, shot, ign and all.


##### Algorithm:

![image 7885](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7885.png)

Figure 94.459 Simulation Options - Algorithm Tab

Convergence Options: speciﬁes values of convergence options.

- • homotopy: the homotopy method for solving convergence problems. Possible methods are gmin, source, dptran, ptran. If you select one of the above methods, the simulator will try this method directly. If a user selects none, the simulator will try without method directly. If a user selects All, the simulator tries all above methods one by one until a DC solution is found. The order is none, gmin, source, dptran, ptran, all.
- • limit: speciﬁes the value of limit. Possible values are delta, log, dev.
- • gmethod: speciﬁes the value of gmethod. Possible values are dev, node, both.
- • dptran_gmethod: speciﬁes the value of dptran_gmethod. Possible values are dev, node, both.
- • try_fast_op: speciﬁes the value of try_fast_op. Possible values are yes and no.
- • convdbg: speciﬁes the value of convdbg. Possible values are none, status and detailed.
- • icpriority: speciﬁes the value of icpriority. Possible value are netlist and ﬁle.
- • nonconv_topnum: speciﬁes the value of nonconv_topnum.


- • gmin: speciﬁes the value of gmin.
- • gmin_check: speciﬁes the value of gmin_check. Possible value are no, max_v_only, max_only and all.
- • gmindc: speciﬁes the value of gmindc.
- • gshunt: speciﬁes the value of gshunt.
- • rforce: speciﬁes the value of rforce. The default value is 1.
- • rthresh: speciﬁes the value of rthresh.
- • rabsclamp: speciﬁes the value of rabsclamp.
- • rclamp: speciﬁes the value of rclamp.
- • rabsshort: speciﬁes the value of rabsshort.


Maxtrix Parameter Options: speciﬁes values of maxtrix parameter options.

- • pivotdc: speciﬁes the value of pivotdc. Possible values are yes and no.
- • dc_pivot_check: speciﬁes the value of dc_pivot_check. Possible values are yes and no.
- • pivrel: speciﬁes the value of pivrel. The default value is 1e-3.
- • pivabs: speciﬁes the value of pivabs.
- • preorder: speciﬁes the value of preorder. Possible values are partial and full.
- • rebuild_matrix: speciﬁes the value of rebuild_matrix. Possible values are yes and no.


##### Component:

![image 7886](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7886.png)

Figure 94.460 Simulation Options - Component Tab

Component Options: speciﬁes values of component options.

- • scalm: speciﬁes the model scaling factor. The default value is 1.0.
- • scale: speciﬁes the instance scaling factor. The default value is 1.0.
- • scalefactor: speciﬁes the value of scalefactor.
- • approx: speciﬁes to use approx models. Possible values are yes and no.
- • macromodels: speciﬁes the value of macromodels. Possible values are yes and no.
- • maxrsd: speciﬁes the value of maxrsd.
- • auto_minductor: speciﬁes the value of auto_minductor. Possible values are yes and no.
- • minr: speciﬁes the value of minr.


Nport Options: speciﬁes values of nport options.

- • nportirreuse: speciﬁes the value of nportirreuse. Possible values are yes and no.
- • nportirﬁledir: speciﬁes the ﬁle directory of nportir.
- • nportcompress: speciﬁes the value of nportcompress. Possible values are yes and no.
- • nportcompressﬁledir: speciﬁes the ﬁle directory of nportcompress.


- • nportunusedportgmin: speciﬁes the value of nportunusedportgmin.
- • nportunusedportrmin: speciﬁes the value of nportunusedportrmin.
- • nport_default_interp: speciﬁes the value of nport_default_interp. Possible values are auto_switch, spline, linear, bbspice.


Model Options: speciﬁes values of model options.

- • vthmod: speciﬁes the value of vthmod. Possible values are std and vthcc.
- • ivthn: speciﬁes the value of ivthn when the vthcc is checked.
- • ivthp: speciﬁes the value of ivthp when thevthcc is checked.
- • ivthw: speciﬁes the value of ivthw when the vthcc is checked.
- • ivthl: speciﬁes the value of ivthl when the vthcc is checked.
- • ivth_vdsmin: speciﬁes the value of ivthl_vdsmin when the vthcc is checked.
- • tmevthmod: speciﬁes the value of tmevthmod. Possible values are 0 and 1


##### Check:

![image 7887](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7887.png)

Figure 94.461 Simulation Options - Check Tab

Error Checking Options: speciﬁes values of error checking options.

- • topcheck: speciﬁes the topology check for circuit. Possible values are no, min, full, ﬁxall.
- • iccapcheck: speciﬁes the iccapcheck. Possible values are yes and no.
- • ignshorts: speciﬁes the check try to ignore shorted components . Possible values are yes and no.
- • diagnose: speciﬁes the value of diagnose. Possible values are yes, no, detailed.


- • redeﬁnedparams: speciﬁes the value of redeﬁnedparams. Possible values are error, ignore, warning.


Device Checking Options: speciﬁes values of device checking options.

- • dochecklimit: speciﬁes the value of check device. Possible values are yes and no.
- • checklimitﬁle: speciﬁes the ﬁle of check device.
- • checklimitdest: speciﬁes the value of checklimitdest. Possible values are ﬁle, psf and both. The default value is psf.
- • checklimitskipsubs: speciﬁes the value of checklimitskipsubs.
- • checklimitskipﬁle: speciﬁes the value of checklimitskipﬁle.
- • opptcheck: speciﬁes check operating point parameters against soft limits. Possible values are yes and no.


##### Annotation:

![image 7888](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7888.png)

Figure 94.462 Simulation Options - Annotation Tab

Annotate Options: speciﬁes values of annotate options.

- • audit: speciﬁes the extent about the various part of the simulation time to be returned. Possible values are no, brief and detailed.
- • inventory: speciﬁes the extent about the simulation components to be returned. Possible values are no, brief and detailed.
- • narrate: speciﬁes narrate to the simulations. Possible values are yes and no.
- • debug: speciﬁes debuggging information to be printed. Possible values are yes and no.


##### Misc:

- • info: speciﬁes information messages to be printed. Possible values are yes and no.
- • note: speciﬁes notice messages to be printed. Possible values are yes and no.
- • maxnotes: speciﬁes the max value of times per analysis issue particular notice. The default value is 5.
- • warn: speciﬁes warning messages to be printed. Possible values are yes and no.
- • maxwarns: speciﬁes the max value of times per analysis issue particular warning. The default value is 5.
- • maxwarnstologﬁle: speciﬁes the value of maxwarnstologﬁle.
- • maxbnotestologﬁle: speciﬁes the value of maxwarnstologﬁle.
- • error: speciﬁes error messages to be printed. Possible values are yes and no.
- • printstep: speciﬁes the step to print. Possible values are yes and no.
- • digits: speciﬁes the value of digits. The default value is 5.
- • notation: speciﬁes the notation to be used. Possible values are sci, ﬂoat, eng.
- • cols: speciﬁes the value of cols. The default value is 80.
- • colslog: speciﬁes the value of colslog.
- • title: speciﬁes the value of title.


![image 7889](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7889.png)

Figure 94.463 Simulation Options - Misc Tab

Quantity Options: speciﬁes values of quantity options.

- • value: speciﬁes the value of quantity.


- • ﬂow: speciﬁes the ﬂow of quantity.
- • quantities: speciﬁes the quantities information extent to be returned. Possible values are min, full and no.


print statistics report: speciﬁes the statistics report to be print. Possible values are basic and detailed.

Sensitivity Options: speciﬁes values of sensitivity options.

sensﬁle: speciﬁes the value of sensﬁle. The default value is “../psf/sens.output” .

sensformat: speciﬁes the value of sensformat. Possible values are tabular and list.

senstype: speciﬁes the value of senstype. Possible values are partial and normalized.

sensﬁleonly: speciﬁes the value of sensﬁleonly. Possible values are yes and no.

sensbinparam: speciﬁes the value of sensbinparam. Possible values are no, uncorrelated and correlated.

Other Options: speciﬁes values of other options.

- • Additional Arguments: speciﬁes the value of additional arguments.

of Alps. Netlist:

##### DSPF:

![image 7891](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7891.png)

Figure 94.465 Simulation Options - DSPF Tab

Convert SP File With DSPF Map File: checks this option which will convert sp ﬁle with dspf map ﬁle. The default value is not checked.

TermDelimiter: speciﬁes the term delimiter in dspf map. The default value is :.

HierDelimiter: speciﬁes the hierarchy delimiter in dspf map. The default value is /.

FingerDelimiter: speciﬁes the ﬁnger delimiter in dspf map. The default value is @.

BusDelimiter: speciﬁes the bus delimiter in dspf map. The default value is <>.

DeviceDefaultPreﬁx: speciﬁes the device default preﬁx in dspf map. DevicePreﬁxForTermCurrent: speciﬁes the device preﬁx for term current in dspf map. AddTermCurrentPreﬁx: speciﬁes whether to output the device preﬁx for diﬀerent devices.

MOS: checks this option which will output the device preﬁx for MOS.The default value is checked.

Diod: checks this option which will output the device preﬁx for Diod.The default value is checked.

Cap: checks this option which will output the device preﬁx for Cap.The default value is checked.

Bjt: checks this option which will output the device preﬁx for Bjt.The default value is checked.

Ind: checks this option which will output the device preﬁx for Ind.The default value is checked.

Res: checks this option which will output the device preﬁx for Res.The default value is checked.

AddPreﬁxForMOS: speciﬁes the preﬁx for MOS in dspf map. AddPreﬁxForDiod: speciﬁes the preﬁx for Diod in dspf map. AddPreﬁxForCap: speciﬁes the preﬁx for Cap in dspf map. AddPreﬁxForBjt: speciﬁes the preﬁx for Bjt in dspf map. AddPreﬁxForInd: speciﬁes the preﬁx for Ind in dspf map. AddPreﬁxForRes: speciﬁes the preﬁx for Res in dspf map. Delete Device Preﬁx For Top Devices: checks this optin which will not output the preﬁx for devices in top cell. The default value is not checked.

: clicks this button to save dspf map ﬁle from DSPF tab. : clicks this button to load dspf map in the txt ﬁle into DSPF tab.

- 94.7.9 Run Monte Carlo Menu: Simulation -> Run Monte Carlo


![image 7913](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7913.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to run Monte Carlo simulation.

![image 7914](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7914.png)

Figure 94.476 Run Monte Carlo Form

Statistical Variation: deﬁnes statistical variation, to be used with a Monte Carlo analysis.

- • Process: speciﬁes the input process statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • Mismatch: speciﬁes the input mismatch statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.
- • All: speciﬁes both process and mismatch statistical variations for Monte Carlo analysis.


Sampling Method: speciﬁes the method of statistical sampling to apply.

- • Random: generates statistical variation random numbers that according to the speciﬁed distributions.
- • LHS: generates statistical variation using Latin Hypercube Sampling(LHS). When this option is selected, the Number Of Bins is enabled.
- • LDS: generates statistical variation using Latin Discrepancy Sampling(LDS).


Number Of Points: sets the number of Monte Carlo points you want to simulate. The minimum value is 1, default is 10.

Number Of Bins: sets the number of bins (subdivisions) in the text ﬁeld for LHS method. The minimum value is 1, default is 10.

Monte Carlo Seed: sets the seed for the Monte Carlo analysis. The minimum value is 1, default is 12345.

First Point: sets the ﬁrst point for the Monte Carlo analysis. The minimum value is 1, default is 1.

Netlist Options: sets the netlist options for the Monte Carlo analysis. The default value is empty.

Save Simulation Data: whether to save simulation directory for the Monte Carlo analysis. If the checkbox is checked, save the simulation directory, otherwise delete simulation dirctory. The default value is not checked.

Save Statistical Data: whether to save montecarlo directory for the Monte Carlo analysis. If the checkbox is checked, save the montecarlo directory, otherwise delete montecarlo dirctory. The default value is not checked.

##### Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo(Unspeciﬁed): clicks this button to show the form Specify Instances Of Monte Carlo.

Default: clicks this Default button, the form will reload the default settings. OK: clicks this OK button, the operation will be saved and executed. Cancel: clicks this Cancel button, the operation will be canceled and the form escapes at the same time.

Selected: speciﬁes the value for Selected, the default value is Process. Unselected: speciﬁes the value for Unselected, the default value is Process. Test: shows the name of test. Instances Speciﬁcation: speciﬁes instances from schematic or subcircuit.

ton to select instances from schematic.

- – Select List: shows all instances in the Cell. Default: clicks this Default button, the form will reload the default settings. OK: clicks this OK button, the operation will execute. Cancel: clicks this Cancel button, the operation will be canceled and the form escapes at the same time.

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This form is used to conﬁgure simulation options. To invoke option form, select Outputs -> Save Options.

![image 7943](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7943.png)

Figure 94.498 Save Options Form

Basic: speciﬁes basic options.

- • save: this option is used to generate voltage information ﬁles. The default value is allpub checked.
- • pwr: this option is used to generate power information ﬁles. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • nestlvl: this option is used to set the number of stages of the output subckt. This options is valid when save is lvlpub or lvl. The default value is empty.
- • currents: this option is used to generate currents information ﬁles. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • useprobes: this option is used to select AC terminal currents. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • subcktprobelvl: this option is used to control up to how many levels deep will current probes be added to subcircuits.
- • saveahdlvars: this option is used to select AHDL variables. The default value is no checkbox checked.
- • Circuit Options: speciﬁes circuit options for output. The default values are modelParameter, element, designParamVals, subckts and < Click To Add > . Click < Click To Add > to add a row. Popup constext menu and click the Delete action to delete the selected rows.


- – Name: speciﬁes name value.
- – What: speciﬁes what value. The values of this option are none, inst, models, parameters, subckts and oppoint. The default value is none.
- – Where: speciﬁes where value. The values of this option are file, logfile, nowhere and rawfile. The default value is rawfile.
- – File: speciﬁes ﬁle. The default value is empty.
- – Extremes: speciﬁes extreme value. The values of this option are no, yes and only.
- – Others: speciﬁes other value. The default value is empty.
- – Enabled: speciﬁes whether the row is enabled. If Enabled is


checked, the row is enabled.

• Output Options: speciﬁes options for output.

– Output Format: speciﬁes the format of output. The default value

##### is ps.

Save By Subckt: speciﬁes subckt options.

![image 7944](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile7944.png)

Figure 94.499 Save By Subckt

- • Subckts: speciﬁes information.


- – Instance: selects a subckt.


- – V[depth]: speciﬁes voltage depth. The default value is empty and checked.
- – I[depth]: speciﬁes current depth. The default value is empty and unchecked.
- – Pwr[depth]: speciﬁes power depth. The default value is empty and unchecked.
- – Compress: speciﬁes whether compression is enabled. The default value is unchecked.
- – Filter RC: speciﬁes whether the ﬁlter is rc. The default value is unchecked.
- – Ports: speciﬁes whether ports is enabled. The default value is unchecked.
- – Exclude: speciﬁes exclude value. The default value is empty and unchecked.
- – Sigtype: speciﬁes sigtype. The values of this option are node, dev, subckt and all. The default value is all.
- – User Options: speciﬁes user options. The default value is empty.


- • Add: the button can add a row.
- • Delete: the button can delete selected rows.

Paths/Files: speciﬁes the search paths and include ﬁles.

- • Include Paths: speciﬁes the search path for all include ﬁles of the analog simulator. It will create a .option search statement in spice top netlist.
- • Include Simulation Files: includes the contents of another ﬁle into current netlist. .inc is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in spice top netlist.
- • Include Digital Files: includes the content of another digital ﬁle into current netlist. .include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in top verilog.
- • Include Pspice Files: includes the content of another pspice ﬁle into current netlist. pspice_include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in current netlist.
- • Include DSPF Files: includes the content of another DSPF ﬁle into current netlist. dspf_include is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in current netlist.


– DSPF Options: speciﬁes the dspf ﬁles options.

∗ Port Order: speciﬁes the port order of dspf ﬁles. sch means take the port order from pre-layout schematic netlist, spf means

take the port order from dspf ﬁle deﬁnition.

∗ Extra Port: speciﬁes the extra port of dspf ﬁles. true means extra ports in dspf ﬁle will change to inner nodes, false means the port number in dspf ﬁle and schematic is same.

∗ Case Sensitivity: speciﬁes the case sensitivity of dspf ﬁles. true means the dspf ﬁle is case-sensitive, false means the dspf ﬁles is case insensitive.

∗ Black Box: speciﬁes the instances which to be considered as

blackboxes. Click Select button to choose black box in schematic. ∗ Bus Delimiter: speciﬁes the bus delimiter of dspf ﬁles to map

with schematic. ∗ Other Options: speciﬁes any dspf_include options that are

not supported in this form of dspf ﬁles. Vector Files: speciﬁes the content of vector ﬁles.

• Include Vector Files: includes the content of another vector ﬁle into current netlist. .vec is used as an abbreviation of suﬃx for the simulation statement in spice top netlist.

This command is used to set up multi-technology simulation. In order to run a simulation in multi-technology mode, the design must include a top-level conﬁguration view, which enables the conﬁguration of MTS blocks via the SimView Editor.

Enable Local Scope Models And Options(MTS): Used to open the settings for MTS, it enables the user to conﬁgure MTS blocks and model ﬁles.

Only Show MTS Blocks: Used to ﬁlter the enabled MTS blocks. Filter/Reset: Used to ﬁlter the MTS blocks by library name and cell name.

- • Library ﬁlter: Speciﬁes the library name for ﬁltering, with support for wildcard matching.
- • Cell ﬁlter: Speciﬁes the cell name for ﬁltering, with support for wildcard matching.
- • Filter: Filters both the cell table and the instance tree based on the speciﬁed library and cell names.
- • Reset: Resets the ﬁltering content for both the cell table and the instance tree.


Cell Table: shows all cells in this table.

- • Info: Used to support additional information related to the design.
- • Library: shows library name of instance in this column.
- • Cell: shows cell name of instance in this column.
- • MTS: Used to set the block as an MTS block.
- • Models: Used to set the model ﬁle for the MTS blocks.
- • scale: Used to set the scale for the MTS blocks.
- • scalem: Used to set the scalem for the MTS blocks.


- • temp: Used to set the temp for the MTS blocks.
- • tnom: Used to set the tnom ﬁle for the MTS blocks.
- • other: Used to set the other variables for the MTS blocks.


![image 8055](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8055.png)

Figure 95.10 MTS Options Instance Tree

Instance Tree: shows all instances in this tree.

- • Instance: shows instances name in this column.
- • MTS: Used to set the block as an MTS block.
- • Models: Used to set the model ﬁle for the MTS blocks.
- • scale: Used to set the scale for the MTS blocks.
- • scalem: Used to set the scalem for the MTS blocks.
- • temp: Used to set the temp for the MTS blocks.
- • tnom: Used to set the tnom ﬁle for the MTS blocks.
- • other: Used to set the other variables for the MTS blocks.

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to set up sweep parameters for simulation. You can display the sweep parameter form by right-clicking the Parameters pane, as shown in the ﬁgure below:

![image 8079](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8079.png)

Figure 95.24 Sweep Parameter by Right-clicking

The Sweep Parameter Form displayed, as shown in the ﬁgure below:

![image 8080](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8080.png)

Figure 95.25 Sweep Parameter Form

##### Range Type: speciﬁes a range type. It includes four types: Start-Stop, Center-Span, Center-Span% and Add Speciﬁc Points.

Start-Stop: speciﬁes start and stop of sweep values, both of them are used together to specify sweep limits.

Center-Span: speciﬁes center and span of sweep, both of them are used together to specify sweep limits. The calculation formula is as follows,

center − 0.5 ∗ span,center + 0.5 ∗ span

Center-Span%: speciﬁes center and span of sweep, both of them are used together to specify sweep limits. The calculation formula is as follows,

center − 0.5 ∗ span% ∗ center,center + 0.5 ∗ span% ∗ center

##### Add Speciﬁc Points: speciﬁes values only by Inclusion List and Exclusion List.

Step Mode: speciﬁes a step mode to check analysis point information. It includes seven modes: Auto, Linear Steps, Linear, Decade, Octave, Logarithmic, Times.

Table 95.1 The Formula Illustrations of Step Modes

|Step Mode<br><br>|Title For Setting|Formula|
|---|---|---|


|Auto<br><br>|Total Steps|![image 8081](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8081.png)|
|---|---|---|
|Linear Steps|Step Size|f(n)=f(n-1)+$step_size|
|Linear|Total Steps<br><br>|f(n)= ($stop-$start)/($steps-1)+f(n-1)|
|Decade|Steps/Decade<br><br>|![image 8082](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8082.png)|
|Octave|Steps/Octave|![image 8083](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8083.png)|


|Logarithmic<br><br>|Total Steps|![image 8084](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8084.png)|
|---|---|---|
|Times<br><br>|Multiplier<br><br>|f(n)=$multiplier* f(n-1)|


||Note: Both $start and $stop are the starting value and the termination value of the actual value range.|
|---|
|
|---|


Inclusion List: this input box is used to add additional analysis points, which can be outside or inside the range of sweep point.

Exclusion List: this input box is used to skip the speciﬁed analysis points. If you keep the default value is empty, it will not skip any analysis points.

##### 95.1.1.4 Corner Setup

This section describes the "Corner Setup" panel inside the "Tests" panel.

Each test has its own corner setup table. In order to measure the performance of the design, designer needs to deﬁne more case scenario. A case scenario contains parameters, temperatures, model sections and so on. A scenario is also named corner. This command is used to create corners, modify values, change corners name and disable some corners.

##### Corner Setup

![image 8093](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8093.png)

Figure 95.32 Corner Setup Form

Corner Setup Table: shows corners information.

- • Corners: speciﬁes corner name in top row. You can modify corner name. Allow to add or delete model ﬁles in corner setup form. You can check corner to enable it or uncheck to disable it. MDE Platform does not simulate the disabled corner.
- • Model Files: speciﬁes sections of model ﬁle. You can check section to enable it and uncheck to disable it.
- • Add...: clicks it to show Model Files Setup form.


Model Files Setup form is used to manage model ﬁles for corners. Through this form is easy to add model ﬁles, delete model ﬁles, move model ﬁles and so on.

##### 95.1.2.3 Corner Setup

This section describes the "Corner Setup" panel inside the "Global" panel.

All the tests are shown in the global corner setup table. In order to measure the performance of the design, designer needs to deﬁne more case scenario. A case scenario contains parameters, temperatures, model sections and so on. A scenario is also named corner. This command is used to create corners, modify values, change corners name and disable some corners. Each test can enable or disable the Nominal and other corners.

##### Corner Setup

![image 8148](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8148.png)

Figure 95.62 Corner Setup Form

Corner Setup Table: shows corners information.

- • Corners: speciﬁes corner name in top row. You can modify corner name. Allow to add or delete model ﬁles in corner setup form. You can check corner to enable it or uncheck to disable it. MDE Platform does not simulate the disabled corner.
- • Model Files: speciﬁes sections of model ﬁle. You can check section to enable it and uncheck to disable it.
- • Add...: clicks it to show Model Files Setup form.


Model Files Setup form is used to manage model ﬁles for corners. Through this form is easy to add model ﬁles, delete model ﬁles, move model ﬁles and so on.

![image 8149](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8149.png)

Figure 95.63 Model Files Setup Form

Model Files Setup Table: shows model ﬁles. : clicks it to move model ﬁle top. : clicks it to move model ﬁle up. : clicks it to move model ﬁle down. : clicks it to move model ﬁle bottom.

![image 8150](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8150.png)

![image 8151](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8151.png)

![image 8152](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8152.png)

![image 8153](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8153.png)

Import: clicks it to import model ﬁles from MDE Platform main window.

Add: clicks it to add new model ﬁle. Delete: clicks it to delete model ﬁle. Help: clicks it to show the manual. Apply: clicks it to make eﬀective without close form. OK: clicks it to make eﬀective and close form. Cancel: clicks it to close form and nothing changed.

- • Parameters: speciﬁes value of parameter. Allow to add or delete parameter in corner setup form. If you uncheck it, MDEL Platform takes nominal value.
- • Add...: clicks it to add parameter. Clicks it twice to open the variable list, where the Parameter Filter is located in the ﬁrst row for ﬁltering variables. Parameter Filter is used to ﬁlter variables and record search history.

![image 8154](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8154.png)

Figure 95.64 Parameter Filter

- • Temperature: speciﬁes temperature.


- • Tests: shows the multi-tests’ checkstate to the Nominal or other Corners.
- • Number Of Corners: shows number of corners in the column. : clicks it to save the corners table as a csv ﬁle. : clicks it to load the corners table form the csv ﬁle. : clicks it to add new corner. : clicks it to delete the selected corner. : clicks it to save the changes of the corner table. : clicks it to discard the changes of the corner table.

### 95.1.4 Results

##### 95.1.4.1 Show Log File

Menu: Context menu -> Show Log File ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 8246](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8246.png)

This command opens the Log File Viewer to display the simulation log. If users attempt to open the same ﬁle multiple times, only one instance of the viewer will be opened.

The Log File Viewer is activated under the following circumstances:

- • Right-click in Results Table: When a cell in the Results table, which is in either Detail or Transpose view mode, is right-clicked and one of the options Show Log File, Show Job Submission Log File, Show SP File, or Show Netlist Log File is selected.
- • Menu Selections: When the menu items Simulation -> Netlist -> Create/Display or right-clicking on a test and selecting Netlist -> Create/Display are chosen.
- • Automatic Display on Run Start: The viewer automatically pops up when starting a run, displaying the simulator log ﬁle for the current run’s unique simulation point.


Figure 95.129 Log File Viewer

Window title: the title displays the path of the log ﬁle. Menu Bar: contains four menus: File, Edit, View, and Help. File: this menu includes options for managing log.

- • Save As...: this option allows users to save the current log information displayed in the viewer to an external ﬁle.
- • Auto Update On/Oﬀ: when Auto Update is On, the log ﬁle content will be refreshed in real-time as the simulation progresses.
- • Close Window: this command closes the current window, having the


same eﬀect as clicking the "X" button on the Log File Viewer’s title bar. Edit: this menu includes options for editing the log ﬁle content

- • Copy: allows users to copy the selected text within the log ﬁle display area to the clipboard.
- • Select All: selects all the content currently visible in the log ﬁle display area.
- • Find: enables searching for a speciﬁc string within the current ﬁle. This function can be accessed via the shortcut Ctrl+F.


Figure 95.130 Log File Viewer - Find

- • Go To Line: prompts the user to enter a line number, jumping to that line upon clicking Apply. This function can be accessed via the shortcut Ctrl+G.


![image 8249](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8249.png)

Figure 95.131 Log File Viewer - Go To Line

View: this menu includes options for viewing settings.

• Highlight Current Line: this option has a checkbox preceding it . When checked, the current line in the log ﬁle is highlighted.

Figure 95.132 Log File Viewer - Highlight Current Line

• Show Line Number: also preceded by a checkbox. When checked, line numbers are displayed to the left of the log ﬁle content, assisting in navigation.

Help: clicking this item opens the manual for the Log File Viewer, providing detailed guidance on its use.

##### Log Information Display Area: this area displays log information.

- • Scrolling Support: if the content of the log ﬁle exceeds the visible display area, horizontal or vertical scroll bars are automatically added as necessary.
- • Syntax Highlighting: to enhance readability and understanding, the display area supports syntax highlighting for various types of log entries.
- • Hyperlinked Directory Paths: critical directory paths within the log text are rendered as clickable hyperlinks.


Example 95.33

The following example shows how clicking on hyperlinked directory paths within the Log File Viewer can perform one of two actions:

1. Open the corresponding log ﬁle in a new Log File Viewer instance.

Figure 95.133 Clicking on line number link of ﬁle opens it in a new Log File Viewer window

2. Open a terminal window at the speciﬁed path.

![image 8252](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8252.png)

Figure 95.134 Clicking on a directory path link opens a terminal window at that location

##### 95.1.4.2 Show Job Submission Log File

Menu: Context menu -> Show Job Submission Log File ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 8253](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8253.png)

This command opens the job submission log with Log File Viewer. A job submission log is created every time a simulation job is submitted to the LSF, OGE or DONAU distributor. The log ﬁle shows the command of the submission and its exit code. It can be used as a debugging clue when a simulation fails.

![image 8254](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8254.png)

Figure 95.135 Show Job Submission Log File

∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for Current function.Select item in harmonic number table.

- – Power: selects the Power function type of the ENVLP analysis.


![image 8880](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8880.png)

Figure 95.759 Main Form - Power - Function

![image 8881](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8881.png)

Figure 95.760 Select

∗ Select: speciﬁes select mode for Power function. ∗ Modiﬁer: speciﬁes modiﬁer for Power function. · Magnitude: selects magnitude of modiﬁer. · dB10: selects dB10 of modiﬁer. · dBm: selects dBm of modiﬁer.

∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for Power function. Select item in harmonic number table.

- – ACPR: selects the ACPR function type of the ENVLP analysis.


![image 8882](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8882.png)

Figure 95.761 Main Form - ACPR - Function

![image 8883](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8883.png)

Figure 95.762 Select

∗ Select: speciﬁes select mode for ACPR function. ∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for ACPR func-

tion. Select item in harmonic number table. ∗ Method: speciﬁes method type for ACPR function.

· Power: selects power of method type. · Power Density: selects power density of method type.

∗ Channel Deﬁnitions(Default Custom): speciﬁes channel definitions for ACPR function.

∗ Main Channel Width: speciﬁes main channel width for ACPR function.

∗ Add: appends the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) in the text boxes into the table above.

∗ Modify: modiﬁes the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) of the selected record in the table and update it with the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) in the text boxes.

∗ Delete: deletes the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) currently selected in the table.

∗ From: speciﬁes the lower bound of the ﬁltering range for ACPR function.

∗ To: speciﬁes the upper bound of the ﬁltering range for ACPR

function. ∗ Strobe Period: speciﬁes strobe period for ACPR function. ∗ Window Size: speciﬁes window size for ACPR function. De-

fault is 64. ∗ Repetitions: speciﬁes repetitions for ACPR function. Default is 2. ∗ Resolutions BandWidth: speciﬁes resolutions bandwidth for ACPR function. ∗ Windowing(Default Rectangle): speciﬁes windowing for ACPR function.

- – Main Channel Power: selects the Main Channel Power function type of the ENVLP analysis.


![image 8884](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8884.png)

Figure 95.763 Main Form - Main Channel Power - Function

![image 8885](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile8885.png)

Figure 95.764 Select

∗ Select: speciﬁes select mode for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Harmonic Number: speciﬁes harmonic number for Main Chan-

nel Power function. Select item in harmonic number table. ∗ Main Channel Width: speciﬁes main channel width for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Reference Resistor: speciﬁes reference resistor for Main Channel Power function. Default is 50. ∗ From: speciﬁes the lower bound of the ﬁltering range for Main Channel Power function. ∗ To: speciﬁes the upper bound of the ﬁltering range for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Strobe Period: speciﬁes strobe period for Main Channel Power function. ∗ Window Size: speciﬁes window size for Main Channel Power function. Default is 64. ∗ Repetitions: speciﬁes repetitions for Main Channel Power function. Default is 2. ∗ Resolutions BandWidth: speciﬁes resolutions bandwidth for

Main Channel Power function. ∗ Windowing(Default Rectangle): speciﬁes windowing for Main Channel Power function.

– Rms Voltage: selects the Rms Voltage function type of the ENVLP

analysis.

- 95.1.4.6.10 NOISE Summary Menu: Context menu -> Print -> NOISE Summary


![image 9050](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9050.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to print the NOISE Summary, which support NOISE/PNOSIE/HBNOISE analysis.

![image 9051](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9051.png)

Figure 95.893 NOISE Summary Form

Data From: speciﬁes the simulation data. Type: deﬁnes the method of computing noise.

• Spot Noise: selects this option, it will use the given frequency to computing noise.

![image 9052](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9052.png)

Figure 95.894 Spot Noise

– Frequency Spot(Hz): speciﬁes the frequency of Spot Noise. • Integrated Noise: selects this option, it will produce a noise summary

integrated over a frequency range.

![image 9053](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9053.png)

Figure 95.895 Integrated Noise

- – From(Hz): speciﬁes the starting value of Integrated Noise.
- – To(Hz): speciﬁes the ending value of Integrated Noise.


Noise Unit: speciﬁes the unit for this noise summary.

- • V^2: speciﬁes noise summary unit as V^2.
- • V: speciﬁes noise summary unit as V.


Hierarchy Level: selects the hierarchy level from the drop-down list, the device from top level to hierarchy level will be computed. Changes the hierarchy level, all the device types from top level to hierarchy level will be listed in the list box, you can select these types by Shift or Ctrl. The default is empty.

Select All: selects all the device types in the list box below. Select None: deselects all the device types in the list box below. Include Instances: lists instances to include.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to include from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all include instances.


Exclude Instances: lists instances to exclude.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to exclude from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all exclude instances.


Truncate: limits the number of devices in the noise summary according to noise contribution, the default is By Number.

- • None: selects this option, it will no limit for noise summary.

![image 9054](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9054.png)

Figure 95.896 Truncate - None

- • By Number: selects this option, only shows the Top number of the highest noise contribution in the noise summary.

![image 9055](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9055.png)

Figure 95.897 Truncate - By Number

– Top: sets the value of Top, the default value is 3.

- • By Relative Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices which the percentage of noise contribution is greater than Noise%.


![image 9056](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9056.png)

Figure 95.898 Truncate - By Relative Threshold

##### – Noise%: sets the value of By Relative Threshold, the default

value is 50.

- • By Absolute Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices which the noise contribution is greater than Noise Value.


![image 9057](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9057.png)

Figure 95.899 Truncate - By Absolute Threshold

##### – Noise Value: sets the value of By Absolute threshold, the de-

fault value is 0.

Sort By: deﬁnes the order of the noise summary, the default is Noise Contribution.

- • Noise Contribution: sorts by the noise contribution from large to small.
- • Composite Noise: sorts by the total noise contribution of each device from large to small. The same device is in the same group.
- • Device Name: sorts by ASCII of the each device name. The same device is in the same group.


Consolidate Iterated Instances: checks this option which will combine the noise contributions of iterated instances to one.

Suﬃx Notation: checks this option which will convert scientiﬁc notaion to suﬃx notaion.

Absolute Noise Precision: sets absolute noise precision, the default is 6. Relative Noise Precision: sets relative noise precision, the default is 2.

Parametric Variable: selects a sweep variable combination. This table only appears when PSS analysis has Sweep checked or HB analysis has Sweep/Loadpull checked.

Example 95.71

This example shows how to print NOISE Summary by Context menu -> Print -> NOISE Summary.

- 1. Set NOISE analysis, as follows:


![image 9058](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9058.png)

- Figure 95.900 NOISE Analysis Setting
- 2. Click Netlist And Run to run simulation.
- 3. After simulation, invoke Context menu -> Print -> NOISE Summary.


![image 9059](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9059.png)

Figure 95.901 NOISE Summary

- 4. The default value of Type is Spot Noise and the default value of Frequency Spot(Hz) is the value of At Frequency in NOISE analysis. When Sweep Variable in NOISE analysis is not Frequency, Type and Frequency Spot(Hz) are not allowed to modify. VDD is the Variable Name in NOISE analysis and its default value is the minimum value of Sweep Range.
- 5. Specify the Hierarchy Level to 1, the types of all devices in layer 0~1 will be displayed in the list box. Click Select All to select all types in the list box. Set the Inlucde Instances and Exclude Instances list (Wildcards are supported).

![image 9060](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9060.png)

Figure 95.902 NOISE Summary - Filter

- 6. Select None from Truncate drop-down list, and check Noise Contribution.


![image 9061](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9061.png)

Figure 95.903 NOISE Summary - Truncate And Sort

- 7. Click Apply, the noise summary information appears as follows:

![image 9062](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9062.png)

Figure 95.904 Simulation Results - Noise Contribution

- 8. Check Composite Noise, and click Apply, the noise summary information appears as follows:


![image 9063](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9063.png)

Figure 95.905 Simulation Results - Composite Noise

- 9. Check Device Name, and click Apply, the noise summary information appears as follows:


![image 9064](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9064.png)

Figure 95.906 Simulation Results - Device Name

##### 10. Check Noise Contribution, Composite Noise, Consolidate Iterated In-stances and Suﬃx Notation. Set Absolute Noise Precision to 4 and setRelative Noise Precision to 3. Click Apply, the noise summary informa-tion appears as follows:

![image 9065](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9065.png)

Figure 95.907 Simulation Results - Noise Contribution and Composite Noise

- 95.1.4.6.11 DCMATCH Summary Menu: Context menu -> Print -> DCMATCH Summary


![image 9066](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9066.png)

ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

This command is used to print the DCMATCH Summary, which only is just for DCMATCH analysis.

![image 9067](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9067.png)

Figure 95.908 DCMATCH Summary Form

Filter: shows all the device types in the list box, you can select these types by Shift or Ctrl. The default is empty.

Select All: selects all the device types in the list box below. Select None: selects all the device types in the list box below. Include Instances: lists instances to include.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to include from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all include instances.


Exclude Instances: lists instances to exclude.

- • Select: selects one or more instances to exclude from schematic.
- • Clear: clears all exclude instances.


Device Type: selects device type from drop-down list. The variations from the device type will be listed in the list box, you can select these variations by Shift or Ctrl. The default is empty.

Select All: selects all the variations in the list box below. Select None: selects all the variations in the list box below.

Truncate: limits the number of devices in the DCMATCH summary, the default is By Relative Threshold.

• None: selects this option, it will no limit for DCMATCH summary.

![image 9068](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9068.png)

Figure 95.909 Truncate - None

• By Number: selects this option, only shows the Top number of devices in the DCMATCH summary.

![image 9069](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9069.png)

Figure 95.910 Truncate - By Number

– Top: sets the value of Top, the default value is 3.

• By Relative Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices which the absolute value of Contribution or sigmaOut is greater than Threshold multiply by the largest absolute value of Contribution or sigmaOut in all devices.

![image 9070](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9070.png)

Figure 95.911 Truncate - By Relative Threshold

##### – Threshold: sets the value of By Relative Threshold.

• By Absolute Threshold: selects this option, only shows the devices which the absolute value of Contribution or sigmaOut is greater than Mismatch.

![image 9071](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9071.png)

Figure 95.912 Truncate - By Absolute Threshold

##### – Mismatch: sets the value of By Absolute threshold.

Sort By: deﬁnes the order of the DCMATCH summary, the default is Output Variation.

- • Output Variation: sorts by the Contribution or sigmaOut from large to small. If same values of Contribution or sigmaOut appeared, it will sort by Device Name.
- • Device Name: sorts by ASCII of the each device name.


Suﬃx Notation: checks this option which will convert scientiﬁc notation to suﬃx notation.

Absolute Precision: sets absolute precision, the default is 6. Relative Precision: sets relative precision, the default is 2.

rameters panel. Chooses the csv ﬁle by button.

• Mode: selects mode for loading csv ﬁle. The default setting is to overwrite.

- – Retain: keeps all the rows on the Parameters panel, and only loads the row with non-duplicate name in csv ﬁle and Parameters panel.
- – Merge: keeps the row on the Parameters panel which is not the same name as that in csv ﬁle, deletes the row on the Parameters panel which has the same name as that in csv ﬁle, and loads all the rows in csv ﬁle.

##### 95.2.6.3 Direct Plot

95.2.6.3.1 Main Form Menu: Context menu -> Direct Plot -> Main Form ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 9145](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9145.png)

This command is used to display signal waveforms in iWave immediately. If the user triggers the current command by right-clicking on a cell in the Spec column or Pass/Fail column of the results table, it will display the iwave for all simulation points, such as all corners, sweeps, and Monte Carlo simulations.

![image 9146](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9146.png)

Figure 95.942 Main Form

Analysis: speciﬁes which analysis result is plotted. Note: The Analysis types displayed are base on the setting in MDE Platform

-> Analysis > Add Analysis.

• TRAN: speciﬁes to plot TRAN analysis simulation result of signal.

![image 9147](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9147.png)

Figure 95.943 Main Form - Tran - Auto Form

– Function: speciﬁes signal types to be plotted, such as voltage or

current. ∗ Auto: plots voltage of net when user selects net in schematic,

and plot current of port when user selects port in schematic. ∗ Voltage: plots voltage of signal. As shown below.

![image 9148](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9148.png)

Figure 95.944 Main Form - Tran - Voltage Form

· Net: selects net signal. · Diﬀerential Nets: selects diﬀerential net signal.

##### · Instance With Two Terminals: selects two instance terminals.

∗ Current: plots current of signal. As shown below.

![image 9149](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9149.png)

Figure 95.945 Main Form - Tran - Current Form

· Terminal: selects terminal signal. · Diﬀerential Terminals: selects diﬀerential terminal signals.

∗ Send To Outputs: sends expression to Outputs Panel. if Send To Outputs is checked, the expression will be added into Outputs Pannel and the iWave will be opened at the same time when clicking schematic.

• Noise: plots NOISE analysis simulation result.

![image 9150](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9150.png)

Figure 95.946 Main Form - Noise - Output Noise Form

– Function: speciﬁes types of signals to be plotted, such as output

noise or input noise. ∗ Output Noise: plots output noise of signals. ∗ Equivalent: selects equivalent circuit nodes. ∗ Squared: selects squared circuit nodes. ∗ Magnitude: selects the magnitude of the signals. ∗ dB20: selects the dB20 signals.

∗ Input Noise: plots input noise of signals. ∗ Equivalent: selects equivalent circuit nodes. ∗ Squared: selects squared circuit nodes.

– Send To Outputs: sends expression to Outputs Panel. if Send To Outputs is checked, the expression will be added into Outputs Pannel and the iWave will be opened at the same time when clicking Plot button.

• Noise Separation: plots noise separation analysis simulation result.

![image 9151](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9151.png)

Figure 95.947 Main Form - Noise Separation

- – Function: speciﬁes types of signals to be plotted.
- – Instance Output: selects instance output of loop waveform.


![image 9152](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9152.png)

Figure 95.948 Main Form - Noise Separation - Instance Output

∗ Signal Level: speciﬁes the signal level, such as V**2/Hz. ∗ Modiﬁer: speciﬁes the modiﬁer.

· Power: selects power of modiﬁer. · dB10: selects dB10 of modiﬁer.

∗ Filter: speciﬁes the ﬁlter of instances. · Select All: selects all the device types in the list box below. · Select None: deselects all the device types in the list box

below. · Include Instances: lists instances to include. · Select: selects one or more instances to include from schematic. · Clear: clears all included instances. · Exclude Instances: lists instances to exclude. · Select: selects one or more instances to exclude from schematic. · Clear: clears all excluded instances.

∗ Truncate: speciﬁes the number of source output. – Source Output: selects source output of loop waveform.

∗ The settings are the same as Instance Output.

– Instance Source: selects instance source of loop waveform.

![image 9153](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9153.png)

Figure 95.949 Main Form - Noise Separation - Instance Source

∗ Signal Level: speciﬁes the signal level, such as A**2/Hz.

– Primary Source: selects primary source of loop waveform.

![image 9154](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9154.png)

Figure 95.950 Main Form - Noise Separation - Primary Source

∗ Signal Level: speciﬁes the signal level, such as A**2/Hz.

– Src.Noise Gain: selects src.noise gain of loop waveform.

![image 9155](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9155.png)

Figure 95.951 Main Form - Noise Separation - Src.Noise Gain

∗ Signal Level: speciﬁes the signal level, such as (Vˆ2/Aˆ2):Hz.

– Send To Outputs: sends expression to Outputs Panel. if Send To Outputs is checked, the expression will be added into Outputs Pannel and the iWave will be opened at the same time when clicking Plot button.

• STB: plots STB analysis simulation result.

![image 9156](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9156.png)

Figure 95.952 Main Form - STB Form

∗ Channel Deﬁnitions(Default Custom): speciﬁes channel definitions for ACPR function.

∗ Add: appends the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) in the text boxes into the table above.

∗ Delete: deletes the Name, From(HZ) and To(HZ) currently selected in the table.

function. ∗ Strobe Period: speciﬁes strobe period for ACPR function. ∗ Window Size: speciﬁes window size for ACPR function. De-

fault is 64. ∗ Repetitions: speciﬁes repetitions for ACPR function. Default is 2. ∗ Resolutions BandWidth: speciﬁes resolutions bandwidth for ACPR function. ∗ Windowing(Default Rectangle): speciﬁes windowing for ACPR function.

Default is 64. ∗ Repetitions: speciﬁes repetitions for Main Channel Power function. Default is 2. ∗ Resolutions BandWidth: speciﬁes resolutions bandwidth for

# Part IX Tools

# Chapter 96 Introduction

Aether has provided abundant tools.

# Chapter 97 Technology Manager

## 97.1 Technology Manager Introduction

A technology database contains process information. A library typically contains a single technology database, and all the designs in the library use that technology database. Alternatively, a you can deﬁne an attachment from one library to the technology database in another library. In this case, all the designs in the library use the attached technology database. Whether in the same library or in a diﬀerent library, the main technology database associated with a design is known as its primary technology database.

Any technology database can contain references to other technology databases. A reference is a mechanism that allows a technology database to inherit information from one or more technology databases. This approach is known as using incremental technology databases.

A referenced technology database can itself reference other technology databases to form a chain, known as a graph of technology databases. All the technology information in a graph is available for the design library. When a design is opened, the primary technology database is opened, and if there are any references, the graph of technology databases is opened as well.

Technology Manager (TM) is the control panel for technology. It mainly manages rules in technology, including

- • Reference
- • Control
- • Purpose
- • Layer
- • Layer Priority


- • GDS Layer Map
- • Constraint
- • Device
- • Via
- • Guardring
- • Metal Slot
- • Metal Fill
- • Gate Rule
- • Label Layer
- • Block Layer
- • Row
- • Connect Rule


![image 9964](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9964.png)

Figure 97.1 TM

You can create, modify and delete rules in TM. Aether can save technology into ASCII ﬁle and load ASCII technology ﬁle. All modiﬁcations are based technology library, so you should select technology library ﬁrst.

### 97.2.3 Load Technology File

Menu: File -> Load Technology File ToolBar: BindKey: None Tcl Command: None

![image 9967](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9967.png)

Technology is stored in binary ﬁle format, which you cannot read it directly. Technology ﬁle contains rules in technology. It is in ASCII format and readable by users. This command is used to load technology ﬁle in technology library.

![image 9968](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9968.png)

Figure 97.2 Load Technology File

ASCII Technology File: speciﬁes the ASCII technology ﬁle path. Classes: speciﬁes which class rule to load. There are:

- • Controls: speciﬁes to load the control in technology ﬁle. Controls have parameters and units. You can set controls in TM.
- • LayerDeﬁnitions: speciﬁes to load the layer deﬁnitions in technology ﬁle. Layer deﬁnitions have techLayers, techLayerPurposePriorities, techDisplays and so on.
- • LayerRules: speciﬁes to load the layer rules in technology ﬁle. Layer rules have labelLayer,streamLayers and so on.
- • ConstraintGroups: speciﬁes to load the constraint groups in technology ﬁle. Constraint groups have spacing and so on.
- • ViaDefs: speciﬁes to load the via defs in technology ﬁle. Via defs have standardViaDefs and customViaDefs.
- • MetalRules: speciﬁes to load the metal rules in technology ﬁle. Metal rules have slotRule and metalFill.
- • Devices: speciﬁes to load the devices in technology ﬁle. Devices have gateRule and guardRing.
- • RouteRules: speciﬁes to load the route rules in technology ﬁle.
- • SiteDefs: speciﬁes to load the site defs in technology ﬁle.


Select All: loads all classes in the ASCII technology ﬁle. Default is in unchecked.

Technology Library: speciﬁes which technology library to load ASCII technology ﬁle. There are two modes to load technology ﬁle.

- • Merge: Aether will merge the contents in technology ﬁle into the technology library. For example, there is a layer named metal1 in technology ﬁle, and layer named metal2 in technology library. After merged, there are two layers in technology library: one is metal1, the other is metal2. It is default mode.
- • Replace: Aether will replace the technology library with the contents in technology ﬁle. The original contents in technology will be destroyed. For example, there is a layer named metal1 in technology ﬁle, and layer named metal2 in technology library. After merging, there is only one layer in technology library: metal1.

### 97.3.3 Purpose

A purpose is referenced along with a layer when creating physical design data. A purpose consists of a purpose name and a purpose number.

Each technology database will have a set of predeﬁned purposes which correspond to the 11 purposes. These predeﬁned purposes are always available, and may not be changed nor removed. This set of predeﬁned purposes consists of the following:

Table 97.1 Predeﬁned Purpose

|Name<br><br>|Number|
|---|---|
|drawing|oavPurposeNumberDrawing|
|ﬁll<br><br>|oavPurposeNumberFill|
|slot|oavPurposeNumberSlot|
|OPCSerif|oavPurposeNumberOPCSerif|
|OPCAntiSerif|oavPurposeNumberOPCAntiSerif|
|annotation<br><br>|oavPurposeNumberAnnotation|
|gapFill|oavPurposeNumberGapFill|
|redundant|oavPurposeNumberRedundant|

This command is used to create, modiﬁed the purpose in technology library.

![image 9986](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9986.png)

Figure 97.11 Purpose in Technology

Name: speciﬁes purpose name. Number: speciﬁes purpose number. Abbrev.: speciﬁes purpose abbreviate. Add: adds a new purpose. Modify: modiﬁes the speciﬁed purpose. Delete: deletes the speciﬁed purpose.

### 97.3.4 Layer

A layer is ultimately referenced when creating physical design data.

A shape or a ﬁg can be placed on a layer. Layers are used for multiple purposes and frequently correspond to the diﬀerent manufacturing layers that exist on chips. A shape refers to a layer using a layer number.

This command is used to create, modiﬁed the layer in technology library. Note: Layer is the same as layer-purpose pair here.

![image 9987](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9987.png)

Figure 97.12 Layer in Technology

Layer List: lists all layers in speciﬁed technology library.

- • Sel: sets all layers to selectable or not.
- • Vis: sets all layers to visible or not.
- • Val: sets all layers to valid or not.


Main Attributes: speciﬁes attributes of layer.

- • Layer Name: speciﬁes layer name.
- • Layer Number: speciﬁes layer number.
- • Layer Abbrev.: speciﬁes layer abbreviate.
- • Purpose Name: speciﬁes purpose name.
- • Priority: speciﬁes priority of layer that use in display.
- • Selectable: speciﬁes whether the layer is selectable or not.
- • Visible: speciﬁes whether the layer is visible or not.
- • Valid: speciﬁes whether the layer is valid or not.


Display Resource: speciﬁes display packet of layer used. If you double-click display packet, Aether will pop up Display Resource Editor to allow you to edit display resource. Add: adds a new layer. Modify: modiﬁes the speciﬁed layer.

Delete: deletes the speciﬁed layer.

### 97.3.5 Layer Priority

This command is used to adjust the layer priority in technology library. Layer priority will result in display order of layer. For example, the layer 0M.drawing priority is zero, the layer RGM.drawing priority is one. And there is an rectangle on layer 0M.drawing, the other rectangle on layer RGM.drawing. These two rectangles overlap. Aether will draw RGM.drawing ﬁrst, 0M.drawing last. User should feel the rectangle on 0M.drawing is on the rectangle on RGM.drawing.

![image 9988](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9988.png)

Figure 97.13 Example of Layer Priority

Now let’s change the priority of these two layers. Aether will draw these two rectangles as follows.

![image 9989](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9989.png)

Figure 97.14 Example of Layer Priority

The layer priority form as follows:

![image 9990](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9990.png)

Figure 97.15 Layer Priority in Technology

Style: shows the display attributes of layers. Priority: shows the priority of layers. The bigger the priority is, the latter the layer is drawn. Name: shows the name of layers.

Reorder: reorder the priority of layers. You can drag drop the layer directly in form. After adjust the priority of layer, you should make modiﬁcation valid by click this button.

### 97.3.6 GDS Layer Map

This command is used to add, modify and delete layer map for GDS in/out. The gds layer map will be stored in gds.map which is under the technology library.

![image 9991](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9991.png)

Figure 97.16 GDS Layer Map in Technology

Use All: speciﬁes to use all layer map when translating GDS ﬁle. Use: speciﬁes to use this layer map when translating GDS ﬁle. Layer: speciﬁes layer-purpose pair to map when translating GDS ﬁle. Stream Number: speciﬁes which stream number in GDS to map when translating GDS ﬁle. Data: speciﬁes which data type in GDS to map when translating GDS ﬁle. Add: adds a new layer map. Delete: deletes the speciﬁed layer map.

Auto Generate: generates layer map from technology automatically. Stream number will be the same as layer number, and data type will be the same as purpose number in this mode. Because purpose number are very large number, data type will be set to zero if purpose is drawing.

See Also: DM -> File -> Export -> GDS 2.7.1. See Also: DM -> File -> Import -> GDS 2.6.1.

### 97.3.7 Constraint

This command is used to add, modify and delete constraint in technology. Aether only supports constraints in foundry in TM.

![image 9992](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile9992.png)

Figure 97.17 Constraint in Technology

Foundry: constraint rules in foundry group. Now Aether only supports it in TM.

Constraint: Aether now support minWidth, minSpacing, minExtension and minEnclosure.

- • minWidth: speciﬁes minimum width of a shape.
- • minSpacing: speciﬁes minimum space between shapes on the same/diﬀerent layer.
- • minExtension: speciﬁes minimum distance required between the inside edge of the reference layer shape to the inside edge of the main layer shape.
- • minEnclosure: speciﬁes minimum extension required in the direction of the parallel edge.


Main Layer: speciﬁes the layer-purpose pair as main layer in constraint rule. Reference Layer: speciﬁes the layer-purpose pair as reference layer in constraint rule.

Value: speciﬁes value of constraint rule. See Also: LE -> Options -> DRD 68.7.

### 97.3.9 Via

This command is used to add, modify and delete via rule in technology. Via rule deﬁnes a via design in a technology database. There are two types via, one is standard via, the other is custom via.

StdVia: A standard via rule has a unique name and is associated with two layers and a list of via parameters with default values. The parameters used to create the standard via rule establish a baseline of default parameter values for the standard via that is created using the standard via rule. The default

ﬂag bits for each of the parameters associated with a standard via rule are set.

– Implant Layer1: speciﬁes implant layer1.

![image 10037](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10037.png)

- • Via: speciﬁes via rule.


- – Layer: speciﬁes the cut(via) layer.
- – Rows: speciﬁes the default rows of via.
- – Columns: speciﬁes the default columns of via.
- – Width: speciﬁes the default width of via.

- Figure 97.65 Y Space of Via


- • Via Spacing: speciﬁes various via spacing deﬁnitions. Various via spacing rules are speciﬁed according to diﬀerent pairs of rows and columns while are written in distinct lines. Note: The generic format is as follows: r[ows] (logic) (rowNumber) c[olumns] (logic) (columnNumber) (xSpacing) [ySpacing] Items in parentheses are necessary, while the ones in brackets are not. logic is one of "> ", "> =", "< ", "< =", "!=" and "==". ySpacing will be deﬁned as xSpacing if it is not customized.
- • Indication: shows the indication for some parameters.
- • Description: shows the description for some parameters.


CustomVia: A custom via rule deﬁnes a via that has its geometry speciﬁed as the contents of a stored design. A custom via rule has a unique name and is associated with a master design and two layers. It is possible for the design that the custom via points at to be a pycell or vcell. In that case the custom via may have a parameter array that provides override values for that pycell or vcell.

- – Layer2(Top): speciﬁes top layer.

• Design: speciﬁes referenced design, it should be vcell or pycell. The Design should exist.

- – Library Name: speciﬁes library name of design.
- – Cell Name: speciﬁes cell name of design.
- – View Name: speciﬁes view name of design.

### 97.3.11 Flexible Path

This command is used to add, modify and delete ﬂexible path template in technology. This template will be used by Create -> Flexible Path.

![image 10062](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10062.png)

Figure 97.83 Flexible Path in Technology

Template List: shows existing templates. Allows to modify or delete the speciﬁed template.

Template Rules: gets templates by loading an existing template ﬁle.

• Load Template: clicks the button to speciﬁes the template ﬁle to load. Template Name: shows the name of the ﬂexible path template. Master Path: clicks the button to display parameters setting form for the master path of the template to be added or modiﬁed.

- • Layer: speciﬁes the layer name of the master path.
- • Width: speciﬁes the width of the master path.
- • Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the master path to the mouse point. A positive value means the master is on the left side of the mouse point, and a negative value means it is on the right side.
- • Choppable: if this option is checked, the master path can be chopped. If the master path is choppable, the subparts must be choppable. If the master path is not choppable, the subparts can be choppable or not.
- • End Type: speciﬁes the type of master path. If the type of master path is truncate, extend or round, the sub paths will follow it. If the type of master path is variable, the type of sub paths will become truncate.


– truncate: this style results in no extension beyond the beginning

and ending points of the path.

– extend: this style results in a one-half width extension beyond the

beginning and ending points for the path.

– round: this style results in an octagonal extension with 3 edges

which extend one-third of the path width.

– variable: this style can have a beginning extension diﬀerent from the ending extension. Only paths with this style may have a Begin Extension and End Extension set.

∗ Begin Extension: sets the beginning extension value to a nonnegative value.

∗ End Extension: sets the ending extension value.This parameter must be set to a non-negative value

![image 10063](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10063.png)

Figure 97.84 End Type

- • Enclose By: speciﬁes the distance between the ﬂexible path and the objects that the ﬂexible path will surround.
- • Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes the reference side on the master path.


- – Left: speciﬁes the left edge of the master path as reference side.
- – Center: speciﬁes the centerline of the master path as reference side.
- – Right: speciﬁes the right edge of the master path as reference side.


Add: clicks the button to add a new template, the new template will be displayed in the template list.

Modify: clicks the button to modify templates parameter conﬁguration. Delete: clicks the button to delete template.

Oﬀset Subpath: clicks the button to display oﬀset subpath parameters and parameter setting table.

- • Del: clicks the button to delete an oﬀset subpath.
- • Edit: clicks the button to apply the modiﬁed parameters to the selected oﬀset subpath.
- • Layer: speciﬁes the layer name of the oﬀset subpath.
- • Choppable: if this option is checked, the oﬀset subpath can be chopped.
- • Begin Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the start of the oﬀset subpath to the start of the master path.
- • End Oﬀset: speciﬁes the distance from the end of the oﬀset subpath to the end of the master path.
- • Justiﬁcation: speciﬁes the reference side on the master path for the oﬀset subpath alignment.


- – Left: speciﬁes the left edge of the master path as reference side. The right edge of the subpath is separated from the left edge of the master path.
- – Center: speciﬁes the centerline of the master path as reference side. The centerline of the subpath is separated from the centerline of the master path.


- – Right: speciﬁes the right edge of the master path as reference side. The left edge of the subpath is separated from the left edge of the master path.


- • Width: speciﬁes the width of the oﬀset subpath.
- • Separation: speciﬁes the distance from the oﬀset subpath to Justiﬁcation.
