## 119.4 dbCrtAngleInst

#### SYNTAX

dbCrtAngleInst -cv cellview -master master | [ -lib lib ] -cell cell [ -view view ] -point point [ -orient orient ] [ -angle angle ] [ -rowPitch row_pitch -colPitch col_pitch [ -rows rows ] [ -cols cols ] ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

inst

#### DESCRIPTION

119.5. dbCrtCascade

This command creates an instance which rotates around its master’s origin by a given degree angle. It returns a ﬁgure identiﬁer when the instance is created.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. point: It speciﬁes the point to set the instance. The type of the argument is point. master: It speciﬁes the instance master identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. lib: It speciﬁes the library name of the angle instance. If it is not speciﬁed, the library of cell view identiﬁer will be used. The type of the argument is string. cell: It speciﬁes the cell name of Instance. The type of the argument is string. view: It speciﬁes the view name of instance. The type of the argument is string. The default value is layout.

orient: It speciﬁes oreint of instance. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

angle: It speciﬁes the angle that the instance rotates around its master’s origin. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.

rowPitch: It speciﬁes the Y coordinate pitch of instance array. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

colPitch: It speciﬁes the X coordinate pitch of instance array. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

rows: It speciﬁes the row number of instance array. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

cols: It speciﬁes the column number of instance array. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

#### EXAMPLES

> set design [dbOpenCV -lib watch -cell main_panel -view layout] > set master [dbOpenCV -lib watch -cell GOA -view layout] > dbCrtAngleInst -cv $design -master $master -point (0,0) -angle 80

## 119.5 dbCrtCascade

dbCrtCascade -cv cellview -lib lib_name -cell cell_name [ -view view_name ] [ -rows row ] [ -cols col ] [ -xpanel xpanel ] [ -reverse reverse ] -pinInfos pinInfos -point point

#### RETURNED TYPE

inst

#### DESCRIPTION

This command creates cascade circuit. It returns an inst identiﬁer if successful; otherwise, returns 0.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. lib: It speciﬁes the source symbol lib name. The type of the argument is string. cell: It speciﬁes the source symbol cell name. The type of the argument is string. view: It speciﬁes the source symbol view name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is symbol. point: It speciﬁes the reference point to create cascade circuit. The type of the argument is point. xpanel: It speciﬁes the xpanel ﬁle path. The type of the argument is string. rows: It speciﬁes the row number of cascade circuit. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1. cols: It speciﬁes the columns of cascade circuit. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1. pinInfos: It speciﬁes the pin info string list. The type of the argument is string_list. reverse: It speciﬁes whether to reversely generate array. The type of the argument

- is bool. The default value is 0. EXAMPLES > set pinInfos {} > lappend pinInfos "H;gate1;;1" > lappend pinInfos "H;gate2;gate1;2" > lappend pinInfos "V;data;;3" > lappend pinInfos "V;com;data;4" > dbCrtCascade -cv $cvId -lib top -cell cell1 -pinInfos $pinInfos -point {0 0}


119.6. dbCrtCircle

## 119.6 dbCrtCircle

SYNTAX

dbCrtCircle -cv cellview -center center -radius radius -layer layer_name [

- -purpose pur_name ] [ -type circle_type ] [ -quadrant start_quadrant ] [ -sides sides ] RETURNED TYPE shape DESCRIPTION

This command creates a circle. It returns a shape identiﬁer if the circle can be created.

ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. center: It speciﬁes the center of circle. The type of the argument is point. radius: It speciﬁes the radius of circle. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. layer: It speciﬁes layer number or layer name. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing. type: It speciﬁes circle type. 1 for circle, 2 for 1/2 circle and 4 for 1/4 circle. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

quadrant: It speciﬁes start quadrant of 1/2 circle or 1/4 circle. Values from 1 to 4 represent top, left, bottom and right. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

sides: It speciﬁes sides for ellipse donut. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 32.

EXAMPLES

> dbCrtCircle -cv $cvId -center (0,0) -radius 1 -layer PWELL > dbCrtCircle -cv $cvId -center (0,0) -radius 1 -layer PWELL -type 2 -quadrant 1

- -sides 32

## 119.11 dbCrtFp

#### SYNTAX

119.12. dbCrtInst

chopPts: It speciﬁes point list which is the chop part. The type of the argument is point_list_list.

mode: It speciﬁes the path mode. The type of the argument is int. chopMaster: It speciﬁes the path mode. The type of the argument is bool. The

- default value is 0. templateFile: It speciﬁes template ﬁle name. The type of the argument is string. EXAMPLES


> dbCrtFp -cv $cvId -mode 0 -refPts {{(0,0) (5,0)}} -chopPts {{(1,0) (2,0)} {(3,0)(4,0)}} -templateFile conﬁg.fp

## 119.12 dbCrtInst

#### SYNTAX

dbCrtInst -cv cellview -point point -master master | [ -lib lib ] -cell cell [ -view view ] [ -inst instName ] [ -orient orient ] [ -justify justify ] [ -rowPitch row_pitch -colPitch col_pitch [ -rows rows ] [ -cols cols ] ] [ -mag mag ] [ -angle angle ] [ -params params ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

inst

#### DESCRIPTION

This command creates an instance. It returns a ﬁgure identiﬁer when the instance is created.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. point: It speciﬁes origin or instance. The type of the argument is point. master: It speciﬁes the instance master identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. lib: It speciﬁes the library name of instance. If it is not speciﬁed, the library of cell view identiﬁer will be used. The type of the argument is string. cell: It speciﬁes the cell name of Instance. The type of the argument is string. view: It speciﬁes the view name of instance. The type of the argument is string. The default value is layout. inst: It speciﬁes the name of instance. The type of the argument is string.

orient: It speciﬁes oreint of instance. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

justify: It speciﬁes justiﬁcation of instance. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are upperLeft, centerLeft, lowerLeft, upperCenter, centerCenter, lowerCenter, upperRight, centerRight, lowerRight and origin. The default value is origin.

rowPitch: It speciﬁes the Y coordinate pitch of instance array. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

colPitch: It speciﬁes the X coordinate pitch of instance array. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

rows: It speciﬁes the row number of instance array. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

cols: It speciﬁes the column number of instance array. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

mag: It speciﬁes the magnify of instance. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The

- default value is 1.


angle: It speciﬁes the angle that the instance rotates around its master’s origin. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.

params: It speciﬁes the parameter array of parameterized cell instance. The type of the argument is string_list.

#### EXAMPLES

> set design [dbOpenCV -lib test -cell test -view layout] > set master [dbOpenCV -lib 018um_PDK -cell n18 -view layout] > dbCrtInst -cv $design -master $master -point (0,0) > dbCrtInst -cv $design -master $master -point (0,0) -rowPitch 2 -colPitch 3 -rows

- 2 -cols 3


> dbCrtInst -cv [aeGetCurDesign] -lib reference_pdk -cell p18 -view layout -inst M1 -params {Length 180n w 1u Fingers 2}

point: It speciﬁes the original point of label. The type of the argument is point. textName: It speciﬁes the text of the label. The type of the argument is string. height: It speciﬁes height of the label. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The

default value is 1.0.

font: It speciﬁes the font of the label. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are euroStyle, gothic, math, roman, script, stick, ﬁxed, swedish, milSpec, modern and contemplate1. The default value is stick.

draft: It speciﬁes whether label is drafting or not. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

#### SYNTAX

The default value is drawing. points: It speciﬁes point list of center line. The type of the argument is point_list. width: It speciﬁes width of path. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

arcSegmentsNum: It speciﬁes the number of circle segments for pt. (Only for AetherMW) The type of the argument is int. The default value is 72.

cornerType: It speciﬁes corner type of path. (Only for AetherMW) The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Square, Mitered, Adaptive _mitered, Curve and Round. The default value is Square.

curveRadius: It speciﬁes the max radius of the path with Curve corner type. (Only for AetherMW) The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.

The type of the argument is ﬁg. cv: It speciﬁes the cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. points: It speciﬁes the point list of the shape. The type of the argument is point_list. box: It speciﬁes the lower left corner and upper right corner of the box. The type of the argument is box. layName: It speciﬁes layer number or layer name. accDir: It speciﬁes the access direction of pin. The type of the argument is enum_list. The values of the enumeration are top, bottom, left and right.

draft: It speciﬁes whether pin name is drafting or not. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

pinnamePurName: It speciﬁes purpose name or purpose number of the pin name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

The type of the argument is string. point: It speciﬁes the ref point to create the wire name. The type of the argument is point. height: It speciﬁes the height of wire name. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The

- default value is 0.0625.

oﬀset: It speciﬁes the oﬀset. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 6.

orient: It speciﬁes the orientation of ﬁgures. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

The type of the argument is string. view: It speciﬁes the view name of instance. The type of the argument is string. The default value is layout.

justify: It speciﬁes justiﬁcation of instance. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are upperLeft, centerLeft, lowerLeft, upperCenter, centerCenter, lowerCenter, upperRight, centerRight, lowerRight and origin. The default value is origin.

- default value is 1.

## 120.1 agrGetSnapPoints

inst: It speciﬁes the list of inst identiﬁer. The type of the argument is inst. points: It speciﬁes point array of the inst. The type of the argument is point_list. type: It speciﬁes the modal shape’s type. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Rect, Polygon and Path.

## 120.7 agrTunnel

#### SYNTAX

##### agrTunnel -inst inst -mode mode -ﬁg ﬁgId | -points points | -bbox bbox [

- -layer layer [ -purpose purpose ] [ -space space ] ] RETURNED TYPE bool DESCRIPTION


This command creates tunnels. When using the Overlap type, the shape type must be Rectangle, Path, Polygon and PathSeg, and the speciﬁed layers can be used; When using the Rectangle type, the layers and bbox must be set; When using other types, layers and points must be speciﬁed.

#### ARGUMENTS

inst: It speciﬁes the inst identiﬁer. The type of the argument is inst.

mode: It speciﬁes the mode to tunnel. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Path, Rectangle, Polygon and Overlap. The default value is Overlap.

bbox: It speciﬁes a bounding box. The type of the argument is box.

points: It speciﬁes point list. The type of the argument is point_list. ﬁg: It speciﬁes the ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is ﬁg. layer: It speciﬁes a list of layer. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing. space: Speciﬁes an expanded space value. The default is 0. The type of the

- argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0. EXAMPLES > agrTunnel -inst $agrId -mode Overlap -ﬁg $ﬁgId


> agrTunnel -inst $agrId -mode Overlap -ﬁg $ﬁgId -layer M0 -purpose drawing

- -space 0.02

> agrTunnel -inst $agrId -mode Path -points {(0,2) (10,2)} -layer M0 -purpose drawing -space 0.04

> agrTunnel -inst $agrId -mode Rectangle -bbox {(0,2) (10,10)} -layer M1 -purpose drawing -space 0

> agrTunnel -inst $agrId -mode Polygon -points {(0,0) (0,1) (1,1) (1,0)} -layer M0

- -purpose drawing -space 0.02

## 120.18 dbConcatTransform

#### SYNTAX

dbConcatTransform -trans1 trans1 -trans2 trans2 | -oﬀsetPoint1 oﬀsetPoint1 [ -orient1 orient1 ] [ -mag1 mag1 ] -oﬀsetPoint2 oﬀsetPoint2 [ -orient2 orient2 ] [ -mag2 mag2 ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command returns a list of the result transform if successful; otherwise, returns nothing.

#### ARGUMENTS

trans1: It speciﬁes the ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is list. trans2: It speciﬁes the second transformation. The type of the argument is list.

- oﬀsetPoint1: It speciﬁes the oﬀset point of ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is point.

orient1: It speciﬁes the orientation of ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

- mag1: It speciﬁes the magniﬁcation of the ﬁrst transformation. The type of the


argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 1.0.

- oﬀsetPoint2: It speciﬁes the oﬀset point of second transformation. The type of the argument is point.


orient2: It speciﬁes the orientation of second transformation. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

- mag2: It speciﬁes the magniﬁcation of the second transformation. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 1.0. EXAMPLES > dbConcatTransform -oﬀsetPoint1 (10,10) -orient1 R90 -mag1 1.0


-oﬀsetPoint2 (0,5) -orient2 R90 -mag2 1.2 > dbConcatTransform -trans1 {"2:2" "R90" "2.0"} -trans2 {"0:2" "R90" "1.0"}

## 120.32 dbFind

#### SYNTAX

dbFind -cv cellview -types types -conditions conditions [ -bbox bBox ] [ startLevel level1 ] [ -stopLevel level2 ] [ -isDelDuplicated isDelDuplicated ] [ -cbFunc callbackFunc ] [ -maxCount maxCount ] [ -withBBox withBBox | -withOrigin withOrigin | -withOutline withOutline | -withLevel withLevel ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

typeless

#### DESCRIPTION

This command ﬁnds a cell view according to bounding box or condition. It returns a list of object identiﬁers and other informations.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes the cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. bbox: It speciﬁes a bounding box, the default is cell view bounding box. The type of the argument is box. startLevel: It speciﬁes the starting traverse level. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0. stopLevel: It speciﬁes the traverse stop level. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0. types: It speciﬁes which type of ﬁgures are traversed. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are shape and inst. cbFunc: It speciﬁes the callback function name. The type of the argument is string. maxCount: It speciﬁes the max query count. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 50000. isDelDuplicated: It speciﬁes whether the ﬁg is can duplicated. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false. conditions: It speciﬁes the condition of query. The type of the argument is string_list.

withBBox: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its boundary box. The boundary box is calculated by coordination of top cell view. If it is false, the element of return value is only a ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

120.33. dbFindInst

withOrigin: It speciﬁes how to return the value. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

withOutline: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its outline points list. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

withLevel: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its level. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

#### EXAMPLES

> dbFind -cv [aeGetCurDesign] -type inst -startLevel 0 -stopLevel 50 -conditions {{LibName == test} {CellName == A}} -withBBox 1

> dbFind -cv [aeGetCurDesign] -type shape -startLevel 0 -stopLevel 50 -conditions {{Layer == PWELL.drawing}} -withBBox 1

## 120.50 dbGetTrueOverlaps

#### SYNTAX

dbGetTrueOverlaps -cv cellview [ -bbox bBox ] [ -layer layer [ -purpose purpose ] ] [ -startLevel level1 ] [ -stopLevel level2 ] [ -shapeOnly shapeOnly | instOnly instOnly | -viaOnly viaOnly ] [ -cbFunc callbackFunc ] [ -attachBBox attachBBox | -attachPoint attachPoint ] [ -condition condition ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

typeless

#### DESCRIPTION

It returns a list of object identiﬁers whose bounding boxes overlap the speciﬁed bounding box.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes the cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. bbox: It speciﬁes a bounding box, the default is cell view bounding box. The type of the argument is box.

layer: It speciﬁes layer number or layer name. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

startLevel: It speciﬁes the starting traverse level. The type of the argument is int. stopLevel: It speciﬁes the traverse stop level. The type of the argument is int. cbFunc: It speciﬁes the callback function name. The type of the argument is string.

attachBBox: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its boundary box. The boundary box is calculated by coordination of top cell view. If it is false, the element of return value is only a ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

attachPoint: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its points list. The points list is calculated by coordination of top cell view. If the ﬁgure is an instance, array, rectangle, ellipse, arc, blockage and boundary, the points list is the boundary of the

ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a polygon, the points list is the vertices of the polygon. If the ﬁgure is a line, guardring, or path, the points list is the center-line point list of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a donut, the points list is only the center point of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a text, the points list only is the original point of the ﬁgure. If it is false, the element of return value is only a ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

shapeOnly: It speciﬁes whether to only get shape. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

instOnly: It speciﬁes whether to only get instance. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

viaOnly: It speciﬁes whether to only get via. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

condition: It speciﬁes the traversing condition. The type of the argument is string. The default value is EO.

#### EXAMPLES

> dbGetTrueOverlaps -cv $cvId > dbGetTrueOverlaps -cv $cvId -bbox {(0,0) (20,20)} -condition E

## 120.52 dbInvertTransform

SYNTAX

dbInvertTransform -trans trans1 | -oﬀset oﬀsetPoint [ -orient orient ] [ -mag mag ]

RETURNED TYPE

list

DESCRIPTION

This command inverts the transform.

ARGUMENTS

trans: It speciﬁes the ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is list. oﬀset: It speciﬁes the oﬀset point of ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is point.

orient: It speciﬁes the orientation of ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

mag: It speciﬁes the magniﬁcation of the ﬁrst transformation. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 1.0.

EXAMPLES

> dbInvertTransform -trans {"2:2" "R90" "1.0"} > dbInvertTransform -oﬀset (2,2) -orient R90 -mag 1.0

## 120.60 dbLayerGen

#### SYNTAX

dbLayerGen -op op -dst dst -layer layer [ -purpose purpose ] -ﬁgs1 ﬁgs1 | -layer1 layer1 [ -purpose1 purpose1 ] -ﬁgs2 ﬁgs2 | -layer2 layer2 [ -purpose2 purpose2 ] [ -isHier isHier ]

120.61. dbLayerHoles

#### RETURNED TYPE

shape_list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command does boolean operation of the shapes which on the diﬀerent layers. It returns a list of shape identiﬁer if these shapes can do boolean operation.

#### ARGUMENTS

op: It speciﬁes the boolean operation. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are OR, AND, XOR and NOT.

dst: It speciﬁes the destination cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design.

layer: It speciﬁes layer number or layer name. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

- ﬁgs1: It speciﬁes the ﬁrst list of shape identiﬁer of input shapes. The type of the argument is shape_list.

layer1: It speciﬁes the ﬁrst layer number or layer name. The type of the argument is string.

- purpose1: It speciﬁes the ﬁrst purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

ﬁgs2: It speciﬁes the second list of shape identiﬁer of input shapes. The type of the argument is shape_list.

layer2: It speciﬁes the second layer number or layer name. The type of the argument is string.

- purpose2: It speciﬁes the second purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.




isHier: It speciﬁes whether to hierarchy the cell. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

#### EXAMPLES

> dbLayerGen -op AND -dst $cvId -layer Gate -layer1 AA -layer2 POLY

## 120.67 dbPadReport

#### SYNTAX

dbPadReport -cv cellview -padLayer padLayer -clockwise clockwise -output output [ -auxLayer auxLayer ] [ -txtLayers txtLayers ] [ -preﬁxName preﬁxName ] [ -ﬁrstPad ﬁrstPad ] [ -sizeLB sizeLB ] [ -sizeUB sizeUB ]

The type of the argument is bool. output: It speciﬁes the ﬁle name of pad report. The type of the argument is string. auxLayer: It speciﬁes the auxiliary layer. The type of the argument is string_list. txtLayers: It speciﬁes the pad text layer. The type of the argument is string_list. preﬁxName: It speciﬁes the preﬁx name. The type of the argument is string. ﬁrstPad: It speciﬁes the point of ﬁrst pad. The type of the argument is point. sizeLB: It speciﬁes lower bound of area size. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. sizeUB: It speciﬁes the upper bound of area size. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

#### EXAMPLES

> set design [dbOpenCV -lib test -cell test -view layout] > dbPadReport -cv $design -padLayer {metal drawing} -clockwise 1 -output test.padreport

## 120.72 dbResize

#### SYNTAX

dbResize -ﬁgs ﬁgures -size size [ -merge merge ] [ -layer layer [ -purpose purpose ] ] [ -deloldobj deloldobj ] [ -truncate trunValue [ -keepOrthogonal keepOrthogonal ] [ -absolute absolute ] ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

ﬁg_list

120.73. dbSchGetOrderPin

#### DESCRIPTION

This command sizes speciﬁed ﬁgures and returns result as a list of ﬁgures.

#### ARGUMENTS

ﬁgs: It speciﬁes a list of ﬁgure identiﬁers. The type of the argument is ﬁg_list. size: It speciﬁes grow or shrink value, it supports the deﬁnition of left/bottom/right/top divided. For example, {0 2 1 1.5} means left is zero, bottom is 2, right is 1 and top is 1.5. The type of the argument is ﬂoat_list. absolute: It speciﬁes whether multiply the truncate value by size value or not. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false. merge: It speciﬁes whether merge original ﬁgures ﬁrstly or not. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is true. keepOrthogonal: It speciﬁes whether keep orthogonal or not. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false. layer: It speciﬁes the layer name or layer number. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes the purpose name or purpose number. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

truncate: It speciﬁes the value to cut oﬀ the sharp angle. It is valid when size value and truncate value are all greater than zero. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

deloldobj: It speciﬁes the ﬂag of deleting the old ﬁgure. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is true.

#### EXAMPLES

> dbResize -ﬁgs $ﬁgures -size 5 > dbResize -ﬁgs $ﬁgures -size {-1 1 1 1}

## 120.88 dbSmashInst

#### SYNTAX

dbSmashInst -inst ﬁgId [ -level level ] [ -smashArrayInst smashArrayInst ] [ -smashVia smashVia ] [ -smashPcell smashPcell ] [ -smashGuardRing smashGuardRing ] [ -smashFlexiblePath smashFlexiblePath ] [ -preDetachedBlockage preDetachedBlockage ] [ -preLabels preLabels ] [ -prePinsGeoms prePinsGeoms | -prePins prePins ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

emy_obj_list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command ﬂattens the ﬁngure with level. The ﬁgure must be an instance, via, guard ring or advance guard ring.

#### ARGUMENTS

inst: It speciﬁes the ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is ﬁg. level: It speciﬁes the number of design hierarchy levels to be smashed. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1. smashArrayInst: It speciﬁes whether to smash an instance,array,or MCell. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0. smashVia: It speciﬁes whether to smash via. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0. smashPcell: It speciﬁes whether to smash Pcell. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0. smashGuardRing: It speciﬁes whether to smash guard ring. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0. smashFlexiblePath: It speciﬁes whether to smash ﬂexible path. The type of the

- argument is bool. The default value is 0.

preDetachedBlockage: It speciﬁes whether to preserve detached blockage . The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

prePinsGeoms: It speciﬁes whether to preserve pin geometries. The type of the

- argument is bool. The default value is 1.


120.89. dbStatMoveTime

preLabels: It speciﬁes whether to preserve labels. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

prePins: It speciﬁes whether to preserve pins. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

#### EXAMPLES

> dbSmashInst -inst $instId -level 49 > dbSmashInst -inst $ﬁg -level 1 -smashPcell 1 > dbSmashInst -inst $ﬁg -level 1 -smashVia 1 -smashPcell 1 -smashGuardRing 1 > dbSmashInst -inst $ﬁg -level 50 -prePins 0 -preDetachedBlockage 0 -prePinsGeoms 0 -preLabels 0

120.92. dbTransformBBox

## 120.92 dbTransformBBox

SYNTAX

dbTransformBBox -bbox bbox [ -orient orient ] -oﬀsetPoint oﬀsetPoint [ mag magniﬁcation ]

## 120.97 dbTraverse

#### SYNTAX

dbTraverse -cv cellview [ -bbox bBox ] [ -layer layer [ -purpose purpose ] ] [ -startLevel level1 ] [ -stopLevel level2 ] [ -insideOnly inside ] [ -types types | -shapeOnly shapeOnly | -instOnly instOnly | -viaOnly viaOnly ] [ -cbFunc callbackFunc ] [ -withBBox withBBox | -withPoints withPoints | -withOutline withOutline | -withTrans withTrans ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

typeless

#### DESCRIPTION

This command traverses a cell view according to bounding box. It returns a list of object identiﬁers whose bounding boxes overlap the speciﬁed bounding box.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: It speciﬁes the cell view identiﬁer. The type of the argument is design. bbox: It speciﬁes a bounding box, the default is cell view bounding box. The type of the argument is box.

layer: It speciﬁes layer number or layer name. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes purpose number or purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

startLevel: It speciﬁes the starting traverse level. The type of the argument is int. stopLevel: It speciﬁes the traverse stop level. The type of the argument is int. insideOnly: It speciﬁes whether only to traverse the objects inside the bounding box or not The type of the argument is bool.

120.97. dbTraverse

types: It speciﬁes which type of ﬁgures are traversed. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are all, shape, inst and via. The default value is all.

cbFunc: It speciﬁes the callback function name. The type of the argument is string.

withBBox: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its boundary box. The boundary box is calculated by coordination of top cell view. If it is false, the element of return value is only a ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

withPoints: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its points list. The points list is calculated by coordination of top cell view. If the ﬁgure is an instance, array, rectangle, ellipse, arc, blockage and boundary, the points list is the boundary of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a polygon, the points list is the vertices of the polygon. If the ﬁgure is a line, guardring, or path, the points list is the center-line point list of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a donut, the points list is only the center point of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a text, the points list only is the original point of the ﬁgure. If it is false, the element of return value is only a ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

withOutline: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its outline points list. The points list is calculated by coordination of top cell view. If the ﬁgure is an instance and array, the points list is the boundary of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a polygon, path, rectangle, ellipse, donut, boundary and blockage, the points list is the outline of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a line, the points list is the center-line point list of the ﬁgure. If the ﬁgure is a text, the points list only is the original point of the ﬁgure. If it is false, the element of return value is only a ﬁgure identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

withTrans: It speciﬁes how to return the value. If it is true, the element of return value is a list which contains a ﬁgure identiﬁer and its transformation. The transformation is used to tranform the ﬁgure to the top cell view coordinate system. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

shapeOnly: It speciﬁes whether to only get shape. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

instOnly: It speciﬁes whether to only get instance. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

viaOnly: It speciﬁes whether to only get via. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is false.

#### EXAMPLES

> dbTraverse -cv $cvId > dbTraverse -cv $cvId -layer metal

## 120.98 dbUnFigGroup

#### SYNTAX

dbUnFigGroup -ﬁggroupId ﬁggroupId [ -level level ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

This command separates the current ﬁggroup.

#### ARGUMENTS

ﬁggroupId: It speciﬁes the ﬁgure group’s identiﬁer. The type of the argument is ﬁggroup.

## 125.2 aeDelCell

bool

The aeDelCell command deletes a cell with the speciﬁed view name, or a category of the speciﬁed library.

#### ARGUMENTS

lib: It speciﬁes the library name. The type of the argument is string. cell: It speciﬁes the cell name.The wildcard character * is supported. The type of the argument is string_list. view: It speciﬁes the view name.The wildcard character * is supported. The type of the argument is string_list. category: It speciﬁes the category name. The type of the argument is string. submaster: It speciﬁes the submaster name. The type of the argument is string. dmCVCkdelete: Valid Value:boolean value 0 and 1 (default=0). 1:Remove cell view ﬁles. 0:Do not remove any cell view ﬁles. The type of the argument is bool.

## 125.4 aeExportStream

#### SYNTAX

##### aeExportStream -ﬁle ﬁle -lib lib_name [ -topCell cell_name ] [ -view view_name

] [ -layerMap layer_map ] [ -cellMap cell_map ] [ -case cell_case ] [ -label label_case ] [ -maxVerti maxVerti ] [ -smashVCell smashVCell ] [ -cellNameLen cellNameLen ] [ -scale scale ] [ -exportHier trans_hierarchy [ -exportLevel trans_depth ] ] [ -propMap pro_map ] [ -logFile log_ﬁle ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

This command exports a gdsII format design from the aether database.

#### ARGUMENTS

ﬁle: It speciﬁes the gdsII ﬁle name. The type of the argument is string. lib: It speciﬁes the library name. The type of the argument is string. topCell: It speciﬁes the cell name. The type of the argument is string. view: It speciﬁes the view name. The type of the argument is string.

case: It speciﬁes the case sensitivity in cell names. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Preserve, Upper and Lower. The default value is Preserve.

scale: It speciﬁes the db scale. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. maxVerti: It speciﬁes the number of loading maximum vertices in polygons and paths. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 2000. smashVCell: It speciﬁes the ﬂag whether smash vcell. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0. cellNameLen: It speciﬁes the ﬂag whether translations the length of cell name. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0. exportHier: It speciﬁes the ﬂag whether seted the translation entire hierarchy. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1. exportLevel: It speciﬁes export level range. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 32. logFile: It speciﬁes the ﬁle name for the log ﬁles. The type of the argument is string. The default value is gdsOut.log. layerMap: It speciﬁes the layer map ﬁle. The type of the argument is string. cellMap: It speciﬁes the cell map ﬁle. The type of the argument is string.

label: It speciﬁes the label case sensitivity in text labels. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Preserve, Upper and Lower. The default value is Preserve.

propMap: It speciﬁes the property map ﬁle. The type of the argument is string.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeExportStream -ﬁle test.gds -lib test

## 125.5 aeImportStream

#### SYNTAX

aeImportStream -ﬁle ﬁle -lib lib_name [ -tech tech_ﬁle | -attachToLib attachToLib ] [ -path lib_path ] [ -topCell top_cell_name ] [ -case cell_case ] [ -layerMap layer_map ] [ -cellMap cell_map ] [ -logFile log_ﬁle ] [ -label label_case ] [ -refLib ref_lib ] [ -renameMode rename_mode ] [ -propMap pro_map ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

125.6. aeLME

#### DESCRIPTION

This command imports a gdsII format design to the aether database.

#### ARGUMENTS

attachToLib: It speciﬁes the library attached to another library. The type of the argument is string.

case: It speciﬁes the cell case sensitivity in cell names. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Preserve, Upper and Lower. The default value is Preserve.

cellMap: It speciﬁes the cell map ﬁle. The type of the argument is string. ﬁle: It speciﬁes the gdsII ﬁle name. The type of the argument is string.

label: It speciﬁes the label case sensitivity in text labels. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Preserve, Upper and Lower. The default value is Preserve.

layerMap: It speciﬁes the layer map ﬁle. The type of the argument is string. logFile: It speciﬁes the log ﬁle. The type of the argument is string. lib: It speciﬁes the library name. The type of the argument is string. path: It speciﬁes the library path. The type of the argument is string. propMap: It speciﬁes the property map ﬁle. The type of the argument is string. refLib: It speciﬁes the all reference libraries. which is {libA, libB, libC} The type of the argument is string_list.

renameMode: It speciﬁes rename cell mode. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Append, Overwrite and Skip. The default value is OverWrite.

tech: It speciﬁes the ASCII technology ﬁle. The type of the argument is string. topCell: It speciﬁes the top cell name. The type of the argument is string.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeImportStream -ﬁle test.gds -lib test

## 129.1 aeCreateBus

SYNTAX

aeCreateBus -number number -width width -spacing spacing [ -style style ] [ -beginExt begin_extend -endExt end_extend ] -point points [ -layer layer

5295

[ -purpose purpose ] ] [ -arcSegmentsNum arcSegmentsNum ] [ -cornerType cornerType ] [ -cutoﬀRatio cutoﬀRatio -curveRadius curveRadius ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

ﬁg_list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command create a bus in layout view.

#### ARGUMENTS

number: It speciﬁes the number of the buses. The type of the argument is int. width: It speciﬁes the width list of the buses. The type of the argument is ﬂoat_list. spacing: It speciﬁes the spacing list between the path. The type of the argument is ﬂoat_list.

style: It speciﬁes the path style. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are truncate, extend, round, antiESD and variable. The default value is truncate.

beginExt: It speciﬁes the value of the begin extend. The type of the argument is

- ﬂoat. The default value is 0.0.


endExt: It speciﬁes the value of end extend. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.0.

arcSegmentsNum: It speciﬁes the number of circle segments for path. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 72.

cornerType: It speciﬁes corner type of path. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Square, Mitered, Adaptive _mitered, Curve and Round. The default value is Square.

cutoﬀRatio: It speciﬁes the cutoﬀ ratio percentage of the path with Mitered or Adapative_mitered corner type. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.3.

curveRadius: It speciﬁes the max radius of the path with Curve corner type. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.

point: It speciﬁes the points list to create the buses. The type of the argument is point_list.

layer: It speciﬁes the layer name. The type of the argument is string_list. purpose: It speciﬁes the purpose name. The type of the argument is string_list. The default value is drawing.

## 129.12 aeCreateText

#### SYNTAX

aeCreateText -point points -height height -textName textName [ -attach attach ] [ -drafting drafting ] [ -font font ] [ -justify justify ] [ -layerName lay_name [ -purpose purpose ] ] [ -non45free non45free ] [ -oﬀsetPoint oﬀset_point ] [ -orient orient ] [ -placeOn placeOn ] [ -skip skip ] [ -spacing spacing ] [ -toPoly toPoly ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

ﬁg_list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command create labels in the current drawing area.

#### ARGUMENTS

point: It speciﬁes the points to create label. If number of points is great than 1, it means drawing lines to query overlapped shapes, label will auto attach to these shapes when attach/placeOn 1 is speciﬁed. The type of the argument is point_list.

height: It speciﬁes the height of label. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. textName: It speciﬁes the label string list. The type of the argument is string_list. attach: It speciﬁes the label will be attach to shape. The type of the argument is bool. drafting: It speciﬁes the label drafting or not. The type of the argument is bool.

font: It speciﬁes the label font. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are euroStyle, gothic, math, roman, script, stick, ﬁxed, swedish, milSpec, modern, simple, merit, contemplate and contemplate1. The default value is stick.

justify: It speciﬁes the justiﬁcation of the label string. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are LowerLeft, LowerCenter, LowerRight, CenterLeft, CenterCenter, CenterRight, UpperLeft, UpperCenter, UpperRight and Original. The default value is LowerLeft.

layerName: It speciﬁes the layer name. The type of the argument is string. non45free: It speciﬁes the non45 edge needs to be converted to 45 edge or not. Only toPoly 1 is speciﬁed The type of the argument is bool. oﬀsetPoint: It speciﬁes the oﬀset point. The type of the argument is point.

orient: It speciﬁes the orientation of ﬁgures. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MX, MXR90, MY and MYR90. The default value is R0.

placeOn: It speciﬁes place new created text on selected shapes which overlap the drawing lines. The type of the argument is bool.

purpose: It speciﬁes the purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

skip: It speciﬁes skip width, if shape’s width great than this value, the label string will not be placed on the shape. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

spacing: It speciﬁes the spacing between polygonals. This argument is valid only if -toPoly 1 is speciﬁed. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

toPoly: It speciﬁes the label needs to be converted to polygon or not The type of the argument is bool.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeCreateText -point {(-15,0)(0,0)(0,-4)} -height 2 -text "1 3 2" -oﬀsetPoint (1,1)

SYNTAX

aeCreateWire -point points [ -drawMode drawMode ] [ -lockAngle lockAngle ] [ -ﬂyLine ﬂyLine ] [ -wireSnapping wireSnapping ] [ -color color ] [ -lineStyle lineStyle ]

The values of the enumeration are white, yellow, silver, cream, pink, magenta, lime, tan, cyan, cadetBlue, orange, red, purple, green, brown, blue, slate, gold, maroon, violet, forest, chocolate, navy, black, gray, winColor1, winColor2, winColor3, winColor4, winColor5, blinkRed, blinkYellow and blinkWhite. The default value is cadetBlue.

lineStyle: It speciﬁes the line style. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are solid, dashed, dots, dashDot, sortDash, doubleDash and thickLine. The default value is solid.

## 130.1 aeAlign

#### SYNTAX

## 130.16 aeResizeSYNTAX

130.16. aeResize

aeResize -selMode selMode -isSize isSize [ -size size ] [ -direction direction ] [ -selTruncate selTruncate ] [ -truncateValue truncateValue ] [ -keepEdges keepEdges ] [ -absoluteValue absoluteValue ] | -isGrow isGrow [ -growParam growParam ] [ [ -layerName layerName ] [ -purpose purpose ] ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

This command is used to magnify or shrink selected shapes by resize operation.

#### ARGUMENTS

selMode: It speciﬁes the select mode. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Object and Cell. The default value is Object.

isSize: It speciﬁes the resize mode that is Size. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

size: It speciﬁes the size for Size mode. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 1.

direction: It speciﬁes the direction to modify. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are XY, XOnly and YOnly. The default value is XY.

selTruncate: It speciﬁes whether to select truncate value mode. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

truncateValue: It speciﬁes the truncate value. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 1.414.

keepEdges: It speciﬁes whether the edge of corner cut is perpendicular to the orthogonal edge. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0.

absoluteValue: It speciﬁes the truncate value. The type of the argument is int.

- The default value is 0.


isGrow: It speciﬁes the resize mode that is Shrink/Grow. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

growParam: It speciﬁes the resize direction and the size of this direction. The type of the argument is list.

layerName: It speciﬁes the layout name. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes the purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeResize -selMode Cell -isSize 1 -size 10

> aeResize -selMode Object -isSize 1 -size 10 -direction XY -selTruncate 1 truncateValue 1.414 -layerName L12 -purpose drawing

## 131.9 aeSmashObj

#### SYNTAX

aeSmashObj [ -level Level ] [ -SmashArrayInst SmashArrayInst ] [ -SmashVia SmashVia ] [ -SmashPCell SmashPCell ] [ -SmashGR SmashGR ] [ -preSel preSel ] [ -preDBlockage preDBlockage ] [ -preLabel preLabel ] [ -prePinGeom prePinGeom ] [ -prePin prePin ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

This command ﬂattens instances according to deﬁnitions.

#### ARGUMENTS

level: It speciﬁes the level number to be smashed. The type of the argument is int.

- The default value is 1.


SmashArrayInst: It speciﬁes the instance to be smashed. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

SmashVia: It speciﬁes the via to be smashed. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

SmashPCell: It speciﬁes the pcell to be smashed. The type of the argument is

- bool. The default value is 0. SmashGR: It speciﬁes the guard ring to be smashed. The type of the argument


- is bool. The default value is 0.


preDBlockage: It speciﬁes the option of preserving detached blockages. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

prePinGeom: It speciﬁes the option of preserve pins geometries. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

preLabel: It speciﬁes the option of preserve label. The type of the argument is

- bool. The default value is 1.


preSel: It speciﬁes the option of preserve selections. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

prePin: It speciﬁes the option of preserve pins. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeSmashObj -level 1

## 137.11 aeGetSelSet

#### SYNTAX

aeGetSelSet [ -instPort instPort | -attachPoint attachPoint [ -subTop subTop ] | -attr attr | -owner owner | order ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

typeless

#### DESCRIPTION

137.12. aeGetSelSetFigPoint

The command returns a list object of the selected in the current window.

#### ARGUMENTS

attachPoint: It returns a selected point list if the value is 1, otherwise, don’t return the selected list. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

attr: Return the attribute of selected objects: Net: Get the objects’s net identiﬁers, the format is {ﬁgId {netId}}. GlueNo: it is only for transistors, it doesn’t support for transistors. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Net and GlueNo. The default value is Net.

instPort: It returns the selected instance port’s identiﬁer if the value is 1, otherwise, don’t return the selected instance port’s identiﬁer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

subTop: It returns the coordinates of point list that based on the sub-top cell if the value is 1, otherwise, the coordinates of point list will not be based on sub-top cell. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

owner: Get the owner at the second return value of the selected object if set the value to 1. For example, if select the instance pin, can get the instance. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

order: Get the object list by select order if speciﬁes this ﬂag. The type of the argument is ﬂag.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeGetSelSet -instPort 1 > aeGetSelSet -attr Net > aeGetSelSet -attachPoint 1 -subTop 1

## 138.1 aeAttachFig

#### SYNTAX

aeAttachFig -ﬁg1 ﬁg1 [ -ﬁg2 ﬁg2 ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

This command attaches or detaches ﬁg. Attach ﬁg1 to ﬁg2 by making ﬁg1 a child of ﬁg2. If ﬁg1 is already attached to another object, it is detached from it and attaches to ﬁg2. If ﬁg2 is not speciﬁed, ﬁg1 is detached from any object.

#### ARGUMENTS

- ﬁg1: It speciﬁes the ﬁgure identiﬁer which will be the child ﬁgure. The type of the argument is ﬁg.
- ﬁg2: It speciﬁes the ﬁgure identiﬁer which will be the parent ﬁgure. The type of the argument is ﬁg.


#### EXAMPLES

> aeAttachFig -ﬁg1 $ﬁg1 -ﬁg2 $ﬁg2

138.2. aeBuildMapLibPathEditor

> aeAttachFig -ﬁg1 $ﬁg1

## 138.4 aeCopyCell

#### SYNTAX

aeCopyCell -lib lib -cell cell [ -toLib toLib ] -toCell toCell [ -hierarchy hierarchy ] [ -opt opt ]

bool

The command copies a cell to the speciﬁed library.

#### ARGUMENTS

lib: It speciﬁes the library the cell to be copied in. The type of the argument is string.

cell: It speciﬁes the cell to be copied. The type of the argument is string. toLib: It speciﬁes the library the cell will be copied to. The type of the argument is string. toCell: It speciﬁes the cell to be copied to. The type of the argument is string.

hierarchy: It speciﬁes the hierarchy level to copy. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are all, noRef and ignoreRef. The default value is noRef.

opt: It speciﬁes the hierarchy level to copy. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are rename, overwrite, ignorecopy and updateinst. The default value is ignorecopy.

## 138.9 aeDisableCheck

#### SYNTAX

aeDisableCheck start | end

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

The command disable the auto check action in schematic when -start is speciﬁed, or enable the auto check action in schematic when -end is speciﬁed. The usage of aeDisableCheck -start and aeDisableCheck -end must be paired, otherwise it may cause unexpected problems. # To disable the auto check action, > aeDisableCheck -start # To continue the auto check action, > aeDisableCheck -end

#### ARGUMENTS

start: It speciﬁes disabling the auto check action. The type of the argument is ﬂag. end: It speciﬁes enabling the auto check action. The type of the argument is ﬂag.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeDisableCheck -start > aeCreateWire -point {(2,3)(2,10)} > aeCreateWireName -point {(1,5)} -name Gate > aeDisableCheck -end

purposeNo: It speciﬁes the purpose identiﬁer. The type of the argument is int.

## 138.19 aeHaltUndo

SYNTAX

aeHaltUndo start | end

RETURNED TYPE

bool

DESCRIPTION

The command suspends the Undo action when start is speciﬁed, or continues the Undo action when -end is speciﬁed. The usage of aeHaltUndo -start and aeHaltUndo -end must be paired, otherwise it may cause unexpected problems. # To suspend the Undo action, > aeHaltUndo -start # To continue the Undo action, > aeHaltUndo -end

ARGUMENTS

start: It speciﬁes suspending the Undo action. The type of the argument is ﬂag. end: It speciﬁes continuing the Undo action. The type of the argument is ﬂag.

EXAMPLES

> aeCreateRect -point {(10,10) (20,30)} -layerName Metal1 //here is checkpoint 1 > aeHaltUndo -start > aeCreatePoly -point {(2,3)(2,10)(5,10)(5,15)(7,15)(7,2)} -layerName Metal1 > aeCreatePoly -point {(1,1)(1,20)(0,20)(0,0)} -layerName Metal2 > aeHaltUndo -end > aeUndo //Do undo command to rollback design to checkpoint 1

## 138.28 aeSetColPat

#### SYNTAX

aeSetColPat -selall selall | [ delLayer | addLayer ] [ -layerNo layerNo ] [ layerName layerName ] [ -purpose purpose ] [ [ [ -outlineColor outlineColor ] [ -ﬁllColor ﬁllColor ] [ -stipple stipple ] [ -style style ] [ -width width ] [ priority priority ] [ -vis vis ] [ -sel sel ] [ -use use ] ] [ -streamNo streamNo -dataTypeNo dataTypeNo [ -apply apply ] ] ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

The command setups the attribute of the speciﬁed layer and purpose.

#### ARGUMENTS

selall: It speciﬁes the selectability of all layers. The type of the argument is bool. apply: It speciﬁes the layer to be stream in/out. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

addLayer: It speciﬁes add the layer. The type of the argument is ﬂag. dataTypeNo: It speciﬁes the data type number. The type of the argument is int. delLayer: It speciﬁes deleting the layer. The type of the argument is ﬂag. ﬁllColor: It speciﬁes the name of ﬁll color. The type of the argument is string. layerName: It speciﬁes the layer name. The type of the argument is string. layerNo: It speciﬁes the layer identiﬁer. The type of the argument is int. outlineColor: It speciﬁes the name of outline color. The type of the argument is string. purpose: It speciﬁes the purpose name. The type of the argument is string. The default value is drawing. priority: It speciﬁes the priority of layer. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0. sel: It speciﬁes the selectability of a layer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

stipple: It speciﬁes the name of stipple. The type of the argument is string. streamNo: It speciﬁes the stream number. The type of the argument is int. style: It speciﬁes the name of line style. The type of the argument is string. use: It speciﬁes the valid of a layer. The type of the argument is bool. The default

value is 1. vis: It speciﬁes the visibility of a layer. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1. width: It speciﬁes the width of line. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 1.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeSetColPat -selall 1 > aeSetColPat -addLayer -layerName "M1" -layerNo 2 -purpose "drawing" -outlineColor "blue" -ﬁllColor "green" -stipple "red" -style "solid" -width 2 -vis 1 -sel 1 -use 1 > aeSetColPat -delLayer -layerNo 2 -purpose "drawing"

## 141.1 aeAddHighLightCircle

SYNTAX

aeAddHighLightCircle -center centerPoint -radius radius [ -color color ] [

-ratio ratio ] [ -zoom zoom ] [ -draw draw ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

ﬁg

#### DESCRIPTION

The command creates a circle cartoon in the drawarea.

center: It speciﬁes the point of circle. The type of the argument is point. radius: It speciﬁes the circle’s radius. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. color: It speciﬁes the color identiﬁer. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0. ratio: It speciﬁes the ratio value. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. zoom: It speciﬁes whether to zoom to the highlighted objects. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1. draw: It speciﬁes whether to draw the new objects immediately. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

#### SYNTAX

## 141.4 aeAddHighLightLabel

#### SYNTAX

aeAddHighLightLabel -point point -label textName -height height [ -orient orient ] [ -justify justify ] [ -font font ] [ -draft draft ] [ -color color ] [ -ratio ratio ] [ -zoom zoom ] [ -draw draw ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

ﬁg

#### DESCRIPTION

The command creates a label cartoon in the drawarea.

#### ARGUMENTS

point: It speciﬁes the original point of label. The type of the argument is point. label: It speciﬁes the text of the label. The type of the argument is string. height: It speciﬁes height of the label. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 1.0.

orient: It speciﬁes the orient of the label. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are R0, R90, R180, R270, MY, MYR90, MX and MXR90. The default value is R0.

justify: It speciﬁes the justiﬁcation of the label. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are upperLeft, centerLeft, lowerLeft, upperCenter, centerCenter, lowerCenter, upperRight, centerRight and lowerRight. The default value is lowerLeft.

font: It speciﬁes the font of the label. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are euroStyle, gothic, math, roman, script, stick, ﬁxed, swedish, milSpec, modern and contemplate1. The default value is stick.

draft: It speciﬁes whether label is drafting or not. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

color: It speciﬁes the color identiﬁer. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0.

ratio: It speciﬁes the ratio value. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. zoom: It speciﬁes whether to zoom to the highlighted objects. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

141.5. aeAddHighLightLine

draw: It speciﬁes whether to draw the new objects immediately. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeAddHighLightLabel -point (0,0) -label "abc" -height 1.0 -orient R90 -justify lowerLeft -font stick

## 141.7 aeAddHighLightPath

#### SYNTAX

aeAddHighLightPath -point points -width width [ -style style [ -beginExt beginExt ] [ -endExt endExt ] ] [ -color color ] [ -ratio ratio ] [ -zoom zoom ] [ draw draw ] [ -arcSegmentsNum arcSegmentsNum ] [ -cornerType cornerType [ -cutoﬀRatio cutoﬀRatio ] [ -curveRadius curveRadius ] ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

ﬁg

#### DESCRIPTION

The command creates a path cartoon in the drawarea.

#### ARGUMENTS

point: It speciﬁes the points of rectangle. The type of the argument is point_list. width: It speciﬁes width of path. The type of the argument is ﬂoat.

style: It speciﬁes style of path. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Truncate, Extend, Round and Variable. The default value is Truncate.

beginExt: It speciﬁes begin extension value of variable path. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.0.

endExt: It speciﬁes end extension value of variable path. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.0.

arcSegmentsNum: It speciﬁes the number of circle segments for path. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 72.

cornerType: It speciﬁes corner type of path. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Square, Mitered, Adaptive _mitered, Curve and Round. The default value is Square.

cutoﬀRatio: It speciﬁes the cutoﬀ ratio percentage of the path with Mitered or Adapative_mitered corner type. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.3.

curveRadius: It speciﬁes the max radius of the path with Curve corner type. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. The default value is 0.

color: It speciﬁes the color identiﬁer. The type of the argument is int. The default value is 0.

ratio: It speciﬁes the ratio value. The type of the argument is ﬂoat. zoom: It speciﬁes whether to zoom to the highlighted objects. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1. draw: It speciﬁes whether to draw the new objects immediately. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 1.

#### EXAMPLES

> aeAddHighLightPath -point $point

axisObject: It speciﬁes axis objects or select frame. The type of the argument is bool. The default value is 0.

The type of the argument is string.

direction: It speciﬁes the direction to arrange the ﬁeld ﬁeld. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are horizontal and vertical. The default value is horizontal.

itemsPerRow: It speciﬁes the number of radio buttons per row. The type of the argument is int.

callback: It speciﬁes the ﬁeld click callback list. The type of the argument is list.

## 147.13 geSetCursor

#### SYNTAX

geSetCursor [ -type type ]

#### RETURNED TYPE

bool

#### DESCRIPTION

This command set the cursor to the speciﬁed cursor. If type is speciﬁed to Restore, the cursor will be set to the last used cursor type. This function should be used as pair. Once changing the cursor, you need to restore back to the last state, Or the cursor state will be in a mess. If the cursor has not been changed by Tcl command, Restore will not make diﬀerence. Default speciﬁes Restore.

#### ARGUMENTS

type: It speciﬁes the cursor type. The type of the argument is enum. The values of the enumeration are Arrow, Cross, Wait, Busy and Restore. The default value is Restore.

#### EXAMPLES

> geSetCursor -type Busy

## 150.5 mdeCreateDesignNetlist

#### SYNTAX

mdeCreateDesignNetlist -cv cell view -destDir destination directory

string_list

## 150.6 mdeCreateMCSimulationNetlist

SYNTAX

mdeCreateMCSimulationNetlist -cv cell view -corner the name of the corner to netlist -ﬁrstRun the MC start run -numRuns the MC number run -destDir destination directory

RETURNED TYPE

string_list

DESCRIPTION

This command creates the netlist scs ﬁles for the speciﬁed simulation point for Monte Carlo simulation, and returns a list of the ﬁle paths. Under a mixed-signal environment, the list may contain multiple ﬁle paths. The returned list can be iterated through by foreach command.

ARGUMENTS

cv: Indicate the cell view identiﬁer The type of the argument is sleade.

corner: Indicate the name of the corner to netlist. The enabled corner names can be retrieved through mdeGetEnabledCornerList command. The type of the argument is string.

ﬁrstRun: Indicate the MC start run The type of the argument is int. numRuns: Indicate the MC number run The type of the argument is int. destDir: Indicate the destination directory where the netlist will be created The type of the argument is string.

EXAMPLES

> set ﬁles [mdeCreateMCSimulationNetlist -cv $cv -corner "C1" -ﬁrstRun 1 numRuns 50 -destDir "/abs/path/to/dest/dir"]

> foreach {ﬁle} $ﬁles { > puts "ﬁle: $ﬁle" > }

#### RETURNED TYPE

string_list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command creates netlist scs ﬁles for the speciﬁed simulation point and returns a list of those ﬁle paths. Under a mixed-signal environment, the list may contain multiple ﬁle paths. The returned list can be iterated through by foreach command.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: Indicate the cell view identiﬁer The type of the argument is sleade.

corner: Indicate the name of the corner to netlist. The enabled corner names can be retrieved through mdeGetEnabledCornerList command. The type of the argument is string.

sweepName: Indicate the name of the sweep to netlist. The enabled sweep names can be retrieved through mdeGetEnabledSweepList command. The type of the argument is string.

destDir: Indicate the destination directory where the netlist will be created The type of the argument is string.

#### EXAMPLES

> set ﬁles [mdeCreateSimulationNetlist -cv $cv -corner "C1" -sweepName "prf=50,nf=25" -destDir "/abs/path/to/dest/dir"]

## 150.8 mdeGetEnabledCornerList

#### SYNTAX

mdeGetEnabledCornerList -cv cell view

#### RETURNED TYPE

string_list

#### DESCRIPTION

This command returns a list containing the names of all the enabled corners of the speciﬁed mde state. If a corner C1 contains sweeps, which leads to four sub-corners, the returned corner name list will contain C1_0, C1_1, C1_2 and C1_3. The returned list can be iterated through by foreach command.

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: Indicate the MDE cell view identiﬁer The type of the argument is sleade.

#### EXAMPLES

mdeGetEnabledSweepList -cv cell view

string_list

#### ARGUMENTS

cv: Indicate the cell view identiﬁer The type of the argument is sleade.

#### EXAMPLES

> set sweeps [mdeGetEnabledSweepList -cv $cv] > foreach {sweep} $sweeps { > puts "sweep: $sweep" > }

# Part XII Python Script

# Chapter 151 Introduction

pyAether is a Python interface based on Aether system, including base and extension modules in API Reference, which is aimed at script development based on Aether system to meet more ﬂexible usage scenarios.

Python is a more modern, user-friendly and object-oriented language than Tcl language. Tcl is not ”deep” enough, and does not have enough data structure. Most importantly, Python is an open language with lots of MIT packages and communities.

According to the above, pyAether is released to help users quickly develop high quality tools based on Aether database for integrated design. In the future, the use of pyAether is a general trend. Join and enjoy it!

# Chapter 152 API Reference

# Part XIII FAQ

# Chapter 153 Data

- 1. Q: What is the input range value in Aether command forms? A: Diﬀerent DBUPerUU values will determine the input range value. That is, when DBUPerUU=1000, the range value is [-2.1e+6,2.1e+6]; when DBUPerUU=100, range value is [-2.1e+7,2.1e+7].
- 2. Q: How to import gds to Aether ? A: Activate the command File ->Import ->GDS, in the GDS File Name ﬁeld, type the name of the ﬁle which you want to translate, in the Library Name ﬁeld, type the name of library which you want to be translated, select the technology ﬁle, then press OK button, the gds is imported to Aether .
- 3. Q: Why the data become 10 times bigger or smaller than the original data after importing gds? A: The reason for this is often caused by inappropriate technology ﬁle. In order to avoid this situation, we suggest that when you activate Import >GDS, please type new library name in the GDS File Name or select Do Not Need Technology.
- 4. Q: Why there are so many warning message when importing gds to Aether sometimes? A: In order to make sure the correctness of data, Aether will check the data straitly, such as vertex number of path or polygon, the width of path, zero-area shape and so on. These may cause many warning message.
- 5. Q: Why the display of data imported to Aether is diﬀerent from the one imported to other tool? A: The gds only contains shape information, does not include any display information. And the mechanism of display in Aether is diﬀerent from other tool. In order to make sure the same display, you may specify the technology ﬁle and display resource ﬁle when importing gds.
- 6. Q: Why some gds cannot be imported to Aether ? A: This is a very rare occurrence, but the reason is often caused by error when


Chapter 153. Data

transfer data, such as transfer gds by ftp. It uses ASCII mode not BIN mode to transfer gds in Linux , that may cause gds error.

- 7. Q: Why the vertex number of path or polygon becomes less after exporting gds from Aether ? A: The gds is a data format with very long history, at the beginning of its formulation, it did not consider to support big data, so it made limitation for the vertex number of path and polygon. In the former version, it only supported 200 vertexes. Now Aether uses the newest gds version, however the newest version only supports 8000 vertexes. So if the vertex number of path or polygon is more than 8000, Aether will cut these shapes in order to make sure the vertex number of these shape is less than 8000.
- 8. Q: In a schematic design, can net A and net A< 0:2> coexist? A: No. In a schematic design, a bus net’s base name should not be the same as a scalar net’s name.
- 9. Q: In schematic, are net a and A the same net? A: No. They are diﬀerent nets.
- 10. Q: Why Aether is so slow, even if only opening a small design in read mode? A: If the design is really small, and Aether opens it very slowly, you should check whether lock ﬁle or cache ﬁle exists or not. Aether will generate some ﬁles for data security, for example, lock ﬁle and cache ﬁle. These ﬁles will be left only Aether exits abnormally. Aether will use server names in these ﬁles to do some checks on data. If Aether cannot connect these servers by name(These servers may be removed from wlan, but Aether can get IP by NIS), all operations about design, for example, open, will be in low performance.

You can use the following command in terminal to ﬁnd these ﬁles find libPath -type f -name "*lck" -print or find libPath -type f -name "*oacache" -print

- 11. Q: How to update PDK to tbcload 1.7? A: Aether has updated tbcload from 1.4 to 1.7 since Sep. 2016. If when Aether starts, there are some errors as follows:


![image 10846](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10846.png)

Figure 153.1 Error Information

It is because old codes in emyLibInit.tcl do not support higher version of tbcload.

5508 Aether Reference Manual, 2025.09

Please open the emyLibInit.tcl under the library, and ﬁnd the codes as follows:

![image 10847](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10847.png)

Figure 153.2 Old Codes

Replace all these codes by loadTbcload. The updated codes can work in the old version of Aether .

12. Q:What is the layer number of system layer? A:Aether has taken the number from 196 to 255 as system layer. So we would suggest you avoid creating layer by the layer number.

Aether Reference Manual, 2025.09 5509

# Chapter 154 Operation

- 1. Q:When Aether running is too slow, how can you get the reason? A:Aether supplies aether_watch to search and print the causes of running slow. For example, when exporting netlist is slow, you can do it like below:

- • Enter ps in the terminal which Aether is launched. There will be two oa2netlist in screen as follows:

![image 10848](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10848.png)

Figure 154.1 Processes in Terminal

- • Please select the bigger id. Here choose 24524.
- • Enter aether_watch 24524 in the terminal.
- • aether_watch will exit automatically when oa2netlist ﬁnished and generate a log ﬁle named aether_watch.log.


- 2. Q: Why Trace Net doesn’t work under hierarchical mode sometimes? A: When Magnify’s value is double-precision value, the Trace Net operation may be failure.
- 3. Q: Why the shortcut of Aether works abnormally when you use Aether by vncviewer and turn Caps Lock on? A: For example, Copy&Chop. The following behavior is in a real rhel5 machine.


5511

Table 154.1 Shortcuts on RHEL5

| |Caps Lock Oﬀ|Caps Lock On|
|---|---|---|
|C<br><br>|Copy<br><br>|Copy|
|Shift+C|Chop<br><br>|Chop|


in other words, shortcuts are not decided by caps of letter. it is decide by combination of keys. The following behavior is in vncviewer/server:

Table 154.2 Shortcuts on VNC

| |Caps Lock Oﬀ|Caps Lock On|
|---|---|---|
|C|Copy<br><br>|Chop|
|Shift+C<br><br>|Chop|Copy|


Besides, the combination of keys Shift+Delete couldn’t work properly.

- 4. Q: Why sometimes I have deleted library A, Aether can not create lib A again? A: In order to avoid delete data in hard disk, if you do not check the option Delete From Disk in Delete Library, Aether only remove library deﬁnition from lib.defs, but do not delete the library ﬁle A from disk. So if you want to create library A again, Aether will remind you that the ﬁle A has already existed. If you really want to delete library A and its ﬁle, please check the option Delete From Disk.
- 5. Q: Why the hierarchical relationship in Show Tree cannot be refreshed in real time? A: Show Tree is independent from Aether , in order to improve the eﬃciency of Show Tree, Show Tree does not refresh in real time when the design has been modiﬁed in Aether . You had better close Show Tree ﬁrst, then modify the hierarchical relationship of designs, then activate Show Tree again.
- 6. Q: How to modify the display of layer? A: Double-click at layer in LSW, it will pop up Layer Setting form, then you can modify the display of layer. We suggest you use Detail mode.
- 7. Q: How to switch Spacing mode in Align quickly? A: Aether supply Space to turn on or oﬀ the option of Spacing in Align.
- 8. Q: How to ﬁnd help document in Aether ? A: Click Help in any command form, it will pop up the corresponding help document.
- 9. Q:Why sometimes I can not create the ﬁrst label when creating bus label using line method?


![image 10849](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10849.png)

Figure 154.2 Can not create A1 on path

A:A larger shape overlaps on it. Aether creates the ﬁrst label A1 on the rectangle. You can set Skip Width in Create Label form to skip it.

![image 10850](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10850.png)

Figure 154.3 Set Skip Width

Aether Reference Manual, 2025.09 5513

![image 10851](Aether_Manual_crop_images/imageFile10851.png)

Figure 154.4 Create A1 on path

- 10. Q:How to change net name in schematic. A:In Aether schematic, if you select wire, activate Property to change wire name, all the segments belong to this net would change at the same time. However, if you select wire name, activate Property to change wire name, only this segment net would change name.
- 11. Q:How to use eduction license? A: Aether supplies to set EMPYREAN_EDU environment variable, set this enviroment variable, Aether only checks education license when doing Export GDS and Export Netlist. Using this license, the maximal number of instances Aether can export is 1200, and gds ﬁle size is not allowed larger than 120M.
- 12. Q:How to solve the problems caused by cross-server login through ssh or XManager? A: Aether supplies to set QT_XCB_NATIVE_PAINTING environment variable, which can solve the startup failure and stuck problems caused by cross-server login through ssh or XManager. For example, you can input the following command into the terminal: setenv QT_XCB_NATIVE_PAINTING 1.
- 13. Q:How to conﬁgure the Text Editor in Settings? A: Aether supports any text editor like gvim or gedit, in addition, you can also use terminal like xterm, gnome-terminal or konsole.

# Appendix B Aether Interface

- 1. Conﬁgure File

The conﬁgure ﬁle name is aether_interface.xml. Put the conﬁgure ﬁle to $HOME/.empyrean and when you start the Aether, the speciﬁed command will be created according to the contents of the ﬁle.

- 2. Conﬁgure File Content

|<Interfaces><br><br><Interface> <name>Hello World TCL . . .</name> <viewtype>layout</viewtype> <readmode>true</readmode> <program>test . t c l</program> <!−−<paradesign>true</paradesign> <parameters>a b</parameters>−−><br><br></ Interface> <Interface> . . .<br><br></ Interface><br><br>. . . </ Interfaces><br><br>|
|---|


- 3. Conﬁgure File Fields


- • <Interface>...</Interface> It means you deﬁne a command.
- • <name>...</name> It is the command name.
- • <menu>...</menu> It is the menu name which the command will be added to. If this parameter is not deﬁned, it will be added to ToolBox in default.


- • <viewtype>...</viewtype> It is the command type, including the layout, schematic and symbol three types.
- • <readmode>...</readmode> It is a bool type which indicates whether the command is displayed in read-only mode or not.
- • <program>...</program> It is the name of the external program to be executed. Aether searches external program from the Linux PATH environment variable.
- • <paradesign>...</paradesign> It is a bool type which will set the libName, cellName and viewName as parameters. If you deﬁne this parameter, the parameters will be ignored.
- • <parameters>...</parameters> It deﬁnes parameters which pass to command.
- • <!– ... –> This is the comment syntax in xml ﬁle.


- 4. Usage and Tutorial
